Through matched causal comparisons such as Fixed Generation and Recorded Replay, the authors isolate self-generated feedback as the causal driver of the damage, showing that writing itself is not the problem since the same update mechanisms improve performance on real text.

entry.title: Same Predictions, Different Harms: Causal Auditing of Patient World Models

author.name: Yicheng Qi, Xiyi Xiong

entry.summary: The paper shows that patient world models used for clinical trial simulation can agree on transition kernels and arm-level risk while disagreeing on the counterfactual fraction of patients harmed by a treatment switch. Using a two-stage structural causal model, the authors derive closed-form sharp bounds on harm for up to three intermediate health states and calibrated outer bounds under relaxed independence assumptions. This exposes a reliability gap in intervention-aware reasoning for medical AI.

entry.title: What Does a Harness Repair? A Preregistered Study of Visibility, Baseline Adequacy and Evaluation Defects

author.name: Bowen Xu, Boyu Chen

entry.summary: This preregistered study examines where harness-search score gains come from when prompts, reasoning switches, token budgets, or parsers change around a frozen model, using three models, three benchmarks, and six injected evaluation defects across 47 primary endpoints. Notably, turning thinking off often raised accuracy, but gains mostly came from questions where the capped setting yielded no readable answer, revealing evaluation defects rather than genuine capability changes.

entry.title: AgentDoxx: Agentic Re-identification of Anonymized Text with Web Search

author.name: Jianing Wen, Tianshi Li

entry.summary: AgentDOXX is an evaluation suite of 822 synthetic interview transcripts grounded in public information about real individuals, used to measure how LLMs with web-search tools can re-identify anonymized text. The study evaluates fifteen model configurations, isolating web search effects and analyzing search trajectories to distinguish retrieval-driven from inference-driven re-identification.

entry.title: Runaway Reaction: When Benign Skills Compose into Malicious Behavior

author.name: Zunlong Zhou, Ziyuan Yang, Mengyu Sun, Yi Zhang

entry.summary: This security study shows that composing individually benign agent skills from public marketplaces can induce malicious behaviors even when every skill passes security vetting. Composition expands the agent's capability space to enable behaviors unavailable to any single skill, and some target behaviors remain achievable through indirect composition strategies. The work exposes a systemic gap in current skill-level security evaluation.

entry.title: Fine-Tuning a 3B-Parameter LLM on a Smartphone: Characterizing Sustained Training

author.name: Andrew Geyko, Marius Mosbach, Andr\'e Brinkmann

entry.summary: First systematic characterization of full fine-tuning runs of a 3B-parameter LLM on a mobile device, measuring memory, per-step latency, thermal throttling, and energy on an iPhone 17 Pro. The striking result is that a phone can fine-tune a 3B model for a typical user within one battery charge, and on-device adapters match server-trained adapters for personalization.

entry.title: MatrixFormer: A Foundation Model for Matrix Completion

author.name: Dwaipayan Saha, Jacob Feitelberg, Kyuseong Choi, Raaz Dwivedi, Anish Agarwal

entry.summary: MatrixFormer is a pre-trained matrix-native transformer that predicts full distributions for every missing entry in a single forward pass, trained entirely on synthetic low-rank and latent-factor matrices under diverse missingness patterns. The same weights perform competitively zero-shot on causal inference panel-data tasks, tabular imputation, benchmark-score completion, and recommendation systems. It matters because matrix completion underlies many statistical and ML problems yet lacks a foundation-model treatment.

entry.title: Dynamic Harness Search: Building Multi-Agent Systems Per-Query via Prediction

author.name: Som Sagar, Shasha Li, Hejie Cui, Ransalu Senanayake, Sercan \"{O}. Ar{\i}k

entry.summary: SHIFT learns a policy over harness-building actions with a local LLM architect and a value function predicting accuracy-cost tradeoffs, then uses Monte Carlo tree search to construct a tailored multi-agent harness per query without executing alternatives at inference time. Evaluated across 9,193 tasks in six benchmarks. This tackles the expensive, manual problem of agent system design.

entry.title: Cross-Trait Transfer in Subliminal Learning

author.name: Xingyu Zhao, Yiqiao Zhong

entry.summary: Studies cross-trait transfer in subliminal learning, where student models acquire teacher behavioral traits from semantically unrelated outputs, introducing a directed trait-transfer matrix based on log-probability gains. It finds trait clusters, with students developing preferences for related but not necessarily identical traits. This has direct safety implications for distillation pipelines and trait control.

entry.title: Hierarchical Credit Assignment for RLVR on Fused Gromov-Wasserstein Geometry

author.name: Qi Yu, Ruizhong Qiu, Zhichen Zeng, Xuying Ning, Yanjun Zhao, Dongqi Fu, Yinglong Xia, Hong Li, Hanghang Tong

entry.summary: HarA improves group-based RLVR (e.g., GRPO) by replacing uniform token advantages with hierarchical credit assignment that identifies semantically novel reasoning behaviors, representing rollouts on a Fused Gromov-Wasserstein geometry rather than relying on local signals like token position or entropy. Targets better reward shaping for LLM reasoning training. An interesting intersection of optimal transport and RL post-training.

entry.title: How Long, Not How Close: A Learned Temporal Metric for Planning in Latent World Models

author.name: Lama Moukheiber, Haotian Xue, Yongxin Chen

entry.summary: The paper introduces TEMPO, a temporal-distance planning objective for latent world models that replaces similarity-based latent distances with a learned metric reflecting the number of environment steps between states. It requires no changes to the frozen world model, learns only from existing demonstrations, and adds negligible planner overhead.

entry.title: Understanding the Weight Averaging Mechanism in LLM Training for Post-Training Quantization

author.name: Hanzhang Wang, Tianqi Shen, Zonglin Liu, Junze He, Difan Zou, Ziye Ma

entry.summary: This work explains why weight averaging during LLM pretraining improves post-training quantization performance relative to learning-rate decay, formulating it as a trade-off between retaining training progress and robustness under perturbation. The mechanistic understanding aims to make the technique's gains consistent and reliable for practitioners.

entry.title: When Low Prediction Error Misleads Planning: Diagnosing Representation, Dynamics, and Decision Failures in Latent World Models

author.name: Rui Min, Xianyao Li, Fang Xu, Jing Du

entry.summary: Shows that the error component dominating a latent world model's prediction loss is often not the one whose repair most improves planning. Using controlled comparisons across four model families and four tasks, the authors find center error dominates MSE in most cells, yet oracle corrections targeting action-relative responses yield better planning quality despite higher latent MSE.

entry.title: ORCA: The Annealed Spectral Conditioning Optimizer for Faster, Better LLM Training

author.name: Yuanshi Liu, Boyuan Jiang, Liang Hou, Xin Tao, Pengfei Wan, Zhouchen Lin, Cong Fang

entry.summary: ORCA addresses why stronger spectral control of weight matrices in LLM optimizers like Muon has yielded only modest gains: concentrated spectra suppress useful gradient directions while permanent constraints limit adaptation. It applies strong temporary soft orthogonality regularization early in training and then removes it, letting weights benefit from broader spectra early and adapt freely later. Results are shown across LLaMA, Qwen3, and other settings.

entry.title: A Fine-Grained Analysis of the LoRA Fine-Tuning Landscape with Implications for Data Selection

author.name: Bowen Zhang, Changrui Fang, Xinsong Ma, Jiaye Teng, Ziye Ma

entry.summary: This paper develops sharper landscape theory for LoRA fine-tuning using modern nonconvex low-rank matrix sensing results, addressing the unresolved question of how to choose adapter rank. The central insight is that the appropriate rank should reflect the conditioning of the optimization landscape, balancing poor conditioning at small ranks against efficiency losses at large ranks, with implications for data selection. It moves beyond guarantees established under restrictive settings.

entry.title: How Sparse Probability Maps Shape Mixture-of-Experts Routing

author.name: Tom\'as Brogueira, Marcos Treviso, Miguel Couceiro

entry.summary: The authors study whether sparsity-inducing router probability maps (sparsemax, entmax, normmax) retain their adaptive, token-dependent expert sparsity after training large top-2 MoE language models at 300M and 1B scale. They find these maps behave very differently in practice than softmax once trained, e.g., at 1B scale entmax discards 30% less probability mass while almost never dropping a selected expert.

entry.title: Conformal Prediction with Paraphrase-Aware Scoring for LLM Uncertainty Quantification

author.name: Jiayi Xin, Evan Qiang, Zihan Zhu, Xiang Li, Weijie J. Su, Qi Long

entry.summary: Proposes a paraphrase-aware uncertainty quantification framework for LLMs that remains stable under meaning-preserving rewordings, training a lightweight proxy on hidden states and aggregating predictions across paraphrases into nonconformity scores. It retains marginal coverage guarantees for conformal calibration under score exchangeability. This addresses a real weakness of formal UQ methods in deployed LLMs.

entry.title: The Poisoned Conversation: Privacy-Leaking Watermarks in Unified Multimodal Models

author.name: Tobias Braun, Jonas Henry Grebe, Emil Sivic, Patrick Mohr Gordillo, Hossein Shakibania, Marcus Rohrbach, Anna Rohrbach

entry.summary: The paper identifies a new privacy threat in unified multimodal models: malicious providers can embed invisible, trigger-dependent watermarks (Privacy-Leaking Watermarks) conditioned on prior chat history, causing later outputs in another modality to leak sensitive information. This undermines the assumption that locally deployed models keep conversations private. The work matters because it exposes a previously unrecognized attack surface in the increasingly common unified text-plus-image architectures.

entry.title: Learning to Learn a Language

author.name: Lennart Carstens-Behrens, Holger Fr\"ohlich

entry.summary: This work presents PFLM, a 300M-parameter byte-level transformer pretrained exclusively on samples from synthetic non-linguistic priors generated by recurrent structural causal models. Despite never seeing real language, the model learns in-context to predict text continuation by inferring an unseen language from its prefix, with training data exhibiting Zipfian and long-range dependence signatures of natural text. This is a striking demonstration of in-context learning emerging purely from meta-learned synthetic structure.

entry.title: Readout Blindness: VLM Scores Miss the Spatial Direction Their Frozen Encoders Retain

author.name: Guangyuan Li, Tianming Du, Yan Jiang, Bihan Wen, Jiancheng Yang

entry.summary: The paper identifies readout blindness: CLIP-like vision-language models score near chance on directed spatial relations because symmetric scoring rules cancel directional information that frozen encoders actually retain. The proposed Antisymmetric Displacement Readout aligns caption words with image patches and scores relations by signed displacement between matched object centroids, improving performance without any training or learned parameters. This shows the spatial-relation failure is a readout problem, not an encoding problem.

entry.title: RealtimeWAM: One-Step Asynchronous World Action Models

author.name: Chengtao Lv, Jinyang Du, Shuyi Feng, Yang Yong, Shiqiao Gu, Shunzi Yang, Ruihao Gong, Shen Ren, Tianwei Zhang, Wenya Wang

entry.summary: RealtimeWAM tackles two inference bottlenecks in World Action Models, which use video generation backbones to guide action prediction: multi-step action denoising within the action expert and sequential waiting between video and action experts. The authors propose Teacher-Anchored Consistency Distillation (TACD) for one-step action generation plus an asynchronous inference scheme, achieving dramatically more efficient real-time embodied action prediction. This is relevant to robotics and interactive applications where latency is critical.

entry.title: How Much Do LLM-as-a-Judge Design Choices Matter? A Systematic Comparison of Prompt Designs, Rating Scales, and Models

author.name: Laur\`ene Vaugrante, Thilo Hagendorff

entry.summary: This systematic study evaluates how LLM-as-a-judge design choices, including prompt design, rating scale, and model selection, affect evaluation verdicts across 10 reasoning models and multiple tasks (sentiment/toxicity rating and QA accuracy classification). The authors find significant disagreements between judge configurations and human ground truth, implying that intuitive design choices can lead two studies to different conclusions about the same facts. It provides a much-needed empirical basis for standardizing judge-based evaluation.

entry.title: Noise Out, Bias In: Targeted Bias Injection in Diffusion Language Models via Closed-Loop Activation Steering

author.name: Sarim Hashmi, Mukul Ranjan, Abdelrahman Elsayed, Muhammad Umer Sheikh, Fahad Shamshad, Nils Lukas

entry.summary: This security paper shows that masked diffusion language models expose their answer distribution at every denoising step before commitment, enabling an adversary with activation access to run a closed-loop steering attack that watches progress toward a chosen demographic answer and adaptively injects bias. It demonstrates targeted bias injection against frozen dLLMs. This reveals a novel attack surface specific to iterative denoising generation.

entry.title: T-Search: An Open Agentic Retriever and Playground for Hard Multi-Step Search

author.name: Olga Tsymboi, Ramil Latypov, Aleksandr Medvedev, Danil Taranets, Dmitrii Stoianov, Nikita Gulyakov, Gleb Alektorov, Anatolii Potapov

entry.summary: T-Search is an open-weight agentic retriever, built on the existing Qwen3.6-35B-A3B model, that performs bounded multi-round search and returns ranked evidence chunks with justifications, decoupling retrieval from answer generation. Trained with round-sliced SFT plus GSPO on a recall reward over adversarially filtered synthetic tasks, it reaches 56.0 Recall@10 with one rollout across seven English and Russian benchmarks, beating larger open models.

entry.title: A differentiable Lagrangian-coupled 3D Gaussian Splatting-SPH model for forward simulation and inverse analysis in solid mechanics

author.name: Tian Xu, Soroush Atashi, Tianju Xue

entry.summary: This paper couples 3D Gaussian Splatting reconstruction with smoothed particle hydrodynamics in a differentiable Lagrangian framework, enabling both forward simulation of deformable solids and inverse identification of material parameters. It extends 3DGS beyond plausible animation toward mechanically interpretable digital models with estimable constitutive behavior.

entry.title: Geometry-Aware Preference Optimization for Text-to-Image Diffusion Models

author.name: Lei Wang, Zhen Wang, Yuexiang Xie, Yaliang Li

entry.summary: This paper revisits Diffusion-DPO for text-to-image alignment through the lens of the manifold hypothesis, arguing that optimizing preferences in the full ambient space ignores the low-dimensional manifold structure of natural images. The authors propose a geometry-aware variant of preference optimization that accounts for this structure. The analysis offers a principled diagnosis of why DPO-style alignment can underperform for diffusion models.

entry.title: BossouChimpanzee: Long-term Chimpanzee Video Dataset

author.name: Daniel Schofield, Susana Carvalho, Vladimir Iashin, Andrew Zisserman, Max Bain, Arsha Nagrani, David Ng, Claudia Sousa, Boniface Zogbila, Jules Dor\'e, Dora Biro, Misato Hayashi, Tetsuro Matsuzawa

entry.summary: This paper releases BossouChimpanzee, a long-term video archive of wild chimpanzees in Guinea spanning three decades (1988-2018) with over 1,200 hours of recordings, including an initial ~74-hour annotated snapshot (23 identified individuals) for individual and action recognition. Authored by a strong interdisciplinary team including Zisserman, Iashin, and Nagrani, it supports cognitive science, primatology, and animal behavior AI. Such longitudinal animal video data is extremely rare and scientifically valuable.

entry.title: InteractionBench: A Real-Time Interaction Benchmark for Streaming Video Systems

author.name: Enxin Song, Suhao Yu, Yifei Xu, Barbara Su, Weili Xu, Wenhao Chai, Yao Tang, Jie Deng, Haiyang Xu, Jiatao Gu

entry.summary: Introduces InteractionBench, a benchmark evaluating whether streaming video assistants decide correctly when to speak and when to stay silent, covering query responses, event triggers, and ongoing updates across 1,060 interactions over 812 videos. It scores content accuracy, timing accuracy, and silence compliance on the video clock, revealing a stark trade-off where even strong systems emit on most silent segments.

entry.title: BabelFake: A Multilingual Audio-Visual DeepFake Benchmark

author.name: Carlotta Segna, Joel Tschesche, Anna Rohrbach

entry.summary: BabelFake is a multilingual audio-visual deepfake benchmark with 399k clips (1,323 hours) from 496 consenting individuals across five European languages, using 11 modern video manipulation types plus audio synthesis. It addresses the English-only, outdated, and consent-deficient nature of existing deepfake datasets.

entry.title: PerturBot: Breaking Shortcut Priors in Vision-Language-Action Models with Perturbative Training

author.name: Mingyu Liu, Chonghao Sima, Tianjian Feng, Hanqing Wang, Cong Chen, Hao Chen, Chunhua Shen

entry.summary: PerturBot identifies modality shortcuts in VLA models, where visual, lexical, or motor cues suffice to predict expert actions without genuine task evidence. It proposes perturbative training to break these shortcut priors, noting that more demonstrations of the same kind can raise success rates while leaving the spurious dependencies intact.

entry.title: Lie Rarely, Lie Big: Stealthy Insider Attacks on LLM Robot Teams

author.name: Sribalaji C. Anand, George J. Pappas

entry.summary: Studies stealthy insider attacks in multi-robot teams whose planning and trust decisions are delegated to LLM agents, using a multi-robot survey task with verifiable measurements and costly verification. The paper derives bounds on the probability that an adversary's false reports evade verification and on the resulting map error, framing stealth relative to the team's own detectors.

entry.title: I-BFM: Reward-Conditioned Robust Humanoid Interaction via Unsupervised Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Ziqi Han, Yitang Li, Junhan Sun, Fanrong Dong, Yaojie Shen, Lei Ye, Zetong Jing, Yongqi Zhang, Yiming Zhang, Xue Wang, Hao Zhao

entry.summary: I-BFM is claimed to be the first behavioral foundation model for humanoid-object interaction, learning a shared representation of humanoid, object, and contact dynamics via forward-backward representations and unsupervised RL. The same policy can then be conditioned on latent commands to execute closed-loop interaction for arbitrary downstream rewards without task-specific fine-tuning. This extends the zero-shot generalization promise of BFMs from locomotion/control to physical manipulation.

entry.title: Research Note: Filtering Subversion-Relevant Information From Pretraining Data Is Feasible

author.name: Kyle O’Brien

entry.summary: Researchers from Geodesic and Redwood Research pretrain multiple 30B LLMs from scratch on filtered versus unfiltered data, removing subversion strategies, defenses, and empirical evaluations of subversion effectiveness. Filtered models know substantially less about subversion while retaining general ML capabilities, suggesting data filtering could reduce the danger of misaligned models. This is a preliminary research note with a full report promised, but the core feasibility result is demonstrated.

entry.title: Decide, Ask, or Defer: Clinical LLMs under Incomplete Evidence

author.name: Mingzhan Yang, Weili Wu

entry.summary: The paper introduces a DECIDE/ASK/DEFER formulation for clinical LLMs, requiring models to judge whether evidence is sufficient for autonomous decisions rather than only choosing between deciding and abstaining, plus a blinded protocol hiding evidence-completeness metadata. Evaluating Qwen, Gemini, and GPT on 200 matched clinical evidence states from DDXPlus reveals substantial disagreement (137 of 200 states) and that targeted versus random information acquisition changes decision likelihood.

entry.title: Readable Before Actionable: Causal Tracing of Indirect Prompt Injection

author.name: Zhe Yu, Wenpeng Xing, Xingxing Yang, Meng Han

entry.summary: This work uses counterfactual role probes, activation patching, and interventions on AgentDojo trajectories to causally trace how indirect prompt injection changes agent actions. Findings show role decoding is robust to content and format changes, and directions estimated from hijacked versus resisted trajectories reduce attack success at specific pre-action and injected-span positions but not at random positions.

entry.title: HERA: Harness-Environment Co-Evolution for Reliable Agentic Abstention

author.name: Han Luo, Bingbing Wen, Guang Yang, Zora Zhiruo Wang, Pan Lu, Lucy Lu Wang

entry.summary: HERA addresses agentic abstention — recognizing when tool-use tasks are infeasible — via harness-environment co-evolution: a pipeline that automatically constructs verifiable feasible/infeasible task pairs through controlled environment mutations, plus a co-evolutionary training scheme. This avoids overfitting to a fixed task set and improves generalization to unseen failure modes.

entry.title: Understanding and Mitigating Hallucination Escape in Tool-Using LLM Agents

author.name: Peigui Qi, Kunsheng Tang, Yide Song, Weiming Zhang, Nenghai Yu

entry.summary: The paper identifies Hallucination Escape, a failure mode where existing tool-hallucination mitigations reduce errors on the configuration they were tuned on while increasing hallucination on other configurations, canceling the gain. It shows hallucination spikes when intrinsic tool-use tendencies conflict with the current tool configuration and that prior methods reinforce rather than suppress these tendencies.

entry.title: Organising Trajectory Evidence for Language-Model Agent Assurance: Fragments, Methods, and the Residual

author.name: Xiaowei Huang

entry.summary: Provides a unifying formal account of LLM agent assurance methods (rule checkers, prefix monitors, execution gates, rare-event estimators), expressing requirements in a two-tier logic combining finite-trace temporal logic over recorded events with an inner logic over the agent's argument structure. Introduces an assurance ledger showing how method claims combine and what remains unchecked.

entry.title: AIProver: Agentic Auto-Formalization of Mathematical Research via Certificate-Driven Evolving Harness

author.name: Prithwish Jana, Viet Bach Hoang, Logan Luna, Viresh Pati, Akash Singirikonda, Cy Xie, Lisa Carbone, Wuyang Chen, Walter Moreira, Joe Stubbs, Sriram Vishwanath, Vijay Ganesh

entry.summary: AIProver is an agentic framework for autonomous proof auto-formalization and proof synthesis that jointly post-trains a 119B open-weight language model, addressing gaps such as concepts missing from Lean's Mathlib and compilation success not guaranteeing semantic preservation. It uses a certificate-driven evolving harness to reduce reliance on frontier models and manually engineered scaffolding, also generating scarce aligned NL-FL training data.

entry.title: Principled Top-$k$ Selection for Language Models with Hybrid Gradients

author.name: Xuchen Gong, Junfei Sun, Tian Li

entry.summary: Proposes a principled objective for training top-k selection modules used in RAG document selection and MoE expert routing, whose gradient naturally combines a supervised-gradient component and a policy-gradient component. This addresses weak gradient signals and poor exploration-exploitation tradeoffs in heuristic approaches. The hybrid gradient idea is broadly applicable to discrete selection in LLM systems.

entry.title: Modeling Deletion Requests in Machine Unlearning

author.name: Christian Cianfarani, Aloni Cohen

entry.summary: Models how users exercising the right to erasure might behave adaptively (updating requests) and collectively (coordinating groups), showing theoretical gaps in unlearning effects between such behaviors and demonstrating that data-valuation-informed deletion requests can significantly alter model behavior. This reframes unlearning as strategic interaction rather than passive removal. Important for privacy policy and unlearning evaluation design.

entry.title: Measuring and Reducing Cross-Vendor Mismatch in Language Models

author.name: Erland Hilman Fuadi, Chong Tian, Xiaosong Ma, Qirong Ho

entry.summary: The paper quantifies cross-vendor GPU numerical mismatch for identical LLM weights and inputs across dense and MoE models using five metric families, tracing one cause to accumulation order in vendor matrix instructions. Notably, keeping only MLPs in BF16 retains 94% of the logit-error reduction from full FP32 upcasting at 1.3x runtime instead of 3x.

entry.title: How (and How Not) to Use Data Augmentation in VLA Post-Training

author.name: Bram Grooten, Joaquin Vanschoren

entry.summary: This systematic study of image augmentation during RL post-training of vision-language-action models finds that augmenting only the critic while keeping actor inputs clean during rollouts and updates is crucial. For pi0.5 and GR00T N1.5, this raises out-of-distribution success on LIBERO-Plus by 7.8 and 10.0 points respectively. The finding offers a simple, widely applicable recipe for robust VLA fine-tuning.

entry.title: RubricArmor: Adversarial Evolution Improves LLM-Based Rubric Generation

author.name: Haocheng Yang, Yuchao Zhang, Licheng Pan, Jiajun Fan, Maolin Wang, Kangning Zhang, Shuai Shao, Shijian Wang, Yuan Lu, Chunyuan Zheng, Hao Wang

entry.summary: RubricArmor addresses reward hacking in rubric-based reinforcement learning for LLM alignment, where LLM-generated rubrics with omitted or underspecified criteria allow policies to earn high rewards with low-quality responses. The method uses adversarial evolution to proactively harden rubrics against exploitation rather than merely improving granularity and coverage. This is a targeted contribution to making rubric-based RLVR pipelines more robust for alignment at scale.

entry.title: Byte Language Models: Scaling, Emergent Abstractions, and Information Allocation

author.name: Jie Wang, Shiwei Luo, Qi Zhang, Yuanbin Wu

entry.summary: This study shows that byte-level Transformers, using token-superposition training and hash embeddings, can consistently outperform subword Transformers as scale increases, and that they spontaneously learn segmentation-like abstractions mimicking external tokenizers. It analyzes how these models allocate information. The work provides evidence that tokenizer-free modeling is viable at scale without specialized architectures.

entry.title: InvestigationWorlds: An Agentic Environment for Legal Investigation

author.name: Albert Yu Sun, Andrew Benard, Sil Hamilton, Anna Teresita A. Marcelo, Yong Jae Kim, Carl-Leander Henneking, Rundong Hu, Yuhong Wang, David Mimno, Bishan Yang, Igor Labutov

entry.summary: InvestigationWorlds builds agentic legal-investigation environments from real US federal court summary judgment motions retrieved via PACER, augmented by attorney-validated generation of role-tagged documents. Each case admits multiple coherent factual readings, only one matching the court-adopted hypothesis, enabling evaluation on 100 real cases.

entry.title: SHarP: Saliency-based Pruning of Agent Harnesses

author.name: Xinyi Gao, Qiucheng Wu, Kaizhi Qian, Handong Zhao, Shiyu Chang, Yang Zhang

entry.summary: SHarP applies neural-network pruning intuition to agent harnesses, using saliency to identify redundant instructions, tools, and workflow modules that add token cost without performance benefit. It offers a principled way to balance task performance against the token overhead that accumulates as harnesses are iteratively patched. This is practically relevant given the rising cost and complexity of production agent systems.

entry.title: ALoDLM: Adaptively Looped Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Liancheng Fang, Zhuowei Li, Youngeun Kim, Tianchen Zhao, Rajat Koner, Jiaye Wu, Linghan Xu, Xuanbai Chen, Xiang Xu, Zheng Zhang, Jakub Zablocki, Nishant Sankaran, Yifan Xing

entry.summary: This paper introduces ALoDLM, a diffusion language model architecture that addresses the quality gap with autoregressive models by replacing uniform computation across unknown tokens with token-adaptive latent recurrence. At each denoising step, the model iteratively refines latent representations and allocates more computation to harder-to-predict tokens while using less for easy ones. This adaptive compute allocation could make parallel-token diffusion generation competitive with autoregressive generation in both speed and quality.

entry.title: AgentPersonaBench: Benchmarking Persona-Driven User Simulation

author.name: Jintao Huang, Yifan Wang, Hongyu Shen, Yi Daniel Lu, Shirley Huang, Minsik Oh, Yewen Wang, Muhammad Ahmed Mohsin, Zhen Xu, Yilan Fan, Zichen Yuan, Ahsan Bilal, Zibu Wei, Sankalp Jajee, Henry Gagnier, Saksham Kapoor, Jicheng Wang, Qianfeng Wen, Yixuan He, Steven Dillmann, Jiashu He, Yucheng Lu, Linqiang Guo, Danyang Zhang, Shi Bo, Raunak Mondal, Haixiang Tang, Weihang Xiao, Allen Nie, Jing Tang, Yueying Li, Yifan Simon Liu, Jianheng Hou, Dianzhuo Wang, Qianyu Zhu, Zhixu Silvia Tao, Zhejian Peng, Zihan Wang, Ishan Gupta, Jinxuan Fan, Wanting Jiang, Shushu Liang, Chenxi Qiu, Yijun Wang, Xiaomin Li, Yuexing Hao

entry.summary: Introduces a benchmark that evaluates whether persona conditioning genuinely steers agent behavior, rather than just conversational style or self-reported traits. It tests latent trait adherence one trait at a time across four increasingly realistic interaction surfaces (survey, chat, web, app) and verifies ground truth strictly from observable actions.

entry.title: VCLMU: Mechanism-Centric Virtual Cell World Modeling for Perturbation Response

author.name: Yuwei Miao, Azim Dehghani Amirabad, Scott Oloff, Junzhou Huang, Tianyu Cui, Rui Liao

entry.summary: VCLMU is a mechanism-centric virtual cell world model that represents cellular state as Latent Mechanism Units (LMUs) and treats genetic perturbations as actions on these latent states, aiming to predict cellular responses to interventions. Each LMU couples a reusable identity grounded in multimodal biological evidence with an observation-specific state, inducing mechanism-specific responses.

entry.title: Autonomous Structuring of Radiology Reports Across Modalities at Archive Scale Using an Open-Weight Large Language Model

author.name: Friedrich Puttkammer, Fabian Drexel, Marlene Fritzsche, Era Stambollxhiu, Miriam Kumpf, Lena Schmitzer, Lea Schumann, Lina Xu, Johannes Moll, Jannik L\"ubberstedt, Zeineb Ben Chaaben, Anirudh Narayanan, Hartmut H\"antze, Renato Cuocolo, Antonios Billis, Alexander L\"oser, Jawed Nawabi, Marcus R. Makowski, Cosmin I. Bercea, Shahrooz Faghihroohi, Lisa C. Adams, Keno K. Bressem

entry.summary: A retrospective study develops an open-weight LLM pipeline using gpt-oss-120B on a single local GPU to convert entire archives of free-text radiology reports into structured reports without human oversight, with 150 hierarchical templates selected via three constrained-decoding steps. It was tested on reports from 2010-2025 at a second center, with template selection scored against expert labels and structuring quality verified field-by-field by five residents.

entry.title: Strong Helps Weak: Directional Cross-Modal Alignment Transfer in Multi-modal LLMs

author.name: Hoigi Seo, Byung Hyun Lee, Minjun Kim, Dohyun Mah, Jongho Lee, Se Young Chun

entry.summary: This paper characterizes an asymmetric phenomenon in multi-modal LLM model merging: merging a well-aligned, data-rich source-modality model (e.g., vision) into a data-scarce target-modality model (e.g., audio or video) transfers alignment capability, sidestepping expensive modality-specific data collection. This offers a practical recipe for improving MLLMs on modalities where training data or model variants are scarce.

entry.title: Are We Measuring Scientific Intelligence? Rethinking the Evaluation of AI Scientists

author.name: Kate Zhang, Yuante Li

entry.summary: This evaluation-methodology paper shows that AI-scientist benchmarks assume evidence grounding, i.e., that correct answers were derived from supplied data, an assumption that often fails since agents can answer from prior knowledge or elimination. The authors test this by building versions of data files with evidence intact, withdrawn, or reversed, verified with pre-registered reference statistics.

entry.title: From Scientific Observations to Mechanisms: Benchmarking Hypothesis Generation by AI Scientists

author.name: Xiaxun Xie, Qingqing Long, Meng Xiao, Wei Ju, Yuanchun Zhou, Xuezhi Wang, Hengshu Zhu

entry.summary: MechHypoBench is the first benchmark evaluating whether AI agents can generate mechanistic hypotheses from empirical data, combining paper-derived mechanisms from 14 scientific fields with real-world datasets totaling about 18 million records. The benchmark retains observational complexity while providing known underlying mechanisms for ground-truth evaluation.

entry.title: MESH-Harness: Self-Improving Agent Harnesses via Bandit-Guided Compositional Evolution

author.name: Zhiwei Shang, Yu Huo, Mingrong Gong, An Yan, Zikun Qu, Junhao Dong, Bryan Kian Hsiang Low, Chenglin Wu, Zhongxiang Dai

entry.summary: This paper introduces MESH-Harness, a method for automatically improving the agent harness — the code that organizes context, maintains state, and coordinates tool calls around a language model — without changing model weights. It decomposes harnesses into functional modules with role-specific interfaces, uses full-covariance LinUCB bandit scoring and mixed-start coordinate ascent to select promising module combinations under a limited evaluation budget, and applies validation traces to guide local code edits. This matters because harness quality increasingly determines agent performance, and the work offers a sample-efficient, principled approach to harness search rather than manual engineering.

entry.title: Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning with Stable Temporal Abstraction for Language Model Agents

author.name: Shayan Mohajer Hamidi, Yize Cheng, Yuanda Xu, Zhengze Zhou, Alborz Geramifard

entry.summary: This paper identifies temporal abstraction instability in hierarchical language agents, where the learned boundary policy swaps or retains subgoals inappropriately across turns. The authors propose STAC, a constrained optimization method that stabilizes subgoal persistence, improving long-horizon control for LLM agents.

entry.title: DiMOS: Doob-Guided Inference-Time Multi-Objective Search for Scientific Design

author.name: Ziqing Wang, Qijie Zhu, Weimin Wu, Zeqi Ye, Minshuo Chen, Han Liu, Kaize Ding

entry.summary: DiMOS is a training-free framework for multi-objective scientific design that guides frozen pretrained masked diffusion models at inference time, avoiding costly fine-tuning. It tackles pass-or-fail constraints and black-box rewards that offer no gradients by using joint rewards and search to navigate small feasible regions within a limited inference budget.

entry.title: ImproveAnyTask: An Autonomous Post-Training Harness for Iterative Model Self-Improvement

author.name: Xingbo Yao, Xiaoman Wang, Zhengwu Lei, Tinghui Luo, YiLin Zhang, Yuefeng Wu, Yijie Xu, Tianfu Wang, Qingyuan Zhan, Ye Guo, Daoxin Zhang, Zhe Xu, Jian Liu, Hui Xiong

entry.summary: ImproveAnyTask is an autonomous post-training harness that iteratively improves LLM task performance under a limited compute budget by organizing adaptation into error attribution, update-direction selection, and executable model updates. It combines metric-level and case-level analysis to identify focal problems and select research-backed training strategies.

entry.title: AgentPrivArena: Evaluating and Auditing Real-world AI Agent Privacy

author.name: Shouju Wang, Haopeng Zhang

entry.summary: AgentPrivArena is a framework for evaluating privacy risks in realistic LLM agent workflows, integrating authentic MCP tools and self-hosted services in a reproducible environment, with trajectory-level privacy metrics that quantify unnecessary information access beyond what final results require. It moves beyond simulated trajectories and outcome-only metrics of existing benchmarks.

entry.title: Efficient Analog-Initialized Latent Transport for Spatially Coherent Probabilistic Downscaling from Global to Kilometer Scales

author.name: Oph\'elia Miralles

entry.summary: This paper introduces a probabilistic downscaling method that generates kilometer-scale atmospheric structure from coarse deterministic forecasts. It combines historical analog residuals, a frozen graph neural network for the deterministic state, and a conditional flow-matching model operating in a large latent space to reconstruct 81 atmospheric channels, including precipitation, at 2.5 km resolution. The approach addresses a key gap in operational weather prediction by making high-resolution ensembles computationally efficient and spatially coherent.

entry.title: Retrieval-Centric Deep Learning in Growing Nonparametric Neural Networks

author.name: Maximilian Schlegel, Rajai Nasser, Seijin Kobayashi, Yanick Schimpf, Oliver Sieberling, Robert Obryk, Kazuki Irie, Jo\~ao Sacramento, Johannes von Oswald

entry.summary: Building on the duality between linear attention and gradient descent, this paper investigates a general-purpose layer that stores key-value representations for every training data point and retrieves them via attention at inference, yielding growing nonparametric networks. The authors show that naively applying linear-attention learning rules to more powerful attention functions fails, and develop approaches that make this retrieval-centric design work.

entry.title: GOTT: Object-centric Dexterous Manipulation with a Reusable Cross-Embodiment Primitive

author.name: Yulin Liu, Lai Wei, Yen-Jen Wang, Akash Sharma, Pieter Abbeel, Henrik I. Christensen, Haozhi Qi

entry.summary: GOTT is a reach-acquire-move framework for multi-fingered dexterous manipulation built around a single cross-embodiment contact-acquisition primitive. It translates manipulation intent from foundation models and human data into reliable multi-fingered robot behavior by combining a closed-loop contact primitive with a pose-conditioned object-motion controller. This addresses a key gap in dexterous robotics: the lack of reusable low-level primitives that work across tasks and robot hand designs.

entry.title: Benchmarking Psychological Dynamics in Generative Agents

author.name: Sumer S. Vaid, Ashley V. Whillans

entry.summary: This work introduces a psychometric benchmark for LLM-based computational replicas of human subjects, scoring personas that carry a fixed identity through evolving event sequences. It evaluates psychological realism along dimensions like internal validity, checking whether generated trajectories reproduce distributions, variance partitioning, and temporal dependence from published human meta-analytic norms.

entry.title: A Bird's-Eye View of Iterative Reward Design

author.name: Logan Mondal Bhamidipaty, Lauren Robson, Linda Petrini, Shengrui Lyu, Kamal Ndousse

entry.summary: BIRD is a benchmark expressing existing LLM-based iterative reward design methods in a unified configuration and evaluation space across MuJoCo, Meta-World, and Assistax. It enables direct comparison of algorithms, ablation of design choices, and prototyping under matched feedback conditions and policy-training budgets.

entry.title: COSMOS: Soft Mechanism Mixtures with Verifiable Routing for Long-Horizon PDE Forecasting

author.name: Anupam Rawat, Manikandan Padmanaban, Jagabondhu Hazra

entry.summary: Proposes COSMOS, a soft mixture-of-experts neural operator where four physics-process specialists (transport, diffusion, wave, reaction) remain active and are continuously mixed by a learned gate, replacing sparse top-K routing. Targets long-horizon PDE forecasting and includes verifiable routing for interpretability.

entry.title: More Value per Key: Asymmetric Sparse Attention for Faster LLM Decoding

author.name: Noam Elata, Itay Lamprecht, Mikey Shechter, Daniel Ohayon, Itay Hubara, Daniel Soudry

entry.summary: The paper observes that with sparse attention, the probability-value multiplication becomes negligible and decoding bottlenecks shift to the query-key step, motivating asymmetric key/value head counts. It proposes SAGA (Sparse Asymmetric Group-Query Attention), decoupling key and value heads, paired with an approximate top-N sparse attention method to accelerate LLM decoding while preserving capacity.

entry.title: DiVeR: Decision-Critical Verifier Learning for VLA Test-Time Scaling

author.name: Seongheon Park, Heecheol Kim, Shulin Tian, Lilika Makabe, Namiko Saito, Katsushi Ikeuchi, Sharon Li, Yasuyuki Matsushita

entry.summary: DiVeR improves verifier-guided test-time scaling for vision-language-action robot policies by training verifiers on decision-critical states, the sparse set of states where candidate actions meaningfully diverge, rather than treating all trajectory states equally. At inference, multiple action candidates are sampled and the verifier selects the one most likely to succeed.

entry.title: StateWise: Diagnosing and Repairing Persistent Operational State Before Agent Actions

author.name: Yongyuan Peng, Zhou Feng, Tongying Wu, Jiahao Chen, Yuan Su, Chunyi Zhou, Tianyu Du, Shouling Ji

entry.summary: StateWise addresses a failure mode of LLM agents where persistent stored records become invalid after environmental changes but are still reused as premises for later actions. The framework audits coding-agent trajectories to find such failure chains and repairs persistent state before action execution using record-level counterfactual replanning. This complements existing action review and provenance tracking mechanisms.

entry.title: FLEX-WAM: Flexible Block-Causal World-Action Models for Long-Horizon Imagination and Planning

author.name: R. Khorrambakht, Joseph Amigo, F\'elix Lebel, Leon Seetoo, Jean Ponce, Zhenzhen Li, Ludovic Righetti

entry.summary: FLEX-WAM is a flexible, efficient block-causal world-action model supporting variable-length contexts, non-causal prediction horizons, and infinite autoregressive generation for unified simulation and policy inference. Its KV-cacheable architecture combines axial attention and blockwise diffusion forcing for efficient streaming long-horizon rollouts.

entry.title: SEA-LM: Egocentric Spatial Audio Understanding for Wearable Microphone Arrays

author.name: Sonal Kumar, Sinan Hersek, Artem Dementyev, Mengzhen Pan, Ishan Chatterjee, Anurag Kumar, Ramani Duraiswami, Dinesh Manocha, Andrea Colaco

entry.summary: Introduces SEA-LM, a spatial audio understanding model for smart-glasses microphone arrays, featuring FOACODER, a layout-flexible encoder trained on sound localization and egocentric voice activity detection over First Order Ambisonics. It augments a multimodal LLM with spatial audio cues that mono-channel models discard, enabling sound localization and better separation of overlapping sources. This matters for embodied AI on wearables, where spatial hearing is a key missing modality.

entry.title: HLA-WM: Hybrid Linear Attention for Long-Horizon Video World Models

author.name: Zhuokun Chen, Feng Chen, Xi Lin, Xiyu Wu, Jiahao He, Jianfei Cai, Bohan Zhuang

entry.summary: This paper addresses long-range memory loss in video world models that use recurrent linear attention, specifically identifying severe forgetting in Gated DeltaNet over extended rollouts. The authors propose HLA-WM, a training-free hybrid framework that combines geometry-guided retrieval of distant scene information with fine-grained linear-state computation, exploiting the affine structure of GDN. This matters because persistent memory is a key bottleneck for deploying video world models in simulation, robotics, and long-form content generation.

entry.title: HuatuoGPT-3: RL-Only Domain Adaptation from Base Models

author.name: Junying Chen, Xinyuan Xie, Ziniu Li, Wenyuan Gu, Jianquan Li, Xiang Wan, Guangjun Yu, Ruoyu Sun, Haizhou Li, Benyou Wang

entry.summary: HuatuoGPT-3 adapts a general-purpose LLM into a medical expert using reinforcement learning only, skipping the standard SFT stage that can reduce exploration diversity. The authors identify two failure modes of mixed-policy RL, Gradient Starvation and Teacher-Distribution Anchoring, and propose One-stage Policy Optimization (OnePO) to address them. The work demonstrates that RL-only domain adaptation is viable from base models.

entry.title: AgentSpy: Making AI Agent Behavior Observable

author.name: Christoph B\"uhler, Matteo Biagiola, Luca Di Grazia, Guido Salvaneschi

entry.summary: AgentSpy observes LLM agents from outside the agent by running them in an isolated environment and recording system calls and network traffic of the agent and all subprocesses, based on a declarative specification. This catches behavior that trajectory logs may omit and supports conformance analyses of what agents actually do. It directly addresses the observability gap for agents executing with user privileges.

entry.title: On the Geometry of Multimodal Saturation: Riemannian VICReg

author.name: Nessim Ben Abbes, Duc Han Le, Sabri Mtibaa, Van-Tam Nguyen

entry.summary: The paper identifies multimodal saturation, a failure where adding a third modality under VICReg and SimSiam harms performance across nine image-text-tabular datasets, occurring in roughly half of paired runs. It attributes this to alignment geometry and proposes Riemannian VICReg, which aligns views via squared geodesic distance on learnable negative-curvature factors and recovers VICReg as curvature vanishes. This substantially increases the probability that a third modality helps.

entry.title: Quantifying the Stability of Multi-Step Reasoning via Error Amplification

author.name: Dongyue Li, Ziniu Zhang, Minxuan Duan, Hongyang R. Zhang

entry.summary: This theoretical work derives an inference error bound for multi-step reasoning governed by the product of spectral norms of Jacobians across generation steps, an error amplification factor that can grow exponentially. It identifies key factors determining whether chain-of-thought and algorithmic reasoning remain stable in autoregressive generation.

entry.title: Sharpen Without Search: On-Policy Distillation of Sequence-Level Power Distribution

author.name: Erfan Baghaei Potraghloo, Seyedarmin Azizi, Arya Fayyazi, Saeid Shokoufa, Mehdi Kamal, Souvik Kundu, Massoud Pedram

entry.summary: The paper shows that a model can be trained to sample as if from its own power-sharpened distribution in a single generation, avoiding costly candidate scoring at inference. On-policy power distillation runs a sequential Monte Carlo sampler where the student generates candidates and a frozen teacher's power distribution weights them. This connects test-time compute scaling (best-of-n / sharpening) with distillation, improving reasoning without parameter changes at deployment.

entry.title: Bayes-Sufficient Compression Is Not Enough: How Does Communication Help Multi-Agent Systems?

author.name: Yi Xie, Zhanke Zhou, Yi Fan, Yong Ge, Bo Han, Bo Liu

entry.summary: Provides a theoretical framework, receiver-relative bounded coordination, for when short messages from a sender LLM improve an executor's decisions versus passing raw context, expressing utility as receiver gain minus protocol tax. It shows even Bayes-sufficient compression can fail for bounded executors and decomposes error sources into externalization, absorption, and action closure.

entry.title: Probabilistic Algorithms for Ising Machines from Optimization to Generative AI

author.name: Corentin Delacour, Xiuqi Zhang, Abdelrahman S. Abdelrahman, Saleh Bunaiyan, Kyle Lee, Shuvro Chowdhury, Kerem Y. Camsari

entry.summary: A review surveying probabilistic algorithms designed for portability across Ising machine hardware platforms, covering simulated annealing, parallel tempering, constraint-encoding extensions, and methods connecting optimization to sampling and generative AI applications. It advocates a top-down, provably-guaranteed perspective on algorithm-hardware co-design.

entry.title: Pareto-Dominant Clarification: Post-Training Coding LLMs via PPO-Lagrangian Budget Constraints

author.name: Abhinav Rajput, Acey Vogelstein

entry.summary: Formulates the decision of when coding agents should ask clarifying questions versus attempting a solution as a Constrained Markov Decision Process, and post-trains Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct with PPO-Lagrangian under enforceable clarification budgets. This avoids the costly per-budget coefficient tuning of penalty-based approaches. The work addresses a practical accuracy-versus-efficiency tradeoff for deployed coding agents.

entry.title: Optimizer Geometry Sets the Pace: Spectral Learning Dynamics in Matrix Factorization

author.name: Mahalakshmi Sabanayagam, Simon Lucey

entry.summary: Studies how optimizer geometry (normalization, curvature correction) and depth jointly govern spectral bias in deep matrix factorization, deriving birth, saturation, and decay laws for singular mode dynamics under balance and alignment assumptions. This clarifies when matrix- and curvature-based optimizers preserve or destroy implicit low-rank regularization. Timely given the rise of Muon and Shampoo-style optimizers.

entry.title: Checkable NTK Positivity and Finite-Width Gradient Descent for Scalar- and Vector-Valued PINNs with Strong-Form, Weak-Form, and Nonlocal Linear Constraints

author.name: Zifan Lyu

entry.summary: This paper develops checkable positive-definiteness criteria for the limiting neural tangent kernel (NTK) of physics-informed neural networks, covering strong-form differential constraints, weak-form residuals, and nonlocal observations in any dimension. It further provides high-probability finite-width gradient-descent convergence guarantees for scalar- and vector-valued PINNs. This closes a theoretical gap since NTK positive definiteness is the key assumption behind most PINN convergence results but is rarely verified.

entry.title: FlexCast: Adaptive Weather Forecasting from Arbitrary Field Sets

author.name: Yuang Zhang, Chen Hui, Weisi Lin, Haiqi Zhu, Xiulai Wang, Sun-Yuan Kung, Feng Jiang

entry.summary: FlexCast is a field-adaptive weather forecasting model that uses a single parameter set to forecast over arbitrary subsets of a 69-field ERA5 registry, via a metadata-conditioned adapter encoding variable identity, pressure level, and field type. This removes the fixed-channel constraint of most deep learning weather models and improves transferability across atmospheric configurations.

entry.title: When Does Longer Reasoning Help? Predicting Mathematical Reasoning Through Discovery and Execution

author.name: Adib Hasan, Lay Jain, Thanic Nur Samin

entry.summary: This arXiv paper introduces a Discovery-Execution (DE) framework that uses short-budget test-time compute runs to predict how mathematical reasoning performance scales when more compute is allocated. By modeling aggregate held-out scaling curves as a convolution of strategy discovery and conditional execution, the authors evaluate four models on 35 fresh Olympiad problems and non-geometry IMO-ProofBench Advanced problems, finding that near-saturated execution predicts geometric scaling behavior as observed for GPT models and characterizing Claude Opus behavior as well. This matters because it offers a cheap predictive tool for deciding whether investing additional test-time compute in a model will pay off on hard reasoning tasks.

entry.title: Disentangling Task Difficulty from Run-Level Failure in Agent Failure Prediction

author.name: Mohsen EsfandyariDoulabi, Lawrence Arkoh, Biruk Tadesse, Vaishvi Patel, Mehul Sharma, Marcelo d'Amorim, Wesley Assun\c{c}\~ao

entry.summary: Investigates whether reported strong performance of LLM-agent failure predictors reflects genuine run-level failure detection or simply memorization of task difficulty from pooled training data. The work proposes evaluation protocols separating these two signals, with implications for when predictors can support mid-trajectory intervention versus compute allocation.

entry.title: Learning Pareto Stationary Fronts via Single-Pass Backpropagation

author.name: Elina Rojin Celik, Marcos Medeiros Raimundo, Isabel Valera

entry.summary: MOSEL is a framework for a posteriori multi-objective optimization in deep networks that recovers a full front of Pareto stationary solutions at the cost of standard single-objective training. It reformulates the problem as a bilevel Stackelberg game exploiting network modularity to decouple representation learning from preference alignment. This enables scalable Pareto front learning in a single forward-backward pass.

entry.title: Learning What to Imitate: Entropy-Aware Distribution Mixing

author.name: Juan Garcia Giraldo, Matteo Santelmo, Eduard Durech, Imanol Schlag, Valentina Pyatkin, Antoine Bosselut

entry.summary: The paper identifies confident conflicts in knowledge distillation from teacher reasoning traces, where a student in a low-entropy state is forced to imitate low-probability continuations, degrading generalization and causing forgetting. The proposed Entropy-Aware Mixing dynamically interpolates student and teacher distributions per token, gated by the student's predictive entropy. This improves small-model post-training on teacher traces.

entry.title: OVAL: Output-Aware Local Page Bases for KV Cache Retrieval

author.name: Ashkan Shahbazi, Chayne Thrash, Soheil Kolouri

entry.summary: OVAL introduces output-aware page encoding for KV cache retrieval in long-context LLM inference, derived from the joint structure of keys and values so that retrieval objectives directly account for how approximation errors affect the value-weighted attention output. The method is training-free and requires no additional value-dependent statistics at inference time.

entry.title: Localize-and-Detect: Auditing Task-Level Poisoning in Instruction-Tuned Models

author.name: Luze Sun, Cristina Nita-Rotaru, Alina Oprea

entry.summary: The paper introduces a two-stage black-box auditing method for detecting task-level poisoning of instruction-tuned language models, where attackers bias outputs on a target task without explicit triggers. Using only base and fine-tuned model outputs, the method localizes the poisoned task and detects biased content despite benign fine-tuning also changing behavior. This addresses a real and under-studied security threat in the fine-tuning supply chain.

entry.title: Latent Safety Filters: When a Lossy Encoder Admits a Transferable Certificate

author.name: Johannes Mootz, Zahra Nili Ahmadabadi, Reza Akhavian

entry.summary: Studies when safety filters certified on learned low-dimensional latent representations can be trusted to transfer to the physical system, showing that transferability is governed by detectability of discarded safety-relevant dynamics. The authors construct a counterexample system where the latent model is exact and always reports safe while the physical state becomes arbitrarily unsafe. This exposes fundamental limits of latent-space safety certification.

entry.title: RESOLVE: Language-Agnostic Validation of GPU Kernels Through Testing, Reduction, and Proof

author.name: Ashkan Vedadi Gargary, Guido Mart\'inez, Sebastian Burckhardt, Gabriel Ebner, Abhinav Jangda, Madan Musuvathi, Tyler Sorensen

entry.summary: RESOLVE is a pipeline for validating AI-generated GPU kernels that combines nondeterminism testing via timing-perturbing binary instrumentation to expose races, reduction to manageable counterexamples, and formal proof, going beyond random-input output matching with numeric tolerances. This addresses a critical gap as AI systems increasingly write production GPU code where races and numeric tolerance can hide bugs. It is notable systems and verification work from a strong team (including Microsoft Research-affiliated authors).

entry.title: Fitting Vision Adapters at Frontier Scales

author.name: Jaehoon Lee, Harry Partridge, Mudith Jayasekara, Charles O'Neill, Max Kirkby, Michael Psenka

entry.summary: This paper trains a 50M-parameter projector to add vision capabilities to large language models without native vision, connecting the vision encoder of Kimi K2.6 to GLM 5.2 and 5.3 while keeping the language weights frozen. It provides a reproducible recipe for training such adapters at frontier scale and studies which vision capabilities scale with the language model side. This informs the debate on how multimodality emerges from pure language models.

entry.title: MIRT: Transformers for Truthful Generative Auctions with Whole-feed Permutation Externalities

author.name: Ali Elahi, Ermis Soumalias, Jason Cheuk Nam Liang, Daniel Yao, Michael J. Curry

entry.summary: MIRT is a transformer-based mechanism class for jointly ordering ads and organic content in a feed, accounting for cross-item externalities on click-through rates. It generates candidate feeds and selects the welfare-maximizing one with exact strategyproofness guarantees, addressing shortcomings of prior learning-based feed mechanisms that fix organic ordering or lack incentive guarantees.

entry.title: Finding Gaussian Structure in Bosonic States

author.name: Alvan Arulandu, Sitan Chen, Ziyun Chen, Jerry Li, Eric Ma

entry.summary: The paper gives efficient agnostic tomography protocols for pure bosonic Gaussian states: given copies of an arbitrary n-mode bosonic state, output the closest pure Gaussian state up to the optimum infidelity plus epsilon. Protocols with strongly polynomial runtime in the high-fidelity regime and (n+1)^poly(1/epsilon) complexity for arbitrary optimum are provided.

entry.title: Do Language Models Need a Trainable Input Embedding Table? Fixed Minimal Token Codes at 1.7B-Class Scale

author.name: A. Bochkov

entry.summary: This paper tests whether trainable input embeddings are necessary by training decoder-only LMs from scratch with either a learned table, canonical 16-bit token-ID codes, or a fixed invertible GF(2) recoding, at roughly 100B training tokens and 1.7B-class scale. Fixed token codes reportedly achieve substantial language-modeling capability without any trainable input projection. If replicated broadly, this challenges a default assumption about LM architecture and could reduce parameters.

entry.title: Causal Improvement Graph for Agentic Harness Optimization

author.name: Junjie Zhang, Shunyu Liu, Haoyu Wang, Ting-En Lin, Yongbin Li, Dacheng Tao

entry.summary: The authors introduce the Causal Improvement Graph (CIG), a graph-structured state representation for automatically optimizing agent harnesses, the runtimes that construct task context and control execution flow for LLM agents. Unlike proposer-centric meta-harness methods that burden an LLM proposer with tracking a growing experiment history, CIG explicitly maintains the improvement state in a governed graph. This addresses a real scalability weakness in automated agent system design and is relevant to the fast-growing agentic infrastructure area.

entry.title: More Than Words: Compositional Tokenization for Efficient Language Models

author.name: Yuval Reif, Guy Kaplan, Roy Schwartz

entry.summary: CoBPE introduces a compositional tokenization approach that represents phrases as a lexical base token plus reusable surface modifiers composed in embedding space and predicted jointly at output, shortening sequences by roughly 30% versus standard tokenization. Controlled pretraining from scratch at 780M and 1.3B scales demonstrates efficiency gains, since fewer predicted positions reduce inference cost. This challenges the assumption that tokenization must be a flat sequence of atomic predictions.

entry.title: HLA: Expressive Hybrid Linear Attention via Chunk-Wise Dynamic Mixing

author.name: Zhuokun Chen, Xi Lin, Xiyu Wu, Jiahao He, Jianfei Cai, Bohan Zhuang

entry.summary: HLA adds query-dependent, content-based routing between recurrent chunk states in Gated DeltaNet-style linear attention, representing each chunk as an exact affine state transition and computing routing gates from pooled representatives. This improves selective access to sparse, distant information that pure linear attention compresses away. It targets the core weakness of linear attention for long-context decoding.

entry.title: Wikidata Search Traces: A Dataset for Training Knowledge Graph Search Agents

author.name: Mohamed Chenene, Carlos Rosas-Hinostroza, Pierre-Carl Langlais, Anastasia Stasenko

entry.summary: This paper introduces a dataset of exploration traces for training language-model agents that answer complex questions by searching the Wikidata knowledge graph rather than relying on parametric memory. It identifies two bottlenecks - lack of solver-exploration training data and unwieldy graph-result interfaces - and tests whether question structure can control search difficulty.

entry.title: Are We Measuring Anticipation? Auditing Privileged Information in Procedural Video Evaluation

author.name: Mahsa Mohammadi, Sareh Rowlands

entry.summary: The authors audit evaluation protocols rather than models, showing that procedural action anticipation benchmarks can pass standard causality and leakage checks while still leaking privileged intermediate information. On the Breakfast dataset, ground-truth-history regimes inflate scores by roughly 32 points over recognizer-history regimes, revealing a mismatch between claimed and measured capabilities.

entry.title: Detecting Defects that Matter: An Application-Driven Benchmark for Anomaly Detection in Manufacturing and Retail Logistics (VAND 4.0 Challenge)

author.name: Lars Heckler-Kram, Dorian Henning, Ashwin Vaidya, Jan-Hendrik Neudeck, Ulla Scheler, Anton Milan, Samet Akcay, Paula Ramos, Sebastian H\"ofer

entry.summary: As part of the VAND 4.0 Challenge, this paper introduces a hidden-test, application-driven anomaly detection benchmark spanning industrial manufacturing (MVTec AD 2) and retail logistics. Results show unsupervised anomaly segmentation remains far from solved, with the best method reaching only about 57% pixel-level SegF1 and zero-shot approaches trailing by roughly 15 points.

entry.title: RSure-Agent: Reliable Use of Tool Observations for Remote Sensing Agents

author.name: Fuyuan Liu, Nayu Liu, Wenhao Yu, Peijin Wang, Yingchao Feng, Fanglong Yao, Liang Wan, Wei Feng

entry.summary: This work studies reliability of tool observations in remote sensing agents, showing across 1,229 trajectories on three benchmarks that at least 22.7% of observation-dependent tasks contain incorrect observations despite successful tool execution, causing error propagation and task failure. The authors propose RSure-Agent to improve how agents evaluate and use tool outputs. It highlights an underexamined failure mode for tool-using LLM agents in Earth observation.

entry.title: Representation--Behavior Alignment for Explainable Weakly-Supervised Video Anomaly Detection

author.name: Chao Huang, Pengfei Wei, Kaige Li, Chengliang Liu, Wei Wang, Wenqi Ren, Xiaochun Cao

entry.summary: This paper identifies representation-behavior misalignment in MLLM-based video anomaly detection, decomposing it into a capacity component (discriminative information never aggregated at the readout position) and a directional component (angular mismatch between the optimal and native normal-abnormal axis). Across benchmarks and backbones the directional component dominates, with residual-stream tracing showing native-axis separability rising sharply in later layers. The analysis yields more explainable, better-aligned anomaly detection.

entry.title: F$^2$ SLAM: Turning Feed-Forward Geometry into Persistent Factors for SLAM

author.name: Zhisong Xu, Fan Zhu, Jiawei Qian, Ziyu Chen, Zhenjun Zhao, Javier Civera

entry.summary: F2SLAM integrates feed-forward 3D geometry models directly into SLAM by converting their predictions into optimization-native target-weighted measurements on a persistent dense factor graph, rather than fusing them post hoc. A high-frequency stream handles local tracking while a low-frequency stream contributes multi-view evidence, reducing drift over long sequences. This bridges two important lines of work: feed-forward geometry models and online SLAM.

entry.title: T-JEPA: A Temporal Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture for Learning Better Remote Sensing Representations

author.name: Bowen Peng, Li Liu, Yongxiang Liu, Weijie Li, Jie Zhou, Zhen Liu

entry.summary: Proposes T-JEPA, a temporal joint-embedding predictive architecture for Earth observation that learns time-gap-conditioned latent transitions using sparse, nonuniform satellite sampling as supervision. A shared single-frame encoder plus a temporal predictor reconstructs masked target latents conditioned on actual elapsed time.

entry.title: KineWorld: Action-Induced Transport Fields for Embodied World Modeling

author.name: Ziying Song, Yuchen Liu, Zhuoran Xu, Ziyang Liu, Jian Jin, Jiangtao Su, Haibao Yu, Lei Yang, Yuanpei Chen

entry.summary: KineWorld improves action-conditioned world models by allocating generative supervision according to robot kinematics: Kinematic Transport Lifting builds renderer-derived transport fields from commanded motion, and Transport-Aware World Diffusion calibrates objectives to emphasize spatially sparse but interaction-critical changes.

entry.title: S2PD: Serial-to-Parallel Diffusion for Physically and Logically Consistent Video Generation

author.name: Jeffrey Hu, Daniel Olmeda Reino, Ayush Tewari

entry.summary: S2PD observes that parallel video diffusion models still violate physical and symbolic rules even with unlimited procedural training data, and proposes hybrid scheduling: autoregressive diffusion at high noise levels to coordinate interdependent events, switching to parallel diffusion at low noise for efficiency. It is implemented both as a from-scratch pixel-space diffusion transformer and as a fine-tuned pretrained model.

entry.title: Reachability-Guided Sequential Quadratic Programming-Guarded Model Predictive Path Integral for Safe Nonlinear Predictive Control

author.name: Alexandre Didier, Jason J. Choi, Namhoon Cho, Claire J. Tomlin, Melanie N. Zeilinger

entry.summary: The paper combines sampling-based MPPI control with Hamilton-Jacobi reachability safety certificates and SQP-guarded updates to handle nonlinear, nonconvex environments under hard state and input constraints. The approach addresses MPPI's unsafe weighted-average updates and the practical limitations of offline HJR value computation and warm-start-dependent nonlinear MPC.

entry.title: Dataset-Free Compliant Humanoid Loco-Manipulation with Dynamic Online Posture

author.name: Seungho Yeom, Zhenyu Wu, Jaeyoung Huh, Diego Williams, Yuheng Zhi, Soofiyan Atar, Michael Yip

entry.summary: OCLO is a humanoid loco-manipulation system trained without human motion data, commanded only through two end-effector targets, generating pelvis height and torso orientation online via an analytic reachability prior refined through policy-in-the-loop sampling. It also learns whole-body compliance through a spring-damper displacement of end-effector references based on measured forces.

entry.title: Generalized Preference Optimization: A Unified Approach to Offline Alignment

author.name: Yunhao Tang, Zhaohan Daniel Guo, Zeyu Zheng, Daniele Calandriello, R\'emi Munos, Mark Rowland, Pierre Harvey Richemond, Michal Valko, Bernardo \'Avila Pires, Bilal Piot

entry.summary: The paper proposes GPO, a family of offline preference optimization losses parameterized by a general class of convex functions, unifying DPO, IPO, and SLiC as special cases and naturally introducing new variants. It clarifies how loss design controls offline regularization and how this relates to the KL regularization implicit in RLHF. This became a reference framework for understanding offline alignment methods.

entry.title: DAG-CLIP: A DAG Learning Framework in the Presence of Latent Variables

author.name: Siliang Zhang, Yunxiao Chen, Irini Moustaki

entry.summary: This paper proposes a general statistical framework for learning directed acyclic graphs when some or all nodes are latent constructs defined by measurement models, accommodating non-Gaussian data such as binary and categorical variables. To handle high-dimensional integration in marginal likelihoods, the authors develop a computational approach (DAG-CLIP) that makes latent-variable DAG learning tractable. This extends causal discovery beyond purely observed variables, which is especially relevant for the social and behavioral sciences.

entry.title: Causally Fair Generation with Large Language Models

author.name: Patrik Okanovic, Torsten Hoefler, Drago Plecko

entry.summary: Brings causal inference to LLM generation fairness, attributing demographic disparities to their generating mechanisms rather than raw statistical associations, which purely correlational approaches cannot do. The work handles the complication that prompts may request multiple causally related variables in non-topological order, developing methods to assess and enforce causal fairness in generated outputs.

entry.title: Learning to Clarify Underspecified Intents Under Limited Interaction

author.name: Pranav M R, Manuel Cherep, Pattie Maes, Nikhil Singh

entry.summary: The paper reframes when AI assistants should ask clarifying questions as a value-of-information problem: acquiring the information whose absence causes the greatest avoidable loss in user utility. It instantiates this in image generation with an RL framework using multi-turn simulated users, validated in a preregistered study with 456 sessions across 76 human participants.

entry.title: AgentDiscover: Autonomous Discovery with Minimal Search Scaffolding

author.name: Mahdi Farahbakhsh, Ilan Sela, Fatemeh Doudi, Vishnu Teja Kunde, Krishna Narayanan, Jean-Francois Chamberland, Dileep Kalathil

entry.summary: AgentDiscover promotes the LLM from proposer to planner in scientific discovery, letting a coding agent own the search strategy, plan experiments using its context as working memory, and record findings, in contrast to frameworks with fixed human-designed search algorithms. The work is motivated by the Bitter Lesson argument that hand-designed search structure gets outscaled by general methods.

entry.title: Hallucination Across the Reasoning Lifecycle: Interface Visibility, Causal Evidence, and Release Control in Large Reasoning Models

author.name: Zhe Yu, Mohan Li, Lei Yu, Ka-Ho Chow, Chengwei Qin, Xingyu Wu, Wenpeng Xing, Shuguang Xiong, Meng Han

entry.summary: This survey synthesizes 312 papers and first-party reports on reasoning hallucinations in large reasoning models around what evidence is observable, what study designs establish, and which corrective actions are supported. It introduces the UIPCA taxonomy covering unsupported premises, invalid inferences, dependent reuse, answer-trace consistency, and action-policy failures, and connects diagnosis to verification, repair, selective release, and persistent-state control.

entry.title: The Functional Structure of Post-Compression Recovery in Low-Rank LLMs

author.name: Zishan Shao, Liang Tian, Georgiy Zemlevskiy, Kangning Cui, Lixun Zhang, Yixiao Wang, Ting Jiang, Jinhee Kim, Yixuan Chen, Rui-Feng Wang, Fan Yang, Hai Li, Yiran Chen

entry.summary: This empirical study shows that different low-rank compression methods for LLMs respond heterogeneously to the same post-compression recovery procedure, with method rankings potentially reversing after recovery. The authors formalize this as a reproducible compression-induced functional structure called recovery pressure and develop a standardized characterization method.

entry.title: From Token-Max to Outcome-Max: How You Use AI Determines Its Productivity

author.name: Chen Xu, Mengqiao Liu, Beibei Li, Chenyan Xiong

entry.summary: The authors argue that treating token consumption as productive effort (token-max) incentivizes AI agents to over-compute, and propose outcome-max, which rewards independently verified task completion per unit cost with a principled stopping rule. They validate the idea with a three-level simulation framework covering immediate interaction, long-run behavioral adaptation, and organizational collaboration.

entry.title: Benchmarking Jailbreak Guardrails for Embodied Agents

author.name: Xunguang Wang, Qingyue Wang, Yuguang Zhou, Zongjie Li, Wenxuan Wang, Shuai Wang

entry.summary: This is claimed as the first systematic evaluation of jailbreak guardrails for embodied agents powered by LLMs and VLMs, built as a pluggable framework that keeps the embodied agent fixed and swaps guardrail modules. It addresses the gap where safety benchmarks evaluate embodied models themselves rather than whether guardrails actually intercept dangerous physical actions.

entry.title: FREA: A Multi-Source Expert Benchmark for Reaction Feasibility Verification

author.name: Botao Yu, Bo Zhou, Daniel Adu-Ampratwum, Frazier N. Baker, Ziru Chen, Reza Averly, Ye Liu, Wenhao Gao, Xia Ning, Huan Sun

entry.summary: FREA is a benchmark of 751 chemical reactions labeled by expert chemists under an explicit feasibility criterion, sourced from retrosynthesis models, zero-yield records, LLM edits, and five negative-generation methods. Evaluation reveals no verifier leads across sources, with criterion-only LLMs competitive with dedicated verifiers and forward models over-rejecting feasible edits.

entry.title: How RL Reshapes LLM Reasoning: Transferability, Coverage, and Scaling Laws

author.name: Ziheng Cheng, Yixiao Huang, Hanlin Zhu, Somayeh Sojoudi

entry.summary: This paper systematically revisits whether RL on mathematics expands an LLM's reasoning boundary or merely reweights its existing reasoning space, across Qwen and Gemma model families. It reconciles seemingly conflicting findings, showing both cross-domain gains and forgetting, with Pass@$N$ coverage increasing on some tasks and decreasing on others, and identifies a shift in reasoning strategies. The analysis motivates a two-stage automated pipeline and offers scaling-law insights.

entry.title: Clean: Second-order LLM Training at Linear Memory Cost via Nystr\"om Sketching

author.name: Beheshteh T. Rakhshan, Sahar Rajabi, Maziar Sargordi Shikai Fang, Guillaume Rabusseau, Sirisha Rambhatla

entry.summary: Clean is a memory-efficient second-order optimizer for LLM training that uses randomized Nystrom sketching to approximate SOAP's left and right preconditioners, reducing optimizer memory complexity from quadratic to linear in model dimensions. It reintegrates off-subspace curvature components to retain rich curvature information at minimal cost. This addresses a fundamental trade-off between Adam-style low-memory optimizers and full-curvature methods that converge faster but were previously prohibitively memory-hungry.

entry.title: GS-Codec: A Gaussian-Splatting Bottleneck for Neural Audio Coding

author.name: Ron Aluf, Alon Canfi, Eliya Nachmani

entry.summary: Proposes GS-Codec, a neural speech codec that replaces the conventional quantizer bottleneck with a parametric decomposition: 1D Gaussian splatting adapted from 3D scene reconstruction, fitting encoder segments as weighted sums of Gaussian primitives via an inner optimization loop. Challenges the assumption that codebook or scalar-grid partitioning is necessary for audio codecs.

entry.title: ScopeSAE: Model-Scope Feature Discovery with Interpretable Layer Selection

author.name: Qingwen Zeng, Zehao Fu, Shuyu Meng, Linghan Huang, Jiayi Zhang, Chenglin Wu, Ling Chen, Huaming Chen

entry.summary: ScopeSAE improves sparse autoencoder-based interpretability by selecting the modeling subspace per token via normalized gradient attribution to the most influential token-layer state, rather than training SAEs per fixed layer. It addresses low feature utilization, dictionary redundancy, and weak behavioral grounding of layer-wise SAEs.

entry.title: Distributed Subliminal Learning: Replacing Model Updates with Random-Carrier Outputs

author.name: Dario Fenoglio, Gabriele Dominici, Martin Gjoreski, Marc Langheinrich

entry.summary: The paper introduces Distributed Subliminal Learning, a collaborative learning primitive where locally adapted models are probed with task-unrelated inputs and only the resulting carrier outputs are transmitted; a coordinator distills pooled outputs into a shared model. This replaces weight-space exchange, avoiding communication scaling with model size and interference from reconciling specializations in weight space.

entry.title: Kandinsky 6.0 Video: Foundation Models for Synchronized Video and Audio Generation

author.name: Team Kandinsky, Julia Agafonova, Bulat Akhmatov, Mikhail Aksyutin, Grigorii Alekseenko, Anastasia Aliaskina, Olga Androsova, Vladimir Arkhipkin, Anna Averchenkova, Alexander Belykh, Serafima Bocharova, Sofiya Bogakovskaya, Anton Bukashkin, Mark Bulygin, Kirill Buzygin, Irina Cheremnykh, Kirill Chernyshev, Mikhail Chernyshov, Vladimir Chernyy, David Chikovani, Georgy Daniltsev, Denis Dimitrov, Anna Dmitrienko, Vladimir Dokholyan, Sergey Emelyanov, Dmitry Ermilov, Georgii Fedorov, Polina Gavrilova, Nikolai Gerasimenko, Aleksandr Gordeev, Andrey Inozemtsev, Andrei Ivaniuta, Alexander Ivanov, Mikhail Karaev, Anastasiia Kargapoltseva, Ivan Kirillov, Nikita Kiselev, Valeria Kobenko, Yury Kolabushin, Denis Koposov, Anatoly Korobov, Vladimir Korviakov, Kirill Kozlov, Denis Krzhivokolskiy, Konstantin Kuklev, Alexander Kunitsyn, Sergey Kuzin, Vladislav Lakhtionov, Alexey Letunovskiy, Maxim Litvinov, Alexander Lyulkov, Georgy Makarov, Kirill Malakhov, Egor Malykh, Mikhail Mamaev, Dmitrii Mikhailov, Polina Mikhailova, Ivan Mikheev, Elizaveta Muromtseva, Nikolai Nazarkin, Tatiana Nikulina, Lev Novitskiy, Stanislav Onuchin, Nikita Osterov, Denis Parkhomenko, Anatoliy Parpara, Vladimir Polovnikov, Konstantin Reznikov, Azat Saginbaev, Nikita Samsonov, Alexander Sentsov, Nikita Shaimov, Artem Sherstyuk, Andrey Shutkin, Egor Silvestrov, Bulat Suleimanov, Matvey Suprunov, Sergey Taranov, Irina Tolstykh, Tatiana Trofimuk, Ilya Trushkin, Aleksandra Tsybina, Olga Varlashina, Viacheslav Vasilev, Ilya Vasiliev, Eugeny Vilisov, Sergey Yakubson, Konstantin Zakharov
