entry.summary: The paper constructs skill-level actions from a flow-matching policy trained on skill-segmented demonstrations, so that one skill execution equals one world-model transition, and proposes four action abstractions of increasing task knowledge. This shortens planning horizons for long-horizon robotic tasks without requiring a hand-designed symbolic skill vocabulary.

entry.title: Lend Me Your Eyes: Instruction-Aware Text Embeddings via Attention Relay

author.name: Yiyuan Luo, Vaggos Chatziafratis

entry.summary: The paper introduces Attention Relay, a training-free method that transfers instruction-following ability from an instruction-tuned LLM to a text embedding model by passing LLM attention weights into the embedder's attention. Experiments across six LLMs and ten embedding models show nearly all combinations become instruction-aware. This is a simple, broadly applicable trick for improving embedding models without training.

entry.title: When Evidence Changes: Evaluating Memory Repair and Re-reading in Language-Model Agents

author.name: Wenhui Chu (University at Albany, State University of New York)

entry.summary: The paper introduces an evidence-revision evaluation on medication and problem-list tasks from ICU records, testing how LLM agents should handle revoked or replaced supporting documents: memory repair (caching, rebuilding, graph-local repair) versus full or filtered re-reading. Across two 7B models, local repair cuts revision tokens 5-10x versus rebuilding, but every memory pipeline costs at least twice full re-reading in held-out conditions.

entry.title: Stance Drift: How AI-mediated Communication Distorts Our Message

author.name: Lingchong Liu, Yanfei Zhou, Jacob Bien, Y. X. Rachel Wang, Lucy Xia, Xin Tong

entry.summary: The authors model AI-mediated communication as a generate-then-extract pipeline over five stance categories and define a stance preservation rate, finding that none of nine LLMs exceeded 0.7 SPR across 112 debate propositions. This quantifies how LLM mediation subtly shifts the positions a speaker is conveying, with implications for trust and faithful communication. Statistically careful and societally relevant.

entry.title: Dataset Signatures in Human-LLM Interactions and User Modeling

author.name: Joseph Suh, Serina Chang

entry.summary: The authors study seven human-LLM interaction datasets, spanning in-the-wild chat logs and human preference data, and show via a Torralba-Efros-style classification experiment that classifiers can identify a conversation's source dataset from user messages alone well above chance. This indicates datasets carry distinct signatures that affect downstream user modeling and research built on them. The work raises important concerns about generalization and representativeness in human-LLM interaction research.

entry.title: Plan Canvas: Fixed Reasoning Regions for Continuous Language Flows

author.name: Miaohe Niu, Pengxiang Li, Jingbo Zhu, Tong Xiao

entry.summary: Plan Canvas addresses how to add chain-of-thought reasoning to continuous/diffusion-style language models that denoise an entire canvas at once, by fixing a fixed-capacity plan region boundary between reasoning trace and answer, with supervised padding and separate denoising clocks for plan and answer. This removes the need for the model to jointly decide trace length, trace placement, and answer content. Relevant to the growing area of diffusion and non-autoregressive text generation.

entry.title: AECP: Artifact-Exclusive Communication Protocol for Multi-Agent Code Generation

author.name: Jiaqi Xue, Yanjun Wang, Xiangci Li, Lingbo Mo, Aritra Sengupta, Shweta Garg, Murali Krishna Ramanathan, Myeongsoo Kim

entry.summary: AECP moves part of multi-agent code-generation coordination from individual agents into the execution harness by making shared artifacts interface-enforced, so shared findings are actually used and deviations from agreed interfaces are detected automatically. This addresses the problem that context-only communication in agent teams often goes unused or unverified. Relevant to scaling coding agents on repository-level tasks.

entry.title: SAFE-MR: Evidence Sufficiency Learning for Selective Multimodal Rumor Detection

author.name: Shiwen Ni

entry.summary: SAFE-MR separates claim veracity from evidence sufficiency in multimodal rumor detection, decomposing image-text posts into verifiable claims and building a relation-aware claim-evidence graph with provenance weighting. Separate veracity and sufficiency heads enable selective prediction, abstaining when retrieved evidence is relevant but insufficient.

entry.title: COMPASS 2.0: psychometric representational similarity analysis distinguishes symptom structure from personal signal

author.name: Baihan Lin

entry.summary: COMPASS 2.0 introduces psychometric representational similarity analysis to test whether speech-derived psychiatric questionnaire scores reflect the person or merely item wording. In pre-registered analyses of 275 clinical interviews, language-derived symptom geometry resembled item wording more than self-report, with no structure beyond wording detected by registered tests - a cautionary negative result.

entry.title: FADE: Frame-Aware Diffusion-Transformer-based Multi-Concept Erasure for Video Unlearning

author.name: Yuchen Li, Kaiyuan Deng, Chaoran Feng, Zhenyu Tang, Li Yuan

entry.summary: FADE is a multi-concept unlearning framework for text-to-video diffusion models that identifies and fixes frame-reactivation gaps where erased concepts resurface in isolated frames. It combines a closed-form key/value edit suppressing all target concepts with per-concept frame-aware low-rank adapters, and evaluates multi-concept erasure that prior work ignored.

entry.title: Rethinking Long-Video Efficiency: A Joint Allocation Perspective on Frames, Pixels, and Front-End Latency

author.name: Sixun Dong, Wei Li, Andong Deng, Qi Qian, Victor Zhu, Zhengping Ji, Chen Chen

entry.summary: This empirical study shows that for long-video VLMs, dense low-resolution sampling beats sparse native-resolution sampling at matched token budgets, resolution-sensitive tasks benefit from selected high-resolution frames, and front-end decoding dominates wall-clock time for hour-long videos. Based on these findings it introduces LoHi, a training-free joint allocation method across frames, pixels, and decoding.

entry.title: LoCoSplat: Real-Time Feed-Forward 3D Gaussian Splatting with Minimal 3D Reasoning

author.name: Sinan Wang, Jinjin He, Yuchen Sun, Duowen Chen, Shenyifan Lu, Bo Zhu

entry.summary: LoCoSplat argues that Gaussian parameters beyond depth can be derived from a fixed local average of neighboring point features rather than a heavy learned 3D network. It uses a 0.14M-parameter pointwise MLP reading coarse and fine grids, achieving real-time feed-forward 3DGS without learned 3D networks or dynamic sparse computation.

entry.title: DriftSR: One-Step Real-World Image Super-Resolution via Distribution Drifting

author.name: Wei Zhu, Kai Zhang, Yu Zheng, Zhaopeng Yang, Lei Luo, Yong Guo, Jian Yang

entry.summary: DriftSR is a one-step real-world image super-resolution framework that exploits pretrained diffusion priors through distribution drifting in a frozen intermediate representation space, avoiding score distillation, adversarial losses, and extra task-specific encoders. Spatial Feature Drifting treats spatial features as distributional samples to enable better detail recovery. It targets the practical goal of efficient, perceptually rich Real-ISR with simpler optimization.

entry.title: PixReenact: Pixel-Conditioned Causal Video Diffusion for Streaming Head-Avatar Reenactment

author.name: Gavriel Habib, Dvir Samuel, Or Shimshi, Rami Ben-Ari

entry.summary: PixReenact is a streaming head-avatar reenactment framework built on causal video diffusion that conditions directly on VAE-encoded reference pixels, avoiding lossy identity/motion extractors while providing robust motion transfer, long-term identity stability, and low latency. It moves past offline clip-based diffusion generation toward continuous streaming output. Relevant to real-time avatars for telepresence, VR, and video conferencing.

entry.title: Learning Conditional Source Distribution via Flow Reversal for Temporal Flow Matching

author.name: Kuan-Hsun Tu, Hsuan-Chi Liu, Jia-Wei Liao, Chien-Sheng Chiang, Tsung-Wei Ke

entry.summary: CNP-Flow introduces a flow matching framework for temporal generation in which a conditional noise predictor produces an isotropic Gaussian source per condition, supervised by source samples recovered through flow reversal of a pretrained FM model, within a three-stage training pipeline that preserves the FM backbone. Standard conditional flow matching instead draws sources from an unconditional Gaussian. Evaluated across video prediction and related tasks, this offers a new conditioning mechanism for generative flow models.

entry.title: Robust Local Optimization Done Right

author.name: James Pritts, Kevin K\"oser

entry.summary: Systematically separates hypothesis selection from refinement in RANSAC-based geometry estimation, isolating the effects of robust-loss shape, mis-specified inlier scales, and optimization strategy for essential/fundamental matrix and homography estimation. Introduces a profile-marginal score that marginalizes nuisance inlier scale and analyzes optimizer behavior on currently-rejected correspondences.

entry.title: FairRSFM: A Biome-Aware Benchmark and Debiasing Framework for Remote Sensing Foundation Models

author.name: Md Aminur Hossain, Omkumar Vaghasiya, Rajeev Ranjan Dwivedi, Vinod Kurmi, Biplab Banerjee

entry.summary: FairRSFM introduces a biome-aware benchmark mapping georeferenced samples from 14 terrestrial biome classes into six ecological macro-groups to reveal disparities hidden by aggregate metrics in remote sensing foundation models. Evaluating Prithvi-EO-2.0, SatMAE, and DOFA under a unified frozen-backbone protocol, it shows consistent biome-dependent performance gaps and proposes a debiasing framework.

entry.title: AnchorGen: Anchored Optimization for Customizable Generative 3D Design

author.name: Hantao Zhang, Oliver Heinimann, Jieke Wu, Yingxuan You, Emilien Seiler, Pascal Fua

entry.summary: AnchorGen introduces a rectified-flow framework trained on joint shape-sketch latents so that 3D shape generation stays consistent with a user-supplied 2D sketch, unlike generic generative priors that drift toward high-density training regions. Constraining the sketch component restricts optimization to the sub-manifold of sketch-consistent shapes.

entry.title: MTOR: Generalizable AI-Generated Video Detection with Multimodal Semantics and Temporal Over-Regularity

author.name: Hang Wang, Chao Shen, Lei Zhang, Zhi-Qi Cheng

entry.summary: MTOR detects AI-generated videos by combining caption-derived textual semantics with visual cues, and by exploiting temporal over-regularity—the finding that generated videos show stronger temporal persistence and lower variability than real footage. This targets generalizable detection as video generation quality improves.

entry.title: VGGT-Bridge: Beyond Sequential Pose Graphs via Coarse-Stride Skip Edges

author.name: Sungjae Choi, Hanna Bae, Sunghyun Baek, Junmo Kim

entry.summary: VGGT-Bridge extends chunk-and-align frameworks for feed-forward visual geometry transformers by adding long-range skip edges between non-adjacent chunks without retraining VGGT, curbing the drift that accumulates through purely sequential pose graphs. This mitigates quadratic attention limits when scaling to thousands of frames.

entry.title: Grounded in Time: A Multi-Source Dataset and Benchmark for Temporal Grounding in Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Yi Wang, Yang Yang, Guangqi Xu, Sumin Lin, Ning Kang, Pengxiang Lu, Xiaotong Chen, Zeyu Xue, Ping Deng, Xing Liu, Chenguang Yang, Zhenyu Lu

entry.summary: GiT introduces a dataset and benchmark for temporal grounding in robotic manipulation, requiring policies to infer task-relevant states from past interactions across biolaboratory, household, and industrial scenarios. It includes real-robot and UMI demonstrations of 18 bimanual tasks, simulation data, and a ManiSkill-based evaluation suite of nine tasks with fine-grained temporal annotations.

entry.title: MOSAIC-SV: Real-Time Adaptive Identification of Vessel Dynamics for the Control and Deployment of Aquatic Robots

author.name: Wensen Liu, Jerry Peng, Shravani Vedagiri, Aaron M. Johnson

entry.summary: MOSAIC-SV is a real-time adaptive system identification and control system for aquatic robots that builds a control-sufficient hydrodynamic model from a spec-sheet prior without dedicated identification trials, re-estimating parameters at every control step. A physically admissible unscented Kalman filter with command-dependent consider projection identifies hydrodynamic, disturbance, and actuator parameters while the controller plans on the evolving model.

entry.title: TacOT: Learning Contact-Rich Dexterous Manipulation from Human Demonstrations via Tactile-Guided Optimal Transport

author.name: Xingting Li, Yifan Han, Zijian Lin, Wei Hou, Chuqiao Lyu, Shoujie Li, Wenbo Ding

entry.summary: TacOT is a human-to-robot transfer framework for contact-rich dexterous manipulation that uses tactile dynamics rather than visual or motion similarity to establish human-robot correspondence, employing action-tactile dynamic time warping and optimal transport to match demonstrations with consistent contact states and force patterns.

entry.title: Tackling Sim-to-Real Mismatch Through Sampling-Based Disturbance Observers: From Analytical Models to Learned World Models

author.name: Tianqi Zhu, Jun Yang, Jianliang Mao, Cong Li, Shihua Li

entry.summary: Introduces the sampling-based disturbance observer (SDOB), extending classical disturbance observers beyond explicit plant models to simulators, cost-query interfaces, and learned world models by separating observable state and cost channels. This provides a unified mechanism to estimate unmodeled disturbances and close the sim-to-real gap across model types.

entry.title: FOCUS: Fine-Grained Open-Vocabulary Change Detection for Uncertainty-Aware Semi-Static Scenes

author.name: Can Xu, Mingfeng Yuan, Mahan Mohammadi, Steven L. Waslander

entry.summary: FOCUS formulates long-term map maintenance in semi-static environments as probabilistic inference, fusing geometric likelihood with appearance likelihood from a 3D Gaussian map to detect object-level changes such as in-place replacement of similar objects. A recursive three-state estimator tracks whether each mapped object persisted, was replaced, or was removed.

entry.title: Arm-wise Compositional Generalization in Dual-Arm Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Zaibin Zhang, Binghao Ran, Yuhan Wu, Zhongbo Zhang, Yifan Wang, Junwei Jiang, Junlan Xiao, Wangcheng Shi, Li Kang, Yiran Qin, Zhenfei Yin, Lijun Wang, Huchuan Lu

entry.summary: ACG-Bench provides a standardized testbed for studying whether dual-arm vision-language-action policies can recompose familiar per-arm atomic skills into new coordination patterns, with 23 task-condition pairs across 8 task families covering reordering, synchronization, and cross-task composition. All methods receive identical per-arm prompts, isolating generalization ability. This systematically probes an underexamined axis of VLA generalization.

entry.title: Exploration-Preserving Policy Optimization

author.name: Hangzhan jin, Mohammad Hamdaqa, Doina Precup

entry.summary: ExPPO is a lightweight advantage-shaping rule for RL with verifiable rewards that redistributes credit using response surprisal and prompt pass rate, aiming to keep diverse solutions accessible under repeated sampling where group-relative objectives favor majority modes. The paper includes theoretical analysis of response-level credit.

entry.title: Asynchronous Is Nearly Free for Evolution Strategies on Long-Horizon Agentic Tasks

author.name: William Hoy, Jingxuan Fan, Nurcin Celik, Xu Pan

entry.summary: This short paper introduces bounded-staleness asynchronous evolution strategies for LLM post-training on long-horizon agentic tasks, where synchronous rollout barriers waste compute waiting for stragglers. Because ES is population-based and backpropagation-free, asynchronous consumption of trajectories avoids much of the off-policy cost that plagues asynchronous RL. The result is a near-free efficiency gain demonstrated on the Endless Terminal benchmark-style setting.

entry.title: LMBuild: Evaluating LLM Agents for Generating Buildable and Functional Structures

author.name: Jiateng Liu, Rushi Wang, Cheng Qian, Xuejun Zhang, Sun Li, Jiayu Liu, Yifan Shen, Xu Cao, Jiarui Yao, Bingxuan Li, Ruhi Sarikaya, Heng Ji

entry.summary: LMBuild is a new benchmark that evaluates LLM agents on generating 3D structures that are not just geometrically elegant but physically buildable and functional. It represents objects as assembled structures with part decompositions, joints, materials, and assembly sequences, and provides a unified reproducible evaluation framework with an interactive environment. This shifts evaluation of generative design agents from aesthetics toward real-world realizability, which matters for manufacturing and robotics applications.

entry.title: Recursive Improvement of a Differentiable Scientific Software Ecosystem

author.name: Pengcheng Hou, Xiaojun Tan, Sihan Hu, Ruisi Wang, Shuo Chen, Lei Wang, Youjin Deng, Kun Chen

entry.summary: The paper presents an environment for AI-agent-driven evolution of differentiable scientific software, connecting research-need identification, development, and quality evaluation through a unified differentiation interface with reusable derivative rules over existing numerical routines. It aims to translate agent coding capabilities into useful scientific software across a heterogeneous ecosystem.

entry.title: PermVLA: Factorization Order as a Regularizer for VLA Learning

author.name: Yanqiao Chen, Yuhan Rui, Dongsheng Hou, Zijie Nie, Yutong Wan, Qi Hao

entry.summary: PermVLA identifies factorization order of action chunks as an overlooked regularization choice in vision-language-action policies and introduces causally anchored permutation (CAP), which samples action reveal orders with a tunable chronological prefix. An auxiliary objective trains one shared policy to predict actions from different known subsets, creating multiple conditional prediction problems per demonstration without extra data while retaining deterministic left-to-right control at deployment.

entry.title: ForkPilot: Self-Evolving Policy for Retrospective Search in Long-Horizon Agents

author.name: Xinyue Zeng, Shivam Shandilya, Guilherme Potje, Leonardo Nunes, Rakshanda Agarwal, Ranveer Chandra, Emre Kiciman, Dawei Zhou, Tusher Chakraborty

entry.summary: ForkPilot addresses when long-horizon agents should invoke retrospective search to recover from compounding errors, introducing Search Value Dynamics to characterize the evolving gain-cost trade-off of searching. It proposes a self-evolving two-stage policy-learning framework that adapts as execution evidence evolves and attribution of delayed outcomes becomes complex.

entry.title: Fusion is the New Mutation: Bandit-Guided Evolution on Workflow Graphs

author.name: Zhiwei Shang, Jiahang Sun, Mingrong Gong, Mingze Kong, Zikun Qu, Pingchen Lu, Junhao Dong, Zhipiao Liu, Hongwei Yang, Guoqing Xie, Yao Shu, Zhongxiang Dai

entry.summary: DAGO is a contextual-bandit-guided framework for automated agentic workflow optimization that learns which parent workflows to fuse under a limited evaluation budget. Each candidate parent combination is an arm represented by pretrained embeddings of workflow code and prompts, scored by a diagonal LinUCB policy with a shared reward model.

entry.title: Second-Order Problem Solving for Recursive Self-Improvement in Formal Verification

author.name: Yuxuan Jiang, Aditya Vempaty, Ashish Jagmohan

entry.summary: SO-RSI elevates recursive self-improvement from first-order parameter patching to second-order diagnostic inquiry, passively monitoring execution traces for structural anomalies (recurrence, opposing edits, expectation mismatch) to trigger targeted mechanism investigations before structural changes. It is applied in formal verification workflows to reduce trial-and-error thrashing.

entry.title: ANT: A Multi-Granularity Network Traffic Dataset and Benchmark for Agents Behavior Auditing

author.name: Fan Li, Xiangyu Gao, Zixuan Liu, Tong Li, Chuanpu Fu, Ziqiang Wang, Ke Xu

entry.summary: ANT is a dataset and benchmark linking LLM agent behavior annotations (risk, scenario, behavior primitive) to network traffic, containing 3,114 execution episodes across 20 tasks and five scenarios with over 276,000 bidirectional flows. It enables auditing agent behavior within organizational networks without inspecting private user content.

entry.title: A Step Towards Forgetting: Optimiser History and the Loss of Answer Mass

author.name: Valeria Ruscio, Seth Nabarro, Keiran Thompson

entry.summary: This paper investigates how optimizer momentum memory contributes to catastrophic forgetting during language model fine-tuning. Across three model families, the authors find that stored gradient contributions from earlier model states consistently reduce the probability assigned to previously learned answers, even when current gradients act to preserve them. The decomposition of old-task loss into answer confusion and answer-mass leakage offers a mechanistic account of forgetting.

entry.title: Human Behavior-Informed Crash Scenario Generation with Real-World Crash Priors for Autonomous Vehicle Safety Evaluation

author.name: Mingxing Peng, Xusen Guo, Long Chen, Xintao Yan, Siyu Teng, Jun Ma

entry.summary: CrashSim generates crash scenarios for autonomous vehicle safety evaluation using real-world crash priors that capture how crashes evolve before impact and how crash types are distributed. These priors guide a generative multi-agent traffic simulator, producing more realistic rare-crash simulations than prior methods that raise collision rates without realistic dynamics.

entry.title: EgoExo-Next:Benchmarking Vision-Language Models on Visual-Option Next-State and Cross-View Reasoning

author.name: Yutong Li, Molin Wang, Xiaotong Li, Yanyan Fang, Daoguo Dong, Ziyi Ye

entry.summary: EgoExo-Next is a benchmark of 2,503 human-curated four-choice questions testing whether VLMs can reason about future visual states from observed action trajectories, rather than merely predicting action labels. It spans six egocentric and ego-exo video sources with four subtasks covering next-state and cross-view reasoning.

entry.title: PIT-GCL: Protein Interaction using Topological Graph Contrastive Learning

author.name: Jae Won Choi, Ryoonki Hong, Alan Liang, Manjula Adiveppa Wader, Bingsong Zeng, Peiyang Tang, Longwei Liu, Ruishan Liu

entry.summary: PIT-GCL is a dual-tower, structure-aware framework for protein binding prediction that encodes each protein from sequence, C-alpha point cloud, and global persistent topological features, trained with graph contrastive learning. It targets screening-scale binary binding prediction where bound complex structures and folding-model confidence scores fall short.

entry.title: TempoBridge: Source-Conditioned Flow Matching with Optimal Transport Couplings for Single-Cell Population Transitions

author.name: Bowen Han, Lingbei Meng, Shihuan Luo, Yupeng Zang, Wenlin LI, Peize He, Yaodi Luo, Lian Zhang, Jianqing Zhu, Jinchao Xu

entry.summary: TempoBridge is a source-conditioned flow-matching framework for predicting population transitions in single-cell biology across temporal, genetic, and chemical perturbations, using minibatch optimal transport couplings only during training. It handles destructive unpaired measurements by fixing an empirical source population summary that conditions the velocity field. At inference no target data are required, enabling counterfactual perturbation prediction.

entry.title: TeleGen: Improving LLM-Based Web Application Generation via Runtime Telemetry

author.name: Yujia Luo, Haonan Zhang, Jiasi Shen, Zishuo Ding, Weiyi Shang

entry.summary: TeleGen improves LLM-generated web applications by instrumenting them to collect runtime telemetry during interactive task execution, then compressing raw telemetry into concise briefs that guide code repair. This addresses the blind spot of generate-execute-repair pipelines that only see final task outcomes or error messages and miss the runtime behavior between browser actions and outcomes. The observability-enhanced feedback loop is a sensible mechanism for diagnosing interaction-level failures.

entry.title: Best-of-$N$ Guidance for Test-time Diffusion Alignment

author.name: Richard Lee Kim, Yeongmin Kim, Gyuwon Sim, Taekyu Kim, Minsang Park, Il-chul Moon

entry.summary: The paper proposes Best-of-N Guidance (BoNG), which improves on standard Best-of-N diffusion sampling by injecting reward information into the reverse diffusion trajectory rather than only at final selection. Standard BoN does not raise the average alignment of generated samples and suits only single-output settings; BoNG guides every intermediate step, improving average sample alignment at test time. This strengthens reward-alignment methods for pre-trained diffusion models without fine-tuning.

entry.title: Green-Routed Neural Operators:\\Physics Determines Where the Network Reads

author.name: Chenhao Si, Ming Yan

entry.summary: GRNO fixes a mismatch where PDE transport fields should select read coordinates but neural operators treat them merely as input values. A parameter-free equation adapter builds a departure map whose values are the coordinates where latent features are sampled, combined with a multiscale encoder-decoder, achieving the lowest mean final relative error across five 2D and 3D PDE systems.

entry.title: Protocol-Sensitive Evaluation of Log Anomaly Detection: Component Costs and Target-Access Sensitivity on HDFS and BGL

author.name: Hang Xiao, Janet Sung, Zhaoyi Li, Gangzhen Qian, Chuhong Xu

entry.summary: This empirical study shows that evaluation protocol choices — split construction, representation visibility, and component costs — can flip conclusions in log anomaly detection benchmarks even when detectors are held fixed, using six configurations on HDFS and BGL datasets. Random splits inflate scores near the average-precision ceiling while group-disjoint and chronological protocols produce lower scores and different method rankings. The work is a methodological audit highlighting that much published progress in log anomaly detection may be an artifact of lenient evaluation protocols.

entry.title: Imagine to Act: High-Fidelity Data Synthesis via Image Editing World Model for Scalable GUI Agent Training

author.name: Yongxin Ning, Runliang Niu, Qianli Xing, Zhiyi Duan, Qingzu He, Pan Wang, Qi Wang

entry.summary: Introduces Infinite-Dreamer, a simulation-free data synthesis method using a pixel-level image editing world model to generate high-fidelity GUI action trajectories, treating GUI transitions as image-editing tasks via VLM guidance. This addresses the scarcity of visual-action training data for GUI agents, preserving pixel-level details (icons, layouts) that text/HTML-based GUI world models discard. Relevant to scaling training data for computer-use agents.

entry.title: ReMem: Streaming Video Understanding With Long Context Retention

author.name: Li Yiheng, He Xu, Wang Shaobo, Shao Ling, Lu Shijian

entry.summary: ReMem is a training-free adaptation that lets vision-language models process arbitrarily long streaming videos while retaining long-context information. Through probing experiments, the authors show most existing memory and token-compression approaches progressively lose long-range context as input streams grow. ReMem improves low-latency online video understanding without retraining.

entry.title: Future Anchored Verification and Online Recovery for World Action Models

author.name: Zhibin Qin, Zhenxiong Tan, Xinchao Wang

entry.summary: FAVOR is a lightweight framework for world action models that uses the model's own predicted future frames as anchors to verify execution and recover when actions drift from predictions. Existing execution monitors decide when to stop but not what to restore; FAVOR instead guides online recovery toward intended states. This improves robustness of prediction-then-decode robotic manipulation.

entry.title: Latent Flow Matching for Molecular Graph Generation

author.name: Mathis Goupillon, Roman Bresson, Konstantinos Divriotis, Michalis Vazirgiannis

entry.summary: The paper performs molecular graph generation in the latent space of a pretrained high-fidelity VAE using flow matching, decoding graphs only at the final step. Across molecular benchmarks it achieves strong validity and FCD with a favorable quality-efficiency trade-off versus explicit graph generative models.

entry.title: IdeaLens: Detecting AI Ideas in Long-form Writing

author.name: Rishanth Rajendhran, Minjoon Choi, Jenna Russell, Ramya Namuduri, Deniz B\"ol\"oni-Turgut, Marzena Karpinska, John Wieting, Mohit Iyyer

entry.summary: IdeaLens shifts AI detection from identifying who wrote the words to identifying who generated the ideas, representing documents as paraphrased outlines that strip surface-level word overlap, and training on 1M FineWeb documents with silver labels from an existing prose detector. This addresses an emerging policy question: idea provenance rather than text provenance. It matters as institutions grapple with AI-use policies that hinge on idea attribution.

entry.title: BAT-NO: A Boundary-Condition-Aware Transformer Neural Operator for Crashworthiness Prediction of Vehicle Components

author.name: Haoran Li, Yingxue Zhao, Haosu Zhou, Mustapha Ziane, Pierre Culiere, Tobias Pfaff, Nan Li

entry.summary: Presents a boundary-condition-aware transformer neural operator for autoregressive prediction of transient displacement fields and crashworthiness responses under varying geometry, impact conditions, and support stiffness, reducing reliance on expensive finite-element crash simulation. A B-pillar simulation framework systematically evaluates generalization across these variations.

entry.title: Learning Latent Protein Languages for Autoregressive Generation

author.name: Mahdi Pourmirzaei, Farzaneh Esmaili, Amir Ziashahabi, Mohammadreza Pourmirzaei, Dong Xu

entry.summary: Introduces two learned latent representations for protein generation: Protein Latent Language, a 4,096-state contextual alphabet from a frozen ESM-2 encoder, and Structure Latent Language, a discrete backbone-coordinate representation built on GCP-VQVAE Lite with auxiliary supervision. Autoregressive transformers pretrained on these tokens aim to improve protein sequence and structure generation over amino-acid-token baselines.

entry.title: Progressive Multi-Ancestor Bit-Depth Distillation

author.name: Adil Mubashir Chaudhry, Osama Ahmad, Zubair Khalid, Murtaza Taj

entry.summary: PMABD is a unified compression framework that progressively converts models from FP32 toward INT4 while transferring knowledge through a growing pool of higher-precision ancestor teachers. This addresses the unstable training and performance degradation seen in simultaneous quantization-plus-distillation approaches. It targets deployment on compute- and memory-constrained devices.

entry.title: Measuring Effective Data Resolution in Guided Diffusion Posteriors

author.name: Ridham Patel, Defu Cao, Jiacheng Pang, Yan Liu

entry.summary: This work introduces effective data resolution, a diagnostic comparing the resolution warranted by an inverse problem against the resolution actually realized by a guided diffusion sampler, estimated via perturbations from black-box sampler queries alone. Validation against exact references shows that guidance weight can strongly distort apparent reconstruction resolution. It gives practitioners a way to tell how much of a reconstruction was actually determined by data versus prior.

entry.title: Score-Calibrated Flow for Sampling from Unnormalized Densities with Applications to Generative Online Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Zeyang Li, Yunan Wang, Risheek Garrepalli, Mohammad Ghavamzadeh, Navid Azizan

entry.summary: SCF is an algorithm for training diffusion/flow policies to sample from unnormalized Boltzmann densities specified by a critic, avoiding the high-variance importance sampling that destabilizes existing generative RL methods; it requires no backpropagation through the sampling trajectory. Applied to online RL, it enables expressive multimodal policies. Bridging generative sampling and RL policy improvement is a timely problem as diffusion policies gain traction.

entry.title: Residual Visual Credit Optimization: Conserved Evidence Routing for Multimodal Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Lin Qiu, Yao Liu, Diyi Hu, Hanqing Zeng, Onur Gungor, Chujie Chen, Jiayi Liu, Jianyu Wang, XueLin Zheng

entry.summary: RVCO addresses credit assignment in RL with verifiable rewards for multimodal reasoning by treating token credit as a conserved routing problem: controlled visual interventions yield per-token evidence responses, and a budgeted entropic router distributes fixed sequence utility according to perceptual dependence. Residual support and analytic corrections keep credit mass exact.

entry.title: LeAVJEPA: A Minimalist Architecture for Audio-Visual Self-Supervised Learning

author.name: Benjamin Robson, Santeri Mentu, Wenshuai Zhao, Arno Solin

entry.summary: LeAVJEPA is the first audio-visual encoder trained under the collapse-free LeJEPA objective, using a single early-fusion ViT for audio, video, and joint inputs. Modality dropout treats a missing modality as another view of the same event, making cross-modal alignment implicit, and ablations identify modality dropout as the key alignment mechanism. The result is a simplified architecture matching heavier AV-SSL designs that rely on EMA encoders, decoders, and contrastive losses.

entry.title: EMG-FM-Bench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Foundation Model Transfer and Adaptation on Electromyography

author.name: Tianhao Wu, Xu Wu, Amirmohammad Radmehr, Jiawei Yu, Yi Wu, Phuc Nguyen, Jian Liu

entry.summary: EMG-FM-Bench unifies 20 public EMG datasets with over one million segments to systematically evaluate nine pretrained foundation models on transfer and adaptation to physiological signals. It examines frozen versus fine-tuned performance and how much pretraining helps relative to training from scratch. This fills a genuine gap in understanding FM transferability for a highly variable biosignal modality.

entry.title: Saying, Not Knowing: Aggressively GGUF-Quantized Small Language Models Still Write Rare Words They Can No Longer Define

author.name: Saurabh Kumar Singh, Yogeshwar Singh Dadwhal, Malhar Vedak

entry.summary: Audits 27 GGUF-quantized models across 13 families and four backbones (0.35B-14B) down to Q2_K precision on 429 rare English words, probing both surface word inclusion and one-sentence definition ability with tiered multi-synonym matching and blind LLM-judge scoring. It reveals three regimes at Q2, including total collapse and severe semantic degradation, showing models can still produce rare words they can no longer define. This characterizes a fine-grained lexical cost of aggressive quantization relevant to open-weight deployment.

entry.title: Learning Task and Motion Plans from Real Demonstrations with Hybrid Flow Matching

author.name: Zuleika Redondo Garcia, Andreu Matoses Gimenez, Javier Alonso-Mora

entry.summary: A hybrid flow matching planner uses a single network to jointly generate symbolic task plans via masked discrete flow matching and motion trajectories via continuous flow matching, learned from a small set of real mobile-manipulation demonstrations and executed in closed loop. This removes the need for symbolic domains or search and reduces reliance on thousands of scripted demonstrations.

entry.title: Retrieval-Based In-Context Learning: A Domain Adaptation Framework

author.name: Yilun Zhu, Naihao Deng, Yingcong Li, Naichen Shi, Clayton Scott

entry.summary: The paper formulates in-context retrieval, where demonstrations are retrieved from a database by similarity, as a domain adaptation problem with a source distribution over the database and a target distribution over queries. It establishes theoretical guarantees on in-context learning performance under a flexible class of distribution shifts, extending prior analyses, with experiments on synthetic and language tasks. This provides rigorous foundations for a widely used but under-theorized technique.

entry.title: A Response Theory Probe for Learned Stochastic AI Simulators, Tested on Lorenz-63

author.name: Jo\~ao B\"oger, Simon Driscoll, Niccol\`o Zagli, Valerio Lucarini, Francisco Camara Pereira

entry.summary: The paper proposes a calibrated, mode-resolved test for learned emulators of chaotic stochastic systems based on linear response theory and fluctuation-dissipation relations, checking whether surrogates respond correctly to forcing rather than merely matching forecast skill or long-run statistics. It is demonstrated on Lorenz-63, decomposing responses over stochastic Ruelle-Pollicott resonances.

entry.title: Copying Before Suppression: What Drives a Below-Chance Dip During Language Model Training?

author.name: Tejas Dahiya, Cole Blondin

entry.summary: The authors study Pythia models during training on the Indirect Object Identification task, identifying an early window where accuracy falls below chance because attention heads preferentially write the repeated name before a suppressing computation matures. This shows that mechanistic computations driving a behavior change while the model is still learning the task. A solid contribution to training-dynamics-aware interpretability.

entry.title: Small Agents with Semantic Search: Efficient Multilingual Code Localization

author.name: Maxence Lasbordes, Aarush Sinha, Raphael Sourty, Am\'elie Chatelain, Djam\'e Seddah

entry.summary: The paper investigates whether code file localization from natural-language requests can be delegated to compact specialized models using semantic search, enabling on-device operation with reduced token usage, latency, and cost versus large agents. It introduces a training framework built around ColGREP, a late-interaction retrieval tool, combining weighted supervised fine-tuning on teacher trajectories with turn-level credit assignment based on retrieval outcomes. Results show accuracy, cross-language transfer, and efficiency gains.

entry.title: D-Loop: Looped Diffusion Drafting for Speculative Decoding

author.name: Kecheng Chen, Yuyang He, Cheng Gong, Hui Liu, Guoping Long, Jiajun Li, Shi Wu, Suiyun Zhang, Haoliang Li, Ziru Liu, Rui Liu

entry.summary: D-Loop improves block-diffusion speculative decoding by adding intra-block causal conditioning through looped drafting, addressing the repetition trap where neighboring positions predict redundant tokens without seeing earlier proposals. It achieves longer accepted drafts without extra causal heads or separately trained drafters. This is a efficiency-relevant contribution for faster LLM inference.

entry.title: SearchJev: A Fast and Calibrated System-1 Model for Search Agents

author.name: Congfeng Cao, Lipeng Zuo, Konstantinos Papakostas, Qiwei Xu, Songwei Xu, Lun Zhou, Zhaochun Ren, Yougang Lyu, Xiaohui Yan

entry.summary: SearchJev decouples fast, short search decisions (relevance, sufficiency, next action) from slower System-2 reasoning, scoring legal options directly without autoregressive generation. Its Soft-Label Learning for Calibrated Decisions trains on uncertain supervision and calibrates confidence so uncertain judgments are delegated to the reasoning system.

entry.title: Kepler4D: Controllable Future Video Generation via 4D Scene State Evolution

author.name: Feiran Wang, Bin Duan, Junyi Wu, Gaowen Liu, Yan Yan

entry.summary: Kepler4D generates controllable future video by evolving an explicit 4D scene state: it builds a shared 3D representation of background geometry and object motion, uses a vision-language model to make structured motion decisions, and renders evolving proxies as geometric conditions for synthesis. The deterministic intermediate rollout allows inspection and editing before generation.

entry.title: Multi-Crop Leaf Disease Recognition: A Unified Benchmark and Cross-Region Study

author.name: Rosemary Nalwanga, Sebastian Bunda, Godliver Owomugisha, Luuk Spreeuwers, Estefania Talavera Martinez

entry.summary: The paper presents the MLD benchmark, unifying six public crop-disease datasets from the USA, Asia, and Africa into a hierarchical taxonomy covering 18 crops, 56 classes, and 167,427 images. It defines standardized single-source and pooled evaluation protocols exposing how near-perfect lab-condition accuracy collapses under realistic cross-region domain shift.

entry.title: Mobile-4DGS: Unified Static-Dynamic Real-time Mobile Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Xiaobiao Du, Beixi Hao, Zhen Fang, Tianqing Zhu, Richard Hartley, Xin Yu

entry.summary: Mobile-4DGS is a lightweight unified framework for real-time static and dynamic Gaussian Splatting rendering on mobile devices, featuring a Monte Carlo Specular Energy Aggregator that compresses high-order radiance into first-order spherical harmonics and pre-baked attribute-conditioned SH offsets. Deploying 4D Gaussian rendering under mobile compute/storage constraints is a demanding systems challenge. Success here broadens AR/VR and on-device graphics applications.

entry.title: Label-Free Coreset Selection with Foundation Models for Efficient Annotation in Computational Pathology

author.name: Tuo Yin, Jennifer Dhont

entry.summary: Presents GCcore, a hyperparameter-free, label-free coreset selection method that embeds whole-slide images with any pathology foundation model and greedily selects samples maximizing coverage, reducing costly expert annotation in computational pathology. Unlike prior coreset methods, it avoids hyperparameters tuned on natural-image benchmarks that fail to transfer to histopathology.

entry.title: ExStereo: Lifting 2D Vision-Language-Action Models to 3D with Explicit Stereo Representations

author.name: I-Chun Arthur Liu, Jason Chen, Gaurav S. Sukhatme, Daniel Seita

entry.summary: ExStereo augments pre-trained 2D VLA models with 3D perception by adding a stereo module that reconstructs scene geometry from stereo image pairs using modern stereo foundation models. Action tokens selectively attend to extracted stereo tokens, injecting metric depth and precise 3D positions without retraining from scratch.

entry.title: AgenticTactileVLA: Contact-Guided Execution-Time Supervision for Generalizable Dexterous Manipulation without VLA Retraining

author.name: Elizaveta Semenyakina, Ivan Snegirev, Mikhail Kiselev, Miguel Altamirano Cabrera, Artem Lykov, Hajira Amjad, Dzmitry Tsetserukou

entry.summary: AgenticTactileVLA is an execution-time supervisor that uses finger-position and motor-effort feedback to adapt a fixed vision-language-action policy during physical interaction, deciding among transparent operation, finger-flexion refinement, configuration retention/release, VLA retry, or compliant control regimes. This shifts object-specific adaptation from prediction time to execution time without retraining the VLA.

entry.title: RiskFly: Frustum-Aligned Spatio-Temporal Risk Fields for One-Stage Agile Flight in Dynamic Clutter

author.name: Luxia Ai, Haopeng Chen, Yuchao Mei, Guohao Zhang, Wenbing Tao

entry.summary: RiskFly is a one-stage learning-based planner for agile drone flight in dynamic clutter that predicts spatio-temporal risk fields aligned with its action space, using paired depth sequences and frustum-aligned range maps. This gives the planner spatially and temporally structured danger predictions, avoiding the late reactive maneuvers of scalar-cost one-stage planners.

entry.title: TUCO: Curating Simulation Demonstrations for Sim-to-Real Robot Policy Co-Training

author.name: Ning Zhu, Mengfei Zhao, Yikai Tang, Zhangyujie Sun, Peihao Li, Dongyue Ni, Jindou Jia, Jianfei Yang

entry.summary: TUCO is the first systematic study of data curation for sim-to-real robot policy co-training, using influence functions to trace how each simulated demonstration affects target-domain scoring rollouts and decomposing effects into trajectory-level utility and set-level coverage. This enables principled selection of simulation data to supplement scarce real-world demonstrations.

entry.title: DexForge: High-Fidelity Physics-Informed Dexterous Retargeting

author.name: Meizhong Wang, Kun Cao, Ruiqi Ni, Lihua Xie, Yiguang Hong

entry.summary: DexForge converts human video demonstrations into high-fidelity robot trajectories using differentiable physics: it reconstructs spherical-Gaussian object models and hand-object motion from visual observations, then performs contact-aware kinematic retargeting with force-aware dynamics optimization in a differentiable simulator combining Gaussian collision detection with differentiable dynamics. This improves cross-embodiment reproduction of dexterous manipulation under physical constraints.

entry.title: Retrieval-Augmented Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Anirudh Goyal, Abram L. Friesen, Andrea Banino, Theophane Weber, Nan Rosemary Ke, Adria Puigdomenech Badia, Arthur Guez, Mehdi Mirza, Peter C. Humphreys, Ksenia Konyushkova, Laurent Sifre, Michal Valko, Simon Osindero, Timothy Lillicrap, Nicolas Heess, Charles Blundell

entry.summary: The paper proposes augmenting RL agents with a learned retrieval process that directly accesses a dataset of past experiences to map them to optimal behavior, instead of distilling all experience into parametric policies via gradient updates. This addresses computational expense, slow experience integration, and model capacity limits. It is an influential DeepMind paper anticipating later interest in retrieval-based and in-context RL.

entry.title: Bradley-Terry model under general comparison graphs

author.name: Ruijian Han, Yuanhang Luo, Yiming Xu

entry.summary: This work establishes uniform consistency of the maximum likelihood estimator for the Bradley-Terry ranking model under general deterministic comparison designs, removing the need for homogeneity or strong compatibility assumptions on comparison graphs. The pairwise error bound decomposes into a pair-specific effective resistance term and a global spectral gap term, and is shown to be tight up to logarithmic factors. This has direct relevance to ranking systems and to LLM preference-based evaluation pipelines.

entry.title: Behavioral History Outperforms Descriptions of the Person for LLM Synthetic Personas

author.name: Khashayar Pourtaheri, Ahmad Zareei

entry.summary: Using a two-wave panel of 845 US adults measured on 14 behavioral biases, the study finds that LLM synthetic respondents predict an individual's later choices better from their earlier survey answers than from demographics, personality traits, or cognitive scores. This has direct implications for the validity of LLM-based social science simulation.

entry.title: Bidirectional Preference Synthesis: Learning Prompt-Conditioned Preferences from Boundary Failures

author.name: Junbo Wang (Kuaishou Technology, Nanjing University), Lidong Lu (Nanjing University), Zhuoqun Li (Kuaishou Technology), Guiping Jiang (Kuaishou Technology), Xiangyu Wu (Kuaishou Technology), Tinghai Zhang (Kuaishou Technology), Tong Lu (Nanjing University)

entry.summary: BPS improves DPO preference data construction for boundary failures, cases where a response violates the given instruction but coherently satisfies a nearby intent, by adding a reverse preference pair under a synthesized achieved prompt alongside the conventional forward pair. The same response is thus rejected where wrong and chosen where right, teaching prompt-conditioned preferences without changing the DPO objective. Industry-academic collaboration from Kuaishou and Nanjing University.

entry.title: Agent Behavior as Code: Efficient and Robust LLM Agents with Programmatic Specifications

author.name: Peng Qi, Chunliang Lyu, Gang Li, Fabian Chan, Cheng Chang, Ignacio Cases, Will Lu

entry.summary: ABCAgent represents full agent behavior as a symbolic program (Python with optional neural functions), addressing error propagation across similar tasks, redundant FM-call cost and latency, and limited context/instruction-following in conventional LLM agents. Compiling recurring workflows into code promises determinism, reuse, and reduced foundation-model dependence at execution time.

entry.title: EmoRSS: Mitigating Emotion-Induced Over-Refusal in Large Language Models

author.name: Shuyi Miao, Yaojin Ma, Chenhang Cui, Xiaohao Liu, Dang Jisheng, Shengda Zhuo, Fei Shen, Tat-Seng Chua

entry.summary: This paper finds that emotional expression in benign user requests systematically increases LLM refusal tendencies, causing over-refusal, and proposes EmoRSS, an activation-steering method that identifies a refusal-sensitive layer and steers representations to reduce emotion-induced over-refusal while preserving refusals on harmful requests.

entry.title: LifeLong Digital Twin: A Unified Modeling Paradigm and Agent Harness for Event-Driven Lifelong Health State Trajectories

author.name: Jin Jiang, Sean Yates, Jasper Chong, Raymond Brooks, Alex Lawson, Yuqin Qin, Liangcai Gao

entry.summary: The authors introduce LifeLong Digital Twin, an event-driven paradigm that organizes life events into daily health states accumulated into a lifelong health context, with an agent harness for integrating multimodal evidence beyond text. They evaluate four language models across 25 diseases on this framework.

entry.title: Copies or Sources? Measuring How LLM Aggregators Count Restated Evidence in Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Jianxin Gao, Runze Li, Tianyi Yu, Liangwei Ren, Bohan Chen, Zining Wang

entry.summary: The paper introduces a copy-weight metric converting reported probabilities into units of independent readings, distinguishing aggregators that count distinct sources from those that double-count restatements. Across three testbeds with fixed evidence but varied restatement and a Bayesian oracle, it measures whether LLM aggregators are misled by repeated statements under different communication protocols.

entry.title: Language models can notice an impossible engineering problem yet still report it as solved

author.name: Shaoliang Yang, Jun Wang

entry.summary: Testing 14 models on 30 pairs of mechanics problems (valid vs. made-impossible variants), the study finds models often fail to reject physically impossible problems even when their calculations reveal impossibility, with 12 of 90 replies from recent models failing to flag flawed versions. This measures a gap between problem recognition and honest reporting under a solved/cannot-solve protocol.

entry.title: BridgeCast: Bridging Ocean Wave Forecasts to Reanalysis via Flow Matching with Exogenous Variables

author.name: Siyu Gan, Dongsheng Luo, Kunxiaojia Yuan, Dongjin Song, Jingchao Ni

entry.summary: BridgeCast is a physics-AI hybrid framework that corrects systematic biases in physics-based ocean wave forecasts using conditional flow matching. The model treats physical model outputs as corrupted observations and learns a continuous-time generative process that transforms their distribution toward that of reanalysis data, producing probabilistic corrected forecasts. This matters for maritime safety, offshore operations, and coastal resilience, where wave forecast accuracy has direct economic and safety consequences.

entry.title: Beware EviLLM: Enabling Vulnerability Injection via Large Language Models

author.name: Zeezoo Ryu, Simon Chung, Muhammad Faraz Karim, Anna Raymaker, Karan Singh Jodha, Yash Chaturvedi, Sukarno Mertoguno

entry.summary: This security paper studies the EviLLM threat model where a third-party adversary compromises an AI code generation pipeline to deliberately inject vulnerabilities, a more realistic scenario than inadvertent vulnerabilities, LLM backdooring, or jailbreaking. The authors implement two EviLLM instances with capabilities comparable to existing cybercriminals and evaluate their effectiveness.

entry.title: What to Preserve in Recursive Computation: A Local Predictive Sufficiency Principle

author.name: Peilin Wang, Feng Shiyang, Hongfu Gao, Cencheng Zhao, Di Yuan, Hui Chen, Guiguang Ding

entry.summary: This theoretical work addresses information loss in recursive computation, where intermediate states are repeatedly compressed. It introduces a local predictive sufficiency principle with recursive predictive closure, proving that controlling local predictive deficiencies at interfaces bounds root-level discrepancy, and derives a tractable variational training procedure from it.

entry.title: Guess My Weight: Profiled Side-Channel Recovery of Floating-Point Neural-Network Weights

author.name: Timon Lum\'ir Fillo, J\'an Mikulec, Anubhab Baksi, Jakub Breier, Xiaolu Hou

entry.summary: Presents a profiled template attack that recovers bit-exact IEEE-754 single-precision neural-network weights from power measurements, targeting the multiplication of a known input with first-layer weights. This extends side-channel attacks beyond reduced-precision settings to the full 32-bit floating-point space.

entry.title: Policy as Data: Replay-Based Policy Dual Averaging via Advantage Regression

author.name: Nianli Peng, Geoffrey J. Gordon, Kiant\'e Brantley

entry.summary: Introduces RDA2C, an actor-critic method that treats replay data as a first-class input to policy improvement: historical advantage estimates contribute directly to a dual score model fitted by regression, from which the current policy is derived via regularized dual averaging with entropy regularization.

entry.title: ResOPD: Tail Residualization for Sparse On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Penghui Yang, Long Xing, Xuanlang Dai, Ziyu Liu, Kai Chen, Yuhang Zang

entry.summary: ResOPD improves on-policy distillation under sparse teacher interfaces by providing unbiased full-vocabulary reverse KL gradient estimation while communicating only sparse teacher signals such as top-k distributions. It resolves the trade-off between high-variance sampled-token estimators and biased top-k objectives via tail residualization.

entry.title: Task-Aware Joint Pruning and Distillation for Efficient Audio Deepfake Detection

author.name: Miao He, Peng Cheng, Zhongjie Ba, Qing Wen, Li Lu, Xin Yang, Kui Ren

entry.summary: The paper proposes a task-aware compression framework for SSL-based audio deepfake detectors that combines cross-domain knowledge distillation with movement-guided structured pruning to preserve forgery-discriminative features under aggressive compression. This enables deployment of deepfake detection on resource-constrained devices where 300M+ parameter SSL models are infeasible.

entry.title: Human-Like Attention? A Psychophysical Comparison of Visual Search in Humans and MLLMs

author.name: Renchi Zhang, Joost C. F. de Winter, Dimitra Dodou, Harleigh C. Seyffert, Yke Bauke Eisma

entry.summary: This study compares visual search behavior between 1,250 humans and MLLMs using identical 2D and 3D stimuli, finding that both show efficient feature search and degraded conjunction search as set size grows, with strong error-rate correlations (rho = 0.82). Divergences also emerged, suggesting MLLMs share some but not all human difficulty signatures.

entry.title: SimpleMark: Fast Multi-Bit Text Watermarking under f -Divergence Constraints

author.name: Benjamin D. Kim, Wanrong Zhang, Weitong Ruan, Lav R. Varshney, Daniel Alabi

entry.summary: Introduces a framework for multi-bit watermarking of LLM text where security is defined via f-divergence from the base model distribution, with per-key, per-message guarantees supporting TV and KL divergences. The coding-based scheme optimally biases next-token distributions under a divergence budget and characterizes the embedding-rate, decoding-reliability, and security tradeoff. Important for provenance and detection of machine-generated text with formal guarantees.

entry.title: Scalable Minimal-Change Learning for Controllable Image Editing

author.name: Shuo Chen, Fengming Huang, Yu Yao, Mingming Gong, Tongliang Liu

entry.summary: The work formalizes minimal-change editing, changing only specified attributes while preserving everything else, as an optimization objective for instruction-based image editing. It uses reinforcement learning with an agentic vision-language reward model that audits candidate edits for unimplemented requested changes and unintended changes, merged via a group-level rubric. This avoids weak proxies like latent L1 regularization and scales without extra supervision.

entry.title: Adaptive Mean Flow for Responsive Closed-Loop Robot Control

author.name: Aksel Vaaler, Marco Job, Christian Holden, Olav Egeland

entry.summary: The paper introduces Adaptive Mean Flow (AMF), a framework addressing the latency of iterative denoising in diffusion and flow-based robot policies that hinders high-frequency closed-loop control. AMF enables responsive action updates using the most recent state information instead of open-loop action chunking. This targets a well-known limitation of modern imitation-learned policies.

entry.title: S$^3$N: A Spherical Spiral Scanning Network for Weather Forecasting

author.name: Fan Yan, Chen Hui, Weisi Lin, Haiqi Zhu, Feng Jiang, Sun-Yuan Kung, Wei Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes a Spherical Spiral Scanning Network for machine-learning weather prediction, with a bidirectional L2Proj mapping to avoid reconstruction errors of HEALPix pointwise mappings and cross-face communication that avoids handcrafted boundary handling. Addresses polar-area distortion and inter-face information flow in global forecasting architectures. An architecture contribution to an active applied area.

entry.title: The Numerical Linear Algebra of Large Language Models

author.name: Abdelkader Baggag, Yousef Saad

entry.summary: A survey/perspective paper by numerical linear algebra authorities (including Yousef Saad) framing LLMs as the latest driver of NLA evolution, following historical waves such as QR algorithms for eigenproblems and sparse solvers. It examines the numerical linear algebra problems underlying LLM training and inference. Such a bridge between the NLA and ML communities can shape research on efficient computation for large models.

entry.title: Your Temporal Link Predictor Is Blind to Who Is Active: A Missing Factor That Transfers Across Models

author.name: Ji Zhang, Zixin Liu, Yiran Ding, Jiayi Wang, Yilu Du, Weijia Xuan

entry.summary: The authors prove that standard negative sampling in temporal link prediction cancels source node activity from the optimal score, so models are never rewarded for learning who is likely to act at all. They propose SNAM, a self-exciting point-process model of source activity fitted to decayed interaction counts, and show this factor dominates under harder historical and inductive negatives.

entry.title: Learning without Overwriting: A Theory of Self-Distillation and Supervised Fine-Tuning in Continual Reasoning

author.name: Shinichi Uemura, Taiji Suzuki

entry.summary: Modeling LLM reasoning as search over a directed acyclic graph, the paper provides a unified theoretical analysis of OPSD and SFT dynamics in continual learning, with optimization guarantees. It shows OPSD with hints from correct outputs enables continual learning without forgetting via sparse yet effective gradients.

entry.title: Task Inference Beyond Least Squares in Behavioral Foundation Models

author.name: Kuan-Hsun Tu, Chien-Sheng Chiang, Hsin-Wei Chen, Ping-Chun Hsieh, Tsung-Wei Ke

entry.summary: The paper identifies that ordinary least squares task-vector inference in behavioral foundation models biases zero-shot policies away from optimality because it leaves reward ordering unconstrained. It proposes BLS, which balances reward reconstruction error against successor-measure mismatch, with a suboptimality gap upper bound.

entry.title: PACMI: Provenance-Aware Cascading Memory Invalidation for Long-Term LLM Agents

author.name: Yiqi Wang, Jiaqi Liu, Jiaqi Zhang, Zhangkai Wu, Yiqun Duan, Mingkai Zheng, Taotao Cai

entry.summary: Proposes PACMI, a framework for LLM agent long-term memory that tracks dependencies among memories and new evidence via a provenance graph with typed edges, assigning records to a four-state validity lattice. It supports cascading invalidation of outdated memories while preserving historically useful records, addressing a real gap in current agent memory systems.

entry.title: WaveGSSM: Graph Wave State Space Models for Propagating Spatio-Temporal Patterns

author.name: Junyou Zhu, Fenying Cai, Ping Xiong, Christian Nauck, Langzhou He, Chao Gao, J\"urgen Kurths, Frank Hellmann

entry.summary: WaveGSSM is a second-order graph state-space model that maintains two coupled latent states per node, representing both the current pattern and its temporal rate of change, with a graph-wave transition updating the motion state. This explicitly models how patterns propagate across graphs, addressing a limitation of space-then-time spatio-temporal GNN architectures. Empirical results show the same field can yield different futures depending on recent rate of change.

entry.title: Dynamic Quadtree Tokenization and Transformer for Adaptive Mesh PDE Forecasting

author.name: Yilin Zhuang, Noah Zambrano, Karthik Duraisamy

entry.summary: WAMRViT is a Vision Transformer for PDE forecasting that tokenizes inputs as balanced quadtrees using a wavelet-inspired refinement criterion, jointly encodes position and refinement level with 3D rotary embeddings, and regrids in cell space for stable long-horizon rollouts. This dynamically allocates resolution to shocks, fronts, and interfaces that occupy small evolving regions. It addresses the quadratic attention cost trade-off between resolution and rollout horizon in neural PDE surrogates.

entry.title: A KKL Observer Perspective on Reservoir Computing

author.name: Anastasia Bizyaeva, Fernando Casta\~nos, Jaime A. Moreno

entry.summary: Shows that the reservoir computing problem is mathematically an extension of the classic Kazantzis-Kravaris-Luenberger observer design problem from systems and control theory. This correspondence allows long-standing open questions in RC, such as why reservoirs learn and how to choose architectures, to draw on the mature KKL literature. A unifying theoretical reframing with cross-disciplinary payoff.

entry.title: DreamTest: World-Model Surrogates for Search-Based Testing of Deep Reinforcement Learning Agents

author.name: Qinghua Xu, Guancheng Wang, Boxi Yu, Liting Lin, Lionel Briand

entry.summary: Introduces DreamTest, a world-model surrogate for search-based testing of deep RL agents in cyber-physical systems. It adapts a recurrent state-space model to learn agent behavior and environment dynamics from training logs, then uses imagined rollouts to produce failure scores that guide test configuration search. This models how tests unfold rather than predicting pass/fail outcomes directly, reducing the cost of finding diverse failures.

entry.title: Ontology Concept Overlap as a Training Signal: Knowledge-Grounded Reinforcement Learning for Clinical Question Answering

author.name: Aditya Tanna, Abhishek Jindal

entry.summary: The paper proposes a soft verifier for RL post-training of language models on clinical QA based on UMLS Concept Unique Identifier overlap computed via scispaCy, providing a graded, externally specified reward without a model in the loop. This is combined within GRPO with an entropy-normalized LLM judge for safety and evidence axes and a small consistency penalty. It fills a gap between preference-based RLHF and binary verifiable rewards for domains where near-correct answers differ by one entity.

entry.title: How Do People Challenge Racial Stereotypes Online? Counter-Story Detection Across Reddit Communities

author.name: Uma Sushmitha Gunturi, Jimin Mun, Maarten Sap, Maria Antoniak

entry.summary: The paper introduces the first computational framework for detecting counter-storytelling against racial stereotypes on Reddit, including a three-dimensional taxonomy grounded in narratology and Critical Race Theory plus a multi-stage detection pipeline. It opens a new area distinct from prior counterspeech research. Strong interdisciplinary social-science contribution.

entry.title: MemStrata: 95% and 90.91% Source-Aware Accuracy on LongMemEval-500 and LoCoMo-1540 with a Local Qwen 3.8 27B Q4_K_M Reader

author.name: Neeraj Yadav (Called It Inc.)

entry.summary: MemStrata is a conversational memory system that achieves 95% on LongMemEval-S and 90.91% on LoCoMo categories 1-4 using a local quantized Qwen 3.8 27B reader with a 24,000-token evidence ceiling, layering nonduplicated, dated, speaker-attributed source spans over a retrieval backbone. It also proposes source-aware grading, where the judge checks the reference against the full source history, yielding notably different scores than reference-only grading. The paper highlights how benchmark grading methodology affects reported long-term memory performance.

entry.title: DeferKV: Rethinking Eviction Timing for One-Shot KV Cache Compression

author.name: Zhe Wang, Jiakai Li, Yujia Sun, Rongzheng Wang, Shuang Liang

entry.summary: DeferKV shows that one-shot KV cache eviction should be delayed from the end of prefill to the first real decoding step, since early decode queries provide attention signals more predictive of subsequent decode attention. Quantitative analysis shows the largest single-step gain occurs at the prefill-decode boundary. This simple timing change improves long-context compression quality.

entry.title: Long-Horizon Textual World Modeling through Structured Reasoning

author.name: Fangxin Wang, Xiang Gao, Yuguang Yao, Kaiwen Dong, Nikash Walia, Kamalika Das

entry.summary: The paper tackles error compounding in long-horizon textual world modeling by introducing structured reasoning that conditions multi-step dynamics predictions on action sequences, addressing weak credit assignment from endpoint-only supervision and information loss in intermediate states. This enables agents to better compare possible futures before acting. It advances language-based world models for planning.

entry.title: DP-ES: Differentially Private Evolution Strategies for Prompt Optimization

author.name: Ziniu Liu, Aiping Li, Yue Han, Han Yu, Junjian Zhang, Dong Zhu, Changjian Li, Shiqiang Zhang

entry.summary: The authors diagnose instability in token-level differentially private prompt optimization (e.g., DP-OPT's high variance on GSM8K) as a structural flaw of greedy token-by-token construction, and propose DP-ES, which evolves a population of full prompts via LLM mutations that never touch the private data, spending privacy budget only on sampled-Gaussian evaluation. Selection is treated as post-processing.

entry.title: From Sight to Foresight: Predictive Spatial Reasoning in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Feiran Wang, Xiaoqi Wang, Ziwei Li, Wenbin He, Yan Yan, Liu Ren

entry.summary: The paper introduces SpatialMind, a metric-scale vision-language model for predictive spatial reasoning that forecasts distances, motion directions, and spatial relations in future, unobserved intervals from a video prefix. A metric depth adapter anchors reasoning to real-world scale and a progressive state chain grounds future prediction in observed dynamics.

entry.title: FLASHSWIN: Unlocking Large Windows and Dense Tokens in Swin Vision Transformers with Memory Efficient Attention

author.name: Tushar Kataria, Gerald Sabin, Ponnuswamy Sadayappan, Shireen Y. Elhabian

entry.summary: FLASHSWIN replaces standard Swin windowed attention, which materializes M-squared-by-M-squared score matrices and full relative-position bias gradients, with a FlashAttention-based memory-efficient implementation. This frees Swin and SwinV2 from the small-window, coarse-token regime, enabling large windows and dense tokens for fine-grained tasks.

entry.title: GeoBridge-VLA: Geometry-Aware Residual Adaptation for Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Hyun Song, Kangmin Kim, Loren Jinsoo Um, Minhui Han, Jaehyeok Park, Taewan Cho, Andrew Jaeyong Choi

entry.summary: GeoBridge-VLA is a two-stage method that learns geometric features from a pretrained VLA's frozen visual encoder with depth supervision, then trains a gated residual interface so these features augment existing visual tokens without a second image encoder or extra tokens. Deployment requires only RGB, robot state, and language, with no depth observations at test time. The method injects precise spatial reasoning into manipulation-focused VLA models.

entry.title: StageVLN: Spatial and Trajectory Auxiliary Guidance for Efficient Vision-Language Navigation

author.name: Anh Dao, Quan-Dung Pham, Le Danh Vinh, The Anh Nguyen, Nguyen Viet Tri Pham, Yiyu Chen, Pham Tuyen Le, Van-Truong Nguyen, Quan Nguyen

entry.summary: StageVLN shapes VLM-based navigation representations during training using privileged spatial and trajectory guidance from a frozen geometry model, while keeping the original lightweight inference pathway intact. This improves scene geometry and progress awareness without deploying depth estimators or explicit maps at test time.

entry.title: Safe Image Generation via Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Eungyeol Han, Jong-Seok Lee

entry.summary: Proposes an in-generation safety framework for text-to-image models that monitors the denoising trajectory, detects emerging NSFW signals from intermediate representations, and intervenes during generation rather than only filtering prompts or moderating outputs afterward. The RL-based intervention targets a broader adversarial space than pre/post-generation checks.

entry.title: Anatomy-preserving unpaired cone-beam CT refinement for image-guided radiotherapy using pseudo-label guided diffusion

author.name: Qi Lai, Yutong He

entry.summary: RefineCBCT is an unpaired diffusion-based framework that removes artifacts from cone-beam CT images while preserving patient-specific anatomy, using pseudo-label guidance and short-step sampling. It achieves best results across metrics on LUNG TCIA data, relevant for image-guided radiotherapy.

entry.title: Video Encoders Built on Image Representations

author.name: Jusheng Zhang, Wenhao Wang, Longqi Cai, Liangzhe Yuan, Yuxiao Wang, Ming-Hsuan Yang

entry.summary: The paper asks whether compact video encoders can be built on frozen image representations by decoupling per-frame representation, cross-frame token allocation, and temporal interaction, using a question-aware selector to allocate frame tokens. This contrasts native video pathways that couple neighboring frames during encoding.

entry.title: Less Context, Better Geometry: Masked Geometric Encoder for Robust 3D Foundation Models

author.name: Zhimin Shao, Xijun Liu, Zhaoliang Zhang, Yutao Tang, Abhay Yadav, Rama Chellappa, Cheng Peng

entry.summary: The paper identifies weaknesses of all-to-all global attention in 3D foundation models, including quadratic complexity and unreliable cross-view evidence propagation. It proposes a Masked Geometric Encoder that strategically drops frame tokens during training and distills from a full-context teacher, yielding more robust geometric representations under incomplete cross-view context.

entry.title: ROOT: Discovering Rewards for User-Specified Embodied Behaviors

author.name: Eren Sadikoglu, Aditya Taparia, Xinyuan Liu, Ransalu Senanayake

entry.summary: ROOT (Reward Optimization via Observable Trees) casts reward design as aligning learned policies with user-specified embodied behaviors, addressing LLM-based reward synthesis failures on subtle visual properties like gait naturalness and posture. Instead of scalar training statistics, it discovers reward functions from observable behavioral descriptions.

entry.title: Recursive Self-Improvement of Visuomotor Policies through Local Recovery Supervision

author.name: Yuzhi Zhang, Xinyu Liu, Yu Zhang

entry.summary: Presents a framework in which visuomotor policies recursively self-improve: each round audits the current policy to locate unresolved failures, generates corrective demonstrations at those failure states via a fixed multimodal tool-using teacher agent, and updates the policy that drives subsequent data collection. A frozen student tests whether teacher interventions support further progress, enabling iterative recovery-focused learning.

entry.title: The Unexpired Plan: A Free Monitor for Accelerated Diffusion Policies

author.name: Yi Zhao, Sebastian Scherer

entry.summary: This paper studies training-free acceleration of diffusion policies through reuse monitors that decide when shortcut denoising is safe, evaluating 114 accelerator configurations across four policy families priced in closed-loop success rather than feature distance. It shows monitor response design matters greatly: published re-arm gates lose twenty points even with an oracle statistic, while an absorbing response recovers performance.

entry.title: Controllable and Photorealistic Pedestrian Risky Motion Generation for End-to-End Driving Safety Evaluation

author.name: Siyuan Liu, Miao Li, Haibao Yu, Haohong Lin, Qing Zhou, Bingbing Nie, Ding Zhao

entry.summary: ControlPed combines trajectory-level conflict synthesis with 3D Gaussian Splatting to generate photorealistic, motion-controllable safety-critical vehicle-pedestrian scenarios for evaluating end-to-end driving systems. It is built on HazardPed, a dataset from 10,352 traffic videos with conflict trajectories, HD maps, and annotated 3D human motions, and lifts synthesized conflicts into 3D human motion before rendering. This bridges the gap between controllable trajectory generators and photorealistic video approaches.

entry.title: Metacognitive Capabilities of LLMs: An Exploration in Mathematical Problem Solving

author.name: Aniket Didolkar, Anirudh Goyal, Nan Rosemary Ke, Siyuan Guo, Michal Valko, Timothy Lillicrap, Danilo Rezende, Yoshua Bengio, Michael Mozer, Sanjeev Arora

entry.summary: The paper provides evidence that strong LLMs possess metacognitive knowledge, such as the ability to name skills and procedures relevant to a given math task, using a prompt-guided procedure to elicit and cluster interpretable skill labels. It validates that these labels are meaningful to the model's reasoning, informing skills-based routing and curriculum approaches. This connects interpretability, reasoning, and self-knowledge in LLMs.

entry.title: CADForge: Agentic Single-View CAD Reconstruction with Explicit Geometry Reasoning

author.name: Keyang Lu, Zhifei Yang, Tianao Dong, Mingzhe Xing, Zhen Xiao, Yikai Wang

entry.summary: CADForge is an agentic framework that reconstructs editable parametric CAD models from single images by decomposing objects into CAD-meaningful components, inferring geometric constraints, and translating them into executable CadQuery programs with a review agent validating results. It addresses practical manufacturing needs where reconstruction must yield editable, precise geometry rather than meshes. Explicit mathematical reasoning replaces end-to-end black-box generation.

entry.title: CORE-RL: Confidence-Oriented Reliability Evaluation of Black-Box Reinforcement Learning Policies

author.name: Santhosh GS, Ananya Ravi, Devika Jay, Abhishek Sarkar, Perepu Satheesh Kumar, Saurav Prakash, Kaushik Dey, Balaraman Ravindran

entry.summary: Proposes a pipeline for evaluating black-box RL policies delivered as opaque executables or remote APIs, integrating early task termination and safety constraint violations into a Unified Reliability Metric. The approach targets deployment in critical domains where policy internals are inaccessible to protect intellectual property.

entry.title: RAGStress: A controlled benchmark for evaluating retrieval-augmented generation under knowledge-base degradation

author.name: Shiqi Yang, Jiekai Ma, Gaoyuan Du

entry.summary: RAGStress is a controlled benchmark for stress-testing RAG systems under systematic knowledge-base corruption, pairing four naturalistic corruption types with three severity levels across 182,546 documents from 57 MMLU subjects and 52,500 evaluations. It reveals how clean-retrieval assumptions break down under realistic KB degradation, an important and neglected evaluation axis for deployed RAG systems.

entry.title: Runtime Authorization of Self-Generated Subgoals in Long-Horizon Tool-Using AI Agents

author.name: Genliang Zhu, Chu Wang

entry.summary: This paper addresses the authorization gap where per-tool permission checks cannot guarantee that an agent's evolving goal graph stays within the principal-approved task. It proposes a formal model with version-bound witnesses for goal-graph mutations, atomic commit boundaries for protected effects, and proofs of trace-policy and forbidden-state preservation under explicit assumptions.

entry.title: EVISKILL: Grounding Skill Evolution in Replayable Evidence

author.name: Yan Zhou, Yili Wang, Yiwei Dai, Qinggang Zhang, Xin Wang

entry.summary: EVISKILL addresses continual skill evolution for LLM agents by grounding edits to procedural knowledge in replayable evidence, preserving behavioral evidence and task contexts that support changes. It recognizes that global validation outcomes incompletely judge constituent changes, discarding locally supported corrections or deferring evidence that needs more experience.

entry.title: DREAM: Dynamic Resolution Assignment For Multimodal Multi-agent Debate

author.name: Khanh-Binh Nguyen, Van Dai Do, Tien Anh Nguyen, Svetha Venkatesh, Hung Le

entry.summary: DREAM improves multimodal multi-agent debate by assigning each agent and sample a dynamic visual resolution instead of a fixed input, and by countering groupthink where agents conform to confident but hallucinated peers. The two-component design targets both visual-scale variation and premature consensus.

entry.title: Grounded Joint-Attention Other-Play for Zero-Shot Coordination

author.name: Giulia Benintendi, Constantin Ruhdorfer, Fabian K\"ogel, Andreas Bulling

entry.summary: The paper introduces MATE, a multi-agent RL method inspired by human joint attention in which agents coordinate by aligning visual attention on scene-salient objects during interaction rather than relying on arbitrary partner-dependent conventions. Combined with other-play ideas, this aims at zero-shot coordination with unfamiliar partners.

entry.title: CVIF: A Criticality-Driven Visual Intervention Framework for Geometric Diagram Understanding in MLLMs

author.name: Jiahui Kang, Bifan Wei, Lingling Zhang, Tianwen Jiang, Qiuyong Xiao, Jihong Zhang, Jun Liu

entry.summary: CVIF is a training-free, inference-time method that localizes critical layers in multimodal LLMs and applies visual interventions during the transition from evidence aggregation to semantic decoding, using a Geometry-Constrained Local Relation Reconstruction module and adaptive steering. It targets the tendency of MLLMs to rely on textual priors over visual evidence in geometric diagrams.
