entry.summary: NeuroLens is a self-supervised JEPA-based model that learns denoised, semantically informative latents from chronic neural recordings, using an adaptive encoder to map changing neural populations into a common latent space and a temporal predictor for future latent structure. It addresses the confound between representational plasticity and recording instability in longitudinal neuroscience.

entry.title: Below what training size do deep tabular generators stop beating trivial baselines? A preregistered benchmark on a size ladder of clinical and standard datasets

author.name: Shivam Shrivastava

entry.summary: A preregistered size-ladder benchmark (8 datasets subsampled from 200 to 20,000 rows, 7 generators, 2,220 committed runs) finds that in 23 of 24 dataset-model pairs, no deep tabular generator beats the best trivial baseline beyond seed noise. This challenges claims that deep generative models help in the small-data clinical regimes where they are most often promoted.

entry.title: A Missing Latent, Not a Missing Simulator: Radius-Augmented Inference for Real JWST Retrieval

author.name: Angshuman Chakravertty, P V V Raj

entry.summary: This paper diagnoses why amortized simulation-based inference trained on radiative-transfer simulators collapses on real JWST spectra of exoplanet WASP-39b, ruling out simulator misspecification causes like temperature gradients and opacity sets. The authors identify the missing planet radius latent as the culprit and build MIRAGE, a radius-augmented inference approach that fixes the posterior collapse. The work directly improves the reliability of ML-based atmospheric retrieval on real telescope data.

entry.title: NEEDLEWORK: Offline Rewriting of Robot Data with Verified Local Stitches

author.name: Juntao Ren, Yifan Hou, Shuran Song

entry.summary: NEEDLE is an offline dataset-augmentation algorithm for robot learning that adds short, verified action bridges between recorded observations in high-dimensional demonstrations. It identifies connections that bypass suboptimal detours, broaden action coverage, and incorporate failed trajectories productively, addressing feasibility-verification challenges that prior low-dimensional stitching methods could not handle. This turns imperfect demonstration datasets into improved training data.

entry.title: HyperThink: Text-to-Parameter Hypernetworks for Efficient Reasoning

author.name: Donggyun Kim, Jack Lu, Chanwoo Kim, Mengye Ren, Seunghoon Hong

entry.summary: HyperThink amortizes long chain-of-thought reasoning into a single query-conditioned parameter update: a hypernetwork predicts updates to a small subset of base LLM parameters, with vector-quantized decoding constraining updates to reusable patterns. Trained end-to-end on the base model's own outputs, it eliminates sequential thinking traces at test time.

entry.title: CLIMB: Confidence-Guided Complementary Evidence for Multimodal Retrieval-Augmented Generation

author.name: Hang Gao, Wujiang Xu, Zhixing Zhang, Kai Mei, Jingyi Yang, Dimitris N. Metaxas

entry.summary: CLIMB is a training-free, inference-time framework for multimodal RAG that builds a compact complementary evidence pool via an MMR-style relevance-redundancy objective and then performs confidence-controlled refinement to decide whether answers need further evidence updates. It addresses the limits of Top-K retrieval and reranking, which often return redundant passages and give no control over answer support.

entry.title: FiberGeoText: A Vision-Language Model for Population- Level Organization of Superficial White Matter

author.name: Yuqian Chen, R. Jarrett Rushmore, Guikun Chen, Fan Zhang, Edward Yeterian, Nikos Makris, Yogesh Rathi, Lauren J. O'Donnell

entry.summary: Introduces FiberGeoText, a vision-language model that organizes short-range superficial white matter streamlines from ultra-high-resolution diffusion MRI into population-level clusters, jointly representing fiber geometry and textual context. This tackles the long-standing correspondence problem posed by short trajectories and highly variable cortical folding in brain imaging.

entry.title: Rethinking Fixed Temporal Grids: Frequency-Disentangled Motion Generation

author.name: Yunjiao Zhou, Junlang Qian, Gen Li, Xinying Guo, Lihua Xie, Jianfei Yang

entry.summary: FreqMo proposes a scale-adaptive motion representation that decomposes human motion into wavelet frequency bands rather than uniform temporal tokens, preserving both slow trajectories and fast transients like foot contacts. The representation supports exact reconstruction and temporal localization for motion generation models.

entry.title: VisionMX: Unlocking Microscaling Post-Training Quantization for Vision Models

author.name: Elad Dror Cohen, Ofir Gordon, Lior Dikstein, Idan Achituve, Hai Victor Habi

entry.summary: VisionMX systematically studies microscaling (MX) post-training quantization for vision models, identifying three error sources: block-scale representation, poor alignment of small conv weights with nonuniform grids, and underuse of signed codes by nonnegative activations. It proposes bounded weight rounding optimization and a foldable affine activation correction.

entry.title: Feedforward Novel View Synthesis for Heterogeneous Cameras

author.name: Meng Wei, Cheng Zhang, Boying Li, Yihang Chen, Jianmin Zheng, Hamid Rezatofighi, Jianfei Cai

entry.summary: This work studies feed-forward novel view synthesis across heterogeneous central cameras (perspective, fisheye, panoramic), identifying an ambiguity introduced by tokenization where visual tokens aggregate projection-dependent ray bundles. It proposes token-center relative Camera Positional Encodings combined with additional mechanisms to enable generalization to unseen target projections during training.

entry.title: Learning While Inferring: Local and Parallel Learning for Edge SNNs across Sensing Modalities

author.name: Yanxun Zhang, Yifei Wang, Changze Lv, Jingwen Xu, Yiyang Lu, Xiaohua Wang, Di Yu, Xin Du, Xiaoqing Zheng

entry.summary: Investigates Bidirectional Spike-Based Distillation as an on-device learning principle for edge spiking neural networks that learn while inferring. BSD couples a stimulus-driven forward network with an independent target-driven reverse network aligned via local objectives, allowing parallel forward inference, reverse inference, and learning under tight edge budgets across sensing modalities.

entry.title: Proprioceptive Sketches as Long-Horizon Intent for Generative Action Policies

author.name: Fangyuan Wang, Songhao Huang, Haoxiang Sun, Shipeng Lyu, Chengyang He, Anqing Duan, Peng Zhou, David Navarro-Alarcon

entry.summary: Proprioceptive Action Models (PAM) jointly generate a compact, timing-free sketch of the robot's remaining joint-space path plus a dense executable action chunk within a single transformer, providing explicit long-horizon intent. This avoids the cost of language plans, subgoal images, or video forecasts, which require translation into motion. The sketch representation offers guidance without over-parameterizing the full remaining trajectory.

entry.title: MixVLA: Adaptive Mixing of Non-Invariant Information for Generalizable Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Pingrui Zhang, Yu Zhang, Pengyuan Wu, Bin Wang, Haoming Song, Xianqiang Gao, ZhaxiZhuoma, Zhigang Wang, Dong Wang, Bin Zhao, Xuelong Li

entry.summary: MixVLA is a model-agnostic training framework that improves zero-shot out-of-distribution generalization of VLA models by adaptively and stochastically mixing non-invariant representations, regularizing against reliance on spurious appearance cues. It requires no additional OOD data or architectural modifications and disentangles task-relevant invariant structure from environment-specific factors. It targets the well-known brittleness of VLA policies under distribution shift.

entry.title: Keep It CALM: Analyzing the Limits of Global Unsafety in Text-to-Image Generation

author.name: NaHyeon Park, Minhyun Lee, Hyunjung Shim

entry.summary: The paper provides a geometric analysis showing that global-unsafety assumptions underlying training-free text-to-image safeguards suffer a coverage-selectivity trade-off: compact unsafe subspaces miss diverse unsafe semantics while broader ones distort benign prompts. It proposes CALM, a training-free safeguard using prompt-local counterfactual correction routed to active unsafe categories. This reframes how safety signals should be applied in image generation.

entry.title: TasteBench: Multimodal Benchmark for Sensory Prediction, from Molecules to Sustainable Foods

author.name: Anna T. Thomas, Sohum Patnaik, Caroline Cotto, Benjamin Sanchez-Lengeling

entry.summary: TasteBench is a multimodal benchmark and privacy-preserving competition for sensory prediction, with a food-level ranking task built on 21K+ human evaluations across 215 plant-based foods and a molecular taste classification task over 15K flavor molecules. It aims to provide computational proxies for sustainable protein discovery, where human sensory panels currently bottleneck the design-build-test loop.

entry.title: MetaRubric: Learning to Reward for Rubric-Based Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Yuxuan Fan, Jaehong Yoon

entry.summary: MetaRubric identifies a failure mode in rubric-based RL called Vacuous Credit, where judges award high scores to criteria whose required content is absent from the response, potentially flipping GRPO advantages. The method alternates evidence-aware policy optimization with counterfactual rubric adaptation, changing one task-relevant fact per prompt to verify credit assignment.

entry.title: HASTE: Evolving Agent Harnesses Against Emerging Attacks Using Sparse Evidence

author.name: Xiqiao Xiong, Moxin Li, Zhixin Ma, Ouxiang Li, Wenjie Wang, Fuli Feng, Xiangnan He

entry.summary: HASTE is a multi-agent framework that automatically evolves agent-harness defenses from sparse threat evidence, such as brief descriptions or a few examples in threat reports, through adversarial interplay between safety-specification generation and attack-case generation. Specifications guide harness updates while generated attacks probe for remaining vulnerabilities.

entry.title: MOF-VERIFY: A Failure-Aware Agentic Harness for MOF Hypothesis Verification

author.name: Donghyun Lee, Taehoon Lee, Geonhee Ahn, Jieun Kim, Jihyun Park, Suyeon Cho, Yoona Kim, Chaerim Shin, Hoi Ri Moon, Jonggeol Na, Sukho Hong, Jihwan Oh, Soo Kyung Kim

entry.summary: MOF-VERIFY provides a diagnostic benchmark and agentic harness for verifying AI-generated hypotheses about metal-organic frameworks, covering structural grounding, synthesis-condition verification, evidence sufficiency, and MLIP-based computational verification. The work addresses reliability gaps in AI co-scientist pipelines where evidence is heterogeneous and identifiers are ambiguous. It exposes where LLM-based verification fails in chemistry.

entry.title: KV$^2$: A Self-Refining KV Cache

author.name: Johannes Wesch, Danni Liu, Jan Niehues

entry.summary: KV2 is a query-agnostic KV-cache compression method that uses a lightweight proxy scorer to identify informative tokens, then reprocesses only that subset for accurate reconstruction-based eviction scoring. This selective refinement approach targets the reusable-context setting where one prefilled context serves many queries. It improves over baselines on RULER, Needle-in-a-Haystack, and LongBench.

entry.title: Refinement Buys Intelligibility, Search Buys Identity: What Test-Time Compute Buys in Masked-Diffusion TTS

author.name: Nityanand Mathur, Hamees Sayed, Ayush Pratap Singh

entry.summary: Training 15 masked-diffusion codec TTS models (19-133M parameters, 3 seeds) on 2,000 hours of speech, the paper sweeps refinement steps at inference and measures an asymmetry: refinement closes 86.2% of the intelligibility range but only 46.4% of speaker identity range. This test-time compute asymmetry persists under longer training schedules. The work offers scaling insight into what inference compute can and cannot buy in diffusion language models.

entry.title: Knowledge or Calculator? Decomposing the Skill Premium in Verifiable Financial Agent Workflows

author.name: Jermyn Zhen Yong Bek, Zhuang Qiang Bok, Zhongtian Sun

entry.summary: FinSkillBench is a 2,603-episode evaluation suite across 12 financial subtasks with deterministic verifiers and hidden regenerable ground truth, executed over 17,820 episodes across 9 models. The study finds curated skill packages raise scores by +16.2 points while single-episode generated skills add only +0.5, and decomposes the skill premium into knowledge versus quantitative-execution components.

entry.title: DeskForge: Dense Supervision from Desktop Environments for Computer-Use Agents

author.name: A. Said Gurbuz, Ahmed Nassar, Sunghwan Hong, Marc Pollefeys, Peter W. J. Staar

entry.summary: DeskForge is a controllable desktop environment that generates large-scale dense supervision for computer-use agents by varying application states, layouts, and appearances, and fusing screenshots, accessibility trees, and window geometry with executed-action outcomes. It produces DeskForge-1M, a million-scale corpus for grounding action targets in complex desktop scenes. With authors including Marc Pollefeys and ETH/Microsoft affiliation, it addresses a key data bottleneck for computer-use agents.

entry.title: How Causality Bridges the Semantic Gap

author.name: Shuhao Zhang, Xuran Zhou, Han Guo, Pengtao Xie, Yujia Zheng

entry.summary: Formalizes structure-constrained semantic alignment, assigning semantics to unlabeled or unmeasured variables by solving embeddings under dependence relations implied by a causal graph, rather than relying on human knowledge with its biases. Grounds variable meaning in causal structure—how variables act on others—rather than in annotation.

entry.title: MuonIO: Principled Norm-Aware Descent for Embedding Tables and Language Model Heads

author.name: Linkai Ma, Xinyu Luo, Mengbo Wang, Ananth Grama, Petros Drineas, Brian Bullins

entry.summary: Extends the Muon optimizer to embedding tables and language model heads, which standard Muon implementations leave to AdamW, by using the 2-to-infinity operator norm for the output head (motivated by softmax Lipschitz geometry) and the 1-to-2 norm for embeddings. This yields a single principled Muon-style update across all major weight matrices of an LM.

entry.title: Revealing Epistemic Uncertainty in MLLMs via Causal-Invariant Masking

author.name: Haoyang Luo, Linwei Tao, Jie Gui, Xinghao Chen, Chang Xu, Jianyuan Guo, Minjing Dong

entry.summary: The paper proposes Causal-Invariant Masking (CIM) for uncertainty quantification in multimodal LLMs, measuring semantic shift between original predictions and predictions conditioned on a causally-focused masked view to isolate epistemic from aleatoric uncertainty. This targets hallucinations arising from superficial associations when query-relevant signals are weak.

entry.title: OmniAct3D: Leveraging Foundation Geometry and Evidence-Grounded Reasoning for Panoramic 3D Detection

author.name: Runtong Wu, Fei Teng, Di Wen, Guoqiang Zhao, Kunyu Peng, Kailun Yang

entry.summary: OmniAct3D adapts perspective-trained vision foundation model detectors to equirectangular panoramic imagery for 360-degree 3D detection in mobile embodied agents, introducing an ERP-Ray geometry adapter to resolve the projection mismatch while preserving transferable VFM priors. It combines this with evidence-grounded reasoning for robust surround perception.

entry.title: ULTRADISCOVERY: Abductive Exploration in an Interconnected, Epistemically Open Universe

author.name: Weihan Li, Tianshi Zheng, Yangqiu Song, Ginny Y. Wong, Simon See

entry.summary: ULTRADISCOVERY is an interactive benchmark of five domains testing abductive scientific discovery, where agents must revise an initially successful theory and predict outcomes of unseen cross-domain interventions. A 2x2 design independently varies whether the representation is disclosed and whether evidence is distributed, isolating two distinct demands of open-world reasoning.

entry.title: Uncertainty as a Proxy for Semantic Correctness in Diffusion-Based Medical Image Synthesis

author.name: Yuxuan Ou, Konstantinos Kamnitsas, OxAAA Study, AICT Consortium, Regent Lee, Vicente Grau

entry.summary: The authors study NCCT-to-CECT synthesis with AortaDiff, a multitask diffusion framework that jointly generates contrast-enhanced CT images and lumen segmentations. They investigate whether model uncertainty can serve as a proxy for anatomical correctness, since pixel-similarity metrics do not capture semantic errors in synthesized medical images.

entry.title: FrugalEvo: Towards Cost-Aware LLM-Guided Program Evolution

author.name: Hui Chen, Xuan Qi, James Xu Zhao, Zhaopeng Feng, Shilong Liu, Kuang Xu, Pang Wei Koh, Bryan Hooi

entry.summary: FrugalEvo reframes LLM-guided evolutionary program search (in the style of AlphaEvolve) around maximizing gain per unit cost rather than gain per iteration. It pairs a stronger, expensive LLM that proposes solution strategies with a cheaper LLM that implements and refines code, and uses prefix-sharing prompts to maximize prompt-cache reuse. The framework addresses the practical economics of LLM-driven optimization.

entry.title: Why Does Adaptive Batching Help LLM Pretraining? A Perspective from Unbounded Variance

author.name: Arda Fazla, Antesh Upadhyay, Ege C. Kaya, M. Berk Sahin, Abolfazl Hashemi

entry.summary: This paper explains adaptive batch-size scheduling in LLM pretraining via the Blum-Gladyshev noise model, which permits gradient variance growing quadratically with distance from initialization. The authors empirically characterize variance growth in real LLM pretraining and show batch-size schedules control it. This provides one of the first theoretical justifications for a widely used but poorly understood practice.

entry.title: Reward Inflation: A Healthy Stimulus for Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Ganghun Lee, Minji Kim, Minsu Lee, Byoung-Tak Zhang

entry.summary: This paper proposes reward inflation, a gradual scaling of reward magnitudes over training, showing theoretically that it induces implicit recency weighting and sustains gradient signals as policies saturate. This suppresses dormant neurons and preserves plasticity in RL agents. Empirical results on ALE games and MuJoCo corroborate faster adaptation and healthier learning dynamics.

entry.title: Mind the Refinement Gap: When Safe High-Level Robot Plans Produce Unsafe Executions

author.name: Stabak Das, Priyesh Ranjan, Xiangfang Li, Lijun Qian

entry.summary: The paper audits a trace-completeness assumption in language-enabled robot systems combining semantic-graph planning with temporal-logic safety monitors: whether the monitored high-level action sequence captures implicit execution effects. Using RoboGuard and SPINE across 28 controlled and 14 end-to-end cases, it shows safe high-level plans can refine into unsafe executions under the same LTL specification. This exposes a concrete safety-verification gap in LLM-driven robot planning.

entry.title: No-Free-Graph: Learning When Multimodal Data Should Be Graphified

author.name: Zekai Chen, Kai Hu, YuXin Zeng, Xunkai Li, Xun Wu, Yinlin Zhu, Zhengyu Wu, Xu Wang, Rong-Hua Li

entry.summary: This work questions the default practice of graphifying multimodal data, showing empirically across diverse datasets, tasks, and graph constructors that adding relational structure is not consistently beneficial and can even hurt. It proposes treating graph construction as a selectable, learnable decision rather than an assumed preprocessing step.

entry.title: SlimKV: Joint Token-Feature KV Cache Compression with Reconstruction-Free Beacon Attention

author.name: Zihan Teng, Jiayu Zhao, Wentao Ren, Minhao Fan, Tianrui Ma, Song Chen, Weichen Liu

entry.summary: SlimKV is a joint token-feature KV-cache compression method that uses low-rank-aware training to condense long contexts into beacon memory states with layer-adaptive rank allocation. It also exploits a positional asymmetry by removing key-side reconstruction, avoiding the decoding slowdowns of prior feature-wise approaches.

entry.title: Pivot-SD: Efficient Self-Distillation for Masked Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Seo Hyun Kim, Sunwoo Hong, Younwoo Choi, Chen-Hao Chao, Se-Young Yun, Rahul G. Krishnan

entry.summary: Pivot-SD is an offline self-distillation framework for masked diffusion language models that supervises only high-impact token commitments, or pivots, which sharply reduce uncertainty over remaining masked positions during denoising. By using an information-based criterion to select pivots rather than training on final text or whole denoising steps, it addresses the distinct credit-assignment challenge of dLMs efficiently. This improves post-training quality for parallel text generation models.

entry.title: Hamiltonian locality testing and certification do not achieve the Heisenberg limit

author.name: Francisco Escudero Guti\'errez, Junseo Lee, Sebastian Zur

entry.summary: This quantum computing theory paper proves lower bounds of Omega(1/epsilon^2) total evolution time for testing whether a Hamiltonian is k-local and for certification against a target Hamiltonian, given access to time-evolution without inversion. The bounds tightly match recent upper bounds, resolving the query complexity of these tasks. This settles the fundamental limits of Hamiltonian property testing.

entry.title: HARPO: Hallucination-Aware Reinforcement Learning for Faithful and Creative Language Generation

author.name: Tiezheng Yu, Yuxin Jiang, Jinpeng Li, Shuning Sun, Fei Mi, Haoli Bai, Lifeng Shang

entry.summary: HARPO is an RL framework that jointly optimizes faithfulness and creativity via a hallucination-aware generative reward model trained with verifiable feedback, a selective activation mechanism that applies writing rewards only to hallucination-free outputs, and a curriculum shifting from creative writing to hallucination-centric tasks. The Qwen3-4B-based HA-GRM achieves strong performance on RAGTruth.

entry.title: Learning from Repaired Reasoning: Root-Cause-Guided On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Chenglei Shen, Haoyang Yao, Weijie Yu, Song Jin, Xiao Zhang, Jun Xu

entry.summary: RC-OPD improves on-policy self-distillation by supervising students with repairs of their own faulty reasoning rather than reference solutions, arguing that reference-based hindsight can leave student reasoning errors unresolved while encouraging borrowed conclusions. The method targets the root cause of failure and varies guidance across the trajectory to avoid a distillation trap where valid reasoning is unnecessarily constrained.

entry.title: Social bot detection in the age of ChatGPT: Challenges and opportunities

author.name: Emilio Ferrara

entry.summary: Emilio Ferrara surveys the state of social bot detection in the era of sophisticated AI chatbots, identifying gaps in current techniques and emerging threats from AI-generated conversations and behaviors. The paper proposes research directions including generative agents for synthetic evaluation data, and multimodal, cross-platform detection based on coordination signatures.

entry.title: MeshQuery: Agentic Seam Planning for UV Parametrization

author.name: Marco Schouten, Arthur Roullier, Elie Michel, Ruben Wiersma, Axel Paris, Tamy Boubekeur

entry.summary: Introduces MeshQuery, a training-free agentic system in which a VLM plans artist-aligned UV seams using edge-selection tools, a queryable mesh representation, and a domain-specific language, refined through a UV-quality feedback loop. On Adobe Substance 3D and Toys4K meshes it produces 2.9x to 4.29x fewer charts than baselines.

entry.title: Kinematics-Induced Multimodal 3D Human Pose Estimation with Subject-Level Privacy

author.name: Kaushik Bhargav Sivangi, Fani Deligianni

entry.summary: The paper presents a multimodal 3D human pose estimation framework fusing RGB, LiDAR, and mmWave radar with kinematics-induced alignment, paired with subject-level privacy auditing. It formulates a black-box subject membership inference attack and pointwise maximal leakage analysis to quantify and mitigate privacy risks from subject-correlated training data.

entry.title: PocketSplat: Mobile Gaussian Reconstruction via World-Space Latent Allocatio

author.name: Wenzhi Guo, Xianda Chen, Dongxuan Chen, Guangchi Fang, Bing Wang

entry.summary: PocketSplat is a feed-forward framework for budgeted 3D Gaussian reconstruction on mobile devices, organizing latent candidates in predicted world space and allocating exact integer capacity across cells under a prescribed output budget. This decouples asset size from input resolution and view count, suiting downstream mobile use.

entry.title: EVEWorld: Physical Evolution Supervision for Embodied World Models

author.name: Kaiqi Wang, Songxin Zhang, Zejian Xie, Xiao Xiong, Zhuoyang Song, Ziwei Wu, Jun Yu Lu, Yitan Teng, Ziying Song, Jiaxing Zhang

entry.summary: EVEWorld tackles Model Laziness in embodied world models, where visual fidelity is prioritized over physical reasoning, by introducing physical evolution supervision with Instance-Guided Restoration and Temporal Instance Alignment components. It also proposes a Model Laziness Ratio metric to quantify physically consistent target evolution during simulated robot interactions.

entry.title: DuoMatching: Joint-Marginal Distribution Matching for Few-Step Video Generation

author.name: Jiahao Zhan, Yan Wang, Yongrui Ma, Qunliang Xing, Ruchang Yao, Runtao Liu, Shijie Zhao, Tianfan Xue

entry.summary: DuoMatching extends distribution matching distillation for streaming video generation by adding a marginal matching objective alongside joint frame-distribution matching, providing dedicated frame-level supervision from an image generator. This unified joint-marginal formulation transfers complementary visual and semantic priors to improve quality and semantic alignment in few-step video generation.

entry.title: Budgeted-GS: Real-Time Large-Scale Gaussian Splatting via Factoring LOD

author.name: Haipeng Wang

entry.summary: Introduces Budgeted-GS, a post-hoc method that converts any trained 3D Gaussian Splatting model into a factoring tree of moment-matched multi-resolution aggregates. After seconds of construction, a single quality parameter selects per-view LOD to fit device memory, enabling city-scale real-time rendering across GPUs of widely different capacities.

entry.title: Parallel Time-Aligned Spiking Self-Attention for Consistent Integer-Valued Training and Spike-Driven Inference

author.name: Peng Xue, Wei Fang, Kaiwei Che, Qingyan Meng, Zhengyu Ma, Yonghong Tian, Huihui Zhou

entry.summary: Identifies Temporal Interaction Mismatch, an operator-level discrepancy when spiking self-attention is applied to compressed I-LIF counts or SFA firing rates, introducing cross-time interactions absent during spike-driven inference. PT-SSA reconstructs virtual spike slices and computes attention only between time-aligned slices in parallel, restoring train-inference consistency.

entry.title: Real-time Event-camera Stereo Visual Odometry via Keytime Gaussian Process Regression

author.name: Nikan Nobari, Jonathan D. Gammell

entry.summary: The paper presents a continuous-time event-camera stereo visual odometry pipeline that processes asynchronous events at their native microsecond resolution while achieving real-time performance. A keytime Gaussian process regression scheme reduces the estimation state that grows prohibitively large under naive white-noise-on-acceleration priors. Event cameras offer high dynamic range and motion-blur resilience that this pipeline preserves.

entry.title: RoboBridge: A Self-Evolving Embodied Agent Framework for Sim-to-Real Transfer

author.name: Chenxi Li, Zhangrui Zhao, Rui Li, Yuan Gao, Kehui Liu, Jiarui Li, Dong Wang, Tong Si, Minting Pan, Wanli Ouyang, Dongzhan Zhou

entry.summary: RoboBridge is a self-evolving embodied agent framework supporting sim-to-real transfer and continual post-deployment adaptation, combining tool-using agent orchestration with procedural-knowledge transfer. Unlike VLA policies that require calibration and extra demonstrations, it emphasizes experience reuse and ongoing adaptation across environments. The framework aims to bridge the gap between simulation-trained capabilities and real-world execution.

entry.title: DR-IPC: Disturbance-Resilient Integrated Planning and Control for LiDAR-Based Quadrotor Navigation

author.name: Peng Liu, Jingyan Wang, Qipeng Ye, Wen Li, Jinya Su, Zuo Wang, Shihua Li, Yunda Yan

entry.summary: DR-IPC unifies LiDAR-based quadrotor path guidance with nonlinear model predictive control that directly outputs angular velocity and thrust, integrating an extended Kalman filter and nonlinear disturbance observer for robust navigation in cluttered environments. The formulation jointly handles quadrotor dynamics, actuator constraints, local motion generation, and safe-flight corridor penalties.

entry.title: Reducing synthetic markers makes some SDF false facts linearly indistinguishable from pretraining-acquired knowledge

author.name: Jason Zeng

entry.summary: This alignment research post examines synthetic document finetuning (SDF), the state of the art for implanting false beliefs into LLMs, and identifies synthetic markers in generated training documents that make implanted false facts linearly detectable by probes on middle-layer activations. Reducing these markers yields subtly-implausible false facts indistinguishable from pretraining knowledge under linear probes, though downstream propagation remains inconsistent and overtraining is detectable. The work directly informs both deception-detection and evaluations of belief-implantation robustness.

entry.title: World Action Modeling with Progressive Visual Planning

author.name: Fei Zhang, Zhaochong An, Duncan Frost, Yikai Wang, Pengfei Liu, Ya Zhang, Michal Drozdzal, Amir Bar

entry.summary: ProWAM is a progressive world action model for robotic control that jointly predicts actions and an ordered sequence of sparse visual sub-goals rather than dense video rollouts or a single future frame. The sparse sub-goals provide explicit visual guidance anchoring action generation throughout task execution, improving long-horizon prediction efficiency. The design scales naturally since sub-goal prediction can extend without dense video generation.

entry.title: Labels Override Definitions in Jev-Style Typed Decision Models

author.name: Seyedarmin Azizi, Erfan Baghaei Potraghloo, Massoud Pedram

entry.summary: This paper studies typed decision models that answer fixed questions by scoring caller-defined options with labels and written definitions, asking whether model probabilities follow the definitions or the label strings. Across four open-weight models, the authors find pervasive option-label bias where labels override stated definitions, with implications for routing, moderation, and triage deployments.

entry.title: JOVE: Joint Execution and Verification for Resource-Aware LLM Task Graphs

author.name: Haoran Zhang, Dongjun Kim, Seohyeon Cha, Kevin S Chan, Ananthram Swami, Gustavo De Veciana, Haris Vikalo

entry.summary: JOVE is an online framework that jointly assigns subtasks of a decomposed reasoning query to heterogeneous LLMs and selects intermediate outputs for paid verification, improving future allocations asynchronously. It optimizes the explore-exploit-style tradeoff between current execution spend and future learning under long-term budget and latency constraints. This targets practical multi-LLM orchestration economics.

entry.title: Geometry Meets Physics: Data-Efficient Pre-Training for Unstructured Neural PDE Solvers

author.name: Luis Medrano-Navarro, Giacomo Baldan, Qiang Liu, Benjamin Holzschuh, Jan Hagnberger, Mathias Niepert, Nils Thuerey

entry.summary: The authors introduce a disk-data-free pre-training framework for neural PDE surrogates on unstructured 3D geometries, avoiding costly pre-computed datasets. For steady-state problems they use geometry-driven intrinsic shape descriptors, and they extend the approach to transient regimes, improving data and compute efficiency of pre-training.

entry.title: CONTRA: Discovering and Qualifying Behavior-Changing Questions for Selective Clarification in LLM Code Generation

author.name: Zheng Fang, Yongmin Li, Yichang Zhang, Dongming Jin, Haoyu Wang, Shuai Wang, Zhi Jin, Ge Li

entry.summary: CONTRA is a training-free method that identifies which clarification questions actually change intended code behavior, combining broad question discovery with semantic and execution-based qualification to avoid unnecessary interruptions. It complements work like ClarifyCodeBench by making clarification selective rather than exhaustive. Early clarification of underspecified requirements reduces costly downstream corrections in agentic coding.

entry.title: Geometry-Aware Time Reparameterization for Flow-Map Distillation

author.name: F\'elix Dedek, Makoto Yamada

entry.summary: Proposes reparameterizing the teacher's time variable in flow-map distillation so that trajectory segments with large normal acceleration—hypothesized to be hardest to distill—receive more student learning time, while preserving geometric paths and the terminal distribution. Includes a theoretical shared-clock construction and a practical robust approximation.

entry.title: Improving Atomic-Fact Recall via Focused Views in Unstructured Knowledge Editing

author.name: Ding Wu, Ye Zhang, Haoyu Wang, Tianci Liu

entry.summary: This work addresses context reliance in unstructured knowledge editing of LLMs, where edited models can repeat the editing passage but fail to recall its individual facts without the original context. The authors propose training editors on focused views to improve atomic-fact recall while preserving unrelated knowledge.

entry.title: NegT2IBench: When Negation Changes the Picture. A Polarity Benchmark for Text-to-Image Models

author.name: Omar Elfatairy, Maria A. Bravo, Jessica Bader, Zeynep Akata

entry.summary: NegT2IBench is a 4,800-prompt benchmark measuring whether text-to-image models can satisfy negated constraints such as generating a non-red cup, with prompts organized by polarity so negation effects are separated from prompt complexity. It uses detector-based evaluation and reveals systematic weaknesses in handling negation across T2I models.

entry.title: SPEAR: A Spectral-Disentangled MoE Neural Operator with Knowledge-Guided Expert Aggregation for Large-Scale PDE Pretraining

author.name: Dengdi Sun, Xiaoya Zhou, Xiao Wang, Wanli Lyu, Jin Tang, Bin Luo

entry.summary: SPEAR is a mixture-of-experts neural operator for PDE foundation-model pretraining that decouples features into low- and high-frequency components, sharing transferable dynamics while specializing to PDE-specific patterns. A knowledge-guided expert aggregation strategy reduces expert redundancy, a common MoE failure mode in this domain.

entry.title: Capability Scaling-Down Laws for LLM Compression

author.name: Xueqi Cheng, Liang Wu, Kelly Wan, Liangjie Hong, Yushun Dong

entry.summary: This paper systematically studies capability scaling-down laws for LLM compression across pruning, quantization, and distillation, relating capability loss in math, code, and QA to model size, training stage, compression settings, and data availability. It develops simple predictive relations validated on unseen configurations and model states. Predictable capability loss would make compression configuration selection far less empirical.

entry.title: Activation Sparsity with Weight Approximation for Faster LLM Decoding on Offloaded Weights

author.name: JuneHyung Kim, Sankeerth Durvasula, Nandita Vijaykumar

entry.summary: This work improves LLM decoding speed on consumer GPUs by combining activation sparsity, which skips weight transfers for near-zero activations, with weight approximation. The key insight is that weights associated with small-magnitude activations collectively matter sharply, so naive sparsity-based skipping degrades quality; replacing those weights with approximations improves the quality-speed tradeoff. This addresses a practical deployment bottleneck for memory-constrained inference.

entry.title: A Controlled Audit of Personal AI Memory for Rating Prediction

author.name: Shivam Gupta

entry.summary: The paper audits whether personal AI memory systems genuinely use historical item-rating associations or merely user rating tendencies, by permuting histories within users while preserving rating distributions and metadata. Testing a Mem0 pipeline with Qwen and Phi readers on Coat and MovieLens benchmarks, it finds measurable accuracy degradation relative to full history, suggesting memory extraction loses useful signal.

entry.title: Do ResNets Route? Sparse Interaction Experts in Residual Networks

author.name: Liang Yan, Siying Chen, Kaijie Chen, Bo Li, Jinghao Zhang, Mu Miao

entry.summary: The paper decomposes trained ResNets as set functions over residual-branch masks using Möbius inversion, exactly separating individual residual corrections from higher-order interactions, with each k-way interaction shown to scale as O(lambda^k). Exhaustive analysis of ImageNet-trained ResNet-18/34 reveals interaction mass peaks at surprisingly high orders (five and ten), and shifting residual scale moves the spectra but changes predictions.

entry.title: Operator-informed initialization for Fourier features physics-informed neural networks

author.name: Juan Molina, Paris Perdikaris, Mircea Petrache, Mat\'ias Courdurier, Francisco Sahli Costabal

entry.summary: Analyzing Fourier-feature PINNs in the NTK regime, the authors derive an explicit frequency-domain error evolution equation showing convergence of each frequency is governed by the product of the differential operator symbol and initialization spectral density. They propose a PDE-specific informative initialization strategy that mitigates spectral bias.

entry.title: UniIntervene++: An Adaptive Intervention Agent for Efficient Real-World Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Yudong Lin, Haoyuan Deng, Zhuoxuan Yuan, Zaijia Yang, Yuanjiang Xue, Ziwei Wang

entry.summary: UniIntervene++ is an adaptive intervention agent for online robot RL that learns when to hand control between autonomous policy execution and heterogeneous assisted behaviors. It formulates the evolving policy, trajectory correction, and a task-structured CodePolicy as options in a unified semi-MDP, learning their relative values online so assistance adapts as policy competence grows. This improves sample efficiency and safety of real-world online RL for robotics.

entry.title: Wrong Organ, Right Physics: Transferring Echocardiography Pretraining to Lung Ultrasound for Tuberculosis Screening

author.name: Christiaan M. Geldenhuys, Joshua M. Jansen van V\"uren, V\'eronique Suttels, Trevor Brokowski, Ablo P. Wachinou, Mary-Anne Hartley, Rensu P. Theart, Grant Theron, Thomas R. Niesler

entry.summary: This study asks whether ultrasound encoders pretrained on echocardiography (a high-resource domain) transfer to lung ultrasound for tuberculosis screening in low-resource settings, comparing seventeen encoders across three architecture families including matched V-JEPA2 and EchoJEPA variants. Results indicate encoder choice does not resolve classification challenges on its own, providing sobering evidence about the limits of cross-domain ultrasound pretraining. The work targets a high-impact global health application.

entry.title: Evaluating LLM-as-a-Judge Beyond Score Alignment: A Psychometric Analysis of Residual Judging Difficulty

author.name: Longwei Cong, Sonja Hahn, Sebastian Gombert, Leon Camus, Fabian Zehner, Hendrik Drachsler, Ulf Kroehne

entry.summary: Using Many-Facet Rasch Models on summarization ratings, the authors decompose human and LLM judge scores into latent quality, rater severity, and threshold components, defining residual hardness to compare which cases each finds difficult. Across 17 open-weight LLM judges on SummEval, they find that aggregate score agreement conceals substantial differences in the difficulty structure of human versus LLM judging.

entry.title: Collective Bias Mitigation via Model Routing and Collaboration

author.name: Mingzhe Du, Luu Anh Tuan, Xiaobao Wu, Yichong Huang, Yue Liu, Dong Huang, Huijun Liu, Bin Ji, Jie M. Zhang, See-Kiong Ng

entry.summary: This paper introduces Collective Bias Mitigation (CBM), a framework that reduces bias in LLMs by learning fine-grained model behavior and routing queries across diverse LLMs that share knowledge with each other, rather than relying on single-model self-debiasing. It targets deployment domains such as public health, finance, and governance where both accuracy and societal alignment matter.

entry.title: FactorSplat: Appearance-Controllable Gaussian Proxies for Medical Volume Rendering

author.name: Zhongpai Gao, Benjamin Planche, Meng Zheng, Anwesa Choudhuri, Terrence Chen, Ziyan Wu

entry.summary: Introduces FactorSplat, a per-scene N-dimensional Gaussian splatting proxy for medical volume rendering that accepts region-specific intensity-to-RGBA transfer-function curves at inference rather than baking one appearance into the representation. Using a shared functional encoder and low-rank per-Gaussian factors, it improves PSNR and changed-region error over baselines across seven CT and MR scans.

entry.title: RYOPO: Bringing End-to-End Category-Level Object Pose Estimation into Real Time

author.name: Hakjin Lee, Junghoon Seo, Jaehoon Sim

entry.summary: RYOPO is an end-to-end query-based RGB-D set predictor that jointly detects, segments, and estimates 9-DoF poses of unseen category instances in real time, without CAD shape priors or a separate segmentor. Shared scene encoding avoids costly per-object crop processing that hampers prior methods.

entry.title: DEPICT: Scoring Text-to-Image Alignment by Answer Agreement

author.name: Vasco Ramos, Sandra Godinho Silva, Joao Magalhaes, Ricardo Rei, Pedro Henrique Martins

entry.summary: DEPICT is a metric for image-text alignment that scores text-to-image generation by answer agreement, addressing failures of fine-tuned metrics (backbone-bound), holistic VLM metrics (missing fine details), and decomposed verification pipelines. It targets fine-grained issues such as missing objects, swapped attributes, miscounts, and ignored negations for T2I benchmarking and hallucination detection.

entry.title: Evolutionary Computation for Trustworthy AI: From Attacks and Defenses to Self-Evolving Era

author.name: Junhao Dong, Chenkai Wang, Xuanhui Lin, Mingrong Gong, Siyu Wang, Yuqing Wen, Jiao Liu, Catherine Huang, Gary G. Yen, Xin Yao, Yew-Soon Ong

entry.summary: A survey-style paper arguing that trustworthy AI's scope has expanded from model-level robustness to system-level reliability covering tool use, context, and environment interactions. It reviews how evolutionary computation and related search methods suit the black-box, discrete search problems posed by attacks and defenses, extending to the era of self-evolving AI agents.

entry.title: SceneFactory-3D: Lifting 2D Traffic Scenes into 3D Physical Counterfactuals for Scalable Physically Grounded Safety Evaluation

author.name: Yicheng Zhu, Linfeng Tian, Tianmu Zhao, Yang Chen, Fan Zuo, Tao Li, Zilin Bian

entry.summary: SceneFactory-3D is a GPU-batched, physics-grounded multi-agent driving simulator where vehicles execute commands via suspension- and friction-limited forces at each wheel-contact point, with spatially varying friction, 3D heightfields, gravity, and rigid contact. It lifts 2D traffic scenes into 3D physical counterfactuals to evaluate how adverse road conditions alter vehicle execution and propagate through traffic. Per-world terrain isolation enables scalable batched simulation.

entry.title: CORNAV: Construction-Aware Reasoning for Robot Navigation on Active Worksites

author.name: Parastoo Ali Pour, Deepak Prakash Kumar, Tommy Zhou, Pramod Khargonekar, Mohammad Abdullah Al Faruque

entry.summary: CORNAV is a blueprint-grounded, schedule-aware navigation framework for robots on active construction sites, using 2D CAD drawings and project schedules rather than relying solely on semantic scene understanding. It is motivated by construction labor shortages, productivity losses exceeding 1.6 trillion dollars annually, and high injury rates.

entry.title: Choosing Before Acting: Comparative Value Estimation for Long-Horizon Tool-Use Agents

author.name: Yu Li, Zheng Zhang, Xin Liu, Shengtian Yang, Guangfeng Cai, Lei Feng

entry.summary: This work argues that tool-use agents should estimate the long-horizon value of candidate tool invocations before executing them, and introduces comparative supervision over alternative invocations under the same context as the training signal. This sidesteps the weak credit assignment of final-outcome rewards and the cost of step-level human or LLM judgment. The approach targets more reliable decision-making in long-horizon agentic tasks.

entry.title: How To Train Your World Model: Fine-tuning vs RAG for LM-based World Modeling

author.name: Dhananjay Ashok, Shantanu Agarwal, Vivek Datla, Jonathan May, Alfy Samuel

entry.summary: The paper systematically compares fine-tuning and retrieval-augmented generation for LM-based world models across five text environments spanning embodied, web navigation, and social settings. Fine-tuning often outperforms RAG, with fine-tuned world models enabling higher agent rewards on 15 of 2x configurations. The study fills an evidence gap since RAG for world modeling has been underexplored despite its success elsewhere.

entry.title: Spend Teacher Tokens Where They Matter: Success-Referenced On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Xiang Chen, Futao Su, Kong Wang, Jiayi Chen, TanLin Li

entry.summary: SR-OPD reduces the cost of on-policy distillation by selectively allocating teacher supervision, using successful student rollouts as references to prioritize failed rollouts whose hidden-state trajectories show sustained divergence from the success. It also accounts for estimated teacher-input cost when selecting prompts and rollouts to supervise.

entry.title: Harness-Aware Distillation for Small Language Model Agents

author.name: Moonseok Choi, Taehong Moon, Giung Nam, Juho Lee

entry.summary: Harness-Aware Distillation (HAD) observes that when distilling an agent into a smaller model, the surrounding harness persists, so students mainly need teacher abilities the harness cannot supply. It complements on-policy distillation with an action preference component contrasting teacher actions with and without harness information.

entry.title: RIFAR: Reliability and Forgetting-Aware Replay for Continual Robot Learning

author.name: Zirong Song, Zheng Lu, Haoran Liao, Wanqi Zhong, Yunhe Ni, Lijie Wang, Xiuying Chen

entry.summary: RIFAR combines reliability screening with drift-aware replay selection for continual robot learning, using world-action models to reconstruct past experience instead of storing full demonstrations. It addresses the problem that visually coherent rollouts may contain unrealizable actions, and that new-task adaptation can erode prior skills. The goal is lasting, transferable robot skills from continuous experience.

entry.title: Multi-Task Evolution for Zero-Shot Cross-Problem Generalization using LLMs

author.name: Zhouliang Xie, Changliang Zhou, Genghui Li, Zhenkun Wang

entry.summary: MECo is an LLM-driven multi-task evolutionary framework that maintains task-conditioned heuristic populations and uses a cross-task transfer gap to guide heuristic recombination, enabling zero-shot generalization to unseen combinatorial optimization problems. This addresses the limitation that LLM heuristic search usually requires feedback from the target problem. A comprehensive evaluation supports the cross-problem transfer claims.

entry.title: LEAP: Learning Efficient Action Proposals For LLM Agents

author.name: Zhen Xu, Qizheng Zhang, Gerry Wan, Shang Zhu, Ce Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes LEAP, which learns dedicated action proposal models for LLM agents rather than using off-the-shelf large drafters (accurate but slow) or small drafters (fast but mismatched), analyzing what determines end-to-end rollout speedups. This extends speculative execution ideas from token decoding to the action-selection phase of agent rollouts.

entry.title: How to Find and Reuse Policies for Continuous Adaptation in Lifelong Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Saptarshi Nath, Inish M. D'Souza, Antonio Carta, Soheil Kolouri, Andrea Soltoggio

entry.summary: AMSC addresses lifelong RL by finding and composing previously learned policies for new tasks, estimating task similarity online via non-parametric Wasserstein embeddings of state-action-reward samples and using sparsemax-derived weights to select and combine a variable-size policy support. This tests the hypothesis that task similarity suffices for effective transfer in continual settings.

entry.title: LiBRA: Detection-Aware Image Watermark Removal via Bidirectional Latent Optimization

author.name: Saibo Ye, Huajie Chen, Xin Guo, Le Yang, Chi Liu, Xiangyu Hu, Jingjing Guo, Tianqing Zhu

entry.summary: LiBRA is a watermark removal attack that makes image watermarks undetectable while preserving quality, fixing a failure mode of prior removal attacks that push watermarks toward inversion and thereby remain detectable. It adjusts images in latent space to conceal watermarks without unnecessary further degradation, highlighting weaknesses in watermarking schemes used for AI-image attribution.

entry.title: Learning the Latent Structure: A Feature-Centric Approach to Graph Data Augmentation

author.name: Yu Song, Zhigang Hua, Yan Xie, Bingheng Li, Jingzhe Liu, Bo Long, Jiliang Tang, Hui Liu

entry.summary: The paper proposes a feature-centric graph data augmentation framework that operates directly in embedding space rather than explicitly modifying graph structure. Using a self-supervised inverse masking process, it recovers missing structural information while avoiding the label dependence, cost, and transductivity of prior graph augmentation methods. This addresses the common problem that real-world graphs are incomplete.

entry.title: Controlling Polar Exposure to Delay Memorization in Diffusion Models

author.name: Xuanchen Wang, Heng Wang, Weidong Cai

entry.summary: The paper studies how fast optimization in diffusion models compresses the window between reaching useful sample quality and memorizing training examples, analyzed through update geometry. It proposes Quality-Gated De-whitening (QGD), which retains a fast polar-update prefix then restores fixed-gain momentum, with a random-feature analysis establishing a finite-exposure condition that delays memorization proportionally to dataset size.

entry.title: RNADyn: A Benchmark for Generating and Understanding RNA Dynamics

author.name: Yiming Huang, Lennart Bastian, Hanqun Cao, Luis Vollmers, Tolga Birdal

entry.summary: RNADynBench is a standardized RNA molecular dynamics benchmark with 2585 quality-controlled 100-ns all-atom trajectories and leakage-controlled splits. Building on it, RNADynNet is a unified model that uses a shared backbone for both trajectory generation and dynamics fingerprint extraction from a single conformer, combining coordinate denoising and single-frame-to-trajectory alignment. This addresses the scarcity of large-scale RNA dynamics data and unifies two previously separate tasks.

entry.title: PoCoFL: POlicy-COmpliant Federated Learning

author.name: Dominik Roy George, Varesh Mishra, Aysajan Abidin

entry.summary: PoCoFL is a verifiable federated learning framework that decouples FL type, policy semantics, and cryptographic realization, providing formal guarantees that clients submit policy-compliant contributions and that aggregators process them correctly. This generality addresses the fragmentation of prior verifiable-FL systems tied to specific workflows and cryptographic constructions. It strengthens trust and auditability in collaborative ML.

entry.title: Output Language Confusion under Multilingual Prompt Contamination

author.name: Riju Marwah, Ritvik Garimella, Khusham Bansal, Atishay Jain, Amit Sheth

entry.summary: The paper introduces Multilingual Distractor Interference, a lightweight protocol where factual questions are preceded by irrelevant foreign-language sentences, revealing severe metric confounds: for Llama-3.1-8B, a Hindi distractor causes 58% of correct answers to be emitted in the wrong language, breaking exact-match scoring. This mimics real multilingual deployment conditions like RAG with mixed-language passages.

entry.title: Where to Look Is Not How to Fix: Pre-Denoising Diagnostics and Modality-Dependent Control in Diffusion Composition

author.name: Fangzheng Wu, Brian Summa

entry.summary: This controlled study separates diagnosis from intervention in compositional failures of text-to-image diffusion, introducing a text-only Compositional Stress Index across SD1.5, SDXL, and SD3 text paths. A matched localization study shows embedding adapters and cross-attention interventions produce distinct outcomes, indicating modality-dependent fixes.

entry.title: UniDynamics: Event-RGB Fusion for Unified Future 4D Dynamic Scene Generation

author.name: Daikun Liu, Xin Zhan, Teng Wang, Xiaoping Wang, Changyin Sun

entry.summary: UniDynamics is a diffusion-based framework generating future 4D dynamic scenes (RGB, depth, optical flow) from a single event-RGB pair, using event streams as motion priors without long histories or control inputs. It includes an Event Latent Enhancement module for diffusion-compatible conditioning and perceptual dynamics supervision to enforce geometric and motion constraints.

entry.title: Self-Repairing Recurrent Ensembles for Real-Time Recovery from Distribution Shift

author.name: Julian Lemmel, Pedro D. Wendel Garcia, Taisuke Kobayashi, Radu Grosu

entry.summary: Presents a controller ensemble of recurrent networks, each observing a randomly masked observation subset, whose Gaussian outputs combine via sequential Kalman fusion so confident members dominate. At deployment the consensus serves as self-supervision, enabling online unsupervised recovery from sensor drift, failure, and noise-induced distribution shift.

entry.title: Learning Reflexive Behavior for Contact-Rich Manipulation

author.name: Quan Nguyen, Yunho Kim, Joonho Lee

entry.summary: The paper learns a proprioceptive reflex policy in simulation on three simple interaction primitives — spring, plane, and rail — mapping task-space commands to joint-position targets using state history. The reflex exploits contact interactions as information about local geometry, enabling compliance with environmental constraints while preserving task intent, without prescribed stiffness or force directions. This departs from standard position, hybrid force-position, and Cartesian impedance control.

entry.title: A Unified Framework for Empowerment and Predictive Control

author.name: Wooyoung Chung, Tristan Shah, Volodymyr Makarenko, Stas Tiomkin

entry.summary: This paper unifies empowerment — a goal-agnostic objective derived from the channel capacity between agent inputs and future states — with sampling-based model predictive control. It addresses two limitations of prior empowerment controllers: the disconnect between virtual probing policies and executed behavior, and the computational cost of empowerment estimation.

entry.title: DeReAct: Decomposed Reasoning and Acting for Reliable AI Agents

author.name: Ajay Vohra, Tao Chen, Neeti Narayan, Caron Zhang

entry.summary: DeReAct is a modular agent architecture that externalizes gating policies from a single LLM policy: a Critic validates proposed actions before execution and a Context Manager reconstructs environment-supported state and certifies completion. On GAIA and SWE-bench Verified it improves Pass@1 most for weaker base models, with 6.5-7.0 point gains for Qwen3-Coder-480B. The design targets error propagation and unsupported completion claims in ReAct-style agents.

entry.title: Learning to Revise Reasoning with Segment-wise On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Yuxiang Zhang, Ding Cao, Shuting Cui, Lei Wang, Weijieying Ren, Tianxiang Zhao

entry.summary: This work extends token-wise on-policy distillation to segment-wise supervision that provides coherent alternative reasoning steps showing how a student's intermediate step should be revised. It also tackles the degenerate-prefix problem where teacher supervision conditioned on a poor reasoning prefix may reinforce bad patterns, using controlled reasoning interventions for analysis.

entry.title: Reliable Self-Evolution with Imperfect Proxy Rewards

author.name: Kangjun Noh, Soyu Kim, Kyungwoo Song

entry.summary: CISE makes LLM-based self-evolving search robust to imperfect proxy rewards by constructing candidate-specific reward intervals via conditional conformal inference and iteration-wise online density-ratio estimation, preventing false positives from contaminating outputs and feedback. It targets scientific discovery settings where full-fidelity evaluation is prohibitively expensive.

entry.title: Personalized Automatic Speech Recognition for a Dysarthric and Tracheostomic Speaker using Artificial Conversations

author.name: David Nadrchal, Monorama Swain, Florian Schmid, Gerhard Widmer, Paul Primus

entry.summary: The authors build a personalized ASR system for a Czech speaker with a tracheostomy and severe dysarthria, releasing a 33-hour annotated dataset collected via a novel artificial conversation protocol. A multi-stage Whisper Base fine-tuning pipeline achieves a 50% relative reduction in character error rate. The work demonstrates practical accessibility impact for extremely low-resource speech.

entry.title: Jumping the Line: Exploiting Length Predictions in LLM Scheduling

author.name: Yuyang Dai, Rana Shahout, Mahmood Sharif

entry.summary: The paper introduces JIL, an attack on prediction-based LLM serving schedulers that uses adversarial suffixes to make length-prediction probes underestimate a request's output length, thereby gaming shortest-job-first prioritization. Evaluations across two datasets, four LLMs, and varied deployment configurations show substantial reductions in predicted lengths and completion times for the attacker.

entry.title: MIRROR: Multipath Quorum Integrity for LLM Multi-Agent Communication

author.name: Ryuichi Yamafuji Lun, Jingzhen Wang, Shreyas Kolte, Ruiteng Li

entry.summary: MIRROR defends LLM multi-agent systems against agent-in-the-middle attacks, which manipulate messages in transit without compromising agents, by replicating a canonicalized payload across k logical routes and accepting only strict-majority-consistent messages. It avoids the inference cost and false-blocking of semantic validation and the TLS-termination blind spot of transport-layer encryption. This opens a new communication-layer security perspective for multi-agent AI.

entry.title: Out of Sync, Out of Sight: Phantom State Attacks against IIoT Intrusion Detection

author.name: Sabrine Ennaji, Elhadj Benkhelifa, Nadia Kabachi

entry.summary: Introduces phantom state attacks that exploit temporal synchronization assumptions in ML-based industrial IoT intrusion detection systems, which reconstruct operational state by aggregating telemetry into time windows. The attacks reshape packet timing to manipulate the detector's windowed view without gradient access, model queries, or mimicking a learned benign model.

entry.title: Test-time Calibration Learning for Large Language Model Reasoning

author.name: Zizhuo Zhang, Xiong Peng, Jingwei Sun, Rong Yao, Shixiong Kai, Mingxuan Yuan, Bo Han

entry.summary: Proposes Test-Time Calibration Learning, which adapts LLM confidence calibration at inference time without ground-truth labels, addressing the limitation of prior RL-based calibration approaches that require labeled correctness supervision. Reliable verbalized confidence is essential for real-world deployment and decision-making under uncertainty.

entry.title: Distributionally Robust Survival Models under Subpopulation Shift and Outlier Contamination

author.name: Seonghwi Kim, Sung Ho Jo, Minwoo Chae

entry.summary: This paper proposes a distributionally robust framework for survival analysis that jointly handles latent subpopulation shift and outlier contamination via a minimax formulation: an outer minimization refines the nominal distribution by down-weighting contaminated samples while an inner maximization targets the worst-case subpopulation. This directly addresses models that perform well on average but poorly on minority subgroups.

entry.title: From Behavior to Provenance: Attributing Tabular Foundation Models to Synthetic Pretraining Data

author.name: Mohamed Bouadi, Nassim Bouarour, Shivam Dubey, Aditya Tanna, Vinay Kumar Sankarapu

entry.summary: This work makes training-data attribution experimentally testable by using a provenance-rich synthetic task generator with full lineage over mechanisms like missingness, confounding, and distribution shift. It combines behavior-conditioned attribution with counterfactual retraining and provenance-aware interventions to test task-level faithfulness and mechanism-level consistency for tabular foundation models. This provides a rare ground-truth testbed for attribution claims.

entry.title: Online Verification of Language Model Responses Under Cost Constraints

author.name: Erfan Hajihashemi, Yanning Shen

entry.summary: The paper addresses online verification of LLM multi-step reasoning outputs where ground-truth oracles are costly. Rather than relying on a single fixed weak verifier to gate strong-verifier queries, it develops methods for combining multiple verifiers under cost constraints as query difficulty and subject matter drift over time. This improves reliability at scale for deployed reasoning systems.

entry.title: LatticeSMC: Where to Spend Inference-Time Compute in Chunked Sequence Generators

author.name: Xuanchen Wang, Heng Wang, Weidong Cai

entry.summary: LatticeSMC formulates inference-time steering of chunk-by-chunk generators (music, motion, video) as Feynman-Kac sequential Monte Carlo on a two-dimensional lattice of chunk index and denoising step. Under budget-matched comparisons, telescoping results show chunk-additive rewards induce identical weights across axes, clarifying where resampling compute should be spent.

entry.title: Sample complexity of variance-reduced policy gradient: weaker assumptions and lower bounds

author.name: Gabor Paczolay, Matteo Papini, Alberto Maria Metelli, Istvan Harmati, Marcello Restelli

entry.summary: This theory paper proposes a Defensive Policy Gradient algorithm achieving O(epsilon^-3) sample complexity for variance-reduced REINFORCE without unrealistic variance assumptions on importance weights. It also establishes matching lower bounds of Theta(epsilon^-4) and Theta(epsilon^-3) in a generalized black-box policy-optimization model with hidden states and actions.

entry.title: Causal Representation Learning with Instantaneous and Lagged Relations via Nonstationarity

author.name: Tatsuya Yamada, Hiroshi Morioka, Yoshinobu Kawahara

entry.summary: The authors establish sufficient conditions for identifying latent states and their instantaneous and lagged causal structures in nonstationary time series, up to component permutation and component-wise invertible transformations, using an observed auxiliary variable. This fills a gap in jointly handling mixed-lag causal relations and nonstationarity.

entry.title: Forecasting from Counterfactual Simulator Rollouts: A Sim2Real Evaluation

author.name: Angel Wang, Dominique Perrault-Joncas, Alvaro Maggiar, Dean Foster, Carson Eisenach

entry.summary: This paper evaluates using simulator rollouts of a new decision policy to train prediction models that face a cold-start problem, since historical data reflects older policies. Using two real-world inventory-control deployments, the authors assess simulator fidelity, zero-shot transfer to reality, and backtesting of the sim2real-trained model against real observations. It offers rare empirical evidence on when simulator-based forecasting actually transfers to deployment.

entry.title: Learning Query Encoders Can Be Hard Even When Vector Retrieval Is Geometrically Easy

author.name: Anders Wikum, Nina Mishra, Amin Saberi, Tal Wagner

entry.summary: This paper studies a new notion of geometric capacity for vector retrieval: the maximum recall achievable for a frozen document index. It shows empirically that single-vector query encoders often fall far below what document indices can support, and provides theoretical analysis of when learned query encoders can or cannot reach this ceiling.

entry.title: Predictively Oriented Gaussian Process Posteriors

author.name: Callum Lau, Jeremias Knoblauch, Louis Sharrock

entry.summary: PrO-GPs treat predictive uncertainty, rather than fit to latent function values, as the primary inferential target of Gaussian process modeling, providing robustness to kernel and observation-model misspecification. The authors derive a reduced formulation and practical sampling scheme making computation tractable for nonparametric models. Empirical results on synthetic and real data support improved robustness over standard GPs.

entry.title: Beyond Correctness: Resolving Underspecification in Agentic Text-to-SQL

author.name: Wen-Zhi Li, Yue Gong, Konstantinos Kanellis, Balakrishnan Murali Narayanaswamy

entry.summary: This paper shows that in agentic text-to-SQL, a correct execution result can mask unverified assumptions about underspecified user queries, partly due to premature termination of clarification. Ambiguities concentrate in early turns, so forced extra questions are inefficient, and agents often abandon clarifications they had already identified, motivating better clarification planning.

entry.title: Structured Composition of Verifiable Atomic Insights for Table-to-Report Generation

author.name: Teng Lin, Xinyu Liu, Nan Tang

entry.summary: This paper tackles table-to-report generation by systematically discovering verifiable composite insights across tables, attributes, and analytical perspectives, organizing them into traceable evidence chains rather than relying on reactive data agents that suffer from exploration bias. The structured composition approach aims for coherent, complete, and verifiable analytical reports.

entry.title: EmbPASS: Towards Cross-Embodiment Open Panoramic Segmentation

author.name: Pujun Guo, Yuanfan Zheng, Fei Teng, Mengfei Duan, Guoqiang Zhao, Yuheng Zhang, Kai Luo, Kailun Yang

entry.summary: The paper introduces cross-embodiment open panoramic segmentation as a new task, with EmbPASS, a multi-platform benchmark spanning vehicle, drone, wearable, and quadruped platforms under a unified semantic taxonomy. It targets consistent panoramic perception despite heterogeneous viewpoints and spatial layouts across embodied platforms.

entry.title: Fed-ADApt: Federated Anytime Depth Adaptation for Resource-Aware Medical Image Segmentation

author.name: Abhijeet Parida, Zhifan Jiang, Pooneh Roshanitabrizi, Austin Tapp, Maria J. Ledesma-Carbayo, Syed Muhammad Anwar, Ziyue Xu, Marius George Linguraru, Holger R. Roth

entry.summary: Fed-ADApt is a depth-adaptive federated learning framework for UNet-based medical image segmentation that lets each participating site train according to its local compute budget via multi-depth supervision and hierarchical depth-wise aggregation, with dynamic depth selection at inference. It was evaluated on multi-site retinal fundus and 3D brain tumor segmentation tasks, broadening FL participation to low-resource institutions.

entry.title: HexVIO: Towards All-Day Stereo-Inertial Tracking Through Commodity DSPs

author.name: Patrick Wolf, Mateo de Mayo, Daniel Cremers

entry.summary: Proposes HexVIO, which offloads the visual frontend of a stereo-inertial odometry system to the Hexagon DSP found in many smartphones and XR devices while keeping the backend on the CPU. This improves efficiency for robots, wearables, XR devices, and drones, enabling cooler, lighter devices with better battery life and all-day tracking.

entry.title: LLA-MPC on Embedded Hardware: Rapid Adaptive Control with Thousands of Parallel Models

author.name: Henry Z. Liao, Maitham F. AL-Sunni, John M. Dolan

entry.summary: This work generalizes LLA-MPC, a learning-free adaptive MPC framework, from a fixed-structure simulation-only racing demo to modular dynamics validated on the physical F1TENTH platform. It identifies tire parameters online by evaluating thousands of candidate models in real time on embedded hardware, completing high-speed tracking on low-friction, changing surfaces where a fixed nominal model fails.

entry.title: MintFlow: Minimal Trajectory Intervention for Constrained Flow Matching

author.name: Yesom Park, Kelvin Kan, Qifan Chen, Thomas Flynn, Hayden Schaeffer. Xihaier Luo

entry.summary: MintFlow is a training-free framework for constrained sampling in flow matching models that treats constraint enforcement as a minimal intervention on the pretrained flow trajectory. It finds the smallest perturbation of an intermediate flow state so the subsequent evolution satisfies constraints like physical laws or measurements. This addresses the common trade-off where enforcing constraints displaces samples far from the pretrained data distribution.

entry.title: Learning What to Investigate Next: Meta-Reasoning for Long-Horizon Research Agents

author.name: Ankur Samanta, Yonathan Efroni, Paul Sajda, Kaveh Hassani, Anirudh Goyal

entry.summary: MIRA is a hierarchical architecture for long-horizon research agents that separates allocation from execution: an outer-loop meta-reasoner curates context from a persistent research record and writes work orders, while a fresh inner-loop executor performs each investigation. Without policy training, MIRA improves long-horizon inference. It addresses sparse decision points and delayed consequences in extended research traces.

entry.title: Decoupling Memory from Context: Structured Memory for Token-Efficient Test-Time Continual Learning

author.name: Yehya Farhat, Michael Desmond, Anastasios Kyrillidis

entry.summary: This paper proposes structured memory decoupled from context for test-time continual learning, addressing the token cost growth and context-window limits of approaches that continually append information to shared context. It enables agents to carry forward useful experience across interactions without costly trial-and-error context engineering at inference time.

entry.title: VIGOR: Zero-Shot Visual Generalization via Latent-Space Consistency in Model-Based Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Mingyu Park, Samyeul Noh, Hyun Myung, Donghwan Lee

entry.summary: VIGOR tackles the fragility of model-based RL under unseen visual distractions by enforcing latent-space consistency, addressing a two-level vulnerability where encoder errors compound through recursive latent rollouts. It enables zero-shot generalization to background, lighting, and camera changes while preserving sample efficiency.

entry.title: PLCWorld: Benchmarking LLM-Generated PLC Programs in Closed-Loop Plant Simulation

author.name: Yunji Kim, Yunseok Lee, Hyunwoo Seo, Jaerim Choi, Woojin Lee

entry.summary: PLCWorld introduces a closed-loop benchmark that evaluates LLM-generated programmable logic controller programs by simulating plant responses and sensor feedback, rather than checking code statically. It includes 100 synthetic tasks and 473 task-condition pairs across motion control and material handling. This fills a real gap in safety-critical industrial code evaluation.

entry.title: Toward Controlling Biology with Language:Offline Learning of Prompt-Conditioned Interventions for Cells, Organoids, and Biobots

author.name: Nam H. Le, Douglas Blackiston, Michael Levin, Josh Bongard

entry.summary: This paper explores using language models as a natural-language interface to biological interventions, learning a prompt-conditioned mapping from archived intervention-outcome datasets using a vision-language model as a judge, avoiding new wet-lab experiments. Authored by prominent figures including Michael Levin and Josh Bongard, it targets cells, organoids, and biobots. The work is a forward-looking step toward language-controllable living systems with implications for synthetic biology.

entry.title: Efficient Neural Field Learning via Adaptive Coverage and Focused Sampling

author.name: Guang Zhao, Xihaier Luo, Huan-Hsin Tseng, Seungjun Lee, Shinjae Yoo, Yihui Ren, Wei Xu

entry.summary: Proposes ACES, a sampling framework for training implicit neural representations that decouples domain coverage from sample importance using adaptive spatial partitions and region-level importance, mitigating redundancy from point-level high-error sampling. This improves training efficiency for modeling high-dimensional continuous fields.

entry.title: Instance-Dependent Regret for CMDPs with Step-Wise Constraints

author.name: Qian Zuo, Francesco Emanuele Stradi, Leyang Xue, Sattar Vakili

entry.summary: Proposes Safe Variance-Adaptive Exploration (SVAE) for episodic tabular constrained MDPs with step-wise safety constraints, learning candidate safe subgraphs and performing variance-adaptive optimistic planning within them. Achieves instance-dependent cumulative regret bounds exploiting the structure that constraints induce on reward variance.

entry.title: Generalization Properties of Score-matching Diffusion Models for Intrinsically Low-dimensional Data

author.name: Saptarshi Chakraborty, Quentin Berthet, Peter L. Bartlett

entry.summary: Provides finite-sample statistical generalization guarantees for flow-matching generative models in Wasserstein-p distance, explicitly accounting for intrinsic low-dimensional structure in real data such as natural images and molecular geometries. The analysis avoids restrictive assumptions on the estimated velocity field that limited prior work.

entry.title: When Can We Trust the Matching Principle? Robust Deployment Geometry Under Finite-Sample and Model Uncertainty

author.name: Vishal Rajput

entry.summary: This paper quantifies when spectral matching of model representations is reliable, introducing a trust ratio that compares estimation uncertainty to spectral separation and proving oracle-relative drift scales quadratically with it in the Davis-Kahan regime. It then proposes Confidence-Calibrated Matching, a policy that switches between directional matching and isotropic penalty spreading depending on the trust ratio, validated empirically.

entry.title: Beyond Single Videos: Benchmarking and Active Evidence Seeking for E-Commerce Cross-Video Reasoning

author.name: Jinghan Zhao, Yiman Hu, Liang Wu, Jian Xu, Bo Zheng

entry.summary: AdsCVR is the first e-commerce cross-video reasoning benchmark with 2,483 videos and 6,110 QA pairs across six reasoning dimensions, requiring models to locate fine-grained evidence across many videos. The accompanying AdSeek framework is an agentic method that dynamically selects visual and audio tools during multi-turn exploration instead of static single-pass processing.

entry.title: Mapping and Advancing the Scalability-Accuracy Frontier of Nonlinear Causal Discovery

author.name: Hendrik Suhr, Sascha Xu, Jilles Vreeken

entry.summary: This paper empirically compares four major algorithmic families for scalable nonlinear causal discovery: differentiable structure learning, amortized structure learning, score-matching, and combinatorial search. The authors find complementary bottlenecks — differentiable and amortized methods scale well but lag in accuracy, score-matching degrades with feature count, and combinatorial methods stay accurate but slow due to redundant computation — and propose improvements based on these insights. The work matters because it provides a systematic map of the accuracy-runtime trade-off space in a field where method comparisons have been fragmented.

entry.title: State-Space Unlearning for Non-Stationary Bias in Land Surface Forecasting

author.name: Anidipta Pal

entry.summary: SSU-LSF introduces the first machine-unlearning framework for Mamba-family state space models in geoscientific forecasting, where non-stationary confounders like irrigation booms or sensor recalibrations get absorbed into state-transition matrices and silently bias predictions. It develops EKFac influence functions specialized to Mamba state matrices with closed-form matrix-exponential gradients, plus spectral-radius-weighted thresholding to localize the confounding footprint. This addresses unlearning for a model class where standard influence methods do not directly apply.

entry.title: Does Every User Need a Private LoRA? Decoupling Personalization from Per-User Adaptation

author.name: Songyuan Sui, Srikanth Malla, Chiho Choi, Joon Hee Choi

entry.summary: The paper revisits per-user LoRA adapters for personalized LLMs, finding that independent user adapters contain substantial cross-user reusable structure and that user histories support compact individual corrections. It proposes allocating personalization capacity between shared and user-specific components, improving scalability as user populations grow. This challenges the default one-adapter-per-user paradigm.

entry.title: LiteEMG-FM: An Efficient and Deployable Foundation Model for Robust EMG Sensing

author.name: Tianhao Wu, Xu Wu, Amirmohammad Radmehr, Jiawei Yu, Yi Wu, Phuc Nguyen, Jian Liu

entry.summary: LiteEMG-FM is a hybrid CNN-Transformer foundation model pretrained on 16 upper- and lower-limb EMG datasets to generalize across users, sessions, and hardware for wearable sensing. It includes a hierarchical wake-up architecture where an always-on lightweight model triggers a larger model only when needed, enabling real-time deployment on resource-constrained devices. This matters for assistive devices and human-computer interaction applications.

entry.title: Differential Privacy of Gradient Descent on Perturbed Objectives

author.name: Austin Watkins, Raman Arora

entry.summary: This theory paper analyzes the differential privacy of releasing finite iterates of gradient descent on an objective-perturbed empirical risk, where a single Gaussian perturbation is drawn before optimization. The authors prove that the map from the noise vector to the iterate is a C1-diffeomorphism under strongly convex, smooth objectives, enabling a direct change-of-variables privacy analysis of the finite iterate.

entry.title: Constraint-Aware Training

author.name: Jinwoo Kim

entry.summary: This paper examines constrained decoding for code-generating language models, where program analyses filter out tokens that violate syntax or typing rules at inference time. It asks whether such filtering can be externalized from training, defining a general constraint-aware objective and formalizing benefits via three theorems about model size and data requirements.

entry.title: Objects Without Morphisms: What LLMs for Mathematics Do Not Represent

author.name: Yanli Wang, Suijin Wang, Xiaopeng Yuan, Haohan Wang
