entry.summary: The paper probes whether LLMs genuinely represent mathematical structure, testing translation between dialects of neighboring mathematical subfields where fidelity requires inferring the implicit level of generality. Introducing an instrument that codes translation truth, it argues that search-augmented expert-level competition performance masks missing structural representation.

entry.title: A Path Integral Surrogate for Multi-Step Gradient Inversion in Federated Learning

author.name: Agnivo Ghosh, Saumik Bhattacharya

entry.summary: This paper addresses gradient inversion attacks in federated learning, where an adversary tries to reconstruct a client's private training images from shared model updates. Under FedAvg, multi-step local training hides the weight trajectory between two endpoints, and the authors propose a path integral surrogate that reads gradients along the full hidden path rather than at a single point. This advances understanding of privacy leakage in federated settings and motivates stronger defenses.

entry.title: Generalizable single-cell perturbation response prediction using energy-guided flow matching

author.name: Jianan Wei, Jiajun Hong, Guikun Chen, Ning Yang, Lifeng Fan, Wenguan Wang

entry.summary: scEGFlow is an energy-guided flow matching framework for predicting single-cell perturbation responses that models continuous transitions from control to perturbed cell populations. Condition-specific energy gradients steer and correct predictions at inference time without retraining, addressing the fixed-mapping limitation of prior methods under distribution shift and novel perturbations. This improves generalization in a biologically important prediction task.

entry.title: Flow Matching for Fast Posterior Sampling in Bayesian Inverse Problems

author.name: Jan Blechschmidt, Oliver G. Ernst, Moritz Poguntke, Bj\"orn Sprungk

entry.summary: This paper evaluates conditional flow matching as an amortized alternative to MCMC for sampling posteriors in PDE-based Bayesian inverse problems with function-valued parameters. It derives computable accuracy estimates using the flow's tractable density, providing an MCMC-literate error analysis for approximate posterior samples produced at negligible online cost.

entry.title: RMCW: A Deletion-Robust Watermark Based on Reed--Muller Codes for Language Models

author.name: Yi Wang, Baicheng Chen, Yu Wang, Jian Zhao, Yilei Chen, Tianxing He

entry.summary: RMCW is an LLM watermarking scheme based on Reed-Muller codes designed to survive deletion attacks, which shift token positions and break watermark alignment. It detects surviving local algebraic structure via affine-line restrictions of codewords rather than global codeword recovery, improving robustness under post-processing attacks.

entry.title: ParaGeo: Decomposing Paralinguistic Variation into a Shared Latent Geometry

author.name: Yuhan Liu, Yuxuan Ou, Ruoxi Su, Mohamed Ahmed Zaki, Yunbo Long

entry.summary: ParaGeo probes how paralinguistic attributes (emotion, delivery style) are represented in a frozen speech language model by replaying matched content with fixed prompts and projecting pooled K/V representations into a shared low-dimensional space. Using a GLM-4-Voice probe across 80 control attributes, it shows content-held-out centroid accuracy far above permutation baselines, indicating a shared geometric organization of paralinguistic variation. This provides interpretability insight into how speech models encode speaker intent independent of content.

entry.title: When Is Accuracy Evidence? A Unified Theory of Generalisation, Validation, and Information Fusion

author.name: JM Gorriz

entry.summary: The paper generalizes Cross Upper-Bound Validation through a single exponential framework controlled by a cumulant envelope, yielding a family of risk bounds covering Hoeffding, Bernstein, dependency-aware, PAC-Bayesian, and heterogeneous source-fusion settings. It models dependence between K-fold CV fold-wise gaps via a joint sub-Gaussian proxy matrix, addressing the common misuse of cross-validation as evidence of out-of-sample performance. This is a substantive contribution to validation theory.

entry.title: From Mixing to Tearing: Graph Decomposition in Decentralized Optimization via Message Passing

author.name: Kuangyu Ding, Gesualdo Scutari

entry.summary: This paper develops a first-principles framework for decentralized optimization over undirected graphs, jointly designing local optimization subproblems and the communication scheme via graph decomposition, moving beyond the standard mixing/aggregation view of gossip and spanning-tree methods. It targets smooth strongly convex minimization where each agent holds one function and communicates only with neighbors.

entry.title: OmniConfess: Eliciting Token Confessions to Mitigate Omni-Modal Hallucination

author.name: Huiqiang Rong, Haoran Luo, Hui Feng, Zhonghong Ou, Kaiwen Xue, Guoxin Zhang, Yifan Zhu

entry.summary: OmniConfess is a training-free method for omni-modal hallucination mitigation that re-scores a candidate response at token resolution under channel-wise evidence interventions, producing a token-by-channel confession of which modality sustained each commitment. The confession is then used to preserve grounded content and revise commitments backed by irrelevant or contradictory evidence.

entry.title: Hindsight-Guided Rationale Distillation for Rare Disease Diagnosis

author.name: Aarav Singh, Animesh Pathak, Navyansh Singh

entry.summary: The paper fine-tunes a 1.5B student on chain-of-thought traces from an 8B teacher that sees the ground-truth diagnosis during generation, and finds that only the contamination-filtered student variant beats the teacher, with gains concentrated in well-represented diseases. It identifies a GT hallucination artifact in label-visible generation and shows filtering, not hindsight distillation itself, drives the improvement.

entry.title: A Simulation-Grounded Agentic VLM Framework for Wildfire Monitoring and Reporting

author.name: Duowen Chen, Yuchen Sun, Zhiqi Li, Yuxuan Liao, Sinan Wang, Bart van Bloemen Waanders, Bo Zhu

entry.summary: Presents a framework that converts 2D wildfire simulations into labeled video episodes via a fixed Blender mapping and controllable video generation, building a reusable multimodal memory for a training-free multi-agent VLM system that relates visual evidence to fire physics. The approach sidesteps the scarcity of real wildfire videos with synchronized physical annotations.

entry.title: A Benchmark for Spatially Grounded Gesture Generation

author.name: Anna Deichler, Rishabh Dabral, Fethiye Irmak Dogan, Anindita Ghosh, Jonas Beskow

entry.summary: The authors introduce a benchmark for spatially grounded gesture generation with roughly 2K pointing-annotated clips from naturalistic VR dialogue and ground-truth 3D referents. It defines a task where systems decide when, how, and where to point during speech, with a protocol separating temporal alignment from spatial grounding.

entry.title: LAS-CLIP: A Lightweight Adapter Steering Approach for CLIP's Visual Encoder

author.name: Anh-Khoa Dinh-Duc, Duc-Tai Dinh, Tam V. Nguyen, Minh-Triet Tran

entry.summary: LAS-CLIP adds a compact MaskAdapter (116K-145K parameters) that injects per-head attention biases into a fully frozen CLIP visual encoder to enable region-level tasks without compromising pre-trained representations. Because the backbone is untouched, the model reverts to vanilla CLIP behavior when no mask is provided, preserving zero-shot capabilities.

entry.title: Event-guided Neural Video Compression

author.name: Jiyun Kong, Jungwoo Kim, Enes Eray Demirtas, Touradj Ebrahimi, Jong-Seok Lee

entry.summary: Proposes ENVC, a neural video codec that exploits event-camera streams shared between encoder and decoder to improve RGB compression. It uses an event-guided motion prior plus coded motion residual for motion coding, and an event-conditioned predictor with gated temporal context refinement for frame coding, with synthesized RGB-event pairs for training on standard datasets.

entry.title: Who Went Where When on the Lunar Surface: Forensic Trajectory Analysis to Identify Byzantine Rovers

author.name: Lachlan Holden, Feras Dayoub, Melissa de Zwart, David Harvey, Tat-Jun Chin

entry.summary: This robotics paper introduces the problem of forensic trajectory analysis for non-cooperative planetary rovers, including Byzantine agents that submit falsified or miscalibrated telemetry to disguise their true paths. The work addresses post-hoc reconstruction of rover trajectories from sparse data such as odometry, pose priors, and relative detections, in order to verify compliance with constraints like Lunar Safety Zones when multiple rovers share a deployment region. It notes that standard outlier-robust pose graph optimization is insufficient in this adversarial setting, motivating new robust estimation techniques for space mission assurance.

entry.title: MATS × CG Pitch Week: What Happened, What We Learned

author.name: Patryk Wielopolski

entry.summary: A retrospective writeup of the first MATS x Coefficient Giving Pitch Week in Q2 2026, a four-week program taking AI safety researchers from early idea to a funding decision. Of 15 teams that pitched, six received grants totaling $4.3M, and the authors report that funding success correlated with idea maturity and evaluability (named first user, concrete deliverable, bounded scope, feasibility evidence) rather than observable founder characteristics. This matters because it documents an experimental new funding pipeline for AI safety org-building and shares transferable lessons about what funders look for.

entry.title: FSPO: Policy-Consistent Risk and Pareto-Feasible Control for Budgeted LLM RL Post-Training

author.name: Miaobo Hu, Shuhao Hu, Xiaobo Guo, Xin Wang, Bokun Wang, Daren Zha, Jun Xiao

entry.summary: FSPO introduces a feedback-state controller for budgeted RL post-training of LLMs that jointly handles online tuning of rollout temperature, group size, clipping, KL regularization, and verifier allocation. It learns a policy-consistent risk-to-go model and certifies Pareto-feasible multi-resource continuations, addressing miscalibration under selective action choice.

entry.title: SoftGene: Protein Language Model-Enhanced Soft Prompting for Interpretable Gene Set Annotation

author.name: Drew Ross, Arya Hadizadeh Moghaddam, Dongjie Wang, Xiaoyu Zhang, Zijun Yao

entry.summary: SoftGene combines a protein language model (ESM) encoder with LLM soft prompting to annotate gene sets, capturing protein sequence structure that symbolic gene-name approaches miss. The hierarchical attention-based encoder represents gene sets informed by molecular activity and interactions. This aims to reduce manual curation burden in functional genomics.

entry.title: Optimal Planning in a Dynamic World

author.name: Devin Wild Thomas (University of New Hampshire, USA), Solomon Eyal Shimony (Ben-Gurion University of the Negev, Israel), Wheeler Ruml (University of New Hampshire, USA), Erez Karpas (Technion - Israel Institute of Technology, Israel), Shahaf S. Shperberg (Ben-Gurion University of the Negev, Israel), Andrew Coles (King's College London, UK)

entry.summary: This paper addresses classical planning when feasible states or actions change over time - such as path planning among moving obstacles - and the execution start time is unknown until planning completes. It analyzes how optimal plans and their durations depend on start timing, filling a gap where prior work assumes known start times or ignores dynamism. The author group includes established heuristic search researchers.

entry.title: NeutronGym: Physics-Graded Neutron Instrument Design for LLM Agents

author.name: Lijie Ding, Changwoo Do

entry.summary: NeutronGym is the first executable environment for neutron instrument design, where agents build instruments via validating tools, McStas ray-tracing simulates results, and a level-resolved ladder grades syntax, runtime, structure, and science without any LLM judge. Seven evaluated models solve at most 7 of 16 McStasBench tasks drawn from published instruments, revealing large gaps between reciting and doing physics.

entry.title: RxnOptBench: Benchmarking LLMs for Reaction-Condition Optimization in Organic Methodology

author.name: Lingli Ge, Yubin Wang, Junyuan Gao, Jiahe Song, Jiaxing Sun, Boyu Zhu, Haote Yang, Jingchao Wang, Lixin Ma, Jiang Wu, Yuqiang Li, Conghui He

entry.summary: RxnOptBench benchmarks LLMs on chemical reaction-condition optimization, requiring models to read real condition-screening tables from 2025 organic-methodology papers and select the best catalyst, solvent, temperature, and other settings. Every option is a genuine wet-lab entry scored by a continuous relative yield/stereoselectivity metric. It fills a real gap between chemistry benchmarks that test labeling or SMILES manipulation and actual judgement-laden optimization.

entry.title: DAGS: Disentangled Appearance-and-Geometry Steering of a Frozen Image DiT for Temporally Stabilized Generative Rendering

author.name: Karthik Mohan Kumar, Damian Andrysiak, Pedro Antonio Pena, Kunal Tyagi, Rama Harihara

entry.summary: Proposes DAGS, a lightweight attention-free conditioning scheme that steers a frozen image diffusion transformer via disentangled appearance and geometry features injected as per-layer element-wise residuals, avoiding quadratic attention cost. Targets high-fidelity, faithful, independently controllable renders with temporal stabilization for generative rendering.

entry.title: Predicting Steering Vectors and Adapter Weights for Few-Shot Author-Style Transfer

author.name: Leonard Popp, Danni Liu, Supriti Sinhamahapatra, Jan Niehues

entry.summary: The paper studies style-conditioned abstract generation from a few examples per author, comparing contrastive activation steering, a network that predicts steering vectors, and a hypernetwork that predicts LoRA adapters. It finds a consistent trade-off between style imitation and quality, with the hypernetwork achieving the best balance while fine-tuning gains style at the cost of fluency.

entry.title: Single or Multiple Policies for Phase-Structured Reinforcement Learning?

author.name: Guilhem Loussouarn, Nancy Nayak, Kin K. Leung

entry.summary: This work analyzes phase-structured RL problems, clarifying when a single state-augmented policy can theoretically match any multi-policy solution and yet when multiple policies outperform a shared one in practice. It resolves previously unexplained empirical advantages of multi-policy approaches for non-stationary but structured problems.

entry.title: Rethinking What to Cache in Few-Step Diffusion Transformers: Solver-Aware Target Selection

author.name: Shuo Yang, Lihao Fang, Yi Zhang, Haixiang Wang, Xincheng Ye, Shufan Chen, Jipeng Guo, Youqing Wang

entry.summary: The paper presents AutoTarget, a method that adaptively selects which tensor to cache in few-step diffusion transformer sampling, accounting for the larger inter-step gaps introduced by step distillation. Using a small calibration set, it chooses cache targets suited to a given model, solver, and reuse schedule, reducing error versus fixed caching choices. This improves the efficiency of image and video diffusion inference.

entry.title: MuLoRA: Spectrally Balanced Low-Rank Adaptation for Continual Learning

author.name: Junkang Liu

entry.summary: This paper identifies spectral plasticity collapse, where sequential LoRA adaptation concentrates update energy in a few singular modes and wastes available low-rank capacity. MuLoRA jointly controls capacity allocation and utilization using historical whitening and spectrally balanced updates. The finding that protecting old representations does not guarantee usable capacity for new tasks is a useful reframing of continual LoRA limitations.

entry.title: Prompted to Discriminate: Generalizing Malicious-Input Probes in the Wild

author.name: Elad David, Max Fomin

entry.summary: This paper examines whether appending a classification-instruction suffix before reading activation probes for prompt injection, jailbreaks, and unsafe requests actually helps, especially on attack types unseen in training. It tests whether the LLM-as-judge-style prompting trick generalizes to the in-the-wild regime that deployed monitors face. This addresses a practical question for runtime safety monitoring.

entry.title: Autoregressive Differentiable Method for Integer Programming

author.name: Ouns El Harzli, Yudong Cao

entry.summary: The authors train a transformer to solve 0-1 integer programs autoregressively by predicting binary variables in a fixed order while staying in the feasible set. Training combines feasible incumbents from conventional solvers, a Lagrangian penalty for infeasibility, and Gumbel-softmax exploration of the relaxed objective. On dense non-convex quadratic knapsack instances, the method consistently beats state-of-the-art open-source solvers.

entry.title: Toward Omni Multimodal Graph Foundation Model: A Topology-Driven Binding Approach

author.name: Xunkai Li, Chenxi Wan, Yinlin Zhu, Wang Luo, Hongchao Qin, Rong-Hua Li, Guoren Wang

entry.summary: GraphBind is a topology-driven multimodal graph foundation model that uses graph topology as a structural reference to bind heterogeneous modality information into a unified shared space, addressing incomplete node attributes in real-world multimodal-attributed graphs. It aims to improve pretraining scale and generalization where attribute data is sparse.

entry.title: When Does Synthetic Relational Data Teach Models to Use Relations? Tracing Predictive Structure from Pretraining Data to Model Behavior

author.name: Shivam Dubey, Mohamed Bouadi, Nassim Bouarour, Varun Kulkarni, Aditya Tanna, Vinay Kumar Sankarapu

entry.summary: This data-attribution study asks which properties of synthetic pretraining corpora cause relational foundation models to actually learn relational computation rather than exploiting row-level statistics. Using four Relational Transformer checkpoints trained on corpora from different generators under matched compute, it traces a measurable data property to learned computation and downstream behavior.

entry.title: ZeroMAG: Zero-Shot Multimodal Adapter Generation for Plug-and-Play EEG Foundation Models

author.name: Yubo Wang, Jingying Ma, Xinliang Zhou, Yangxuan Zhou, Jiquan Wang, Sha Zhao, Yiyuan Yang, Yi Ding, Ziyu Jia, Chenyu Liu, Cuntai Guan

entry.summary: ZeroMAG generates multimodal adapters for frozen EEG foundation models in a zero-shot manner, using unlabeled target recordings and companion physiological signals without target labels or target-side optimization. Target datasets are fully held out from training and selection, enabling plug-and-play extension of EEG models to heterogeneous multimodal recordings.

entry.title: Confidence-Gated Cloud-Edge Cascade Triage via Variational Risk Minimization for Medical Imaging

author.name: Xinye Yang, Zhusi Zhong, Scott Collins, Michael Bernstein, Grayson Baird, Terrence Healey, Michael Atalay, Mahesh Jayaraman, Xuyu Wang, Zhicheng Jiao

entry.summary: This paper introduces Variational Risk Minimization, a distillation framework for emergency chest X-ray triage that treats LVLM-generated report variants as Monte Carlo samples of latent clinical interpretations. By learning from a variationally marginalized teacher distribution rather than a single target, VRM provides uncertainty-aware supervision under the missing-modality gap where reports arrive after triage decisions. It improves calibration and shows robustness to hallucinated supervision.

entry.title: WakeKV: Reactive, Reversible KV Residency for Heads That Change Their Minds

author.name: Utkarsh Ranjan

entry.summary: WakeKV is a KV-cache management policy that reacts to attention heads changing their reading behavior during generation, rather than freezing head classifications made at prefill. It moves cooling heads to a recoverable CPU reservoir instead of evicting them, improving cache miss rates at matched memory budgets across needle retrieval, chain-of-thought, and multi-turn regimes.

entry.title: FALCON: A Model and Dataset Agnostic Framework for Synthetic Data Generation for NL2SQL Pairs

author.name: Darian Lee, Shannon Rumsey, Jack St. Clair, Xinyi Tang, Aditya Bansal, Yuanming Shi

entry.summary: FALCON generates realistic, ambiguity-aware synthetic NL-to-SQL training pairs using reserved-word SQL seeding and persona-based prompting, matching the complexity of challenging real-world benchmarks at low cost with compact open models. It addresses the common weakness of prior synthetic data pipelines that produce oversimplified queries ignoring linguistic ambiguity. Relevant to improving text-to-SQL systems without expensive annotation.

entry.title: AptMQL-Bench: From Text-to-SQL to Text-to-MQL via Access-Pattern Schema Design and Data-Preserving Migration

author.name: Hy Nguyen, Nabi Rezvani, Robin Vujanic

entry.summary: AptMQL-Bench provides a rigorous pipeline for converting text-to-SQL benchmarks into document-database (MongoDB/MQL) settings, showing that prior heuristic conversions fail to migrate many databases, silently drop up to 25.9% of rows, and produce degenerate schemas. The benchmark introduces access-pattern-driven schema design and data-preserving migration.

entry.title: Oracle headroom without signal: null-calibrated evaluation of candidate selection for thermal heart rate estimation

author.name: Mohammad Rakibur Rahman, Nhi Nguyen, Sasan Sharifipour, Le Nguyen, Manuel Lage Ca\~nellas, Miguel Bordallo L\'opez, Constantino \'Alvarez Casado

entry.summary: Analyzes a subtle evaluation flaw in camera-based physiological monitoring: oracle-based selection of the best candidate signal among K estimates rewards chance agreement, with expected oracle error decreasing roughly as 1/K even for signals unrelated to the reference. The paper derives order-statistics bounds and validates them on 96 thermal recordings with 168 candidates per window.

entry.title: A Fully Automatic Pipeline for 3D Dendrite Instance Segmentation in SBF-SEM

author.name: Zewen Zhuo, Ilya Belevich, Eija Jokitalo, Alejandra Sierra, Jussi Tohka

entry.summary: The paper presents a fully automatic pipeline for 3D instance segmentation of dendrites in serial block-face electron microscopy, combining SAM prompting guided by YOLOv6, iterative 2D mask refinement, random forest instance linking, and nnU-Net high-resolution refinement. It enables quantification of dendritic structural plasticity on hippocampal datasets, including control and epileptic rat tissue, without manual annotation.

entry.title: ManifoldSplat: Language-Guided Semantic Shape Editing of 3D Gaussian Head Avatars

author.name: Antonio Canela, Jordi S\`anchez-Riera

entry.summary: ManifoldSplat is an end-to-end framework for language-guided semantic shape editing of animatable 3D Gaussian Splatting avatars reconstructed from monocular video, performing edits within the structured FLAME manifold to preserve identity and rigging. It introduces DeltaRegion for per-region control, avoiding slow per-prompt optimization or identity compromise of prior text-driven approaches.

entry.title: SocialVLA: A Social Perception Gateway for Human-Reaction-Based Failure Detection and Recovery in VLA Manipulation

author.name: Sofya Konstantinova, Miguel Altamirano Cabrera, Artem Lykov, Dzmitry Tsetserukou

entry.summary: Introduces SocialVLA, a local policy-agnostic gateway that converts spontaneous human reactions (vocal, facial, verbal) into runtime intervention signals for VLA manipulation. It fuses causal paralinguistic detection, reaction recognition, stop phrases, and robot-relevance estimation via asynchronous first-event fusion to trigger holds and recovery.

entry.title: Register-Routed Delayed Fusion: Rewiring Shortcut-Prone Observation Fusion in Visuomotor Imitation

author.name: Jieting Long, Weidong Cai, Weiming Zhi

entry.summary: RRDF investigates fusion topology in visuomotor imitation policies, showing that dense token fusion lets compact proprioceptive cues shortcut into spatial visual representations early in their formation. It masks direct compact-visual attention and stages cross-modal interaction through a learned register workspace with an isolate-collect-route schedule. The goal is to improve visual responsiveness and downstream policy behavior.

entry.title: DataWeave: Deploying Human-LLM Analytics for Exploratory Structured Data Analysis

author.name: Raquib Bin Yousuf, Harith Laxman, Vitaliy Shkremetko, Eunice Son, Shambhavi Verma, Brian O'Leary, Venketesh Subramony, Sylvain Nazef, Jacquelyn Elias, Ron Coddington, Chris Contakes, Michael Riley, Naren Ramakrishnan

entry.summary: DataWeave is a deployed system helping data journalists explore large structured datasets, addressing recurring LLM failures in real newsroom workflows such as schema mismatches, misread domain semantics, and silent assumptions. It combines human and LLM analytics to support trend and accountability reporting across hundreds of variables and multiple datasets.

entry.title: Bounded Reachability & Jailbreak Detection via Contraction-Constrained State Space Models

author.name: Omanshu Thapliyal

entry.summary: This work provides formal robustness guarantees for SSM-based safety heads, proving that exact interval bound propagation certification is possible when the state transition matrix satisfies a contraction condition (norm of A below 1). It characterizes bounded reachability of classifier outputs under embedding perturbations, enabling certified jailbreak detection.

entry.title: Toward SLM-based agentic task-tool intent matching

author.name: Chiara Troiani, Arash Salarian, Majed El Helou, Benjamin Ryder, Jean Diaconu, Herv\'e Muyal, Marcelo Yannuzzi

entry.summary: The paper proposes using small language models for low-latency, on-premises oversight of agentic tool calls, checking not whether a call is authorized but whether it logically serves the task's intent. This goes beyond conventional authorization schemes that cannot assess agent cognition. It targets risks from rogue or nudged agents making individually-allowed but collectively off-intent call combinations.

entry.title: From Benchmarks to Production: A Text-to-SQL System for Complex Financial Data

author.name: Arijit Sehanobish, Bruno Gomes Coelho, Guillaume Michel, Sophia Zhi, Valerie Faucon-Morin, Kristen Howell

entry.summary: The paper presents FLINT, a domain-specialized Text-to-SQL system for production financial databases where opaque integer keys and multi-join schemas cause general-purpose systems to fall below 50 percent accuracy. It combines a lookup agent for resolving concepts to reference-table constraints, embedding-based retrieval of similar queries, and other components to close the benchmark-to-production gap.

entry.title: CORE: COverage CAlibration and Evicted-Mass REdistribution for KV Cache

author.name: Shuxin Liu, Qing Liu, Yi Du, Ou Wu

entry.summary: CORE improves KV cache compression for long-context LLM decoding by grounding retention in an exact error factorization: eviction error equals evicted attention mass times a directional centroid gap. It calibrates coverage using query utility and log-determinant coverage, then redistributes evicted mass into memory writes. This matters for serving long-context models under tight memory and bandwidth constraints.

entry.title: Hop-Decayed Influence: New Vulnerabilities of Structural Auxiliary Indexing in GraphRAG Pipelines with LLM

author.name: Jisung Park, John Le, Heath Cooper

entry.summary: This paper formalizes a novel attack surface in GraphRAG pipelines: schema-level auxiliary structures built during offline indexing, such as semantic summaries, hierarchical edges, and pre-computed scores. The proposed Hop-Decayed Influence attack uses query-aware influence propagation to identify and corrupt high-impact targets post-indexing, demonstrating effectiveness across HotpotQA and 2WikiMultiHopQA with Microsoft GraphRAG and HippoRAG architectures. It reveals that prior graph-poisoning work overlooked schema-level structures.

entry.title: SideKernel: A Usable microVM Sandbox for AI Coding Agents on macOS

author.name: Dimitrios Prasakis

entry.summary: Presents SideKernel, an open-source microVM-based sandbox for AI coding agents on macOS designed around usability, motivated by a survey showing fewer than 40% of agent users sandbox their agents. Identifies adoption barriers and benchmarks the system against existing sandbox options.

entry.title: Correcting Guided Diffusion Trajectories with Spectral Alignment

author.name: Gihoon Kim, Taesup Kim

entry.summary: Shows that spectral alignment of intermediate diffusion states offers a principled criterion for assessing whether classifier-free guidance trajectories are progressing as intended, and introduces Spectral Correction Guidance to adaptively correct guided sampling. This addresses CFG's lack of an explicit progress criterion in conditional image generation.

entry.title: Adaptive Spectral-Koopman Dynamics Modeling for Temporal Domain Generalization

author.name: Tengxue Zhang, Yu Ke, Yang Shu, Chenchen Sun, Yisheng An, Chenjuan Guo, Bin Yang

entry.summary: AdaSpecK is a spectral-Koopman framework for temporal domain generalization that applies spectral-aware filtering in latent space to extract denoised low-frequency trajectories and learns a Koopman operator for linearized dynamics modeling. It targets overfitting to domain-specific noise and loss of interpretability in existing TDG methods on streaming data with distribution shift.

entry.title: Information Limits of Low-Rank Approximation Certification

author.name: Kang Liu, Bohao Qu

entry.summary: The authors characterize the minimum number of matrix-vector products needed to certify that a low-rank approximation meets an error tolerance, deriving exact dimension-uniform minimax query constants for single candidates. They also show that a single validation batch can certify an entire nested path of approximations, with a sqrt(log(W+1)) concentration bound across W paths.

entry.title: DriftTTS: Few-Step Text-to-Speech Without Distillation via Distribution-Matching Drift

author.name: Mohammad Nur Hossain Khan, Subrata Biswas, Bashima Islam

entry.summary: DriftTTS is a few-step mel-spectrogram generator trained without distillation, teachers, or adversarial losses, using a distribution-matching drift objective in a feature space defined by raw mels and a frozen masked-autoencoder encoder. On LJSpeech at four function evaluations it nearly matches a distilled baseline in MCD and WER.

entry.title: Parameter-Free Interval-Dynamic Regret under Heavy-Tailed Noise

author.name: Vaneet Aggarwal

entry.summary: The paper studies online convex optimization with one stochastic subgradient per round under heavy-tailed noise with unknown conditional p-th moment (1 < p <= 2), achieving parameter-free interval-dynamic regret bounds that adapt to comparator path length without knowing G, sigma, p, or interval statistics. The analysis preserves distinct mean-gradient and noise exponents and extends to comparisons against predictably available expert distributions. This is a strong theoretical result in adaptive online learning.

entry.title: Mitigating Convergence Collapse in Fixed-Target Anomaly Detectors via Kernel-Anchored Locality Regularization

author.name: Jos\'e Lucas De Melo Costa, Fabrice Popineau, Arpad Rimmel, Bich-Li\^en Doan

entry.summary: The paper characterizes convergence collapse in tabular anomaly detectors that fit a neural map to a fixed target, showing that better optimization actually destroys the residual-based anomaly signal. It argues effective detection structurally requires a locality constraint blocking unconstrained extrapolation, and proposes kernel-anchored locality regularization. This connects classical local detectors like kNN to modern neural approaches.

entry.title: BaCP: Backbone Contrastive Pruning for Preserving Representations in Extremely Sparse Neural Networks

author.name: Mohammad Haroon Khawaja, Muhammad Haseeb, Mohammad Fatim Shoaib, Muhammad Tahir

entry.summary: BaCP tackles representational collapse in extremely sparse pruned networks by regularizing the sparse network's embedding space to align with pretrained, fine-tuned, and historical snapshot models via contrastive objectives. Building on the CAP framework, it is evaluated across 90 matched-budget settings with multiple pruning criteria. It substantially improves accuracy in extreme sparsity regimes where standard pruning fails.

entry.title: Scale-Recursive Rectified Flows for Few-Step Precipitation Ensembles

author.name: Shunya Nagashima, Takumi Bannai

entry.summary: The paper proposes a scale-recursive rectified flow for generating ensembles of high-resolution precipitation fields, generating broad patterns before local details. It allocates sampling steps by comparing ensemble variability with prediction error across spatial scales, addressing the problem that fewer sampling steps make ensemble members too similar and understate uncertainty. This supports flood risk assessment and water management.

entry.title: Jumping up and down: Denoiser diffusion models for discrete ordinal data

author.name: Yair Shenfeld, Ricardo Baptista, Stefano Peluchetti

entry.summary: The authors introduce JUD, a family of denoiser-based diffusion models for discrete ordinal (integer-valued) data, filling a gap between continuous diffusion for images and categorical diffusion for language. JUD centers training on denoisers with bi-directional perturbations, offering a simple objective suited to modalities like gene counts and ordinal signals.

entry.title: Neural Data Needs Semantic Tokenization: Behavioral Events as Boundaries of Session-Transferable Tokens

author.name: Sangyoon Bae, Jiook Cha

entry.summary: The paper argues that neural foundation models for electrophysiology fail on new sessions because they tokenize individual neurons, which never repeat across sessions. It proposes semantic tokenization based on population-activity states bounded by behavioral task events, yielding units that persist across neuronal turnover and carry behavioral meaning.

entry.title: Predicting and Repairing Merge Collapse in Large Language Models

author.name: Jungseob Lee, Seungyoon Lee, Sugyeong Eo, Hyeonseok Moon, Jaehyung Seo, Heuiseok Lim

entry.summary: The paper shows that the variance of task vectors across fine-tuned specialists predicts which model merges will collapse below the base model, deriving a pre-merge score from a noise model of averaging interference. Across 22 merge configurations from four model families, only destructive merges exceed the score threshold, and the measure also calibrates repair strategies.

entry.title: Bidirectional Voronoi-biased Exploration Curriculum for Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Juri Pfammatter, Kaixian Qu, Clemens Schwarke, Victor Klemm, Marco Hutter

entry.summary: BVER is a bidirectional curriculum for goal-conditioned RL that grows start states outward from the goal and goals outward from the start, inspired by bidirectional RRT planning. This avoids the one-sided expansion of automatic start-state/goal curricula for sparse-reward long-horizon tasks without requiring demonstrations or shaped rewards.

entry.title: Get a GRIP, this will be a long TRIP: A Quantifiable Long-Range Framework for Verifying Over-squashing

author.name: Ferran Hernandez Caralt, Simon Heilig, Adri\'an Bazaga, Asja Fischer, Moshe Eliasof, Pietro Li\`o

entry.summary: The paper introduces four verifiable axioms (Predictability, Tightness, Strictly k-Range, Topology-Invariance) that any benchmark must satisfy to genuinely test long-range interactions in GNNs, addressing the saturation of the Long Range Graph Benchmark by short-range models. This provides a principled certificate of long-rangedness for arbitrary graphs.

entry.title: Simulation-Free Learning of Population Dynamics with Wasserstein Lagrangian Residuals

author.name: Fedor Sergeev, Markus Heinonen, Daniel Waxman, Tim Cooijmans, Ricardo Baptista, Dmitry Batenkov, Eli Bingham

entry.summary: This paper proposes Double-Stitch, a simulation-free method for learning Lagrangian mechanics in Wasserstein space, which unlike Wasserstein gradient flows can model conservative and periodic population dynamics. It penalizes the residual of the equation of motion along a learned population path, derived from a Clebsch variational principle, avoiding costly numerical solvers at every training step. This makes learning of evolving distribution dynamics far more tractable.

entry.title: Characterizing the Performance Gap in Human Activity Recognition for Older Adults

author.name: Hossein Khayami, Sungjin Hwang, Eshed Ohn-Bar, David E. Conroy, Amanda Lazar, Eun Kyoung Choe, Hernisa Kacorri

entry.summary: Using the annotated MyMove dataset of free-living older adults (mean age 71), the authors show that accuracy improvements on younger-adult HAR benchmarks fail to transfer to older populations, with the gap often widening. Richer representations and certain training regimes mitigate but do not eliminate the disparity.

entry.title: Learning When to Commit from Partial Speech for End-to-End Simultaneous Speech Translation

author.name: Hieu Hoang, Amittai Axelrod

entry.summary: The authors adapt a full-utterance speech language model for simultaneous speech translation using prefix supervision derived from the model's own complete and partial waveform translations, requiring no transcripts or human translations. On FLEURS and CoVoST2 across three language directions, prefix training improves quality-latency trade-offs, with confidence thresholds providing the most consistently competitive policy.

entry.title: DeepStratNet: A Context-Aware Coordinate Regression Framework for Seismic Horizon Tracking under Sparse Labels

author.name: Aniq Ahmad, Musham Ahmad Malik, Ahmad Mustafa, Heather Bedle

entry.summary: Reformulates seismic horizon tracking as context-aware coordinate regression rather than dense semantic segmentation, avoiding the background-label and post-processing pitfalls of U-Net approaches under sparse annotations. The formulation naturally captures inter-slice context without the prohibitive cost of full 3D models.

entry.title: Bridging Research and Practice: A Systematic Evaluation of Generalist and Dermatology-Specific Models in Clinical Skin Lesion Classification

author.name: Emanoel dos Santos, Kelvin Cunha, Rodrigo Mota, Fabio Papais, Thales Bezerra, Natalia Lopes, Erico Medeiros, Shirley Cruz, Jessica Araujo, Paulo Borba, Tsang Ing Ren

entry.summary: This work systematically benchmarks generalist vision models against dermatology-specific architectures on heterogeneous, recent clinical skin lesion data, examining generalization across acquisition devices, quality, and demographics. It aims to inform safe and equitable translation of dermatology ML into practice.

entry.title: OuroReward: Sequential Reward Scheduling for Reinforcement Learning in Text-to-3D Generation

author.name: Bingyang Cui, Yujie Zhang, Yiling Xu, Yunfeng Guan

entry.summary: OuroReward proposes interference-aware sequential reward scheduling for RL-based text-to-3D generation, estimating pairwise dependencies among quality dimensions (e.g., semantic alignment, texture clarity) and constructing a cyclic optimization path that minimizes cumulative interference. This avoids the imbalanced optimization caused by simultaneous multi-reward aggregation.

entry.title: ZAGNet: Zone-Aware Graph Aggregation Network for Patient-Level Lung Ultrasound Diagnosis

author.name: Li Chen, Shubham Patil, Rashid Al Mukaddim, Jochen Kruecker, Balasundar Raju, Alvin Chen

entry.summary: ZAGNet performs patient-level lung ultrasound diagnosis by representing temporally tracked pathology findings as graph nodes connected by anatomical zone adjacency, using a graph transformer and a virtual global node to propagate contextual information across lung regions. This handles variable and incomplete scanning protocols with missing zones, outperforming heuristic max/mean pooling aggregation.

entry.title: One Photon, Many Worlds: Posteriors and Predictions with Single-Photon Cameras

author.name: Haejoon Lee (Carnegie Mellon University), Mohit Gupta (University of Wisconsin-Madison), Vijayakumar Bhagavatula (Carnegie Mellon University), Aswin C. Sankaranarayanan (Carnegie Mellon University)

entry.summary: Studies inverse problems with SPAD cameras, where each frame is a binary photon-arrival image, framing single-frame reconstruction as a fundamentally one-to-many problem. The work characterizes how posterior uncertainty shrinks with accumulated binary measurements and enables near-deterministic inference at sufficient photon counts.

entry.title: Around the World: Unified Learned Locomotion on a 270 g Continuous-Rotation Quadruped

author.name: Arturo Flores Alvarez, Nathan Lintu, Dennis Hong

entry.summary: This paper demonstrates onboard closed-loop learned locomotion on MiNI-Q, a 270 g quadruped with continuous-rotation legs that can place supporting configurations on either side of the body. A single posture-conditioned RL policy using a continuous torus joint-space reference connects upright walking, inverted walking, and landing recovery without state machines. A sub-100k-parameter policy runs entirely onboard the micro-scale robot.

entry.title: PsyEvo: A Personalized Counseling Agent That Self-Evolves at Test Time

author.name: Yuting Yan, Shihao Xu, Junhao Yu, Mingcong Zuo, Lu Chen, Nan Xiang, Haiyang Geng, Dongjie Tao, Minghao Wang

entry.summary: PsyEvo is an LLM counseling framework that personalizes interventions per client and improves its response policy at test time, using a Hierarchical Bayesian Skill Policy, response-policy adaptation from ongoing interaction, and additional components for therapeutic learning. It targets scalable mental-health support where practitioners are scarce.

entry.title: IntentCoding: Amplifying User Intent in Code Generation

author.name: Zheng Fang, Yihong Dong, Lili Mou, Dongming Jin, Zhi Jin, Ge Li

entry.summary: The authors show empirically that LLM code generation degrades quickly as the number of user-intent constraints grows, and that user intent under-influences logits during decoding. IntentCoding addresses this by masking the intent and applying multi-strength contrastive decoding to amplify its influence at generation time, improving adherence to fine-grained multi-constraint instructions.

entry.title: Latent-MOPD: Latent Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Zhengyu Fang, Seoyeon Hong, Jie Yang, Muyang Li, Koyoshi Shindo, Brandon Joseph Lwowski, Jing Li

entry.summary: Latent-MOPD is the first representation-level multi-teacher on-policy distillation method for LLMs, integrating specialists through both output predictions and hidden states without additional teacher training. It coordinates representation supervision via late-layer target selection, shared projections for unequal hidden widths, and domain-grouped updates, with supervision gradually shifting from hidden states to token predictions. This extends on-policy distillation beyond output-distribution matching.

entry.title: Conditional Capacity and Routing in Mixture-of-Experts Particle Transformers

author.name: Kaushik Pendiyala, Haris Zia, Trevin Lee, Timothy Legge, Alejandro J. De Leon, Zihan Zhao, Aaron Wang, Abhijith Gandrakota, Jennifer Ngadiuba, Richard Cavanaugh, Javier Duarte

entry.summary: The paper studies dense versus MoE particle transformers on the 188-class JetClass-II benchmark, varying expert count, routing capacity, top-K, and auxiliary losses. Findings include that top-1 MoE improves over dense at nearly unchanged compute when token dropping is avoided, more stored experts yield little gain, and expert assignments grow more strongly associated with physics classes over training. This grounds MoE design choices in a real scientific domain.

entry.title: Peer Effects in Signed Networks: Separating Influence Through Positive and Negative Ties

author.name: Xiaojing Du, Jiuyong Li, Lin Liu, Debo Cheng, Jixue Liu, Thuc Duy Le

entry.summary: The paper defines causal peer effects through positive and negative ties in signed social networks, including sign-composition effects of reallocating treatment between tie types, and provides identification formulas. It proposes SiDE, a signed-exposure doubly robust estimator, proving double robustness and showing that sign-blind analysis mixes opposing influences.

entry.title: Coverage You Can Steer: Online Conformal Calibration for RL-Driven Hardware-Aware NAS

author.name: Pedro Brandimarte, Nerea Aranjuelo, Marcos Nieto, Oihana Otaegui

entry.summary: The paper addresses the failure of distribution-free conformal guarantees in RL-driven neural architecture search, where the improving policy and layer-by-layer construction violate exchangeability. It replaces one-shot quantile estimation with online adaptive conformal inference to prune candidates while retaining coverage guarantees throughout the search.

entry.title: Localized Conformal Safety Monitoring with Vision-Language Models for Autonomous Driving

author.name: Lu\'is Marques, Rong Fang, Disha Kamale, Dmitry Berenson

entry.summary: The authors propose SLLCP, a post-hoc conformal calibration layer over frozen vision-language models that converts unreliable VLM collision-likelihood estimates into distribution-free safety bounds for trajectory monitoring in autonomous driving. This addresses the gap between VLM reasoning ability and the guarantees required for safety-critical deployment.

entry.title: Depth Hypothesis Guided Iterative Refinement for Event-Image Monocular Depth Estimation

author.name: Daikun Liu, Teng Wang, Changyin Sun

entry.summary: HypoDepth reframes event-image monocular depth estimation from direct full-depth regression into a constrained depth search using a discrete Depth Hypothesis Volume, with a 3D cost volume and multi-scale correlation search guiding residual refinement. The lightweight cost-volume design enables efficient iterative refinement suited to event cameras' dynamic properties.

entry.title: FlashSinkhorn 2: Block-Sparse Entropic Optimal Transport

author.name: Felix X. -F. Ye, Yu Chin Fabian Lim, Naigang Wang, Davis Wertheimer

entry.summary: FlashSinkhorn 2 is a GPU solver for entropic optimal transport with squared-Euclidean cost that couples a coarse centroid-based stage with a block-sparse fine stage, avoiding evaluation of all pairwise point interactions per Sinkhorn iteration. It solves large discrete OT problems to a prescribed marginal residual on a single GPU. Morton-ordered blocks enable screening and fused kernel execution.

entry.title: Hypothesis-guided discovery of cognitive algorithms via program refinement

author.name: Huiwen Alex Yang, Mark K. Ho, Bill D. Thompson

entry.summary: The paper proposes a hybrid approach to cognitive modeling that treats discovery of cognitive algorithms as program refinement: human-created cognitive models expressed as probabilistic programs are handed to LLM agents tasked with refining them against behavioral data. This combines the interpretability and human expertise of traditional cognitive modeling with the scalability of LLM-based model generation. It targets harder tasks like algorithm recovery than prior LLM-based approaches.

entry.title: Time Series Forecasting Benchmarks Need Scenario-Grounded Stress Testing

author.name: Yuyang Zhao, Lian Xu, Hao Xue

entry.summary: This position-style paper argues that time series forecasting evaluation is too narrow, rewarding low held-out error and treating robustness as Gaussian noise or bounded perturbations. The authors contend that real input-side anomalies reflect structured events causing regime shifts and broken cross-variable dependencies, and advocate scenario-grounded stress testing to capture semantic, causal, and system-level failures.

entry.title: Modeling Shared and Individual Structure for Cross-Subject Continuous Affect Regression from EEG-fNIRS

author.name: Xuan Wang, Bing Wang, Shuai Chang, Hao Yuan, Xinbo Qi, Xinyue Zhang

entry.summary: The paper tackles zero-shot cross-subject continuous valence-arousal estimation from synchronized EEG-fNIRS recordings, decomposing affect trajectories into stimulus-shared structure and individual structure estimated from a label-free EEG marker. It predicts raw-scale trajectories for test subjects whose labels are never observed, a harder setting than typical subject-dependent affect modeling.

entry.title: AMBER: Multi-View Adaptive Budget Allocation for Listwise Vision-Language Reranking

author.name: Wenteng Chen, Jiachen Zhu, Rong Shan, Tianyi Xu, Yuxiang Chen, Congmin Zheng, Teng Wang, Junjie Wu, Weiwen Liu, Changwang Zhang, Weinan Zhang, Jun Wang, Jianghao Lin

entry.summary: AMBER is an online, budgeted framework for multimodal listwise reranking that treats fragmented VLM outputs as local tournaments maintained via continuous Elo updates, then allocates VLM calls adaptively across candidate views. It replaces fixed call schedules with dynamic global resource allocation to reduce expensive inference costs.

entry.title: Relevant Evidence Decoding for Audio-Visual Hallucination Mitigation

author.name: Hyunjae Ra, Aecheon Jung, Jungin Park, Sungeun Hong

entry.summary: This paper identifies a cross-modal interference problem in audio-visual LLMs where joint inference can weaken correct single-modality predictions, such as losing confidence in a heard violin when a guitar appears visually. Its Relevant Evidence Decoding method extends contrastive decoding to select the perceptual evidence a given question actually requires.

entry.title: Lightweight, Rubric-Guided Trajectory Evaluation for Production AI Agents

author.name: Linh-An Phan, MingXue Wang, Guangyu Wu, Feng Pan, Zhaoyu Pang, Yanbin Zhang

entry.summary: LiteTrajEval is a budget-bounded architecture for evaluating LLM agent trajectories: it derives domain rule profiles offline, preprocesses trajectories with heuristic failure signals, serializes under a fixed token budget, and invokes a single rubric-guided LLM judge. Evaluated on Magentic-One-style and tau-bench-style trajectories, it targets the cost problem of repeated production evaluation. The output is structured diagnostic reports.

entry.title: CVE2AP: Automated Generation of PDDL-Encoded Attack Paths via Large Language Models

author.name: Lin Cui, Vincenzo Scotti, Raffaela Mirandola

entry.summary: CVE2AP uses LLMs to automatically convert CVE threat intelligence into formally machine-verifiable attack paths encoded in PDDL, replacing expert-driven manual modeling. This improves scalability of cybersecurity analysis for vulnerability exploitation and attack progression reasoning.

entry.title: Do Large Language Models Know Colombian Law? A Reliability Benchmark for the Colombian Legal System

author.name: Rub\'en Manrique, Michelle Castellanos, Jorge Morales, Juan David Guti\'errez, Antonio Barreto Rozo, Joaqu\'in V\'elez Navarro

entry.summary: This paper introduces an expert-validated 1,042-item benchmark of Colombian law across ten legal areas and three question formats, built with a human-in-the-loop multi-stage expert review pipeline. Evaluating 15 proprietary and open-weight models shows wide accuracy ranges on closed questions (0.577 to 0.905 for Gemini 3.1 Pro, an established model since early 2026) and significant factual reliability gaps in free-text legal answers.

entry.title: Causal discovery identifies pathways linking physical activity to dementia risk in the UK BioBank

author.name: Wasif Khan, Panayiotis V. Benos, Joshua K. Wong, Ruogu Fang

entry.summary: This study combines LLM-guided causal discovery with mediation analysis on 42,293 UK Biobank participants to identify pathways through which moderate-to-vigorous physical activity lowers dementia risk, including depression, functional capacity, smoking, hypertension, and cardiovascular disease. It demonstrates how LLMs can guide causal structure learning in large-scale epidemiological data. The work matters for both AI methodology and clinical science around dementia prevention.

entry.title: Network-in-the-Loop at Scale: GPU-Batched 5G Simulation for Massively Parallel Robot Learning

author.name: Zifan Zhang, Mingzhe Han, Kannan Athreya, Yuchen Liu

entry.summary: Isaac-Net is a GPU-batched 5G New Radio simulation module that advances uplink scheduling of thousands of environments in lockstep with Isaac Lab physics, enabling network-in-the-loop training for multi-robot fleets on private 5G networks. It bridges the gap between GPU robot simulators that oversimplify networking and packet-level simulators that cannot keep pace. This matters for realistic training of networked multi-robot policies.

entry.title: FinDialogLens: Event Extraction over Multi-Party Dialogue for Missed-Trade Identification in Financial Chatrooms

author.name: Chin-Lun Fu, Hong Ni, Behrouz Madahian

entry.summary: Presents FinDialogLens, a hybrid LLM pipeline for event extraction over multi-party financial chatroom dialogue to recover missed trades, using compact fine-tuned classifiers as scaffolds to detect RFQ triggers and outcomes, segment per-event windows, and fill argument roles. Achieves 92.1% and 94.3% on key metrics with GPT-4o on a challenging industrial task.

entry.title: From Fragments to Global Maps: Learning Vectorized Map Aggregation with Large Language Models

author.name: Ziwei Li, Yi-Tang Chen, Xiaoqi Wang, Wenbin He, Han-Wei Shen, Liu Ren

entry.summary: Proposes MapMergeLLM, a data-driven framework that formulates aggregation of noisy, fragmented, overlapping local map predictions into global HD maps for autonomous driving as conditional sequence generation with LLMs, replacing hand-crafted association thresholds. Aims to handle road-structure variation and detector-specific errors without manual tuning.

entry.title: TPBench: A Turning-Point Benchmark for Dialogue Compression

author.name: Minji Park, Seunghyun Yoon, Hyuk Lim

entry.summary: TPBench is a benchmark for dialogue compression that targets turning-point eviction — the failure where a compressor preserves facts but drops the turn that changed the conversation state, such as a user correction or revised constraint. It evaluates three information targets (initial goal, current revised slot value, and both) at fixed retention budgets, grounding answers in human dialogue-state annotations from MultiWOZ and SGD. This exposes failure modes hidden by single aggregate retention scores.

entry.title: Nearly Optimal Fixed-Confidence Best-Arm Identification with 1-Bit Feedback

author.name: Khang Luong, Dinh Thai Son, Hoang Ta, Hung The Tran, Tuan Quang Dam

entry.summary: The paper studies best-arm identification in bandits when only one bit of feedback per round is available, via threshold queries over a query set of arms. It develops a time-uniform 1-bit mean-estimation primitive and embeds it into fixed-clipping and phased-elimination algorithms with near-optimal (epsilon, delta)-PAC guarantees.

entry.title: WebFovea: When the Model Is Right but the Click Is Wrong -- Reliable Round Trips for Vision-Based Web Agents on Live Websites

author.name: Jiangang Han

entry.summary: WebFovea is a vision-based web agent that placed second in the WebRetriever Challenge 2026, and the paper analyzes why a correct model decision can still fail in execution: parsing of the reply, action application, result reporting, and verification must each succeed. It emphasizes harness engineering and round-trip verification for reliable operation on live websites.

entry.title: SyntaxBench: A Statistical Diagnostic Framework for Character-Level Reasoning in Large Language Models

author.name: Mohsen Larni (Department of Computer Science, University of Nevada, Las Vegas), Sobhan Ebrahimi Azar (Department of Computer Science, University of Nevada, Las Vegas), Pouyan Nahed (Department of Computer Science, University of Nevada, Las Vegas), Kazem Taghva (Department of Computer Science, University of Nevada, Las Vegas)

entry.summary: SyntaxBench is a benchmark with five core character-level reasoning tasks (counting, containment, palindromes, edit distance, longest-string selection) plus a harder substring-extraction stress test, using matched English and random-string inputs with multiple shot settings. It evaluates whether current LLMs handle small syntactic errors that matter in real deployments.

entry.title: The Price of Greenwashing: Algorithmic Verification and Market Discipline using Conformal Machine Learning

author.name: Sourav Bose, Taoufik Bouraoui

entry.summary: The authors fuse SEC financial fundamentals with facility-level EPA greenhouse gas registries to build a statistically guaranteed baseline of physical corporate emissions, using gradient boosting with Mondrian Conformal Prediction. They quantify the gap between self-reported and algorithmically estimated emissions via a Conformal-Weighted Coefficient, offering an objective greenwashing measure for financial markets. The work targets a real econometric gap beyond subjective ESG ratings.

entry.title: Co-design Gym: A Unified Benchmark for Embodiment-Policy Co-optimization

author.name: Aviraj Newatia, Yordan Tsvetkov, Leonard Pleiss, Andrew Spielberg, Rika Antonova

entry.summary: This benchmark addresses the joint optimization of an agent's embodiment and its control policy, a problem class where optimizing each separately is suboptimal. Co-design Gym provides a unified suite spanning robotics-style tasks so the community can study co-optimization explicitly, moving beyond the fixed-embodiment assumption in most RL benchmarks. Co-designed by a credible academic team including Andrew Spielberg and Rika Antonova.

entry.title: VisAudit: Evaluating Multimodal Agents for Visual Diagnosis and Repair

author.name: Shicheng Liu, Adam Kahirov, Qi Zhang, Zhimin Hu, Song Wang, Junhong Lin, Julian Shun, Yada Zhu

entry.summary: VisAudit is a benchmark for evaluating whether multimodal agents can autonomously review visualizations: recognizing when a chart is wrong, deciding what to change, repairing it without breaking correct content, and verifying success. It goes beyond existing benchmarks that test chart generation or defect detection in isolation, providing configurable auxiliary evidence such as source tables and code. This fills a gap in agentic evaluation for data visualization workflows.

entry.title: DISSOLVR: An Interpretable and Fast Framework for Aqueous and Organic Solubility Prediction

author.name: Vansh Ramani, Har Ashish Arora, Dhairya Kuchhal, Sayan Ranu, Tarak Karmakar

entry.summary: DISSOLVR is a transparent framework for molecular solubility prediction that couples molecular structure with thermodynamic behavior, challenging the trend of opaque deep-learning architectures in chemistry. The authors perform a comprehensive literature review and benchmarking, showing the interpretable approach approaches or matches state-of-the-art performance across aqueous and organic solubility. This matters for pharmaceutical development and environmental modeling.

entry.title: Structural-Functional Brain Connectivity Generation via Multimodal Hypergraph-based Flow Matching

author.name: Chyong Yi Poh, Hwa Hui Tew, Junn Yong Loo, Rapha\"{e}l C. -W. Phan, Fuad Noman, Pew-Thian Yap, Chee-Ming Ting

entry.summary: The paper proposes MHG-FM, a multimodal hypergraph flow matching framework for jointly generating and translating between structural and functional brain connectivity networks. By using hypergraphs instead of pairwise graphs, it captures higher-order interactions and preserves cross-modal structure-function relationships that independent generation methods miss.

entry.title: On Unlearning for Time-series Forecasting

author.name: Zeyu Shi, Yanhui Luo, Ziming Hong, Chongyang Gao, Kezhen Chen, Shanshan Ye, Lixu Wang

entry.summary: The paper tackles machine unlearning for time-series forecasting, where deleted observations participate in multiple causally connected windows, making gradient-based unlearning unstable. It proposes methods tailored to these dependencies to honor deletion requests without costly retraining in sensitive longitudinal-data domains.

entry.title: Dirac-Interconnected Neural Elements: Discovering Modularity in Physical Systems Without Reduction

author.name: Reiho Li, Razmik Arman Khosrovian, Takaharu Yaguchi, Hiroaki Yoshimura, Takashi Matsubara

entry.summary: DINEs are a neural architecture that represents physical systems as interconnections of components using Dirac structures, discovering modularity without requiring it to be known a priori or reducing the system to an ODE that discards algebraic constraints. This preserves the physical structure of interconnected dynamical systems during data-driven modeling.

entry.title: Learn Feasibility Once, Optimize All Objectives: Derivative-Free Diffusion Models for Chance-Constrained Programming

author.name: Ziwen Liu, Yan Liu, Congying Han, Tiande Guo, Yao Yan, Weichen Zhao

entry.summary: D3Opt disentangles constraint modeling from objective optimization in chance-constrained programs by training a risk-conditioned diffusion model on constraint-filtered decisions once, then freezing it as a reusable prior for post-specified objectives. This enables derivative-free optimization of non-convex, non-smooth objectives under fixed chance constraints.

entry.title: 16-bit Precision of Convolutional Neural Networks on Microcontroller Units for 8-bit Costs

author.name: Rui Liu, Benjamin Paa{\ss}en

entry.summary: The W16A16 quantization scheme achieves 16-bit precision inference on Armv7E-M microcontrollers at the speed and energy cost typically associated with 8-bit approaches. The paper analyzes the architecture to explain the performance advantage, reporting roughly 10 times lower quantization error along with measured time and energy savings.

entry.title: On the Convergence of Success Conditioning for Policy Optimization

author.name: Matthew Brun, Xu Andy Sun

entry.summary: This paper provides formal convergence guarantees for success conditioning, a widely used strategy that reinforces actions leading to successful outcomes in stochastic environments. The authors prove convergence to optimal policies on a broad class of MDPs and derive rates, including O(1/eps^p) iteration bounds for discounted MDPs and results for single-period settings. This puts a common heuristic in RL practice on firmer theoretical footing.

entry.title: RINS: Residual-Image Neural Subspace Solvers for Large Sparse Linear Systems

author.name: Zhongyan Ouyang, Weixin Liao, Mingquan Feng, Yehui Tang, Junchi Yan

entry.summary: Gate-RINS is a neural subspace solver for large sparse linear systems from PDE discretizations that generates polynomial correction bases from cached residual probes, modulated by a lightweight pointwise gate. The projected least-squares update is unchanged, so the neural component only picks expansion directions while numerical closure tests them. Experiments across six PDE-derived benchmarks plus a hybrid controller schedule show improved solver behavior.

entry.title: High-Dimensional Asymptotics and Dataset Selection for Private Transfer Learning

author.name: Filip Kova\v{c}evi\'c, Edwige Cyffers, Stefano Sarao Mannelli, Marco Mondelli

entry.summary: The paper models when acquiring external, potentially sensitive data justifies its cost for transfer learning, using high-dimensional regression with heterogeneous sources and weighted ridge estimation. It accounts for negative transfer and the noise injected by differential privacy, providing theoretical guidance for data purchasing and collaborative learning decisions.

entry.title: Clinical Concept Centers in LLMs

author.name: Aishik Nagar, Abhishek Vaidyanathan, Arun-Kumar Kaliya-Perumal, Elijah Tzen Hsuen Boey, Stefan Winkler

entry.summary: This work extends mechanistic interpretability into clinical decision support, asking whether clinical concepts are linearly encoded in LLM latent spaces. Building on findings that internal representations encode more than verbalized output, it probes whether latent-space evaluation can reveal clinically relevant structure that stated reasoning omits.

entry.title: Mixture-of-Experts for Cryptocurrency Order Execution: Training Stability, Tail Risk, and Failure Modes

author.name: Alexander Ardaiz, Varun Budati, Ali Habibnia

entry.summary: This paper evaluates DDQL and K-means-partitioned mixture-of-DDQL-experts against parameter-matched dense networks on BTC/USDT limit order book data, finding no learned configuration significantly improves mean implementation shortfall over vanilla DDQL, and all underperform simple baselines like TWAP. It highlights training-seed variance as a source of spurious architectural gains and analyzes tail risk and failure modes. A valuable cautionary result about RL in financial execution.

entry.title: Amortized Structured Stochastic Variational Inference for Gaussian Process Latent Variable Models

author.name: Maksym Tretiakov, Sarah Lucie Filipp, Vincent Fortuin, Ruth Misener, Ruby Sedgwick, James Odgers

entry.summary: The paper improves uncertainty estimation in Gaussian Process Latent Variable Models by replacing the standard mean-field variational approximation with amortized structured stochastic variational inference, allowing the latent-space posterior to be conditionally dependent on GP inducing points. This captures epistemic uncertainty of the learned manifold more faithfully. Results demonstrate improved behavior over the mean-field baseline.

entry.title: EpiWorld: Grounding LLM Policy Agents in Epidemiological World Models

author.name: Zeeshan Memon, Yiqi Su, Kai Shu, Naren Ramakrishnan, Liang Zhao

entry.summary: EpiWorld is a closed-loop framework that grounds an LLM policy agent in a learned action-conditioned epidemiological world model plus a tiered skill library of public-health protocols and surveillance tools. It aims to let LLMs reason about epidemic interventions with realistic dynamics, quantitative signals, and institutional constraints.

entry.title: Adaptive Mutual Distillation for Balanced Multi-Task Post-Training of Large Language Models

author.name: Baohang Li, Xiaocheng Feng, Yichong Huang, Chengpeng Fu, Wenshuai Huo, Zekun Zhou, Zekun Yuan, Tingjia Zhang, Bing Qin

entry.summary: AMD is a post-training framework in which two LLMs trained with different task-balancing strategies distill from each other, using short shared training probes to adaptively weight cross-model supervision across tasks, transfer directions, and training stages. It aims to combine complementary task strengths in multi-task post-training.

entry.title: Investigating the Role of Reasoning-Language Alignment in Monolingual Retrieval-Augmented Generation

author.name: Oliver Hauck, Mario Sanz-Guerrero, Katharina von der Wense

entry.summary: This study examines whether forcing models to reason in a non-English language degrades RAG accuracy, extending prior short-prompt findings to settings where the model must integrate large amounts of retrieved German evidence. It builds a fully monolingual German RAG testbed over The Dark Eye tabletop RPG world, a niche but richly documented German domain.

entry.title: Writerslogic at PAN 2026: Process over Content for Robust Detection under Domain Shift

author.name: David L. Condrey

entry.summary: This paper describes systems for three PAN 2026 shared tasks unified by a shared analytical framework: feature robustness under distribution shift is governed by support overlap between training and test distributions, yielding a taxonomy of domain-anchored, domain-portable, and domain-invariant features. It explains why generator-specific features fail under domain shift while vocabulary fingerprints, compression measures, and character n-grams survive.

entry.title: Confidence-Controlled XAI Auditing for Pedestrian Detection under Domain Shift

author.name: Ruben Dario Florez-Zela

entry.summary: Audits post-hoc explanation faithfulness for a YOLOv8s pedestrian detector across the PIE and JAAD driving datasets using ROI-based D-Deletion, confidence stratification, and statistical corrections. Findings show deletion-based faithfulness is strongly coupled to detection strength at explanation time, and after controlling for it, D-RISE faithfulness remains domain-dependent in central confidence bins.

entry.title: Capturing Dynamics: The 4D Facial Expression Intensity Dataset

author.name: Zesheng Wang, Alexandre Bruckert, Pierre Lebreton, Patrick Le Callet, Yante Li, Guoying Zhao

entry.summary: Introduces 4DFEID, a dataset of 2,869 mesh sequences generated with parametric face models under controlled geometric variations, enabling study of facial expression intensity in genuinely 3D and temporally continuous form rather than frame-level 2D representations. The dataset supports perception and analysis tasks relevant to affective computing and human-computer interaction.

entry.title: CrowdOcc: Monocular Semantic Scene Completion for Quadruped Robots in Crowded Indoor Environments

author.name: Feiyang Chen, Jincheng Hu, Yiduo Chen, Jihao Li, Yue Liang, Bingzhao Gao, Yanjun Huang, Yuanjian Zhang

entry.summary: CrowdOcc contributes an RGB-D dataset of 25.1K frames from 11 crowded indoor scenes plus a monocular semantic scene completion framework for quadruped robots. It combines normal-guided geometry fusion for occlusion robustness with human-centric sparse interaction modeling to improve human occupancy prediction.

entry.title: Geometry-Aligned Semantic Matching for Cross-Modal Planar Image Registration

author.name: Zhiwei Wang, Defeng He, Yuxing Li, Meilu Zhu, Edmund Y. Lam

entry.summary: CDPM addresses cross-modal image matching by progressively adapting DINOv3 to produce geometrically consistent semantic representations, then preserving their dominance during fine-grained correspondence estimation. The method bridges the gap between semantically consistent but geometrically loose features and accurate local CNN details.

entry.title: Interpretable Deepfake Detection in Videos via Explicit Forensic Features and Temporal Modeling

author.name: Chahira Benhama, Mohand Sa\"id Allili, Assia Hamadene

entry.summary: This work proposes an interpretable deepfake video detection framework that explicitly encodes physically grounded forensic cues over temporal windows of identity-consistent facial trajectories, using 68 structured descriptors per frame. The explicit representation enables transparent analysis and improved generalization across datasets compared to end-to-end black-box detectors.

entry.title: From Language Priors to Field Adaptation: Preference Learning for Traversability Estimation

author.name: Simon Schwaiger, David Seyser, Alessandro Scherl, Zlatan Ajanovi\'c, Wilfried W\"ober, Gerald Steinbauer-Wagner

entry.summary: Proposes sample-efficient preference learning for image-based traversability estimation, using von Mises-Fisher mixture prototypes in a frozen vision-language feature space. Natural-language relative rules provide a commonsense prior while sparse relative image annotations adapt the prototypes to a target domain, matching fully supervised WayFAST accuracy with far fewer labels.

entry.title: RUL-Aware RRT*: Degradation-Balanced Motion Planning for Robotic Manipulators

author.name: Haibo Li, Zhiguo Zeng, Xu Li

entry.summary: This work extends RRT* motion planning for robotic manipulators by incorporating joint remaining-useful-life (RUL) information, adaptively shifting joint usage away from the most degraded actuators. Evaluated across full-health, heterogeneous-degradation, and other scenarios, it aims to prevent premature failure of the weakest joint and reduce unplanned downtime. This connects prognostics and health management with motion planning.

entry.title: Cross-Fitting Under Nonregularity: Normality and Inference via Locality

author.name: Bruno Fava

entry.summary: This statistics paper studies confidence intervals for cross-fitted estimators when standard asymptotics fail due to nonregularity, as in model-comparison via cross-validation, heterogeneous treatment effect testing, and optimal treatment regime estimation. Using a new locality condition, the author proves a central limit theorem still holds but with an asymptotic variance corrected for cross-fold correlation. This yields valid inference in settings where naive cross-fit intervals undercover.

entry.title: Label-Efficient Time Series Classification at Scale: A Dual-Stream OSSE-LSTM with Counterfactual Attribution

author.name: Nguyen Ho, Bach Tung Tran, Trung Ky Nguyen, Zhenchang Xia, Bolong Zheng, Long Van Ho

entry.summary: The paper studies few-shot time series classification in a fixed-label regime with only K labeled examples per class, proposing Dual-Stream OSSE-LSTM, an episodic metric-learning framework pairing an Omni-Scale CNN with Squeeze-and-Excitation recalibration and counterfactual attribution. It targets label-scarce industrial, wearable, and clinical monitoring settings.

entry.title: DNAlign: Dynamic Null-Space Safe Alignment for LLMs

author.name: Jisheng Dang, Yushuo Zhao, Dewei Liu, Junfeng Fang, Bimei Wang, Tiantian Rao, Hong Peng, Bin Hu, Tat-Seng Chua

entry.summary: DNAlign is a lightweight safety alignment framework that treats the LLM as a dynamic system and applies control-theoretic perturbations restricted via null-space projection to the harm-related subspace, aiming to steer generation toward safe behavior without degrading general capabilities. It targets the persistent safety-utility trade-off in alignment.

entry.title: When to Compile a Computer-Use Agent? Measuring Payback and Making Compilation Decisions for Token Efficiency

author.name: Yulong Ming, Jie Xu, Zihan Wu, Xiaohua Jia

entry.summary: PACE is a system that decides when compiling repeatedly executed GUI procedures into programs is worthwhile, with a measurement protocol recording successful and failed compilation costs and an online algorithm weighing uncertain payback against unknown future reuse and GUI drift. It compares agent and program execution costs on matched inputs to estimate per-use savings.

entry.title: MRVQ: One Resident Index for Dimension- and Rate-Elastic Vector Search

author.name: Sean Culatana, Shang-En Huang, Kang Li

entry.summary: MRVQ (Matryoshka Residual Vector Quantization) is a post-hoc quantizer for frozen embeddings whose single maximum-rate code can be truncated both by dropping residual stages (lowering rate) and dropping coordinates (lowering dimension), so one artifact serves every dimension-rate pair. Across two datasets, four embedding families, and multiple code sizes, it achieves the lowest RAM of evaluated designs with strong quality.

entry.title: EviDent-CBCT: Evidence-Bottlenecked Report Generation from Dental CBCT under Non-Exhaustive Report Supervision

author.name: Ruiyang Hao, Zhi Qin Tan, Yulan He, Owen Addison, Yunpeng Li

entry.summary: EviDent-CBCT generates dento-maxillofacial CBCT reports from 3D scans under incomplete supervision, where non-mention of a finding may reflect absence or non-reporting. An anatomy-aware network produces a discrete evidence record, a dental-logic consistency projection reconciles incompatible findings, and an image-blind local language model renders the report from that record. The evidence-bottleneck design addresses both reliability and the messy realities of clinical documentation.

entry.title: Approximation Property of Dropout Neural Networks: Sobolev Rates and Confidence Bounds

author.name: Jia-He Yao

entry.summary: This theory paper establishes finite-sample, high-probability uniform approximation rates for ReLU networks with independently dropped edges, constructing constant-depth networks of size on the order of p^-9 times Sobolev-unit-ball error terms with confidence bounds. It also derives matching Sobolev lower bounds. The work quantifies how dropout randomness affects approximation, bridging universal approximation and probabilistic guarantees.

entry.title: Bandits via Additive Quantized Representations

author.name: Ami Tavory, Noam Touitou, Tal Sarig, Frank Cheng, Ido Guy

entry.summary: The paper uses offline-trained residual quantization codebooks as a representation layer for contextual bandits, mapping continuous contexts into discrete multi-level centroid assignments with bounded O(1)-style memory. This yields additive bandit algorithms with nonlinear expressivity without retraining or large replay buffers, beating non-RQ counterparts across 13 datasets. Likely from an industrial team addressing online efficiency.

entry.title: Efficient Memory Crystallization for Graph Learning under Non-Stationary Distribution Shifts

author.name: Yue Hou, Ruomei Liu, Yingke Su, Junran Wu, Ke Xu

entry.summary: EMC is a training-free test-time framework that distills each incoming graph domain into a compact memory via a closed-form solution to a memory-oriented objective, avoiding costly auxiliary generative modules used for cross-domain graph adaptation. This targets non-stationary graph distribution shifts more efficiently than generative memory synthesis.

entry.title: Adaptive Second-Order Solvers for Fast Stochastic Diffusion Sampling

author.name: Ella Kemperman, Luca Ambrogioni

entry.summary: The authors adapt proportional-integral step-size control to diffusion model sampling using a diffusion noise-normalized error estimator, incorporating previous errors for smoother step adaptation. They also show per-sample trajectories share structure that can be aggregated into a fixed schedule, retaining speed benefits without runtime adaptation.

entry.title: Dual-Context Analog Retrieval for Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Jung Min Choi, Ngoc Son Le, Ibram Abdelmalak, Vijaya Krishna Yalavarthi, Lars Schmidt-Thieme

entry.summary: DuoTS improves long-term time-series forecasting by retrieving past states analogous to the present and progressively integrating their observed continuations as evidence, rather than relying on a single nearest match. It combines a parallel patch encoder base forecast with retrieval-augmented refinement to avoid unreliable single analogs and redundant patch candidates.

entry.title: Conformal Prediction for Time Series with Deep Sequence Models

author.name: Junghwan Lee, Jonghyeok Lee, Yao Xie

entry.summary: This paper surveys how deep sequence models, including RNNs and Transformers, can be integrated into conformal prediction frameworks for time series, where exchangeability-based coverage guarantees fail. It systematizes the design space and studies how deep model properties interact with conformal calibration for reliable uncertainty quantification in forecasting. This serves as a structured reference for a fast-moving area.

entry.title: Explainable Molecular Structure Inference from GC--MS with Diffusion Models and LLM Reranking

author.name: Changlin Liu, Tianyu Yi, Chengchun Liu, Boxuan Zhao, Fanyang Mo

entry.summary: DiffGCMS is a spectrum-conditioned discrete graph diffusion model for de novo molecular structure elucidation from GC-EI-MS data, addressing the limitation of reference-library matching for unknown compounds.
