entry.summary: Quantifies the decomposition tax: accuracy lost when pipeline stages cannot see the original problem, showing losses up to 40.5 points across 21 open-weight models on GSM-Hard and MATH-500 with rigorous multiple-comparison corrections. A placebo control confirms the effect is informational, not token-length related.

entry.title: Logical subspace in LLMs

author.name: Hope Kean, Enric Boix-Adsera

entry.summary: This paper introduces the minimal viable subspace (MVS) method, which finds the lowest-rank activation subspace at a layer that preserves task performance when all other directions are ablated. Inspired by a human brain network specialized for abstract formal reasoning, the authors show that Gemma and Qwen models contain low-rank subspaces supporting logical inference that are dissociable from other capacities: retaining these late-layer logic subspaces preserves inference while impairing factual knowledge, working memory, cognitive control, and arithmetic. This matters because it provides causal, mechanistic evidence that formal reasoning is spatially localized in LLMs, paralleling findings in neuroscience and informing interpretability and targeted editing research.

entry.title: Population Physics, Population Problems: Safety and Emergence in LLM Societies

author.name: Adrian de Wynter

entry.summary: This paper introduces a framework for measuring self-organisation in societies of LLM agents, applied to a Schelling grid, a social network, and a Twitter-like misinformation simulation. All three systems exhibit statistically significant emergent self-organisation whose relaxation dynamics depend on environmental information, arguing that single-agent analysis tools do not scale to collectives. This is directly relevant to AI safety given recent incidents involving autonomous agentic systems.

entry.title: Weeding Out Bad Seeds: Initial-Noise-Robust Unlearning for Text-to-Image Diffusion Models

author.name: Arian Komaei Koma, Seyed Amir Kasaei, Aida Aryafar, Matin Ghiasi, Ali Aghayari, Amirhossein Souri, Mohammad Mosayyebi, AmirMahdi Sadeghzadeh, Mohammad Hossein Rohban

entry.summary: This paper reveals probabilistic forgetting in text-to-image unlearning: state-of-the-art methods appear to erase a concept but it re-emerges under specific random initial-noise conditions. The authors trace the failure to misalignment between uniform Gaussian noise sampling and the unlearning objective, and propose noise-robust unlearning that targets the initial-noise regions where concepts actually manifest.

entry.title: OmniTaskonomy: When Does Visual Generation Improve Visual Understanding?

author.name: Jiaxin Ge, Yiming Qin, Ji Xie, Haozhe Jiang, Xiaochuang Han, Junyi Zhang, Andrew Dai, Yinfei Yang, Jitendra Malik, Ranjay Krishna, Sewon Min, Haiwen Feng, Le Xue, Baifeng Shi, Trevor Darrell, XuDong Wang

entry.summary: This large-scale study asks when and how image-to-image generation supervision improves image-to-text visual understanding, using controlled task pairs expressing the same problem in different output modalities. It finds that with the right recipe, generation training improves understanding with gains scaling in data volume, and maps which generation tasks transfer to which understanding capabilities.

entry.title: Rethinking Representations for World-Action Modeling

author.name: Haoyi Jiang, Liu Liu, Xinjiang Wang, Zhihao Sun, Zequn Chen, Sen Wang, Xinjie Wang, Xia Chen, Jingfeng Yao, Weiheng Zhao, Shanglin Yuan, Zhizhong Su, Wei Sui, Wenyu Liu, Xinggang Wang

entry.summary: This paper studies the representation space shared by robot policies and future-observation prediction in world-action models, finding via controlled comparisons that neither reconstruction fidelity nor pre-trained perceptual features alone ensure effective policy learning. It proposes ReWAM, built on DINO features with Feature Calibration, a Temporal Representation Bottleneck, and Action-Grounded Representation Shaping that routes only action-loss gradients so the policy shapes the representation. This is a principled contribution to robot learning architectures.

entry.title: PhysWAM: Physically Consistent World Action Model for Autonomous Driving

author.name: Dhruv Parikh, Fengcheng Yu, Quankai Gao, Jiawei Yang, Junjie Ye, Maulik Bhatt, Thang Vu, Charles Ochoa, Rowan McAllister, Igor Vasiljevic, Rajgopal Kannan, Viktor Prasanna, Vitor Guizilini, Yue Wang

entry.summary: PhysWAM co-denoises multiview video, metric depth, and ego motion within a single flow-matching transformer for autonomous driving. Its Coupled Point Projection unprojects generated depth into 3D points, transforms them with generated SE(3) ego motion, and constrains them against LiDAR points, imposing a shared geometric constraint on world and action predictions. This promotes physical consistency between predicted scene evolution and planned actions.

entry.title: Rho: A Foundation for Efficiently Adaptable VLA Models

author.name: Rho Team, Simran Bagaria, Daphne Chen, Dean Fortier, Jianlong Fu, Michael Harrison, Tess Hellebrekers, Neel Joshi, Andrey Kolobov, Dalton Moore, Galen Mullins, Michael Murray, Eduardo Salinas, Reuben Tan

entry.summary: Rho is a family of open-weights VLA models for bimanual manipulation across three representative dual-arm embodiments (YAM Box, UR AI Trainer, FR3 Duo), designed for data-light downstream adaptation. The paper systematically ablates action-expert architecture and training recipe, showing that embodiment midtraining improves downstream adaptation, with variants matching or outperforming existing open-weights VLAs. Open weights plus a rigorous ablation study make this a useful reference point for the community.

entry.title: Transformers Stop Thinking Too Early, and a Tiny LoRA Fixes It

author.name: Zehao Jin, Ruixuan Deng, Junran Wang

entry.summary: This interpretability-flavored paper finds that pretrained transformers use little of their depth for in-context reference chains: thirteen base models reliably follow only 1.4-3.6 lines. A task-trained rank-8 LoRA at one early layer, with all other weights frozen, dramatically extends this, Qwen3-8B jumps from 15.5% to 99% accuracy on 24-line chains, and a relay mechanism through middle layers is identified via attention analysis.

entry.title: Breaking the Illusion of Review Reliability under Static Evaluation: SCOPE Fuzzing for LLM-based Scientific Reviewers

author.name: Zhuo Chen, Hao Zeng, Jiawei Liu, Guoxiu He, Le Cai, Liu Haotan, Li Wenbo, Yong Huang, Wei Lu

entry.summary: SCOPE constructs a three-level fuzzing framework perturbing surface presentation, argumentative logic, and value judgment to stress-test LLM-based scientific reviewers beyond static template perturbations. Experiments reveal stratified vulnerability, where perturbation effects depend on paper characteristics, undermining prior conclusions about reviewer reliability. The work has direct implications for the growing use of LLMs in peer review.

entry.title: Train Ahead, Distill Back: Bootstrapping On-Policy Self-Distillation for Large Language Models

author.name: Zheng Zhang, Xinyue Tan, Lufei Li, Xinyi Zhang, Yexin Li, Kan Ren

entry.summary: B-OPSD recycles a model's own optimization progress to build a stronger self-teacher: the policy is temporarily trained ahead to obtain a future teacher, the student is restored to its original state, and the future teacher provides dense token-level supervision on the student's own trajectories. This escapes the ceiling where self-distillation quality is limited by the current policy's ability to exploit privileged information. The bootstrap idea is simple and potentially broadly applicable.

entry.title: MoRE: Scaling mixture of experts with hardware-aware low-rank routing

author.name: Honam Wong, Surbhi Goel, Enric Boix-Adser\`a

entry.summary: MoRE factorizes the MoE router weight matrix to low rank r, reducing per-token routing cost from Theta(Mh) to O((h+M)r), which becomes critical as architectures move toward many small experts. The paper proves logarithmic rank suffices for routing expressivity with fixed active experts, is necessary up to precision factors, and preserves load balance in a Gaussian memorization model.

entry.title: Simple Diffusion Language Models Are More Effective Few-Step Generators Than Reported

author.name: Hasan Amin, Ming Yin, Rajiv Khanna

entry.summary: This paper argues that the reported quality gap of diffusion language models at few generation steps is largely an artifact of suboptimally configured samplers rather than model capability. With modest sampler sharpening and no retraining, an older masked diffusion LM rivals newer successors, achieving lower generative perplexity in 16 steps than the standard sampler achieves in 1024 steps while improving judged quality and semantic diversity. This reframes the few-step generation literature.

entry.title: Can LLMs Value the Right Evidence? Evidence-Value Misalignment in Dynamic Medical Diagnosis

author.name: Kehua Feng, Yunsheng Lu, Yitong Qiao, Tiantian He, Lei Liu, Yue Shen, Jian Wang, Jinjie Gu

entry.summary: The paper introduces Evidence-Value Misalignment, the hazard of LLMs reaching correct diagnoses from insufficient or misleading evidence, which outcome-based accuracy metrics reward as lucky guesses. MedEVM, a dynamic benchmark with 1,050 cases across 24 disease systems, forces models to decide turn by turn whether to gather more evidence or commit to a diagnosis, revealing patterns like miscalibrated evidence tracking across nine LLMs. This has direct clinical safety relevance for LLM-assisted diagnosis.

entry.title: Planetary Feature Fields are Scalable Earth Representations

author.name: Arjun Rao, Sebastian Loeschcke, Anthony Fuller, Isaac Corley, Nico Lang, Evan Shelhamer

entry.summary: Planetary Feature Fields jointly model satellite observations, precomputed embeddings, and map products as continuous functions of space and time at planetary scale, using spatially local hybrid neural fields that share a factored feature volume across products with lightweight per-product implicit decoders. This compresses petabyte-scale, redundant earth data products while preserving spatial and temporal detail.

entry.title: WorldLine: Action-Driven Visual Simulation for Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Shenghe Zheng, Wenbo Li, Jiyao Zhang, Bin Xia, Haoyang Huang, Nan Duan, Jiaya Jia

entry.summary: WorldLine is an action-driven visual simulator that decouples transferable dynamics learning from heterogeneous action grounding, learning manipulation dynamics from over 10,000 hours of action-free robot videos and grounding them to specific embodiments separately. This addresses the scarcity of embodiment-specific action-conditioned data and improves action following versus purely plausible video generation. It enables scalable prediction of action outcomes before physical execution.

entry.title: Divide and Inject: Can Agents Reconstruct an Indirect Prompt Injection from Fragments?

author.name: Michael Lee, Zhipeng Wei, Yue Dong, N. Benjamin Erichson

entry.summary: This security paper introduces AdaLCPI, an adaptive long-context prompt injection attack that splits a malicious objective into incomplete fragments distributed across retrieved content, betting that the agent will reconstruct the instruction from pieces. The attack combines long-context fragmentation with adaptive search and a reconstruction signal. It exposes a new attack surface beyond complete-injection assumptions.

entry.title: SCA: Spatial Credit Assignment for Reinforcement Learning of GUI Agents

author.name: Shengtian Yang, Ziyu Xiong, Kaibing Yang, Guangfeng Cai, Yewen Li, Peng Jiang, Gai Kun, Qingpeng Cai, Lei Feng

entry.summary: SCA improves group-relative RL for GUI agents by using the screen coordinates of sampled clicks to provide finer-grained credit than binary success/failure rewards. It predicts held-out responses' rewards from other group members and uses prediction residuals to adjust credit, giving signal even when all sampled clicks fail. This directly addresses sparse, uninformative reward signals in GUI agent training.

entry.title: Boundary-State Control for Tool-Using Language-Model Agents: Commit-Time Consistency under State Drift

author.name: Wesley Shu

entry.summary: This paper addresses the proposal-to-commit gap in tool-using agents, where an authorized action executes only after security-relevant state has changed. BSC-R binds single-use commit authorization to the exact action and a semantic projection of the justifying state; on 2,847 attacked AgentDojo episodes it preserves baseline utility (80.576%) while holding attack success to 1.616%, and rejects all ten specified drift/replay classes in a frozen-proposal study.

entry.title: EngiWorld: What Can Frontier Agents Deliver in Professional Engineering Environments?

author.name: Hongcheng Gao, Hailong Qu, Yu Lei, Henghui Sun, Haoyang Li, Yipeng Wei, Naihao Xue, Xiaohan Yu, Zhuo Tao, Yihe Zang, Yajiao Wang, Jingyi Tang, Yi Li, Jingjing Zhou, Jie Luo, Bohan Zeng, Chengyu Shen, Hao Jiang, Chong Chen, Bowen Qu, Olive Huang, Zeqiang Wang

entry.summary: EngiWorld is a benchmark of 1,301 expert-curated tasks spanning six engineering domains (CAD, CAE, CAM, BIM, EDA, 3D visualization) and 26 professional software platforms, with GUI and CLI interfaces, six task types, and artifact-centric evaluation via a unified domain-verifier suite. It targets the gap between general computer-use progress and reliable automation of professional engineering workflows requiring geometric and physical reasoning.

entry.title: Cheap to Hypothesize, Costly to Verify: The Defense Surface of Agentic Vulnerability Discovery

author.name: Kaikai Zhang, Zihan Zhang, Yuchong Xie, Zesen Liu, Shuangjie Yao, Zhixiang Zhang, Dongdong She

entry.summary: The paper characterizes autonomous LLM-driven vulnerability discovery as a resource-bounded selective-verification process, showing that verifying hypotheses is far costlier than generating them. It introduces RedHerring, a defensive technique that inserts certifiably safe decoy vulnerabilities to exhaust an attacker agent's verification budget. This reframes defense around draining adversarial compute rather than patching bugs.

entry.title: The Uneven Decline of Collective Knowledge Production: Evidence from Stack Overflow After Generative AI

author.name: Myokyung Han, Taegyoon Kim, Jinhyuk Yun, Lanu Kim

entry.summary: This empirical study treats ChatGPT-3.5's release as a natural shock to analyze how generative AI affected collective knowledge production on Stack Overflow, using over two million questions from 2020-2025. It goes beyond aggregate participation decline to identify which kinds of knowledge are lost first, tracking difficulty and data availability dimensions with difference-in-differences methods. The findings illuminate how AI may erode the public knowledge commons.

entry.title: SCOUT: Synergizing Reasoning and Tool-Use for Computer-Use Safety

author.name: Jianxing Chen, Xiao Yu, Shipra Agrawal, Zhou Yu

entry.summary: SCOUT is a two-stage agentic safety verifier for computer-use agents that combines task-specific harmfulness reasoning with active investigation of the environment, since screenshots alone cannot reveal what actions actually changed. This addresses subtle harm detection that screenshot-only LLM-as-judge verifiers miss.

entry.title: Inducing Process Supervision from Outcome-Only Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Shengda Fan, Xin Cong, Zhong Zhang, Haotian Chen, Yankai Lin

entry.summary: TIPS trains generative process reward models using outcome-only RL, avoiding expensive human step annotation and Monte Carlo estimation. The model generates a chain of thought followed by step-level and outcome labels, with reward depending solely on outcome correctness, inducing step-level supervision through group-relative optimization. This offers a low-cost path to the strong PRMs that support post-training and test-time reasoning for LLMs.

entry.title: Trajectory Soup: Pushing the Compute-Scaling Frontier of LLM Mid-training via Diverse Trajectories

author.name: Zhehao Huang, Changxin Tian, Qingyuan Yang, Kunlong Chen, Ziqi Liu, Zhiqiang Zhang, Xiaolin Huang, Jun Zhou

entry.summary: The authors observe that returns from LLM mid-training saturate under serial compute, and that branches forked from a shared checkpoint under different recipes explore measurably different parameter regions with compatible diversity. Their Trajectory Soup method distributes a mid-training budget across multiple runs and merges them, extending the compute-scaling frontier. This is a notable efficiency result for how mid-training compute should be allocated.

entry.title: GLaS-JEPA: Gaussian-Regularized Speech SSL without Engineered Prediction Targets

author.name: Gaspard Bott\'e, S\'everin Baroudi, Samir Sadok, Francesco Paissan, Thomas Hueber, Xavier Alameda-Pineda, Ricard Marxer, Mirco Ravanelli

entry.summary: GLaS-JEPA shows that speech self-supervised learning can work by directly predicting the encoder's own continuous representations at masked positions, using SIGReg regularization to prevent collapse, without contrastive learning, discrete targets, or EMA teacher encoders. A 57M-parameter model trained on 960 hours of LibriSpeech achieves 6.89% WER on frozen-encoder SUPERB ASR, outperforming the best non-distilled baselines. It significantly simplifies the recipe for speech SSL.

entry.title: VC Dimension and Expressivity of Real-Valued Transformers

author.name: Gavin Dooley, Andy Yang, Yijia Jessica Zhu, David Chiang, Peter Cholak, Anand Pillay

entry.summary: Under minimal assumptions, this theoretical work derives upper bounds on the VC dimension and split VC dimension of real-valued softmax-attention transformers (O(n^4) and O(n^6) in input length n) and constructs transformers achieving Omega(n) lower bounds. Consequences include the result that transformers can uniformly express all symmetric functions within that class.

entry.title: A Solvable Theory of Pre-training Data Poisoning: Regime-Dependent Scaling Exponents

author.name: Indranil Halder, Rastri Dey, Cengiz Pehlevan

entry.summary: Motivated by controlled OLMo-style pre-training runs where clean-data perplexity degradation from poisoning follows a power law with non-integer exponent, the authors develop a theory of how poisoning rate affects model performance. They prove an analyticity barrier showing such non-integer exponents require regime changes, providing a solvable framework for poisoning damage scaling beyond backdoor analyses.

entry.title: Save Your Saturated Data: Learning Beyond Reward Saturation in Group-Based RL

author.name: Ziyuan Yang, Yike Wang, Shangbin Feng, Yulia Tsvetkov

entry.summary: This paper tackles reward saturation in group-relative RL (GRPO-style) for increasingly capable language models, where all sampled responses receive equally high rewards and learning signals vanish. It systematically studies interventions at data, rollout, reward, and advantage levels to recover useful learning signals from saturated reasoning data.

entry.title: Do We Really Need KL Divergence for On-Policy Distillation of Large Language Models?

author.name: Wenze Lin, Jiyuan Long, Jiale Zhao, Shenzhi Wang, Xitai Jiang, Ce Luo, Rui Lan, Qianli Ma, Fukang Wen, Hui Wu, Liyuan Chen, Shuoling Liu, Jiangpeng Yan, Gao Huang

entry.summary: This paper challenges the default use of KL divergence in on-policy distillation, showing that simply preserving the update direction toward the teacher suffices — specifically on the small subset of tokens where teacher and student strongly disagree, even a simple +1/-1 reward assignment works. This simplifies and potentially cheapens OPD for LLM post-training. The finding questions long-standing distillation orthodoxy with broad practical implications.

entry.title: No Free Efficiency: Revisiting the Trade-off Between Training Efficiency and Model Vulnerability

author.name: Yiyong Liu, Jun Sakuma, Michael Backes, Rui Wen

entry.summary: Presents the first systematic cross-domain investigation of whether efficiency-oriented training strategies such as selective data sampling, efficient pre-training, and simplified RL pipelines increase model susceptibility to adversarial and privacy attacks. Across vision and language models, the study shows that efficiency gains come at a measurable robustness and security cost.

entry.title: Broken Symmetry in BF16 Attention: Why FlashAttention Gradients Blow Up Late in Training

author.name: Junlin Chen, Daize Dong, Huanwei Di, Haolong Jia, Jiawei Wu, Haotian Xie, Mingkai Zheng, Yang Li, Leshang Chen, Huishu Wang, Eric P. Xing, Hongyi Wang

entry.summary: While pretraining a 450M transformer on 50B tokens with FlashAttention-3, the authors found gradients grew a thousandfold after 25B healthy tokens, ending 0.2 nats above FP32 attention without any NaN. They diagnose a fused multiply-add bug in the forward softmax plus an additional symmetry-breaking query-gradient issue, with recomputation and repairs that stop the blow-up.

entry.title: One Rollout Is All You Get: Fully Test-Time Adaptation for GUI Agents

author.name: Ziqiang Wang, Li Gu, Zhixiang Chi, Linlian Jiang, Zihuan Jiang, Linqiang Guo, Siobhan Reid, Zhi Liu, Yang Wang

entry.summary: This work formalizes fully test-time adaptation for GUI agents, where no ground truth exists, actions can be irreversible, and only a single rollout is available per task. The proposed SOLO method uses auxiliary judge and proposer-verifier models to select and relabel episodes for lightweight weight-space updates during deployment.

entry.title: VEX-Bench: Benchmarking Verification Complexity of LLM-Generated Misinformation

author.name: Hanxun Huang, Yutao Wu, Qizhou Wang, Silvia Monta\~na-Ni\~no, Yige Li, Xiang Zheng, Elif Buse Doyuran, Phoebe Matich, Xiao Liu, Xingjun Ma, Sarah Erfani, Christopher Leckie

entry.summary: VEX-Bench is a benchmark for measuring how hard LLM-generated misinformation is to verify during screening, with dimensions drawn from journalistic and fact-checking practice including checkability, harm potential, source credibility signals, and imposter legitimacy. It quantifies the growing asymmetry between cheap AI misinformation production and costly verification.

entry.title: First Learn, Then Memorize: The Spectral Bias of Diffusion Models

author.name: Rapha\"el Urfin, Tony Bonnaire, Giulio Biroli, Marc M\'ezard

entry.summary: Identifies the mechanism behind the timescale separation in diffusion models between generating novel samples and later collapsing onto training data, showing that score-training dynamics are governed by the Gram matrix of the NTK on noisy training data. Demonstrates that multiple noise realizations per sample restructure this spectrum, producing the learn-then-memorize behavior.

entry.title: ReSPO: Reshaped Sequence Policy Optimization for Gradient Starvation in Off-Policy Learning

author.name: Yihang Chen, Yuanhao Ban, Cho-Jui Hsieh

entry.summary: The paper identifies a sign-dependent gradient starvation problem in clipped policy optimization for RLVR, where clipping suppresses under-generated positive responses while over-generated negative responses dominate. ReSPO replaces clipping with a smooth two_branch sequence-level kernel derived from an alpha-divergence objective plus variance control, preserving useful gradient signal.

entry.title: ScAn-Bench: Evaluating Scaling Analysis Methodology

author.name: Artin Sermaxhaj, Nastaran Alipour, Donat Sinani, Johannes Hog, Neeratyoy Mallik, Jenia Jitsev, Danny Stoll

entry.summary: ScAn-Bench introduces surrogate benchmarks built from 4524 language model and 8024 vision-language model checkpoints to systematically evaluate how scaling laws and scaling prescriptions are derived. It enables the first controlled study of data acquisition and extrapolation methodology for scaling analysis across model types, addressing a notable blind spot given how much compute decisions rest on scaling laws.

entry.title: Prompting Particle Physics: Tokenized Multi-modal Foundation Models for Combinatorially Many Tasks

author.name: Nilotpal Kakati, Daniel Murnane, Baran Hashemi, Samuel Klein, Jeffrey Krupa, Eilam Gross, Lukas Heinrich, Michael Kagan

entry.summary: The authors build a shared token vocabulary over collider objects (tracks, calorimeter cells, clusters, particles, jets) and train one model to map any modality subset to any other, making particle flow, detector simulation, and energy subtraction directions through the same weights. This foundation-model approach replaces chains of specialized algorithms while retaining interpretable intermediate objects.

entry.title: Transformer MLP Gate Thresholds Are Couplings to a Carried Reference Direction

author.name: Olli Tuomi

entry.summary: Using exact decompositions in Phi-2, the author shows that the corpus-mean residual stream direction is functionally significant: at mid-stack layers the resting inhibition of over 99.9% of MLP gates is carried by the coupling to this mean direction, at 48-56x the explicit bias, and the effect is direction-specific with Spearman rho up to 0.95. This challenges the standard practice of mean-centering before interpretability analysis.

entry.title: Contamination, Prior, or Evidence? Decomposing and Training Evidence Use in Whole-Slide Vision-Language Models

author.name: Wenhao Zhang, Zhongliang Zhou, Shiyuan Zhang, Yiqing Yang, Pinqiao Wang, Lehan Yang, Hanyin Wang, John Kang, Sheng Li

entry.summary: This study shows that most public pathology VLMs perform nearly identically whether given whole-slide images, annotated lesions, or no image at all on lymph-node metastasis prediction, indicating accuracy conflates contamination, priors, and genuine image evidence. The authors introduce CleanSlide, a 149K-question TCGA-based VQA benchmark audited to remove contamination, and methods to train models that actually use image evidence.

entry.title: Masking Frequent Tokens Sharpens Direct Preference Optimization

author.name: Harshvardhan Saini, Samyak Jha, Yiming Tang, Dianbo Liu

entry.summary: The paper identifies a pathology in DPO: a tiny set of high-frequency token types dominates cumulative sequence-level reward differences while appearing symmetrically in preferred and dispreferred responses, causing gradient entanglement that dilutes the preference signal. The authors quantify this strikingly (69 token types account for 55.1% of response tokens and 85.9% of within-pair shared mass on Anthropic HH-RLHF under Qwen tokenization) and propose masking frequent tokens to sharpen optimization. This is a simple, actionable improvement to a core alignment technique.

entry.title: Residual-Stream Burden Shapes Representation Learning in Diffusion Transformers

author.name: Tongtong Liang, Siqi Kou, Ziqiao Xi, Esha Singh, Kun Zhou, Zhijie Deng, Alexander Cloninger, Yu-Xiang Wang, Rahul Parhi

entry.summary: This paper explains a striking empirical asymmetry: diffusion transformers on large pixel patches succeed with clean-data prediction but fail with noise or velocity prediction, even though the targets are mathematically interconvertible. The authors argue that noisy targets force the residual stream to preserve noise-dependent variation through depth, burdening downstream layers, while spectrally concentrated clean targets impose lighter demands. This offers a mechanistic account of prediction-target choice in diffusion models.

entry.title: Maintaining Benchmarks Against Increasingly Capable Agents: Detection and Remediation of Unearned Passes

author.name: Weijun Luo, Kelvin Luu, Xinyi Liu, Guangze Luo, Miguel Romero Calvo, Soham Dan, Daniel Yue Zhang, Ying Liu, Mohamed Elfeki

entry.summary: The paper introduces a process-verification framework that audits passing trajectories on agentic benchmarks to distinguish evidenced reward hacking from verifier weakness and localize exploitable surfaces for repair, defining an integrity gap metric. Analysis across 3,810 passing trajectories from 29 model-benchmark cohorts shows confirmed violations often increase with model generation but not monotonically.

entry.title: Understanding Generalization Requires Universal Induction

author.name: Aram Ebtekar, Marcus Hutter, Danica J. Sutherland

entry.summary: This theory paper argues that classical statistical learning theory cannot explain general-purpose AI generalization because No Free Lunch theorems apply even to meta-learning, forcing any successful learner to rely on an externally supplied inductive bias. The authors connect this to Solomonoff induction, showing that biasing toward short programs yields a universal learner competitive against all computable learners. The work provides a conceptual framework for why inductive bias is unavoidable in modern ML.

entry.title: Solving Every Step Is Not Enough: Milestone Oracles Reveal a Composition Gap in LLM Math Reasoning

author.name: Zhuohan Wang, Haoran Ma, Tianyu Wu, Yuanlin Duan, Zichun Liao, Jieming Yu

entry.summary: OracleLadder is a diagnostic that gives models increasing levels of oracle help on multi-step math problems — roadmap, roadmap plus milestone answers, or isolated milestones — to sort failures into five reasoning gap types. Testing six models from 8B to 671B parameters on NuminaMath problems reveals a composition gap: models can solve every step individually yet fail the whole problem.

entry.title: Spontaneous Context Restoration: How Language Models Recover from Corrupted Inputs

author.name: Pranjal Garg, Jacob Beck

entry.summary: This mechanistic interpretability study shows that language models can recover correct outputs from corrupted inputs (deletions, replacements, misspellings) via an emergent two-phase process the authors call context restoration. Using controlled attention-only transformers plus five pretrained LLMs from 1B to 32B parameters, they find restoration arises spontaneously without any denoising training objective, with early layers localizing repairs and later layers integrating them. The work provides new insight into inherent robustness mechanisms inside transformers.

entry.title: ActionLens: Diagnosing Spatial-Temporal Binding Failures in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Gueter Josmy Faure, Min-Hung Chen, Hao Ping Wang, Timoth\'ee Lardy, Hung-Ting Su, Winston H. Hsu

entry.summary: ActionLens is a diagnostic benchmark of 6,701 multiple-choice video questions targeting spatial-temporal binding (associating the right action with the right person at the right time), with ground truth derived deterministically from 1.58 million per-second per-person annotations. Across 20 VLMs that score above 80% on popular benchmarks, the best model reaches only 68.8% overall and lower on the human-reviewed subset.

entry.title: StructRL: Online Structured Reinforcement Learning for Long-Horizon Vision-Language-Action Tasks

author.name: Ziyi Yin, Sangmin Woo, Kang Zhou, Sungyeon Kim, Aosong Feng, Haibo Ding, Jun Huan

entry.summary: StructRL is an online RL framework for vision-language-action models that decomposes long-horizon manipulation tasks into verifiable subtasks and grants intermediate rewards only after prerequisite subtasks complete, replacing sparse terminal-only supervision. This structured supervision distinguishes partial progress from early failure and improves learning on multi-step dependent manipulations from single commands. It addresses a key bottleneck for scaling VLA policies to long-horizon robotics tasks.

entry.title: Waypoint-1.5: A Real-Time Video World Model for Consumer Hardware

author.name: Rajit Rajpal, Shahbuland Matiana, Liew Wei Pyn, Anmol Agarwal, Ryan Craig, Andrew Lapp, Mithun Hunsur, Sami BuGhanem, Scottie Fox, Aaron Sanders Carson Poole, Irene Park, Dave Rossi, Spencer Frazier, Louis Castricato

entry.summary: Waypoint 1.5 is a real-time diffusion world model for interactive video generation on consumer-grade hardware, pretrained on 100,000 hours of control-aligned video game data across hundreds of games and conditioned on full keyboard and mouse input. It ships two resolution variants and formalizes rendered FPS, latent FPS, and control rate as distinct metrics.

entry.title: Texture Space Material Diffusion

author.name: Jacob Munkberg, Peter Kocsis, Jon Hasselgren

entry.summary: This paper finetunes a video diffusion transformer to generate high-quality materials for 3D objects directly in texture space, exploiting the known image-to-texture projection so the diffusion process generalizes across arbitrary geometries while reusing pretrained video diffusion priors. Applications include material reconstruction from posed photos under unknown lighting and material upscaling.

entry.title: HybridCUA: Learning to Orchestrate GUI and CLI for Computer-Use Agents

author.name: Tongbo Chen, Junbo Niu, Zhengxi Lu, Niu Lian, Fei Tang, Yuchen Yan, Yike Hong, Yong Du, Yizhou Liu, Bofan Chen, Yongliang Shen

entry.summary: HybridCUA argues that computer-use agents should combine graphical interface interactions with command-line operations, gaining GUI generality plus shell efficiency, and develops a data construction pipeline plus training approach to teach models when and how to invoke the CLI during task execution. This addresses the scalability limits of per-application API integration.

entry.title: LongLive-Plug: Once-for-All Distillation for Video Generation

author.name: Shuai Yang, Luozhou Wang, Wei Huang, ZhiFei Chen, Bohan Zhang, Xiao Fu, Qianli Ma, Chen-Hsuan Lin, Weian Mao, Bryan Chu, Song Han, Yukang Chen

entry.summary: LongLive-Plug introduces a once-for-all distillation framework that learns reusable capabilities, such as single-pass classifier-free guidance, few-step sampling, and long-context error correction, as LoRA adapters on a base model that plug into compatible downstream video diffusion models without retraining. This eliminates the repeated per-model distillation stage that currently burdens specialized video model development. It includes authors from Song Han's efficient-ML group.

entry.title: RawVLA: Embodied Neural Image Signal Processor For Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Shuhong Liu, Heng Zhou, Lingfeng Qian, Yuhao Fang, Xianbao Hou, Qianyu Zhou, Lin Gu, Wei Sui, Jianfei Yang, Ziteng Cui

entry.summary: RawVLA examines an overlooked design choice in vision-language-action models: reliance on fixed ISP-produced RGB images. The authors systematically study five ISP dimensions (gain, sensor noise, chromatic response, tonal response, bit depth) and show RAW-to-RGB processing materially affects manipulation success. They introduce a streaming neural ISP that adaptively renders RAW observations for frozen VLA policies, concentrating capacity on task-relevant image content.

entry.title: When do data mixtures improve scaling laws? Insights from high-dimensional regression

author.name: Diyuan Wu, Lehan Chen, Theodor Misiakiewicz, Marco Mondelli

entry.summary: The authors study when auxiliary-domain data genuinely improves scaling laws versus merely adding samples, using a high-dimensional mixed-data regression model with a shared regression function, heterogeneous covariances and noise levels, and differently growing dataset sizes. They establish minimax risk under an ellipsoidal constraint and derive deterministic equivalents clarifying when mixture reweighting helps. This provides much-needed theory for the largely empirical practice of data mixture selection in modern LLM training.

entry.title: Introducing Quine: An AI research system designed for the complexity of biology

author.name: Nicolo Fusi, Jonathan M. Carlson

entry.summary: Microsoft Research introduces Quine, a multimodal world model of biology with an interactive harness connecting models, scientific tools, literature, and researchers. In collaboration with the Broad Institute, the system prioritized compounds predicted to drive therapeutic tumor-state shifts, with top candidates validated across multiple wet-lab assays. A Quine Fellows program will extend access to external scientists, with eventual productization through Microsoft Discovery.

entry.title: Towards an AI Software Factory for Data Systems

author.name: Anna Pavlenko, Bogdan Crivat, Brandon Haynes, Carlo Curino, Fotis Psallidas, Jaro Slawinski, Johannes Freischuetz, Laura Pereira Sanchez, Markus Weimer, Mathieu Demarne, Matthias Jasny, Mauktik Gandhi, Max Bovykin, Mirco Milletari, Purbasha Ghosh, Qiushi Bai, Raghu Ramakrishnan, Rahul Pandita, Sergiy Matusevich, Shivaram Venkataraman, Subru Krishnan, Md. Tareq Mahmood, Tiemo Bang, Venkatesh Emani, Xuan Zhao, Yiwen Zhu

entry.summary: This Microsoft paper describes progress toward an AI software factory that accelerates all SDLC stages (targeting, coding, reviewing, ops), producing metadata exhaust used to fine-tune model weights and update a World Model data substrate. Focusing on evolutionary coding tasks with measurable objectives, it reports scaled deployments across tens of Microsoft repositories achieving 3x engineering efficiency over agentic coding alone. This is a substantive industrial report on AI-accelerated software development beyond code generation.

entry.title: WEFT: Scaling Tool-Use Post-Training for General-Purpose Agents

author.name: Bo Mao, Hang He, Linting Wang, Lizhi Lin, Maosen Zhou, Guanming Liu, Jinxiu Liu, Tianyu Huai, Chaoyun Zhang, Bingxuan Li, Kepeng Lei, Guanting Dong, Zhou Shao, Rui Zheng, Hang Yan, Jie Zhou, Chengcheng Wan, Tao Gui, Liang He, Xipeng Qiu

entry.summary: WEFT argues that scaling executable environments alone does not guarantee tool-use post-training gains, and couples whole-system agentic interaction construction spanning environment, task, harness, and evaluator with execution-driven self-evolution and stable post-training. It targets reliable learning signals for general-purpose tool-using agents.

entry.title: From Judgment Quality to Downstream Utility: Rethinking LLM-as-a-Judge for Open-Ended Tasks

author.name: Zheng Zhang, Lufei Li, Xinyue Tan, Yuanhao Zeng, Ziwei Shan, Yexin Li, Kan Ren

entry.summary: This systematic study examines how LLM-judge protocol choices (verdict granularity, critique usage, evaluation batching) affect both intrinsic judgment quality and downstream utility in policy training and test-time inference such as Best-of-N selection and judge-guided reranking. It argues against naively converting judgments into rewards without attending to judgment quality. The work clarifies the pipeline from judge design to RLHF-style outcomes.

entry.title: FOCUS: Training-Free Decision-Preserving Context Compression for LLM Agents

author.name: Shantanu Dixit, Anson Bastos, Xuchao Zhang, Chetan Bansal, Saravan Rajmohan

entry.summary: FOCUS recasts agent context compression as causal decision preservation over discrete interaction units, asking which past interactions causally shape future decisions, and does so training-free rather than learning compression policies offline. This avoids upfront compression costs and adapts dynamically to evolving test-time trajectories, addressing quadratic inference cost growth and attention dilution.

entry.title: Thinking Before Thinking: Scaling Agentic Inference Through Meta-Reasoning

author.name: Paras Dahal, Anton Bakhtin, Taco Cohen, Zhengxing Chen, Carole-Jean Wu, Rob Fergus, Scott Yih, Gabriel Synnaeve, Ruslan Salakhutdinov, Sanjeev Arora, Jason Weston, Anirudh Goyal

entry.summary: This paper introduces agentic meta-reasoning, an inference-time harness in which a controller model consolidates run state, evaluates next options under the remaining budget, and dispatches work to worker models with context from persistent memory. The controller carries only a compact account of the run between decisions rather than replaying full history, making long agent runs more scalable and controllable.

entry.title: In-Context Learning Amplifies a Latent Symbolic Circuit

author.name: Melissa Wessel

entry.summary: The paper traces a three-stage symbolic reasoning circuit (abstraction, induction, retrieval) across shot counts in three model families, finding it functional before high accuracy is achieved. Per-head causal contribution grows up to 8x from 1- to 10-shot, and activation patching or function-vector injection substantially rescues accuracy at low shot counts, largely substituting for the induction stage.

entry.title: Cooperative Multi-Agent Vision-Language-Action Models via Reinforced Fine Tuning

author.name: Ruixiao Xu, Wong Lik Hang Kenny, Zhiqian Liu, Jianing Guo, Hanxiao Li, Kejian Shi, Shuning Zhang, Pu Feng, Yongjia Ma, Yuqing Ma, Kai Chen, Qi Dou, Yaodong Yang, Xianglong Liu, Simin Li

entry.summary: This paper studies RL methods for cooperative multi-agent vision-language-action models, noting that VLAs pretrained on single-agent data lack inter-robot coordination skills that SFT on demonstrations cannot fully supply. The authors present a three-stage reinforced fine-tuning pipeline featuring initialization-aware data collection that invokes human demonstrations only when the pretrained VLA repeatedly fails. This enables VLAs to improve from their own experience toward multi-robot collaboration.

entry.title: Making LLMs Truly Forget: Deep Unlearning by Searching, Selecting, and Severing Knowledge Paths

author.name: Jialu Wang, Peizhi Niu, Haoteng Yin, Hans Hao-Hsun Hsu, Pan Li, Rongzhe Wei

entry.summary: This paper tackles the problem that unlearned facts often remain recoverable through multi-hop reasoning over retained supporting knowledge. The proposed deep unlearning framework searches reasoning paths in both explicit responses and latent representations, compiles them into a confidence-aware subgraph, and applies graph minimum cut to sever recovery paths while preserving unrelated knowledge.

entry.title: PDMD: Projected Distribution Matching Distillation for Video Diffusion Models

author.name: Zimo Wang, Junkun Yuan, Angtian Wang, Haotian Yang, Canyu Zhang, Siyuan Yuan, Xingchang Huang, Bo Liu, Yizhi Wang, Yiding Yang, Chongyang Ma, Gordon Guocheng Qian

entry.summary: PDMD addresses training instability in Distribution Matching Distillation for video diffusion models, tracing progressive oversaturation and artifacts to critic errors accumulating in successive student updates. The method projects out the component of the DMD update parallel to the student-critic endpoint residual, proven to be an unbiased estimate of the critic's endpoint error, enabling few-step video generation. This matters for making video diffusion models cheaper at inference.

entry.title: On the Behavioral Traits of LLM Agents

author.name: Haokai Zhao, Jie Gao, Yunze Xiao, Xintao Wang, Weihao Xuan, Aditya Joshi, Mark Dredze, Jen-tse Huang

entry.summary: The paper proposes A-B-D, a method to infer behavioral traits of AI agents bottom-up from behavioral data in real trajectories, rather than unreliable self-reports or costly LLM-judge informant ratings. From 345,667 real-world trajectories spanning 80 models, 12 tasks, and 50 harnesses, it extracts 318 candidate features capturing agent actions and communication. This grounds AI personality research in observed behavior at scale.

entry.title: TCSAlgBench: Benchmarking Automated Proving for Research-Level Theoretical Computer Science

author.name: Chutong Yang, Xiyuan Zhang, Yu Huang, Boran Han, Soonho Kong, Shuai Zhang, Vihang Prakash Patil, Zhen Han, Michael Bohlke-Schneider, Bernie Wang

entry.summary: TCSAlgBench comprises 398 theorem-level natural-language proof challenges drawn from 138 STOC and COLT 2026 papers, with expert-designed rules to complete paper context, preserve computational assumptions and quantitative guarantees, and withhold constructions when discovering algorithms is part of the task. It provides a reusable pipeline for evaluating research-level automated proving.

entry.title: OTT3R: Multi-View 3D Reconstruction and Fast Dataset Generation at 1% Compute

author.name: Brandon Leblanc, Charalambos Poullis

entry.summary: OTT3R is a knowledge-distillation framework that compresses a 959M-parameter feed-forward 3D reconstruction model into a 102M-parameter student, achieving 9.4x compression, up to 7x faster inference, and training at about 1.6% of VGGT's compute on a two-GPU workstation. It also provides an integrated pipeline for generating 3D pseudo-labels without sensors, replacing slow Structure-from-Motion supervision. This democratizes feed-forward 3D reconstruction research for resource-limited groups and enables edge deployment.

entry.title: HyperSAM: A Promptable Foundation Model for Hyperspectral Remote Sensing

author.name: Li Pang, Xinqiao Wu, Jing Yao, Pedram Ghamisi, Jun Zhou, Zhengchao Chen, Deyu Meng, Xiangyong Cao

entry.summary: HyperSAM is a promptable foundation model for hyperspectral remote sensing that couples a data-centric synthesis pipeline with spectral adaptation of vision foundation model priors, addressing the scarcity of jointly high-resolution and densely annotated hyperspectral corpora. It aims to reuse geometric and interactive priors from modern vision foundation models rather than training from scratch.

entry.title: Representational Simplicity and Circuit Size Dissociate in a Threshold-Dependent Way: A Controlled Test via Adversarial Training

author.name: Adam Elimadi

entry.summary: This paper uses adversarial training as a controlled instrument to test whether clean representations and concentrated feature attributions predict smaller, more tractable causal circuits in neural networks. The findings show representational orderliness and reverse-engineering complexity dissociate in a threshold-dependent way, challenging common interpretability heuristics.

entry.title: LongCat-DeepResearch Technical Report

author.name: Meituan LongCat Team, He Zhu, Yue Xu, Wanli Wu, Haolin Ren, Yuxin Bian, Jiarui Zhao, Rongzhi Zhang, Quanchi Weng, Jinghao Cui, Yu Fan, Yuhan Liu, Yunhu Ye, Jiyuan Ren, Fengcheng Yuan, Zhao Yang, Jiacheng Zhang, Yuchuan Dai, Ruixuan Xiao, Haozhe Sun, Xiangyuan Liu, Cheng Sun, Yao Du, Yiming Hao, Hongbo Guo, Shuo He, Lei Wang, Xunliang Cai, Yan Chen, Fan Yang, Lingchuan Liu

entry.summary: Meituan's LongCat team presents LongCat-DeepResearch, a multi-agent deep research system combining an enhanced LongCat model with a workflow that separates global planning from parallel section-level investigation and targeted local revision. The system produces comprehensive, evidence-grounded reports and supports reproducible construction of research corpora.

entry.title: Towards Mitigating Deceptive Safety Alignment in Large Reasoning Models

author.name: Xiangyu Zhou, Saleh Zare Zade, Rafi Ibn Sultan, Alexander Kotov, Dongxiao Zhu

entry.summary: This work identifies deceptive safety alignment in large reasoning models, where the chain-of-thought trace and the final answer convey inconsistent safety signals because RL rewards depend only on final answers. The authors introduce DSAR, a metric that jointly assesses reasoning traces and answers to quantify this inconsistency, and show the phenomenon is pervasive across models and benchmarks. This directly addresses a safety-relevant gap in how reasoning models are supervised.

entry.title: MAADBench: The Refreshable Paradigm for Anomaly Detection in Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Lei Ma, Dennis Hofmann, Haowen Xu, Joshua DeOliveira, Peter VanNostrand, Lei Cao, Elke Rundensteiner

entry.summary: Motivated by reported 41-87% failure rates in LLM-based multi-agent systems, this paper presents MAADBench, the first refreshable benchmark for anomaly detection in MAS. It addresses benchmark staleness via a huge generative task space (roughly 10^37 tasks) to resist memorization, plus reliable automated labeling across evolving LLM backbones. It enables systematic evaluation of MAS failure detection as models change.

entry.title: Can Agents Design Libraries for Agents?

author.name: Gabriel Orlanski, Alex L. Zhang, Avi Trost, Vincent Sunn Chen, Frederic Sala, Aws Albarghouthi, Ludwig Schmidt

entry.summary: LibraryDesignBench is a two-phase benchmark where one agent implements a full library from a specification without prescribed design, and three user agents from different model families evaluate it via correctness and simplicity of programs they write. Spanning 242 expert-validated problems across 15 tasks in four languages, results show agent designers reproduce good abstractions on eleven of fifteen tasks. It measures whether agents can build reusable infrastructure for other agents.

entry.title: SIPO: Unifying Reinforcement Learning with On-Policy Self-Distillation

author.name: Zhenrui Yue, Huimin Zeng, Yueqi Wang, Yaokun Liu, Fengran Mo, Jinghan Zhang, Mung Yao Jia, Gyuseok Lee, Yang Zhang, Na Wei, Dong Wang

entry.summary: SIPO combines reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards and on-policy self-distillation by introducing a contrastive self-teacher that provides dense token-level credit assignment. It addresses the overconfidence and long-trajectory penalty problems that plague standard self-distillation approaches for LLM post-training.

entry.title: Learn from the Gap: Differential-Aware Advantage Pruning with Adaptive Rollout Sampling for GRPO

author.name: Jiahua Yang, Zhiwei Yang, Xianpeng Zhang, Dongyu Chen, Xing Chen, Tianhuang Su, Haonan Lu, Quanlong Guan, Kai Tang, Chuangchuang Wang

entry.summary: FastRL is a plug-and-play framework that improves GRPO-style reinforcement learning by pruning low-information advantages and adaptively allocating rollout sampling, targeting the heavy compute overhead of per-question multi-rollout training. The goal is to simultaneously cut training cost and improve the learning signal from homogeneous trajectory groups. If validated, this lowers the barrier to RL fine-tuning of LLMs.

entry.title: CoEM: Empowering Long-Context Reasoning with Commit-on-Evidence Memory

author.name: Jingguang Li, Yebo Wu, Zuyi Guo, Kailang Ma, Xianjie Dai, Han Zheng, Benwang Chen, Li Li, Can Rong, Heye Huang

entry.summary: CoEM tackles degradation of LLM reasoning over long contexts by learning when to compress source evidence into memory facts: potentially useful excerpts are held verbatim in a pending set under a fixed memory budget until later context clarifies their relevance. This defers irreversible compression and preserves critical details for downstream reasoning steps. The approach addresses a known weakness of chunk-wise long-context processing.

entry.title: CADOC: Cache-Aware Dynamic Object Context for Long-Horizon Agents

author.name: Junjie Yao, Zhangchen Zhou, Zhi-Qin John Xu

entry.summary: CADOC is an online algorithm for long-horizon agents that replaces structured history objects with compact retrieval cards while keeping exact originals recoverable on demand. Its key novelty is scheduling context edits in a cache-aware way, balancing accumulated waiting cost against shared prefix-cache reconstruction costs. This addresses the practical tension between context compression and KV/prefix-cache efficiency in agent systems.

entry.title: actr: aligning thoughts and responses for multilingual safety in reasoning llms

author.name: Xianhui Zhang, Jian Yu, Chengyu Xie, Chenhang Cui, Shuyi Miao, Pengyang Shao, Yu Zheng, Fei Shen, Tat-Seng Chua

entry.summary: ACTR addresses the finding that reasoning LLMs can produce unsafe responses in low-resource languages even when their reasoning traces correctly identify safety risks. The framework introduces a think gap score measuring how much safety reasoning influences attention outputs across languages, and aligns cross-lingual thoughts with responses to strengthen the use of existing safety reasoning. This improves multilingual safety alignment without retraining safety from scratch.

entry.title: Commitment Hierarchies under Intent Revision: A Belief-Revision Account of Salvage in Tool-Use Agents

author.name: Spandan Ghose Chowdhury

entry.summary: This paper studies how tool-using LLM agents should handle mid-task user intent changes, deciding whether to keep, patch, or discard already-computed sub-results (salvage). The key finding is architectural: having the model classify the revision once and propagating that decision through a deterministic layer over a commitment hierarchy matches cost-optimal oracle behavior across three models, whereas per-node querying is unreliable.

entry.title: SINGED: Correct Outputs Do Not Certify Safe Execution in LLM Agents

author.name: Xiaoyu Xu, Zi Liang, Minxin Du, Qipeng Xie, Qingqing Ye, Yuyuan Li, Haibo Hu

entry.summary: SINGED studies functional counterfeits: third-party tool implementations that return the requested output while adding effects forbidden by the task contract, which output-based evaluations miss. It provides a controlled benchmark spanning five primary and two held-out task families, varying rank, evidence depth, decision policy, and agent configuration, with separate task and process oracles to verify both artifact and execution path.

entry.title: Similarity Is Not Validity: Defending LLM Semantic Caches Against Poisoning

author.name: Zihan Zhang, Shuangjie Yao, Zesen Liu, Zhixiang Zhang, Wai Ip Lai, Dung Hiu Hilton Yeung, Chun Kit Zhang, Fuchen Ma, Yuanyuan Yuan, Yu Jiang, Dongdong She

entry.summary: This paper identifies a cache-poisoning vulnerability in LLM semantic caches, where attackers can store malicious responses under queries with high embedding similarity to benign ones. Rooting the problem in an information-bottleneck gap between retrieval similarity and answer validity, the authors propose a defense that recovers distinguishing information from the raw text of cached entries. The work matters as semantic caching becomes a common cost-saving deployment technique.

entry.title: FLOORA: A Human-Aligned Domain-Specific Language Model for Architectural Design

author.name: Sahand Rezaei-Shoshtari, Patryk Wozniczka, Shu Ishida, Gregg Streuber, Farnoosh Javadi, Jeffrey Landes, Angela Ju, Muhammad Azam, Bryan Lim, Johan Luttun, Indrajeet Haldar, Jonathan Shaw, Beatriz Guerra, Ivan Sosnovik, James Stoddart, Robert Giaquinto, Adam Gaier

entry.summary: FLOORA is a family of small domain-specific language models (0.6B parameters) for architectural floor layout generation, combining a token-efficient DSL, custom tokenization, domain-specific pretraining, and RL-based alignment. The small model outperforms much larger frontier models, achieving up to 92% VLM-judge win rates on out-of-distribution real-world buildings and being preferred by humans in 89.3% of evaluations. This demonstrates that targeted domain specialization can beat scale in structured engineering domains.

entry.title: PreviewDiff: Multimodal Critic-Guided Search over Diffusion Latents

author.name: Vighnesh Subramaniam, Boris Katz, Brian Cheung, Chun-Liang Li, Tomas Pfister, Yale Song

entry.summary: PreviewDiff is a training-free test-time search method that converts diffusion sampling into critic-guided search over intermediate latents, decoding partial previews at denoising checkpoints to repair promising trajectories before they fail. This addresses compositional failures (object counts, attribute binding, spatial relations) that Best-of-N sampling cannot fix post hoc.

entry.title: FineART: Fine-grained Annotated Robotic Trajectory Dataset and Vision-Language-Action Model for Bimanual Manipulation

author.name: Jade Choghari, Pepijn Kooijmans, Mansi Agarwal, Yusuf Umut Ciftci, Aseem Doriwala, Catherine Weaver, Mouli Sivapurapu, Kai Yang, Jackson Lee, Thomas Wolf, Pragna Mannam

entry.summary: FineART is a densely annotated bimanual manipulation dataset with 40,543 episodes, 1,718 hours, and 533,913 subtasks across 151 tasks, far exceeding the annotation depth of prior single-arm datasets. The accompanying FineART-VLA policy predicts its own next subtask, and mid-training on subtask prediction yields substantial improvements. This addresses a key data bottleneck for long-horizon, two-handed robot manipulation.

entry.title: How Medical VLMs Underutilize Their Vision Encoders: A Dermatology Perspective

author.name: Janet Wang, Yunbei Zhang, Xiao Wang, Jihun Hamm

entry.summary: This work documents a large performance gap in dermatology where the MedSigLIP vision encoder outperforms the full MedGemma multimodal model by over 10 percentage points even with zero target-task labels, suggesting medical VLMs fail to exploit their visual representations. The authors systematically test hypotheses for why plausible-sounding diagnoses lack grounding in image evidence. The findings matter for trustworthiness of clinical multimodal systems.

entry.title: Constitutional adapters: Inference-time interventions for misalignment and misuse

author.name: Adam S. Lowet, Mark Kurzeja

entry.summary: This work distills constitution-consistent behavior from synthetic corpora into lightweight low-rank adapters and steering vectors that increase jailbreak defense and measured alignment without the model ever seeing harmful requests or jailbreaks during training. The interventions perform particularly well at long context lengths and against multi-turn attacks, outperforming prompted and steered baselines. Subtracting control-trained from constitution-trained objects isolates the alignment-relevant component.

entry.title: Lost in Conversation or Lost in Translation? Diagnosing Multi-Turn Degradation in RAG

author.name: Pranav Handa, Ariful Azad

entry.summary: This study identifies a major evaluation gap: RAG and GraphRAG systems are almost always tested on single-turn, fully specified queries, while real users ask underspecified questions that build up over multiple turns. The authors run a large-scale simulation converting multi-hop QA benchmarks into conversations, evaluating ten LLMs and eight retrieval systems across 1.5 million contexts. The findings matter because they quantify how much current RAG performance claims may overstate real-world conversational robustness.

entry.title: LongSpark: Efficient speculative decoding with a fixed-cost parallel drafter

author.name: Hao-Yuan He, Peng-Fei Liu, Si Shen, Ming Li

entry.summary: LongSpark is a block-diffusion speculative decoding drafter whose decoding cost is independent of prefix length, exploiting the fact that a drafter only proposes candidates the target verifies. Existing state-of-the-art drafters become increasingly expensive as context grows, eroding speculative decoding benefits. The fixed-cost parallel drafting design eliminates this scaling penalty.

entry.title: ToolFence: Fine-Grained Authorization for Secure Tool-Using LLM Agents

author.name: Yanjie Li, Xiangyu He, Xuelong Dai, Bin Xiao

entry.summary: ToolFence defends tool-using LLM agents against indirect prompt injection by compiling a typed authorization blueprint before execution and enforcing it with a deterministic monitor that authorizes effects rather than inspecting content. It targets within-tool attacks that manipulate tool arguments, which content-based and consensus defenses miss, while offering much lower latency than data-flow-control systems like CaMeL. This is a meaningful advance in practical agent security.

entry.title: Do-JEPA: From Masking to Intervention in Latent World Models

author.name: Hossein Resani, Javen Qinfeng Shi

entry.summary: Do-JEPA trains latent world models to predict the causal effect of actions by comparing latent futures under an action versus a reference action from the same simulator state, yielding effect, support, propagation, and invariance losses. Unlike masking-based objectives such as C-JEPA that intervene on visibility, this intervenes on physical dynamics. This separates what an action caused from what merely co-occurred with it.

entry.title: Predictive Self-Supervised Learning Provably Identifies Stochastic Signals under Nuisance

author.name: Fabian A. Mikulasch, Friedemann Zenke

entry.summary: The authors prove that common latent-space predictive self-supervised learning methods can distinguish unpredictable-but-relevant stochastic variation from true nuisance information, implicitly instantiating a latent-variable model with stochastic dynamics and observation-private nuisance. They trace this capability to two complementary principles involving prediction in latent space. This provides a theoretical answer to a puzzling question about why predictive SSL works so well.

entry.title: ExceptionDrive: A Planning-Oriented Counterfactual Corner-Case Benchmark for Autonomous Driving

author.name: Ziyi Luo, Zhe Sun, Yehao Lu, Lei Zhou, Lisheng Wu, Xuewei Li, Zequn Qin, Xi Li

entry.summary: ExceptionDrive is a counterfactual benchmark that inserts safety-critical hazards into real nuScenes scenes using VLM-assisted screening, localized multi-view editing, and quality auditing, spanning 21 tasks across six hazard families. Because hazard insertion invalidates recorded human trajectories, it proposes a reference-free protocol with metrics such as Unsafe Rate and Hazard Clearance Compliance. This addresses the gap between strong routine-driving scores and unreliable planner behavior in rare dangerous events.

entry.title: $S^3$: Spectral Null-Space Swap Makes Reasoning Models Efficient

author.name: Hongbo Ma, Sansheng Cao, Jiajun Fan, Bangji Yang, Ge Liu

entry.summary: This work finds that reasoning capacity in chain-of-thought models largely resides in weight components within the null space of the corresponding non-thinking model's dominant singular directions, and proposes S3, a training-free method that composes paired thinking and non-thinking models to improve reasoning token efficiency without accuracy loss. This offers a novel spectral analysis perspective for making expensive reasoning models cheaper at inference.

entry.title: Breaking the Uniformity Trap: Scaling Video Diffusion Model via SplitMoE

author.name: Yu Xu, Yuxin Zhang, Xiao Yang, Haotian Yang, Yizhi Wang, Xinwei Huang, Minxuan Lin, Angtian Wang, Chongyang Ma, Fan Tang

entry.summary: The authors identify a uniformity trap in visual mixture-of-experts models, where independent token-wise routing and uniform expert-usage regularization fragment semantically coherent patches across experts, causing structural distortion in video generation. They propose SplitMoE, a split-role sparse architecture that assigns complementary roles to experts to better match the spatiotemporal redundancy and long-tailed semantics of video data.

entry.title: On-Policy Attention Linearization

author.name: Arian Raje, Anupam Nayak, Anthony Fei, Akaash Parthasarathy, Mohamed Abdelfattah, Gauri Joshi

entry.summary: The paper addresses the collapse of distilled hybrid linear-attention transformers on long-context retrieval and reasoning by proposing on-policy attention linearization, since off-policy distillation never teaches the student to recover from fixed-state drift over long sequences. The method trains the linearized model on its own rollouts where efficiency gains matter most. It targets a key failure mode of the increasingly popular full-attention-to-linear distillation paradigm.

entry.title: Can Circuit Alignment Predict OOD Generalization?

author.name: Ayan Banerjee, Abhra Chaudhuri, Josep Llados, Umapada Pal, Anjan Dutta

entry.summary: The paper shows that standard representational similarity metrics (CKA, SVCCA, RSA) are provably insensitive to the structural rerouting caused by distribution shift, and introduces the Circuit Alignment Score (CAS), which compares class-specific circuits across domains using graph kernels. With a Lebesgue-integral formulation and Monte Carlo estimation, CAS provably recovers the ground-truth ranking of models by OOD accuracy using weights alone, without target-domain data.

entry.title: HM-ROUTER: Joint Model and Harness Routing for Agentic Systems

author.name: Hao Mark Chen, Royson Lee, Yasuyuki Okoshi, Dimitris Anastasiou, Wayne Luk, Hongxiang Fan

entry.summary: HM-ROUTER jointly routes each query to the best pair of a language model and an agent harness, recognizing that agent performance depends on both components and their compatibility. It learns shared model and harness representations with a CP-tensor-decomposition-inspired interaction term so samples from observed pairs generalize to unobserved combinations, and it curates a benchmark spanning 12 public agent benchmarks. This addresses a growing cost-and-capability tradeoff in deploying agentic systems.

entry.title: What Can a Leaderboard Certify? Compositional Controllability for Fair Evaluation and Training of Biomedical Literature-Review Agents

author.name: Zhaowei Han, Xiang Zhang, Lingxiao Guan, Danqi Hu, Kai Liu, Kevin Chang, Jie Liu

entry.summary: Introduces compositional controllability, a framework for certifying when comparisons between long-horizon agents (e.g., biomedical literature-review agents) are fair, by bounding the gap between observed and controlled score differences over a chosen comparison window. The framework yields an admissibility test applied before inspecting scores, refusing inadmissible comparisons and certifying orderings only when gaps exceed the bound.

entry.title: On the Pitfalls of Verbalized Confidence Priors for Calibrating Large Reasoning Models

author.name: Shuoyuan Wang, Beier Luo, Hao Zeng, Chengyao Yu, Songxin Zhang, Zejian Xie, Bingyi Jing, Hongxin Wei

entry.summary: The paper shows that large reasoning models concentrate their verbalized confidence on a few high values, and that this concentration persists through confidence-aware RL, suppressing gradient updates for rare confidence values and inflating Brier risk. The authors prove this theoretically and propose CalibSFT, a plug-and-play supervised fine-tuning step to reshape the confidence prior before RL. This addresses overconfidence in reasoning models, an important safety-adjacent issue.

entry.title: Allspark: Weak to Strong Transfer via Alternating Chain of Thought

author.name: Kaizhao Liang, Junxiong Wang, Chen Liang, Zhendong Wang, Qiang Liu

entry.summary: Allspark enables weak-to-strong transfer of reasoning ability: a weak teacher trains alongside a frozen copy of itself, alternating chain-of-thought segments, and at inference a stronger student replaces the frozen partner with both models fixed. This allows reasoning improvements learned by small models to benefit larger models without costly large-model rollouts during RL-style training.

entry.title: Beyond Token Savings: A Systematic Study of Context Compression in LLM Agents

author.name: Ritul Satish, Prasoon Sinha, Akiho Kawada, Neeraja J. Yadwadkar

entry.summary: This paper systematically disentangles what, when, and how much to compress in LLM agent context management across three open-weight models on SWE-bench Verified and Terminal-Bench, using nearly 35,000 agent runs. It finds that fewer tokens do not necessarily mean faster or cheaper execution, challenging fixed compression policies in agentic harnesses.

entry.title: Cost-free Spectral Estimation for Adaptive Newton--Schulz in Matrix Optimizers

author.name: Kristi Topollai, Anna Choromanska

entry.summary: This paper improves matrix optimizers like Muon, which use Newton-Schulz iterations to approximately orthogonalize momentum matrices, by showing that the Gram matrices formed inside those iterations already contain enough information to estimate the singular-value spectrum at essentially no extra cost. From these spectral moments, the method can adapt the polynomial routine per layer and throughout training instead of using one fixed routine everywhere. Given Muon's rising popularity for training large models, near-free adaptivity could yield practical efficiency and convergence gains.

entry.title: KernelZero: Co-Evolving Proposer and Coder for Continuously Improved GPU Kernel Generation

author.name: Changxin Ke, Rui Zhang, Zixiang Fang, Zhenghong Li, Yuanbo Wen, Jiashuo Shen, Shuo Wang, Jiaming Guo, Ling Li, Qi Guo, Yunji Chen

entry.summary: KernelZero is a co-evolution framework using two specialized models — a Proposer generating Torch modules and a Coder translating them into CUDA/Triton kernels — to continuously improve automatic GPU kernel generation. It addresses data scarcity via frontier-driven module generation and tackles the correctness-performance tradeoff in LLM-based kernel synthesis.

entry.title: Decoupling Token Roles in Autoregressive Pretraining

author.name: Suqin Yuan, Runqi Lin, Kevin Qinghong Lin, Junchi Yu, Lei Feng, Chris Russell, Tongliang Liu

entry.summary: This paper separates the dual roles a token plays in autoregressive pretraining: as a prediction target measured by its own loss, and as context that influences subsequent tokens. Using controlled corruption experiments, the authors find a reversal effect: making a noisy token easier to predict reduces its harm as a target but increases its harm as context. The framework also offers an explanation for behaviors in model-generated text, since generation judges tokens only by fit to the prefix without ever testing their contextual role against an independently determined continuation.

entry.title: Discovering Symmetries in Neural Network Parameter Spaces

author.name: Bo Zhao, Nima Dehmamy, Robin Walters, Rose Yu

entry.summary: The paper formalizes data-dependent parameter space symmetries and provides infinitesimal conditions enabling joint learning of group generators and nonlinear action maps. It systematically uncovers both known and previously unknown symmetries, and establishes when subnetwork symmetries extend to full models, yielding finite-batch symmetry families.

entry.title: Benign Overfitting for General Norms and Distributions

author.name: Daniel Barzilai, Ohad Shamir

entry.summary: The authors extend the theory of benign overfitting beyond minimum-2-norm linear regression with Gaussian data to general norms and general sub-Gaussian distributions, motivated by optimizers like Adam and Muon that induce non-Euclidean geometries. They prove, as a special case, that minimum-p-norm interpolation with p>1 can benignly overfit. This significantly broadens the theoretical foundations for why modern interpolating models generalize.

entry.title: QwenGyre: An Elastic Reinforcement Learning Framework for Training xLong-Horizon Agents

author.name: Weiqi Wang, Yuxin Zhou, Mouxiang Chen, Siyuan Zhang, Yi Zhang, Yuyan Luo, Zhiyu Yin, Chencan Wu, Jiemin Jiang, Wentao Yao, Chujie Zheng, JianWei Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces an end-to-end framework for online RL on extreme-long-horizon LLM agent tasks that can span hours, hundreds of interactions, and nearly a million tokens per rollout. QwenGyre elastically reallocates GPUs between rollout and training without interrupting live executions, and its trajectory processor handles branching-induced trajectory redundancy to improve training efficiency.

entry.title: Steering Language Model Goals with Value Transplant

author.name: Pengcheng Jiang, Fabien Roger

entry.summary: Building on prior work that models track goal progress along an internal value axis, this paper tests value transplant: shifting a host model's activations along a value axis by a scaled donor-host difference to retarget its search toward the donor's goal. Experiments on Qwen3-8B and GPT-OSS-20B fine-tuned into honest and cheating variants probe how model goals can be redirected via activation steering.

entry.title: Learning to Steer, Steering to See: Unveiling the Geometry of RLVR in Large Language Models via Trainable Vectors

author.name: Yuchen Cai, Ding Cao, Qixiang Yin, Xin Xu, Kai Yang, Siye Wu, Pengyuan Wang, Jiaxuan Wang, Weijie Liu, Saiyong Yang, Guangzhong Sun, Guiquan Liu, Junfeng Fang

entry.summary: The authors use vector steering to identify a low-dimensional effective manifold in activation space that accounts for RLVR-induced reasoning gains in LLMs. They characterize capacity limits of this manifold, showing it is highly compressible but not infinitely so, and describe control manifold separation properties that clarify how RL reshapes model behavior.

entry.title: ALICE: In-context, Zero-shot, Mutual Information Estimation

author.name: Giulio Franzese, Simone Rossi, Pietro Michiardi

entry.summary: ALICE is a foundation model for mutual information estimation that eliminates per-distribution training, trained on synthetic distributions and acting as an in-context estimator of rectified-flow velocity fields. It delivers competitive accuracy in low-data regimes where modern neural MI estimators fail, and generalizes across data types.

entry.title: E3J: An Efficient and Open-Source Backend for Euclidean Equivariant Operations on GPU and TPU

author.name: Olivier Peltre, Armand Picard, Adrien Pichard, Miguel Bragan\c{c}a, Luca Giacomoni, Valentin Heyraud, Zachary Weller-Davies, Christoph Brunken, Jules Tilly

entry.summary: e3j is an open-source JAX-compatible backend for Euclidean equivariant operations with optimized CUDA and Pallas kernels for GPUs and TPUs. It achieves state-of-the-art throughput, including up to 34% speed-up over NVIDIA's cuEquivariance on molecular simulations with MACE and over 80% H100 memory-bandwidth efficiency on tensor product operations.

entry.title: eval-unlearn: Benchmarking unlearning in Text-to-Image Diffusion Models

author.name: Mansi, Nikhil Raghavan, Zixia Huang, Kai Sheng Ong, Ji Shen Lim, Brandon Siao Xiang Ling, Francesco Leofante

entry.summary: Introduces eval-unlearn, an open-source Python library unifying benchmarking of concept unlearning in text-to-image diffusion models, integrating twelve unlearning methods and nine evaluation metrics covering erasure efficacy, adversarial robustness, generative quality, and retention. Its plugin architecture supports third-party extensions.

entry.title: Frontier Learning: Training LLM Reasoners at the Edge of Capability

author.name: Robin Faro, Shyam Sundhar Ramesh, Ilija Bogunovic, Aurelien Lucchi

entry.summary: This paper proposes frontier learning, an open-ended post-training approach that uses procedural problem generators online to continually supply informative training problems for RL-based LLM reasoning, instead of a fixed problem pool that becomes stale as the model improves. It treats generator parameters as a search space optimized via a regret signal, targeting problems at the edge of the model's capability.

entry.title: Rethinking Circuit Evaluation: Do Circuits Explain Model Errors?

author.name: Li Zhang, Chuqin Geng, Mark Zhang, Chen Yang, Luke Zhang, Haolin Ye, Xujie Si

entry.summary: This mechanistic interpretability paper shows that circuits validated via standard ablation can reproduce a model's successful decisions while failing to account for most of its errors, suggesting current circuit evaluation is inadequate. The authors propose evaluating exact answer agreement separately on successes and failures across multiple model-task settings including IOI and Docstring.

entry.title: Recipe-Matching, Not Equivalence

author.name: Ali Habibullah, Mohammad Alshiekh, Yazan Alshoibi, Salman Khan, Naeemullah Khan

entry.summary: This paper critiques the MathNet-Retrieve benchmark, showing that much of its measured performance reflects matching the LLM-generated construction recipe (prompt, distractors, judges) rather than true retrieval ability. Controlled experiments with matched models find that half to two-thirds of a 45-point R@1 gap comes from the shared recipe rather than genuine capability.

entry.title: TRAP: Understanding and Mitigating Privacy Memorization in Language Models

author.name: Muhammed Ustaomeroglu, Ziyue Xu, Hanshen Xiao, Peter Cnudde, Guannan Qu, Holger R. Roth

entry.summary: TRAP studies when language models memorize sensitive records during fine-tuning and how to prevent it without knowing which spans are sensitive, introducing the Target Reference Advantage (TRA) statistic that compares token probabilities against a model trained on the complementary corpus half. The paper also characterizes memorization dynamics, showing it keeps growing past validation loss minima, and derives mitigation strategies.

entry.title: RE-0: Verified Recursive Improvement of Embodied Code-as-Policy Agents through Local On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Jiawei Zhang, Xiangrong Zhang, Rui Song, Huanbin Zhou, Chengye Song, Hongzhou Wang

entry.summary: RE-0 is a recursively verified policy improvement framework for code-as-policy embodied agents that avoids assuming the teacher is globally superior. Instead, it requests local corrections from the teacher on the student's own failure histories and verifies in the environment whether each correction genuinely helps before distilling it. This credit-assignment approach yields immediate, verified improvement and addresses a real flaw in standard distillation for agents.

entry.title: Silent Failures in Agentic Security Evaluation: A Validated Harness for Tool-Call Mediation Under Indirect Prompt Injection

author.name: Animesh Shaw

entry.summary: The paper audits an indirect prompt injection benchmark and identifies four defect classes in its evaluation harness, including silent payload non-delivery and scoring attack success by tool identity rather than arguments, each producing plausible but incorrect results. Re-scoring identical traces under corrected definitions quantifies the distortion, and it releases a validated tool-call mediation harness.

entry.title: Byzantine-Robust Federated RAG via Aligned Calibration and Fixed-Membership Conformal Prediction

author.name: Prasanjit Dubey, Aritra Guha, Xiaoming Huo

entry.summary: This paper addresses federated retrieval-augmented generation where document collections stay with their owners and a central hub combines node scores, but some nodes may be Byzantine and report arbitrary scores. The authors combine conformal prediction with aligned calibration to produce answer sets that contain the correct answer with a guaranteed probability even under a bounded number of compromised nodes. This matters because it brings statistical reliability and robustness guarantees to privacy-preserving, multi-party RAG deployments such as those over medical records.

entry.title: One Attack to Fool Them All: Highly Transferable Black-Box Adversarial Attacks on Frontier MLLMs

author.name: Sen Nie, Jie Zhang, Zhongqi Wang, Shiguang Shan, Xilin Chen

entry.summary: O-Attack is a black-box adversarial image attack that transfers across diverse frontier multimodal LLMs by exploiting a broad, cross-modally aligned semantic space in surrogate models beyond final-layer outputs. It demonstrates that a single adversarial image can consistently mislead multiple deployed MLLMs, highlighting safety vulnerabilities.

entry.title: Prospective Interpretation Risk: Principled Communication Control Between LLMs

author.name: Wanrong Yang, Rehan Deen, Julian Ma, Yuheng Fan, Yaoyu Jin, Taher Jafferjee, Ziquan Liu, Dominik Wojtczak, Yalin Zheng, David Henry Mguni

entry.summary: This paper defines prospective interpretation risk (PIR): the probability that an LLM receiver reconstructs a task other than the one a sender intended, framed as a sender-receiver problem with latent receiver types. Using black-box probes over message, intended-task, and reconstruction triples, the method estimates per-receiver interpretation risk before sending, enabling communication control in heterogeneous multi-agent systems. This addresses a real and growing failure mode in LLM agent communication.
