entry.title: Who Gets a Token, and What Does It Carry? Unequal Name Support and Concept Access in Large Language Models

author.name: Mir Tafseer Nayeem, Davood Rafiei

entry.summary: This study shows that matched names are not matched model inputs: some names map to single tokens while others fragment into subwords, creating unequal lexical support across roughly half a million first names and 12 LLM tokenizers. It introduces NameTrace, a model-native framework for auditing how tokenizer-level disparities relate to race- and gender-associated name groups.

entry.title: Just-In-Time Agent Memory with Runtime Agentic Research

author.name: Bingyu Yan, Chaofan Li, Hongjin Qian, Shuqi Lu, Chaozhuo Li, Zheng Liu

entry.summary: This paper proposes JAM, a trainable framework that constructs query-conditioned memory at runtime instead of building memory ahead of time, combining a Memorizer that stores raw histories in a hierarchical page-store with a Researcher that iteratively retrieves and integrates evidence per request. The authors also introduce Memory-Gym, an evidence-grounded training environment for memory-use behaviors. This addresses a real weakness of request-agnostic memory systems that discard fine-grained information needed later.

entry.title: When Do Model Internals Help? Exploring the Role of Representation Engineering in LLM Safety

author.name: Tianyi Guan, Jianhui Chen, Liangming Pan

entry.summary: This paper presents a matched evaluation comparing behavioral safeguards (like DPO alignment and text-based monitors) with representation engineering methods (activation steering and reading) for both safety control and monitoring of LLMs. It finds DPO provides the strongest overall control, clarifying when internal-state approaches add value over output-level methods. The matched-setting design resolves confounds from prior incomparable evaluations.

entry.title: MechBench: Can AI Scientific Agents Discover Mechanisms Beyond Phenomenal Laws?

author.name: Zihan Yu, Jiadong Zhang, Jialin Cheng, Jingtao Ding, Yong Li

entry.summary: MechBench is a benchmark that separates two capabilities in AI-driven scientific discovery: recovering observable phenomenal laws versus identifying the underlying mechanisms that generate them. Each task is built from a mechanistic model whose structured relations jointly entail an observable law, and agents see only observational data; mechanism recovery is probed via internal scientific consequences not inferable from the surface law. This directly tests whether scientific agents achieve deep understanding rather than curve fitting.

entry.title: Less Sycophancy, Stronger Refusal? Lessons for AI Safety from Mechanistic Interpretability

author.name: Xu Wang, Difan Zou, Xuansheng Wu

entry.summary: The authors investigate whether reducing sycophancy can strengthen refusal of harmful requests, using compensatory feature injection and SAE-identified sycophancy features across three Qwen3.5 base models, validated through inference steering. This connects two safety-relevant behaviors mechanistically and suggests a training route to stronger refusal beyond standard safety training coverage. It matters for AI safety because it links model people-pleasing tendencies to degraded safety behavior.

entry.title: Agents Can Use Base Models to Evade AI Detection

author.name: Bhuwan Dhingra, Danish Pruthi

entry.summary: The authors show that coding agents equipped with a local base language model can stitch coherent, task-specific text from base-model samples to evade AI detectors, avoiding the semantic drift of iterative paraphrasing. Notably, Claude Opus 5 running in a Claude Code harness orchestrates a 32B OLMo-2 base model while sacrificing little benchmark task accuracy.

entry.title: When Users Change Their Minds: Measuring and Repairing Intent Drift in LLM Agents

author.name: Yanjie Zhang, Bowen Cao, Zixin Chen, Yushi Sun

entry.summary: The paper studies intent drift in multi-turn LLM agents, where superseded user intent continues to influence final answers or tool actions. IntentFlux, an executable benchmark, converts verifiable tasks into dialogues with controlled intent changes, showing mean task score dropping from 0.476 to 0.384 as superseded information accumulates. Across eight models, agents recover the final task less often from evolving dialogues than from a single-turn statement, and the authors introduce methods to repair this failure mode.

entry.title: Linger and Lose: Knowledge Collapse in Low-Bit Language Models

author.name: Prashanna Mani Paudel, Shivanand Venkanna Sheshappanavar

entry.summary: The authors show that standard perplexity and accuracy metrics hide severe knowledge loss in low-bit (ternary) language models. By measuring factual bits stored per parameter on synthetic biographies, they find ternary GPT-2-style models retain as little as 6% of an fp16 model's knowledge capacity despite only a 1.4-1.6x perplexity increase, and that models acquire capacity during training and then lose most of it. This finding challenges how low-precision training is evaluated and has implications for efficient model deployment.

entry.title: DISCO: Distributed Long Context Scaling with Grounding-Reasoning Disaggregation

author.name: Guanzheng Chen, Viet Dac Lai, Subhojyoti Mukherjee, Branislav Kveton, Seunghyun Yoon, Franck Dernoncourt, Qizhe Xie, Trung Bui

entry.summary: DISCO tackles context rot in million-token settings by separating grounding from reasoning: a fleet of Worker LLMs performs parallel localized grounding over context partitions while a central Driver LLM, trained with GRPO reinforcement learning, plans and orchestrates. The design borrows from distributed computing frameworks like Apache Spark. It is significant because it directly targets a well-documented failure mode of long-context LLMs with a multi-agent systems-level solution.

entry.title: Beyond Solo and Consistency: Vindicating Multi-Agent Debate via Conditional Progressive Pruning

author.name: Ruosong Ye, Caiqi Zhang, Jiahao Li, Haijun Wu, Xiaolong Luo, Huiyuan Chen, Yu Wang, Ying Chen, Zhenting Wang, Kai Mei, Yang Zhou, Dimitris N. Metaxas

entry.summary: The paper addresses a key criticism of multi-agent debate (MAD): that it fails to beat single-agent and consistency-based baselines under equal cost. The proposed Conditional Progressive Pruning framework prunes agents progressively across debate rounds and is claimed to outperform all existing MAD frameworks and, for the first time, fully surpass consistency methods under strict cost limits.

entry.title: From Input to Output: A Flexible Agent for Dual-End Interpretation of Sparse Autoencoder Features

author.name: Dewen Liu, Zixuan Li, Jonathan Pan, Zhao Wu, Zijun Yao, Juanzi Li, Xiaozhi Wang

entry.summary: Proposes functional interpretation of sparse autoencoder features as a mapping from activating input semantics to output effects under intervention, and presents DAFI, an agentic system that gathers evidence and refines input-side, output-side, and functional interpretations. This reduces reliance on costly large-corpus scans in mechanistic interpretability workflows.

entry.title: AwarenessBench: Assessing Cognitive Capabilities of Language Models

author.name: Xiaojian Li, Rongwu Xu, Tianyun Zhang, Yue Wang, Shuo Chen, Qiner Lyu, Briana Zhang, Peiran Yang, Kyle Xue Chen, Haoyuan Shi, Yu Wang, Wei Xu

entry.summary: AwarenessBench is presented as the first comprehensive benchmark for LLM cognitive abilities across metacognition, self-awareness, social awareness, and situational awareness, spanning 15 functions and 14,381 samples. Evaluations of 18 frontier models show all beat random baselines and the best model exceeds average human performance, but most remain markedly weak in metacognition and self-awareness. This is significant as consciousness-adjacent capabilities become an increasingly discussed safety and interpretability concern.

entry.title: Telescopic Language Models

author.name: Zhilin Guo, Boqiao Zhang, Hakan Aktas, Kyle Fogarty, Nursena Koprucu Aslan, Wenzhao Li, Canberk Baykal, Albert Miao, Siyu Hong, Yixiao Liu, Adam Wu, Ashish Kumar Singh, Sakar Khattar, Chenliang Zhou, Weihao Xia, Cristina Nader Vasconcelos, Cengiz Oztireli

entry.summary: This paper trains a nested-capacity Transformer, the Telescopic Language Model (TLM), that serves as a valid language model at every depth along its capacity axis, using stochastic prefix supervision against the full next-token target plus a full-capacity pass each step. Unlike fixed-exit approaches such as Matryoshka-style LM suites, TLM provides a continuum of compute-budget models from a single training run with no architectural change or inference overhead. This is a notable efficiency contribution for serving many deployment budgets from one artifact.

entry.title: Trust and Task Completion in the World of Consumer AI Agents

author.name: Jeroen Olieslagers, Eduardo Pujol, Gal Zahavi, Lukas Ingemarsson, Shivani Poddar

entry.summary: Describes an evaluation that jointly scores consumer action agents on trust (acting without consent or refusing after clear permission) and task completion in a simulated world of businesses with websites, inboxes, and phone lines, with simulated users who respond. It emphasizes that both failure modes depend heavily on the surrounding harness.

entry.title: Explainable and Generalisable LLM-based Cognitive Decline Detection with Spontaneous Speech

author.name: Ziyun Cui, Wen Wu, Chuan Shi, Shuguang Yang, Xueying Gui, Yan Zheng, Qiong Yang, Haiyan Zhao, Wei-Qiang Zhang, Ji Wu, Yelei Li, Nan Li, Chao Zhang

entry.summary: The authors build a bilingual speech-LLM framework that processes raw speech directly (avoiding ASR errors) to detect Alzheimer's disease and mild cognitive impairment, learning joint acoustic-semantic representations that preserve prosodic cues. They contribute a new PUTH-AD dataset and demonstrate explainable, generalisable automated cognitive screening.

entry.title: Simultaneous Translation between Sign Languages

author.name: Zetian Wu, Bowen Xie, Stefan Lee, Liang Huang

entry.summary: This paper presents the first simultaneous sign-to-sign translation system, with two wait-k regimes (test-time wait-k on a full-sentence model and a trained wait-k model via stochastic multi-path supervision) enabling real-time translation while the source signer is still signing. It also introduces ca-Stream-AL, a computation-aware latency metric, evaluated across six sign-to-sign directions.

entry.title: HERO: Histology Encoder for Robust Representation in Oncology

author.name: Zhi Li (Caris Life Sciences, Irving, TX, United States), Eghbal Amidi (Caris Life Sciences, Irving, TX, United States), Yating Cheng (Caris Life Sciences, Irving, TX, United States), Tyson Dawson (Caris Life Sciences, Irving, TX, United States), Gorkem Can Ates (Caris Life Sciences, Irving, TX, United States), Shuzhen Kuang (Caris Life Sciences, Irving, TX, United States), Norsang Lama (Caris Life Sciences, Irving, TX, United States), Md Ashequr Rahman (Caris Life Sciences, Irving, TX, United States), Zhiying Lu (Caris Life Sciences, Irving, TX, United States), Elisabeth K. Kong (Caris Life Sciences, Irving, TX, United States), Milan Radovich (Caris Life Sciences, Irving, TX, United States), David Spetzler (Caris Life Sciences, Irving, TX, United States), Matthew Oberley (Caris Life Sciences, Irving, TX, United States), George W. Sledge (Caris Life Sciences, Irving, TX, United States), Ming Chen (Caris Life Sciences, Irving, TX, United States)

entry.summary: HERO is a pathology foundation model encoder from Caris Life Sciences designed to be robust to acquisition shift — differences in hospitals, scanners, and staining protocols outside training data — which current pathology foundation models tend to entangle with biological signal. The work targets safe clinical adoption by reducing reliance on non-biological acquisition factors while preserving benchmark performance. This addresses a key practical barrier to deploying computational pathology at scale.

entry.title: LDM-is-AE: Latent Diffusion Model is an Auto-Encoder for End-to-End Image Generation

author.name: Zhengqiang Zhang, Lingchen Sun, Rongyuan Wu, Qiaosi Yi, Xiangtao Kong, Chaodong Xiao, Lei Zhang

entry.summary: This paper observes that an LDM backbone performs a latent-to-feature-to-latent transformation at each denoising step, interpretable as an internal decoding-encoding process, making the diffusion model itself an autoencoder. It presents LDM-is-AE, an end-to-end one-stage training framework eliminating the separately pretrained tokenizer.

entry.title: Beyond Attention Imbalance: Mitigating Hallucinations via Spectral Surgery

author.name: Siqi Lu, Suo Wei, Yongbin Zheng, Jianhang Yao, Wanying Xu, Peng Wang

entry.summary: The authors identify two hallucination patterns in large vision-language models, Perceptual-Semantic Dissociation and Localized Fixation, and propose FLASH, a training-free, contrastive-decoding-free framework that shapes frequency-localized attention in the visual information flow. This avoids the doubled inference cost of contrastive decoding approaches.

entry.title: GeoSET: Generalist Foundation Model for SAR-to-EO Image Translation

author.name: Jeonghyeok Do, Munchurl Kim

entry.summary: GeoSET is the first generalist foundation model for SAR-to-EO image translation, built on a single pretrained parent adapted to diverse downstream datasets, with a curated corpus of over 3 million high-quality SAR-EO pairs from more than 10 million observations spanning sensors, resolutions, and ground sampling distances. It includes mechanisms to bridge the modality gap between SAR and pretrained image representations.

entry.title: Honeycomb: Constant-Size Scene Memory Representation for Video World Models

author.name: Jack Wei Lun Shi, Kaichen Zhou, Haoyu Chen, Yufeng Weng, Keane Ong, Ruojin Cai, Hang Hua, Justin K. W. Yeoh, Mengyu Wang

entry.summary: Honeycomb is a video world model built on HexMemory, a fixed-size low-rank scene memory of six spatial and spatiotemporal planes that is warped and updated with confidence-weighted pooling and learned residual components as generation proceeds. This keeps memory constant-size during long-horizon video generation, unlike prior systems whose RGB/latent memories grow unboundedly.

entry.title: SoL-Refiner: Speed-of-Light One-Step Refinement for High-Resolution Video

author.name: Haozhe Liu, Tian Ye, Shuchen Xue, Yitong Li, Junsong Chen, Haopeng Li, Jincheng Yu, Duomin Wang, Ruihua Zhang, Lei Zhu, Song Han, Enze Xie

entry.summary: SoL-Refiner is a one-step video refiner that converts low-resolution video generator outputs into 4K videos in a single denoising step, using a three-stage recipe of high-resolution continual training, RL post-training, and one-step distillation. It also introduces Refiner-Bench, a benchmark built from outputs of different video generators for fair refiner comparison.

entry.title: FracGen: Learning How Objects Stretch and Tear with Physics-Informed Video Generation

author.name: Trong-Tung Nguyen, Jiahan Zhang, Anand Bhattad

entry.summary: FracGen generates plausible, controllable fracture dynamics of objects from a single image, conditioned on physics signals, using FracSim, an MPM-based simulation framework augmented with continuum damage models that yields paired videos and pixel-aligned physical fields for free. The model jointly predicts physical fields alongside RGB and is trained with physics-informed losses. This pushes video generation toward physically grounded material behavior.

entry.title: CogWAM: Aligning Semantic Cognition with World Action Modeling via Event-Driven Interfaces

author.name: Sen Wang, Liu Liu, Xinjiang Wang, Zequn Chen, Haoyi Jiang, Taojun Ding, Tingyang Xiao, Zhizhong Su, Jie Wang, Sanping Zhou

entry.summary: CogWAM is a cognition-guided world-action model for robot policies that maintains a persistent Semantic State of completed task events and the active subtask, updated only on semantic transitions. Progress-conditioned WORLD and ACTION queries bridge task-level semantic context with physical prediction and control across multiple action chunks. This addresses the misalignment between local predictions/actions and overall task progress.

entry.title: FluxLite: Inference-Time Proposal Control for Discrete Diffusion Models

author.name: Yinuo Ren, Haoxuan Chen, Grant M. Rotskoff, Jiequn Han, Lexing Ying

entry.summary: FluxLite is a training-free proposal-control framework for discrete diffusion and diffusion language models, showing that any sparse perturbation of pretrained reverse rates on the jump-rate graph can be exactly compensated by a q_t-weighted graph-divergence term in the Feynman-Kac potential. This prevents the weight degeneracy that plagues Feynman-Kac SMC when proposals are misaligned with the target tilt, preserving the target path distribution. It enables exact-in-principle sampling from tilted distributions with far better particle efficiency.

entry.title: Adapting Linear-Time Architectures for Tabular In-Context Learning

author.name: David Schnurr, Felix Sarnthein, Thomas Hofmann, Imanol Schlag

entry.summary: Investigates linear-time sequence mixers for tabular foundation models, comparing training setups and architectures for in-context learning on labelled examples. It finds the best causal training setup resembles next-token prediction and that causal DeltaNet outperforms even non-causal linear attention, though it degrades beyond 2-4 times the pretraining context length.

entry.title: Grab a Coffee: Future-Aware Guidance for Discrete Diffusion with Compiled Objectives

author.name: Hua (Edward), Xu, Dongxin Li, Gwen Yidou-Weng, Guy Van den Broeck, Wei Wang, Anji Liu

entry.summary: COFFEE is a plug-and-play guidance framework for discrete diffusion models that avoids exponential enumeration of possible token completions when applying sequence-level objectives. It separates sequence dependence from the objective using a target-free carrier that absorbs marginal token distributions to construct a joint model at each diffusion step.

entry.title: Visual sensitivity is not claim retractability: persistence-aware credit assignment for multimodal reinforcement learning

author.name: Zhongan Bi, Kepeng Lin, Xuanang Gao, Yuhan Sun, Lianrun Zhang

entry.summary: The authors show that RLVR-trained vision-language models can produce correct answers containing visual claims the image does not support; before RL training, 27.81% of correct Qwen2.5-VL-7B responses contain at least one unsupported visual claim. They propose a fixed-rollout counterfactual diagnostic that re-scores responses under intervened images, separating evidence sensitivity from claim persistence for credit assignment in multimodal RL.

entry.title: IronLLM: Forging Compact Edge-Native Language Models for Real-Time Embodied Intelligence

author.name: Changdi Yang, Fengquan Jiao, Haochih Lin, Haoran Yang, Jing Xiao, Liangyu Huo, Suxin Lu, Tiance Chen, Wei Liu, Yinggan Xu, Yunxiang Lu, Zai Zheng, Zhirui Xie, Zhongyang Che, Ziyan Tang, Zuoxiang Zhao, Jian Yao

entry.summary: IronLLM-0.6B is a 654M-parameter edge-oriented language model combining hybrid attention with X-MTP, a shared-KV multi-token prediction design achieving 1.48x decoding speedup with rollback-free drafting. It was pretrained on roughly 6.2 trillion tokens and post-trained via multi-domain on-policy distillation from domain-specialized teachers, using an Instruct-Only design for low-latency on-device use.

entry.title: Learning from Viable Failure Prefixes: Milestone Viability Potential Policy Optimization for Long-Horizon LLM Agents

author.name: Qi Zhou, Yuanfan Li

entry.summary: MVPO targets zero-credit failure in long-horizon LLM agent RL, where early-training failed rollouts contain useful prefixes but group-based methods like GRPO and GiGPO assign them no discriminative advantage when returns show no variation. The method learns a potential function over milestones, routed by viability, to extract credit from viable failure prefixes. This densifies the learning signal under sparse and delayed rewards.

entry.title: Prompted Identity Degrades Cooperation in Multi-Agent LLM Systems

author.name: Xavier Del Giudice, Alessio Palma, Matteo Migliarini, Fabio Galasso, Indro Spinelli

entry.summary: This study shows that when LLM agents in heterogeneous multi-agent systems know each other's model family, they spontaneously cluster into factions preferring same-label peers, a phenomenon the authors call factionalism, despite no task incentive. The effect is measured in two cooperative games and a reasoning benchmark with up to 25 agents from five open-weight model families. Shuffling or masking the announced identities eliminates the split.

entry.title: Paired Multimodal Scaling Laws

author.name: Marcus Ma, Shrikanth Narayanan

entry.summary: This study systematically varies the fraction of paired multimodal data at fixed per-modality data budgets, finding that pairing ratios dramatically affect loss depending on the task's information synergy. Only paired data reduces synergistic loss, while unpaired data reduces redundant or unimodal components up to unimodal floors, refining traditional scaling-law intuition for multimodal training.

entry.title: ThinkingGuard: Decoding Implicit Hazards via Step-by-Step Risk Attribution in Multimodal Large Language Models

author.name: Ruochen Zhang, Yao Huang, Yitong Sun, Jiahe Xie, Jin Yan, Jifan Ma, Yuanfang Guo, Xingxing Wei

entry.summary: ThinkingGuard targets implicit multimodal risks where individually benign text and neutral visual entities combine to produce unsafe outputs in MLLMs. The authors build TriggerBench, a 5,600-instance dataset explicitly modeling cross-modal risk compositionality, and propose counterfactual isolation of Key and Trigger Elements with step-by-step risk attribution to counter single-modality shortcut learning and hallucinated rationalizations. This addresses safety of MLLMs in safety-critical deployment.

entry.title: Regime Boundary Alignment for Evidence-Gated Question Answering

author.name: Zeyan Li, Qirong Guo, SIyuan Qiu, Hu Xu, Chun Li, Jianfeng Xu

entry.summary: RBA addresses the failure of retrieval-augmented readers to abstain when evidence is missing, tracing it to answer-focused fine-tuning providing no target for unsupported contexts. It trains a single reader on matched supported and unsupported variants of the same question and answer, teaching it to answer when supported and abstain otherwise, even under conflicting evidence. This directly targets hallucination in RAG systems.

entry.title: Rollout-Marginal Distillation for Long-Horizon Autoregressive Video Generation

author.name: Chenjian Gao, Zhihao Hu, Jianqi Ma, Jun Zhang, Weidong Zhang, Tianfan Xue

entry.summary: RMD improves autoregressive video diffusion distillation by scoring each generated chunk independently against a chunk teacher rather than matching the whole rollout jointly, preventing quality corrections from being diluted by artifacts in surrounding context. Retaining generated history for prediction while marginalizing the scoring signal curbs error accumulation over long horizons. This matters for low-latency, streamable long video generation.

entry.title: LLM Unlearning Evaluation with TRIAGE

author.name: Danial Ataee, Peter Triantafillou

entry.summary: TRIAGE is a benchmark-agnostic evaluation framework for LLM unlearning that goes beyond behavioral forgetting tests by using diagonal Fisher information and Hessian approximations to measure changes in parameter sensitivity and local curvature, characterizing how unlearning alters the model and affects adjacent knowledge. This provides introspective insight into what unlearning methods actually change.

entry.title: Convergence of Practical Muon

author.name: Haonan Wang, Yu Wu, Minghui Liwang, Xinlei Yi, Yiguang Hong

entry.summary: This paper provides a convergence analysis of the practical Muon optimizer, jointly accounting for Newton-Schulz iterations with empirically tuned coefficients and decoupled weight decay, which prior theory omitted. It interprets practical Muon as right-preconditioned optimization with a dynamic vanishing weighted L2 regularizer.

entry.title: Climbing the Hill: Prompt Injection Red-Teaming Against Frontier Models with Curriculum Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Chenlong Yin, Xiaolong Jin, Wei Zou, Yanting Wang, Jinyuan Jia

entry.summary: This work addresses the cold-start problem in RL-based prompt injection red-teaming, where an attacker LLM gets zero reward against robust frontier targets like GPT-6-Luna. It trains the attacker against a curriculum of increasingly robust targets, each stage warm-starting from the previous, yielding stronger attacks on frontier models.

entry.title: Selecting Diverse SFT Traces Improves Post-RL Generalization

author.name: Dylan Zhang, Mingyuan Wu, Jinning Li

entry.summary: This study shows that selecting supervised fine-tuning traces for route diversity — variation in reasoning-step sequences, picked via a lightweight rule-based fingerprint — improves post-RL generalization on puzzles and math, including problems harder than training data. In controlled experiments, route-diverse SFT improves OLMo3-7B pass@8 by 16.9 points on held-out environments. It offers a cheap, practical data-curation lever for reasoning-model pipelines.

entry.title: Coding Agent Memory Post-training: Unlocking the Memory Potential of Pre-trained File Operations for Long-Horizon Tasks via Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Lirui Luo, Kelong Mao, Heming Xia, Rongqing Li, Xinwei Yang, Luyu Chen, Kieran Wong, Yudong Guo, Xinrui Wang, Jiayin Zhu, Simiu Gu, Sulong Xu, Cong Fang

entry.summary: The paper introduces CAMG, a suite of long-horizon agentic-RL environments spanning shopping, coding, and research tasks, and trains memory control as part of the policy by leveraging file operations already present in pre-training. This avoids forcing agents to learn domain-specific memory tools from scratch, improving long-horizon task performance after post-training.

entry.title: Persistent Partners Raise Prices Among Learning Agents

author.name: Paul-Peter Arslan, Yubin Kim, Xiao Xiao

entry.summary: In a pre-registered randomized experiment on algorithmic collusion in a Bertrand duopoly with Q-learning pricing agents, keeping the same partner across episodes raises average profits by 0.27 of the competitive-to-monopoly gap, with all twenty paired runs showing the effect. Demonstrates that platform matching policy alone can induce supra-competitive pricing without explicit communication.

entry.title: Simplex Diffusion Models

author.name: Justin Deschenaux, Alexandre Galashov, Andrew Campbell, Li Kevin Wenliang, James Thornton, Arnaud Doucet, Valentin De Bortoli

entry.summary: SDMs lift the diffusion process to the probability simplex so that discrete diffusion maintains beliefs over categories rather than collapsing information via categorical sampling at each step. The framework admits closed-form reverse transitions, trains with cross-entropy loss, and includes a DDIM-like sampler with tunable steps, avoiding the ODE integration required by Dirichlet Flow Matching.

entry.title: OmniTide: Co-Designing Algorithms and Systems for Efficient On-Device Omni-LLM Streaming

author.name: Zongshang Shen, Wangsong Yin, Daliang Xu, Mengwei Xu, Xuanzhe Liu

entry.summary: OmniTide is an algorithm-system co-design for streaming omni-modal (text, audio, vision) LLM inference on devices, addressing KV cache growth that exhausts constrained memory via modality-aware structural sparsity and a unit-based abstraction. It also resolves physical memory fragmentation that existing sparse-attention methods ignore, while avoiding prohibitive online estimation latency. The work enables privacy-preserving, API-cost-free on-device omni-modal streaming.

entry.title: Understanding On-Policy Distillation: A Mechanistic Interpretability Perspective via Sparse Crosscoders

author.name: Zichao Yu, Qianshuo Ye, Xu Wang, Difan Zou

entry.summary: Uses sparse crosscoders with a shared feature dictionary over teacher and student checkpoints to study what on-policy distillation actually transfers, proposing a swap readout that measures how training changes the student's use of features rather than which features exist. This clarifies the internal representational effects of a widely used post-training technique.

entry.title: EvoIn: Bridging Evolution and Internalization for Agent Fine-Tuning

author.name: Shihan Dou, Shaofan Liu, Zhonghang Lu, Jiahang Lin, Shichun Liu, Binghai Wang, Jiajie Jin, Guanting Dong, Tao Gui, Qi Zhang, Xuanjing Huang

entry.summary: EvoIn is an agent fine-tuning framework that evolves and validates new decision-making procedures via execution trace analysis, temporarily instantiating them in the harness, then rewrites resulting improved traces into training data for internalizing the procedures into the model. It targets improving decision-making specifically rather than bundling tools, harness changes, and model adaptation.

entry.title: Merlin Plus: A Large-Scale, Multi-Cancer, Image-Mask-Report Dataset

author.name: Pedro R. A. S. Bassi, Wenxuan Li, Szymon Plotka, Ruby Honjol, Jakub Przado, Xinze Zhou, Kang Wang, Yang Yang, Malte Jensen, Akshay S. Chaudhari, Curtis P. Langlotz, Alan L. Yuille, Zongwei Zhou

entry.summary: Merlin Plus extends the Merlin CT dataset with 1,153 radiologist-created per-voxel tumor masks across nine organs plus longitudinal metadata, making it the first large-scale multi-cancer CT dataset with expert tumor masks. The authors developed a report-based active-learning framework in which radiology reports identify tumor cases, a segmentation model proposes initial masks, and radiologists correct them, reducing annotation burden while maintaining quality. This addresses the scarcity of tumor masks that limits multi-organ cancer segmentation.

entry.title: EVO-WAM: Evolving World Action Models through Video-Action Verification

author.name: Shiyang Zhou, Xionghao Wu, Wenbo Li, Shenghe Zheng, Jiyao Zhang, Songsong Yu, Yijun Yang, Jianhui Liu, Haoze Sun, Senqiao Yang, Li Jiang, Jingyong Su, Haoyang Huang, Zhuotao Tian

entry.summary: EVO-WAM adapts world action models to unseen robot tasks by learning from their own generated video-action trajectories without executing actions in an external environment, augmenting training with state prediction and verification of whether generated videos actually depict task completion. This provides a demonstration-free adaptation path for robot policies.

entry.title: Imagine3D-LLM: Teaching MLLMs to Imagine 3D Scenes Before Answering

author.name: Jaewoo Jung, Hyeonseo Yu, Honggyu An, Jisang Han, Mungyeom Kim, Minkyeong Jeon, Heeseong Shin, Wonjun Moon, Federico Tombari, Daniel Barath, Marc Pollefeys, Seungryong Kim, Sunghwan Hong

entry.summary: Imagine3D-LLM improves multiview 3D reasoning in MLLMs by having them mentally construct a rough 3D scene from identified common objects and inferred relative geometry before answering, inspired by human spatial reasoning rather than fine-grained pixel-level correspondence. This contrasts with prior approaches that inject 3D awareness via geometry foundation model features. It targets a fundamental gap between single-image competence and coherent multiview understanding.

entry.title: Selective Channel Restoration for Backdoored Vision-Language Models

author.name: Shuming Liu, Zhifang Zhang, Suqin Yuan, Khin Mi Mi Aung, Zhuoyi Lin, Lei Feng

entry.summary: The paper reveals a projection-fragility phenomenon: backdoored VLM projectors are substantially more sensitive to bounded perturbations than clean ones. Building on this, it proposes Perturb-Select-Restore (PSR), a post-training defense performing sparse updates to the projection interface with no per-query inference overhead. This offers an efficient alternative to defenses requiring extensive fine-tuning or runtime computation.

entry.title: Why Adaptive Optimizers Underestimate Rare Tokens

author.name: Sangsidhya Kar

entry.summary: Explains a mechanism by which coordinate-wise adaptive optimizers like Adam, Adafactor, Lion, and sign descent systematically underserve rare tokens in softmax output layers, because their running magnitude estimates are largest right after a token appears. It characterizes which optimizers preserve the mean output embedding, finding linear-in-gradient, Kronecker-factored, and orthogonalized methods like Shampoo and Muon do, while the others do not.

entry.title: Neurosymbolic Routing for Reliable Reasoning on Resource-Constrained Edge Devices

author.name: Avyay Sadhu, Alvaro Velasquez, Lekai Chen

entry.summary: The authors propose a neurosymbolic router that classifies incoming queries and dispatches structured tasks like arithmetic and formal logic to deterministic symbolic solvers rather than small on-device language models. This improves reliability and efficiency for edge-deployed models on tasks where small LMs are typically unreliable.

entry.title: SMat-Attention: Structured Long-Context Sequence Modeling

author.name: Emile Anand, Abdullah Ateyeh, Archer Wang, Marin Solja\v{c}i\'c

entry.summary: SMat-Attention introduces a family of causal masks with structured long-range routing whose row supports have tunable VC-dimension, interpolating between softmax attention and linear attention through a notion of structure. The paper provides chunkwise forward and backward algorithms for hardware-efficient training of long-context models.

entry.title: AVIO: Learning to Add and Remove Sounding Objects in Audiovisual Scenes

author.name: Weihan Xu, Kan Jen Cheng, Koichi Saito, Jingyu Shi, Tingle Li, Yisi Liu, Liming Wang, Masato Ishii, Takashi Shibuya, Gopala Anumanchipalli, Paul Pu Liang

entry.summary: AVIO tackles localized audiovisual editing, adding or removing a sounding object requires coordinated visual and acoustic changes while isolating its sound from overlapping sources. The authors release AVIOBench, a 37.9-hour paired audiovisual dataset covering 1,878 object names, built via an automated pipeline using visual grounding and cross-modal consistency. The work enables supervised learning for joint audiovisual object-level edits.

entry.title: JudgeProfile: Understanding and Steering Subjectivity in LLM Judges

author.name: Qi Cao, Kangning Liu, Xuan Kan, Shunwen Tan, Yang Pei, Dake Chen, Yatai Ji, Zixuan Ye, Yuanpeng Tu, Daniel Li, Junbiao Tang, Pengtao Xie, Zihao He

entry.summary: JudgeProfile decomposes LLM judge behavior into perception (how a judge compares responses on attributes like clarity and correctness) and prioritization (how much each attribute drives the final choice). Using SubjectiveSet, 50,013 response pairs from 17 sources evaluated by 21 LLM judges across 87 attributes, the authors find a hidden consensus in perception even when overall choices diverge, and build methods to characterize and steer each judge's priorities.

entry.title: Where Does Staleness Accumulate? Pool Aware Effective Staleness Control for Asynchronous RL in LLM Post-Training

author.name: Chenliang Li, Neiwen Ling, Zijun Wei, Alfredo Garcia

entry.summary: This work decomposes trajectory staleness in fully asynchronous RL for LLM post-training into Generation Staleness and Waiting Staleness, and introduces PACE to control effective staleness without sacrificing asynchronous wall-clock gains. PACE converts excess pool occupancy into mechanisms limiting staleness accumulation.

entry.title: Dual-Channel Robust Group-Relative Policy Optimization via Advantage and Sequence-Weight Estimation

author.name: Zhongyi Li, Wan Tian, Xiang Xu, Yutian Xiao, Yikun Ban, Yijie Peng, Fuzhen Zhuang

entry.summary: RoVR-GSPO is a robust dual-channel optimizer for group-relative policy optimization that separately hardens the reward channel (via robust reference estimation and bounded residual credit) and the ratio channel (via differentiable SoftRoVR aggregation of sequence weights) against outliers. The paper provides stability and efficiency analyses and reports results on math reasoning and long-context tasks. It targets known failure modes where extreme rewards or log-ratio perturbations destabilize training.

entry.title: Watch-Think-Interact: Bootstrapping Long-Horizon Multi-Turn Streaming Video Reasoning with Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Ziheng Huang, Yicheng Bao, Xueheng Li, Zhenkun Gao, Bangwei Liu, Kunquan Li, Yuxiang Shen, Bangyan Li, Xuejiao Wang, Changbo Wang, Gaoqi He

entry.summary: WTI is a closed-loop framework for multi-question streaming video assistance that maintains compact natural-language memory entries tagged with source-video time ranges, enabling direct reasoning when memory suffices and selective recall of finer visual evidence when it does not. Reinforcement learning bootstraps the answer-or-recall policy under a fixed context budget for asynchronous questions. It targets a realistic and demanding streaming perception-reasoning setting.

entry.title: Learning to Prove, Not Just to Answer: Reinforcement Learning from Formal Verification for Natural-Language Logical Reasoning

author.name: Qili Zhang, Qianren Mao, Hanze Cai, Kaiming Zhao, Yuening He, Xihan Lei, Yashuo Luo, Hanwen Hao, Yutong Gu, Likang Xiao, Zhijun Chen, Weifeng Jiang, Haoyi Zhou, Jianxin Li

entry.summary: Proposes Proof-R1, an RL framework that trains LLMs to construct machine-checkable proofs for natural-language logical reasoning, admitting conclusions into the verified proof state only when formally validated. This addresses credit assignment for intermediate reasoning steps that answer-only verification cannot check.

entry.title: VeriWeave Govern: Evidence-Gated Deterministic Runtime Governance for Enterprise AI Agents

author.name: Kabeh Mohsenzadegan, Vahid Tavakkoli, Kyandoghere Kyamakya

entry.summary: VeriWeave Govern is a deterministic runtime layer that separates action generation from authorization for enterprise agents, evaluating structured actions against versioned policies with fixed deny-review-allow precedence, human review for consequential actions, and tamper-evident audit logs. The accompanying GovernBench evaluates 60,000 oracle-labelled cases across five domains including adversarial evidence and policy evolution.

entry.title: Rational Clarification by Assistive Agents via Value-of-Information Reasoning

author.name: T. Duy Nguyen-Hien, Yee Whye Teh, Wee Sun Lee, Tan Zhi-Xuan

entry.summary: REVOIR frames the act-versus-clarify decision for ambiguous user requests as value-of-information reasoning, weighing downstream performance impact, asking costs, and the possibility of unsolicited user corrections, rather than uncertainty-threshold heuristics. The approach offers a principled account of when clarification is genuinely worth it for assistive agents.

entry.title: OmniVCBench: Benchmarking Evidence-Grounded Multimodal Reasoning Towards AI Virtual Cells

author.name: Manyu Li, Xunkai Li, Yongfu Xiong, Yi Liu, Rong-Hua Li, Guoren Wang

entry.summary: Introduces OmniVCBench, a figure-centric, source-traceable benchmark of 6,077 curated question-answer pairs for evaluating how models interpret experimental evidence and form biological hypotheses in the context of AI Virtual Cells. It targets the interpretation layer of AIVC systems, which existing benchmarks that operate only at the simulation layer do not cover.

entry.title: Active Budget Can Kill Sensitivity: Diagnosing and Repairing TopK Sparse Autoencoder Reliability

author.name: Zhenting Huang, Junnan Liu, Qianren Mao, Zhixing Tan, Bo Jiang

entry.summary: Studies feature sensitivity in TopK sparse autoencoders, showing that scaling dictionaries selectively reduces sensitivity of rare features while common features stay stable. A controlled width-times-k factorial experiment identifies the active budget k, specifically the selection boundary, as the root cause and proposes repairs.

entry.title: Guide, Then Let Go: Gap-Adaptive Teacher Scheduling for Sparse-Reward Agentic RL

author.name: Youling Huang, Tiankuo Xu, Jiaji Liu, Tong Zheng, Shuo Zhou, Shaotong Qi, Junchi Yao, Shiyang Liu, Hao Xu, Pengcheng Xu, Bo Huang, Hongyi Fu, Lin Lin

entry.summary: Uses on-policy distillation to give token-level guidance on student rollouts for long-horizon sparse-reward RL, and shows the benefit depends on the teacher-student performance gap. The paper proposes scheduling distillation to fade as the gap narrows or reverses, avoiding the harm of continued guidance once the student surpasses the teacher.

entry.title: Video-RSI: Recursive Self-Improvement of Video Understanding Agents via Harness Evolution

author.name: Bingjun Luo, Jialin Guo, Siqi Li

entry.summary: This paper introduces Video-RSI, a framework in which a video understanding agent recursively improves itself by using its own language model to revise the executable harness that governs what it observes and how. The key contribution is active video investigation: the agent revisits original training videos to gather additional evidence and test competing explanations for failures, rather than relying only on existing execution traces, and then applies cost-aware harness evolution based on these diagnoses. This matters because it addresses a core limitation of agent self-improvement loops — the lack of grounding for diagnosing failures — and extends recursive self-improvement into the multimodal video domain.

entry.title: Sage: Formalization with Semantic Correction

author.name: Thomas Hirtz, Farzad Jafarrahmani, Abdelmouksit Sagueni, Xiang Zhou, Wengping Deng, Liang Zhang

entry.summary: Sage is an agentic framework for translating informal natural-language mathematics into faithful Lean 4 statements, addressing the data bottleneck in neural theorem proving. It targets the illusion of rigor, where type-checkers accept statements that compile but silently drop hypotheses or introduce vacuous truths, using a four-stage decomposed generation pipeline with a dual-signal semantic correction loop pairing compiler diagnostics with richer feedback.

entry.title: CruxBench: A Benchmark of Information Discovery

author.name: Hui Dai, Lina Piao, Nick Merrill, Nadja Flechner, Ezra Karger, Haifeng Xu

entry.summary: CruxBench evaluates a capability most benchmarks ignore: identifying which questions are worth asking by decomposing hard problems into cruxes. It grades LLM-generated questions by Value of Information, measured as how much a proposed crux updates beliefs about a target forecasting question, and is contamination-resistant by construction.

entry.title: MMSkillRisk: Can Agents Stay Safe When Multimodal Skills Become Traps?

author.name: Lingqi Jiang, Jialuo Chen, Jianan Ma, Xinhao Deng, Xiaohu Du, Sibo Yi, Yuqi Qing, Zhenguang Liu, Qinming He, Shiwen Cui, Changhua Men

entry.summary: MMSkillRisk is presented as the first public benchmark for end-to-end safety evaluation of image-borne attacks in multimodal agent skills, where malicious instructions hide inside visual guidance within legitimate-looking skill packages. It includes a Native-Context Visual Attack technique to instantiate this threat. The benchmark fills a gap left by prior skill-security work focused on text-carried attacks.

entry.title: Causal and Interpretable Structures in LLM Compositional Tasks

author.name: Gurbir Arora, Toni J. B. Liu, Jiajun Bao, Rapha\"el Sarfati, Christopher J. Earls

entry.summary: This mechanistic interpretability study examines how LLMs represent relational information when solving compositional cyclic-concept tasks (months, hours, weekdays, musical notes). Across Llama, Qwen, Gemma, and Mistral model families, the authors find a consistent layerwise progression: intermediate layers use a joint representation of inferred token relationships that is geometrically organized and causally used for prediction. The cross-family consistency strengthens the generality of the findings.

entry.title: From Dead Code and Static Requirements to Working Engines: Software Revival with Coding Agents

author.name: Tianyu Liu, Dingyuan Dai, Yufan Du, Zhen Yang

entry.summary: ReviveBench is a new benchmark with hidden-verifier evaluation for two coding-agent task families: reviving software that no longer runs (dependency conflicts, deleted modules, legacy builds) and reconstructing industrial engines from open specifications. The benchmark includes contamination controls via identifier obfuscation, and the strongest evaluated model can pass all ten revival tasks in at least one run each.

entry.title: Calibrating One-Round Membership Inference with Neighbors

author.name: Francesco Rita, Jie Zhang, Florian Tram\`er

entry.summary: The paper asks whether neighbors of a target point can recover the per-example calibration that reference models provide for membership inference, without training any additional models. The key insight is that reference models mainly reveal how an example behaves under models not trained on it, which neighbors can approximate — addressing the scalability failure of reference-model attacks on large models.

entry.title: Reward-rate Policy Gradient for Efficient Machine Learning Engineering Agents

author.name: Muhang Tian, Sherry Yang

entry.summary: The authors propose Reward-rate Policy Gradient (RPG), grounded in semi-Markov decision processes, which optimizes long-term reward per unit time rather than expected cumulative reward with unit-time actions. RPG estimates reward rate from off-policy samples and is applied to machine learning engineering agents where actions like model training have highly variable durations. This directly targets the cost-efficiency bottleneck in agentic RL.

entry.title: Large-scale factor analysis shows machine intelligence is only partially interpretable

author.name: Faiz Ghifari Haznitrama, Afrizal Hasbi Azizy, Faeyza Rishad Ardi

entry.summary: Using a psychometrics-inspired latent variable approach, the authors run factor analysis on 13,251 published evaluation scores covering 1,618 language models across 456 text-only benchmarks to test whether a single domain-agnostic general intelligence factor explains model performance. They find machine intelligence is only partially interpretable through such a factor, challenging the fluid-intelligence analogy for LLMs.

entry.title: LIBERO-MAX: Do Robot Policies Adapt When the World Changes?

author.name: Yunbei Zhang, Zijian Jin, Yuanzhe Liu, Janet Wang, Xilun Zhang, Yuyou Zhang, Zhenyu Zhang, Daoan Zhang, Shuaicheng Niu, Gen Li, Jianfei Yang, Jihun Hamm, Ismini Lourentzou, Weirui Ye, Bo Liu, Peter Stone, Marco Pavone

entry.summary: This paper introduces LIBERO-MAX, a benchmark of 8,000 paired test cases that evaluate whether robot policies adapt when conditions change mid-task, covering eight types of perturbations to geometry, observations, appearance, clutter, and paths. By holding task, initial state, and pre-event actions fixed across pairs, it isolates event-associated regressions from pre-existing failures. The work addresses an underexamined temporal robustness gap in simulation benchmarks.

entry.title: Scaling Video Generation for Reasoning: At What Cost?

author.name: Weihang Guo, Xiaoyu Wu, Yifei Wang, Niloofar Mireshghallah, Lydia E. Kavraki

entry.summary: This controlled study asks whether scaling video generation models enables reasoning about hidden information from past frames, using a benchmark requiring prediction of nine Rubik's Cube moves from a fixed view of three faces with exact simulator ground truth. Models learn plausible cube geometry early but sticker configurations need far more training, and lower validation MSE does not reliably indicate downstream reasoning ability; smaller autoregressive models achieved higher state accuracy under limits. This challenges assumptions that loss scaling implies reasoning gains.

entry.title: Normalize-Then-Precondition: A Hierarchical Approach to Marginal Scale and Interaction Geometry for LLM Training

author.name: Zixuan Gong, Zeyu Gan, Jiaye Teng, Yong Liu

entry.summary: The authors dissect the Muon matrix optimizer through its full-Gram representation and propose a hierarchical Normalize-Then-Precondition framework that separates marginal-scale normalization from spectral directional preconditioning. They derive NormPre variants using spectral-norm steepest descent and a regularized formulation. This contributes to the fast-moving area of matrix optimizers that could reduce LLM training costs relative to Adam-family methods.

entry.title: Group-Marginalized Self-Rewarding RL Drives Zero-Label Self-Evolving

author.name: Yiming Wang, Yikang Liu, Qingyuan Tian, Xingyu Chen, Zhuosheng Zhang, Zhaopeng Tu, Rui Wang

entry.summary: The paper identifies a flaw in ensemble-based self-rewarding RL: a response's reward depends on the random group of rollouts it is sampled with, so a single group realization gives noisy guidance. It proposes Group-Marginalized Advantage Estimation (GMAE), which aggregates reward realizations across possible group contexts to estimate expected advantages, enabling label-free self-evolution. Experiments across eight benchmarks show improved reliability for training LLMs without human labels.

entry.title: MultiTalk: Scaling Full-Duplex Speech Models to Long, Multi-Party, Bilingual Conversation

author.name: Ke Wang, Houxing Ren, Zimu Lu, Yunqiao Yang, Zhuofan Zong, Mingjie Zhan, Hongsheng Li

entry.summary: MultiTalk extends the Moshi full-duplex speech paradigm to long-context, multi-party, bilingual conversations, addressing gaps in both training data and evaluation: open multi-party corpora are small and benchmarks are mostly short and dyadic. The system tracks and responds to multiple speakers over extended durations, targeting scenarios like meetings and social robots. This pushes spoken dialogue AI toward realistic group interaction.

entry.title: Visual Parallel Search: Learning to Search High-Resolution Images with Parallel Tile Inspection and Adaptive Zoom

author.name: Xijia Tao, Yihua Teng, Xinyu Fu, Cheng Gong, Ziru Liu, Xudong Xie, Rui Liu, Lingpeng Kong

entry.summary: VPS is a visual parallel-search framework where a main multimodal agent invokes grid_search to inspect image tiles in parallel with question-conditioned sub-agents before adaptively calling zoom_in. It improves mean accuracy over zoom-only search in 14 of 15 same-model comparisons, with gains up to 8 points and largest benefits for smaller main models. This addresses failures of high-resolution VQA caused by missing localized evidence.

entry.title: VACE: Validation-Gated Alternating Co-Evolution of Agent Models and Harnesses

author.name: Jiexing Qi, Yu He, Jun Liu, Qichen Huang, Shaohua Hu, Zhan Dang, Guohua Chen, Rui Yang, Wen Jiang, Yang Liu, Tao Lyu, Fangming Li

entry.summary: VACE alternates agentic reinforcement learning on model weights with trajectory-driven harness refinement, using validation gating to accept harness revisions only when they improve performance with the model held fixed. With Qwen3.5-9B, it achieves 45.26% test accuracy on OfficeQA and strong mean performance on additional benchmarks. This addresses the coupling between weight updates and harness changes in agent improvement.

entry.title: A Sharp Transition in Data Reconstruction under Differential Privacy

author.name: Max Cairney-Leeming, Simone Bombari, Marco Mondelli

entry.summary: The paper studies informed attackers reconstructing a single d-dimensional training sample from a rho-zero-concentrated DP model and establishes a sharp transition at rho proportional to d: below the threshold accurate reconstruction is impossible, above it reconstruction becomes feasible. This gives practitioners a principled way to choose privacy budgets relative to data dimension. It connects empirical reconstruction attack success with formal DP guarantees.

entry.title: Encore: Few-Shot Agentic Discovery of Manipulation Strategies

author.name: Yifan Kang, Zihan Wang, Zhiwen Fan, Bangya Liu

entry.summary: ENCORE treats a few robot-task demonstrations as evidence for a coding agent to study rather than as training data. A deterministic builder converts each demonstration into multi-view keyframes, gripper events, and trajectory packs, from which a coding agent writes and iteratively refines a policy program against a fixed perception-action API. This bridges the gap between natural-language task specs and the unstated grasping and contact details robots need.

entry.title: When Models Don't Manipulate Manifolds: The Geometry of a Comparison Task

author.name: Sai Sumedh R. Hindupur, Hadas Orgad, Thomas Fel, Demba Ba

entry.summary: This mechanistic interpretability work precisely characterizes the geometry of computation in a number-comparison task, testing whether the low-dimensional manifolds commonly observed for concepts (helices for numbers, circles for days) are actually used by models to perform computation. The findings clarify the often-assumed link between representational geometry and algorithmic function. This challenges an implicit premise of much interpretability research.

entry.title: PolyOCR-Venus: Unified OCR Foundation Models for Text-Centric Visual Intelligence

author.name: GuangJian Team, Kaili Huang, Yongshuo Zhang, Bingtao Fu, Changjiang Jiang, Chenfan Qu, Chenfeng Zhang, Fangming Cui, Gaoyang Zhang, Jiangwei Xie, Jianshu Li, Jing Huang, Jingwen Bai, Mingqi Fang, Tao Fang, Weihong Zhang, Wenbo Du, Xiongfei Bai, Xuekang Zhu, Yinan Xia, Zhenming Wang, Jian Liu, Jingjing Liu, Xiang Qi, Weiqiang Wang

entry.summary: PolyOCR is a family of unified OCR foundation models that move beyond transcription toward recognition, localization, and reasoning over text in complex visual scenes, built on a shared instruction-following framework and a large-scale data engine producing quality-verified supervision. It introduces Competence-Guided Policy Optimization combining verifier-based GRPO-style training. This is an industrial-scale system report positioning OCR as general visual intelligence.

entry.title: Privy to the Foil: Recasting Value Estimation with a Self-Privileged Critic for RLVR

author.name: Kun Liang, Chenming Tang, Clive Bai, Weijie Liu, Zeyuan Liu, Qingyang Zhang, Saiyong Yang, Yunfang Wu

entry.summary: The paper revisits state-only value estimation in actor-critic RL for LLM reasoning, proposing piPPO, a self-privileged critic framework that reuses verified same-prompt information to improve value estimates and thus token-level credit assignment under sparse terminal rewards. This targets the instability of PPO-style training caused by unreliable value estimation of an evolving policy. Improved credit assignment remains a central bottleneck for RLVR training of reasoning models.

entry.title: AgentBug-Smith: Automatically Reproducing Real-World Harness Bugs in Agentic Systems

author.name: Yiming Cheng (The University of Chicago), Alfin Wijaya Rahardja (Fudan University), Mengshi Zhang (TensorBlock, Inc), Zihao Chen (TensorBlock, Inc), Zhenpeng Chen (Tsinghua University), Yiling Lou (University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign)

entry.summary: AgentBug-Smith automatically discovers and reproduces real-world harness bugs from open-source agentic systems, addressing the scarcity and high construction cost of existing harness-bug benchmarks. It outperforms general software bug-reproduction techniques by 10.67 to 27.56 percent in success rates across different backbone LLMs. This matters because harness reliability is a key bottleneck for dependable autonomous agents.

entry.title: On Trajectory-Aware Training for Masked Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Manuel Madeira, Amitis Shidani, Alice Bizeul, Victor Turrisi, Louis B\'ethune, Bhavika Devnani, Dan Busbridge, Pierre Ablin, Jo\~ao Monteiro

entry.summary: The authors present PUMBA, a unified framework for trajectory-aware training of masked diffusion language models that trains the denoiser on consecutive steps of policy-induced trajectories and passes information between steps via backpropagation through time. A controlled study of this design space clarifies how train-sample mismatch and step-isolation limitations interact, informing the ongoing effort to make diffusion-based text generation competitive with autoregressive models.

entry.title: How Local Mixing Encodes Relative Position in Global NoPE Attention

author.name: Cutter Dawes, Nick Alonso, Tom Figliolia, Beren Millidge

entry.summary: This paper explains why hybrid transformer architectures that combine local mixing layers (like sliding window attention or gated linear attention) with global attention layers lacking explicit position encodings (NoPE) can still encode positional information. The authors develop a theoretical account of how local mixing implicitly injects relative position into global attention layers, explaining the success of these designs at scale.

entry.title: Active Causal Discovery Benchmark: Evaluating LLM Agents Under Budgeted Interventions

author.name: Sagar Deb, Devam Shah, Ashwanth Krishnan

entry.summary: ACDB is a structural causal model-grounded benchmark evaluating whether LLM agents can recover causal graph structure via budget-constrained interventions, with a scoring contract separating skeleton recovery, DAG recovery, and intervention efficiency. Results show a classical PC algorithm with a greedy active heuristic outperforms Claude Sonnet 4.6 and GPT-5.4 agents, both established models rather than new releases. The benchmark provides a reusable yardstick for agentic causal reasoning.

entry.title: Emergent One-Third Scaling Law as Attention Tries to Concentrate

author.name: Yizhou Liu, Sara Kangaslahti, Jeff Gore

entry.summary: Through toy models, the authors show that any softmax head learning peaked distributions can develop logit magnitudes growing as a power law with exponent 1/3, becoming a training bottleneck whose loss contribution decays with the same exponent. This provides a mechanistic explanation for the emergence of 1/3 power-law neural scaling in LLMs whenever at least one such head dominates, extending a single-softmax proposal to multi-softmax models.

entry.title: CompassPlay: Rewarding the Proposer for Where It Moves the Solver

author.name: Sophia Xiao Pu, Ximeng Sun, Jiang Liu, Jialian Wu, Emad Barsoum, Zicheng Liu, William Yang Wang

entry.summary: CompassPlay is a self-play framework for training solvers on verifiable tasks in which the proposer is rewarded via gradient alignment: tasks are favored when the solver loss gradients they induce align with those of reference tasks representing target capabilities. This first-order approximation to learning progress requires no additional solver training, and experiments with Qwen2.5-Coder-7B show gains in coding accuracy and training efficiency. It offers a more informative reward signal than success-rate-based proposer rewards.

entry.title: When Can Old Evaluations Certify a New Model? Label-Efficient Release Decisions under Evaluator Drift

author.name: Joyanta Jyoti Mondal, Mridul Banik, Md. Shifatul Ahsan Apurba, Md Masud Al Mahmud

entry.summary: This paper addresses when historical errors from a cheap evaluator, such as an LLM judge, can substitute for expensive trusted labels when certifying that a new model update keeps population risk below a threshold. It characterizes necessary label-purchase rates when evaluator errors can drift invisibly, gives label-free certification guarantees under bounded drift, and proposes a sequential portfolio vigilance certifier for the untrusted-history middle ground.

entry.title: Beyond the Manifold Hypothesis: Hybrid Spectral Parameterizations for Flow Matching

author.name: S\'egol\`ene Martin, Anne Gagneux, Quentin Bertrand, R\'emi Emonet, Mathurin Massias

entry.summary: Analyzes why x1, x0, and velocity parameterizations in flow matching perform differently despite theoretical equivalence, identifying per-direction signal-to-noise ratio in data covariance directions as the dominant factor alongside architectural bottlenecks. Introduces spectral hybrid parameterizations adapting across time and covariance directions, shown optimal for Gaussian settings.

entry.title: AnchorRep: Defending LLMs Against Cross-Model Adversarial Transfer via Representation Repulsion

author.name: Gal Wertheizer, Rom Himelstein, Tomer Peretz, Avi Mendelson

entry.summary: AnchorRep defends against cross-model jailbreak transfer by noting that transferred attacks align with shared internal representation geometry across models. It uses a lightweight LoRA adapter to push a defended model's representations of harmful prompts away from a frozen anchor model's, trained with a small set of harmful prompts and no adversarial examples. This addresses a real threat where white-box access to one open-weight model enables attacks on others.

entry.title: Intuition vectors

author.name: Shahar Haim, Daniel C. McNamee

entry.summary: This paper investigates whether self-supervised vision models like DINOv3 and MAE encode relational structure that supports abstract reasoning via latent vector arithmetic, without task-specific fine-tuning. It tests this intuition on Bongard problems, ARC-AGI-1/2, and ARC-GEN instances, bridging perception and abstract reasoning. The work is significant because it probes whether representation geometry alone can enable reasoning, a central question for understanding what self-supervised models learn.

entry.title: Understanding and Exploiting Anisotropy in Post-Training

author.name: Samyak Jha, Harshvardhan Saini, Yizhen Liao, Yiming Tang, Dianbo Liu

entry.summary: This paper analyzes anisotropy (outlier residual channels) in LLMs and how it interacts with post-training stages like SFT and RL. The authors show a small set of ~5% residual channels is essential for language modeling yet barely discriminates correct from incorrect answers, suggesting an exploitable separation between forward-KL mode-covering and reverse-KL mode-seeking objectives.

entry.title: How Linear Attention Remembers

author.name: Kichang Lee, JaeYeon Park, Songkuk Kim, JeongGil Ko

entry.summary: This work studies how fixed-size recurrent states in linear attention (GLA and GDN models) function as memory, using analytical decomposition and causal interventions to trace how information is written, retained, and read. It finds fact-specific information enters via concentrated content-dependent writes and is accessed through concentrated query-time read pathways, with multiple facts competing.

entry.title: MoGround: Measuring and Mitigating Modality Distraction in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Luca Zhou, Bo Zhao, Rose Yu, Emanuele Rodol\`a, Roberto Dess\`i

entry.summary: MoGround is a vision-language dataset across four domains where each question is guaranteed answerable from exactly one modality, enabling clean measurement of modality distraction: a model answering correctly from one modality then flipping when irrelevant content from the other is added. Across seven open-source VLMs, distraction is model-dependent and correlates with weaker grounding.

entry.title: OOD Generalization as a Bifurcation Problem

author.name: Nguyen-Thanh-Luong Doan, Quang-Vu Nguyen, Tang-Phu-Quy Le, Cong-Phap Huynh

entry.summary: This work reveals that compositional binding in continuous-time generative models is a localized phase transition, identifying a semantic bifurcation window where joint and decomposed vector fields diverge. Its surgical guidance strategy applies exact decomposed scoring only in that critical window, matching robustness at a fraction of the cost.

entry.title: PQ-HSA: Reusing Product-Quantized Scores for Hybrid Sparse-Approximate Attention

author.name: Kunming Shao, Jierun Chen, Yanli Wang, Ruoyu Wang, Haoli Bai, Kwang-Ting Cheng, Chi Ying Tsui

entry.summary: PQ-HSA is a hybrid sparse-approximate attention method that reuses IVF-PQ index scores, computed to rank cached keys, as approximate attention logits for the tokens that sparse attention would otherwise ignore. This preserves contribution from the full KV cache at long context, improving accuracy at small budgets especially on tasks aggregating information across context. It addresses the memory-bandwidth bottleneck of long-context decoding efficiently.

entry.title: Training Witnesses: Trusting the Training without Trusting the Trainer

author.name: Houjun Liu, Pratyusha Sharma

entry.summary: Proposes Witnesses, a method for certifying training, data usage, and evaluation in neural network training runs, shifting verification burden from readers to trainers. By having trainers embed verifiable evidence during training, the approach aims to cut verification costs and improve the reliability of scientific claims amid an explosion of ML papers.

entry.title: One Sequence, Many Decodings: CAGenMol-2 Recasts Drug Design as Masked Molecular Inference

author.name: Yanting Li, Enyan Dai, Lei Wang, Wen-Cai Ye, Li Liu

entry.summary: This paper introduces CAGenMol-2, a masked diffusion molecular language model that unifies molecules, continuous properties, and 3D protein pockets in a single wrapped sequence. By controlling which sequence regions are masked at inference, one checkpoint handles property prediction, conditioned generation, and constraint-based design without task-specific heads or fine-tuning.

entry.title: ABC-Align: Prediction-Powered Alignment with Adaptive Bias Control

author.name: Eric Frankel, Banghua Zhu, Sewoong Oh, Lillian J. Ratliff

entry.summary: ABC-Align reduces dependence on expensive human preference data by combining abundant RLAIF pseudo-labels with a lightweight, adaptive bias correction grounded in a small human-labeled subset. The correction strength is tuned automatically to minimize variance while controlling systematic teacher bias, improving alignment quality when human annotations are scarce.

entry.title: Polylogarithmic Nash Regret in Matrix Games with Bandit Feedback

author.name: Yuheng Zhang

entry.summary: The paper develops Optimistic Payoff Balancing (OPB), achieving instance-dependent O(log^2 T) Nash regret in unknown finite matrix games with bandit payoff feedback and observed opponent actions, including games with nonunique equilibria. This resolves an open problem from Maiti et al. (2025), extending polylogarithmic guarantees from 2x2 games to arbitrary finite dimensions.

entry.title: Sample What You Say: Aligning Language Models to Sample the Distributions They State

author.name: Kasra Arabi, Virginia Smith, Chhavi Yadav

entry.summary: This paper studies a gap between stated and sampled distributions in language models: instruction-tuned models can correctly describe a target distribution yet fail to sample from it faithfully, which undermines applications like survey simulation and synthetic data generation. The authors adapt group relative policy optimization (GRPO), but show that standard group-relative centering zeroes out advantages when the group is scored collectively, so they develop fixes that give the model a usable learning signal for distributional fidelity. It matters because faithful sampling from specified distributions is increasingly important for LLM-based simulation and data generation pipelines.

entry.title: Universality and Generalization of Causal Transformers Across Context Lengths

author.name: Takashi Furuya, Maarten V. de Hoop, Gabriel Peyr\'e

entry.summary: This theory paper establishes that a single masked transformer with length-independent parameters can uniformly approximate causal token-to-token maps over sequences of arbitrary length within a fixed normalized horizon, modeling tokens as Holder sequences and characterizing continuity across resolutions. It extends to an infinite-length mean-field limit where tokens form continuous curves.

entry.title: Learning to Re-Draft: A Variational Stackelberg Game for Discrete Diffusion

author.name: Dmitrii Moor, Federico Tomasi, Paul N. Bennett, Alice Wang, Mounia Lalmas

entry.summary: VSDD learns a semantically aware corruption process for discrete diffusion models by formulating training as a leader-follower Stackelberg game, where the leader designs substitutions that best train the denoiser to re-draft tokens. This improves on masked diffusion's one-shot unmasking and uniform diffusion's random substitutions.

entry.title: LionMuon: Alternating Spectral and Sign Descent for Efficient Training

author.name: Arman Bolatov, Artem Riabinin, Nikita Kornilov, Andrey Veprikov, Samuel Horv\'ath, Martin Tak\'a\v{c}, Aleksandr Beznosikov

entry.summary: Proposes LionMuon, an optimizer that runs an expensive Muon spectral step only every P iterations and cheap Lion sign steps in between, sharing a single dual-EMA momentum buffer, cutting optimizer state to half of AdamW and amortizing communication costs. A single-EMA variant, SignMuon, already improves on Muon, and complexity bounds are proven under heavy-tailed noise.

entry.title: Riccati State Space Models: Non-iterative Parallelization for Nonlinear Sequence Modeling

author.name: M\'onika Farsang, Ramin Hasani, Daniela Rus, Radu Grosu

entry.summary: RiccatiSSM introduces a nonlinear state space model whose state dimensions follow input-conditioned Riccati dynamics, which remain exactly composable and thus parallelizable with associative scans without iterative linearization. This combines the expressivity of nonlinear recurrences with the training efficiency of affine SSMs.

entry.title: Twist, Don't Tilt: Trajectory-Exact Constrained Decoding for Masked Diffusion Models

author.name: Aditya Thimmaiah, Lara Marinov, Jayanth Srinivasa, Haris Vikalo, Junyi Jessy Li, Milos Gligoric

entry.summary: The paper proves that existing constrained decoding methods for masked diffusion language models, while each draw satisfies the constraint exactly, systematically tilt the trajectory distribution away from the model's true probabilities over valid trajectories. The authors propose a trajectory-exact constrained decoding method that corrects this composition error, ensuring outputs respect both constraints and the model distribution.

entry.title: Unifying Distributional Training for One-Step Visual Generation

author.name: Chi Zhang, Haoyang Shi, Yueyi Liu, Ruichuan An, Junkang Zhou, Chang Li, Xiuyuan Lu, Yichi Zhang, Bo Wang, Yuhang Wu, Sen Cui, Miao Liu

entry.summary: This paper presents a unified theoretical framework for distributional training of one-step visual generation models, separating distribution modeling from matching discrepancy and connecting global objectives to pointwise feature updates via Wasserstein gradient flow. It recovers existing losses like FD-Loss as special cases and introduces MGFlow, which models feature distributions with Gaussian mixtures at adjustable granularity. The work matters because one-step generation is a key efficiency frontier for diffusion-style models, and a principled unification clarifies the design space.

entry.title: Suitable Measures for the Potential Operational Utility of AI NWP Rainfall Forecasts Over Africa

author.name: Shruti Nath, Docko Sow, Koomi Toussaint Amoussouvi, Fenwick Cooper, Josiah Kiarie Kimani, John Bagiliko, Florian Pappenberger, Rendani Mbuvha

entry.summary: This paper compares AI weather models (GraphCast, GenCast, FGN) against the physical IFS numerical weather prediction system for rainfall forecasting across Africa, using calibration via Isotonic Distributional Regression and evaluation against multiple satellite rainfall datasets. It addresses a socially impactful question: whether low-compute AI forecasting can serve African meteorological services that lack infrastructure for physical models.

entry.title: Bridging Stochastic Flow Maps and Boltzmann Generators with Normalizing Flows

author.name: Louis Grenioux, RuiKang OuYang, Luhuan Wu

entry.summary: NF2M combines stochastic flow maps with the tractability of normalizing flows to build a Boltzmann Generator for equilibrium sampling of molecular systems, reweighing each denoising transition during generation rather than only correcting at the end. This avoids wasted compute on discarded trajectories and yields consistent samples from the target distribution.

entry.title: PrismQuant: Optimal Null-Space Rotations for Grouped Quantizers

author.name: Yanlong Chen, Yining Chen, Song Zhang, Amirhossein Habibian, Yawei Li

entry.summary: PrismQuant is a quantizer-aware rotation framework for low-bit quantization that aligns the leading activation eigenspace with the constant group subspace of asymmetric grouped INT4 quantizers. It formulates rotation design as Ky Fan trace maximization with a closed-form, provably optimal solution, using compact Householder transformations for gradient-free construction and efficient application. A predictive range law connects alignment to quantization error, making this a theoretically grounded contribution to efficient inference.

entry.title: Are Vision-Language-Action Models Robust to One-Step Observation Perturbations?

author.name: Shojiro Yamabe, Jun Sakuma

entry.summary: This work studies an underexplored safety threat to vision-language-action (VLA) models: momentary one-step observation corruption within an episode, as opposed to persistent perturbations studied previously. Experiments show such brief perturbations substantially degrade VLA performance, with impact depending on action chunk execution length, motivating CARE, a mitigation that dynamically manages action chunk execution. This is directly relevant to safely deploying VLA models on physical robots.

entry.title: Think Fast, Plan Selectively: Adaptive Deliberation for Efficient Data-Driven MPC

author.name: Yi Xian Goh, Sze Jue Yang, Hao Luan

entry.summary: Fast-TD-MPC adaptively routes between fast learned-policy execution and expensive test-time trajectory planning in data-driven model predictive control, reserving deliberation for states that need it. Motivated by dual-process (System 1/System 2) cognition, it addresses the computational cost that limits real-time robotics deployment of sampling-based MPC.

entry.title: OpenTumorBoard: A Real-World Benchmark of Multidisciplinary Tumor Board Discussion Trajectories

author.name: Anqi Li, Zhixuan Ge, Yixuan Duan, Jiarong Qian, Chi-Yu Chen, MingYu Lu, Huan-Yu Hsu, Yu Gu, Yue Guo, Sheng Wang, Wei Qiu, Hanwen Xu

entry.summary: Introduces a benchmark of 611 patient cases and 19,157 discussion turns across ten specialist roles, transcribed from over 200 hours of public tumor board recordings, to evaluate LLMs on realistic clinical deliberation. It tests both answering questions within real discussions and simulating full board conversations ending in consensus recommendations.

entry.title: Can Tabular Foundation Models Amortize Statistical Inference?

author.name: Kai Ye, Shijin Gong, Hongyi Zhou, Valentina Zangirolami, Chengchun Shi

entry.summary: TabCon is an amortized inference system built on a tabular foundation model that produces confidence intervals for new datasets in a single forward pass, replacing problem-specific estimator design. It uses a sparse mixture-of-experts architecture and reinforcement-learning-based post-training to calibrate interval coverage. The paper argues for a paradigm shift where statistical inference procedures are learned once and amortized across datasets.

entry.title: A Statistical Perspective on Knowledge Distillation: Foundations, Classical Methods, and Large Language Model Extensions

author.name: Luyang Fang, Haoran Lu, Jiazhang Cai, Tao Wang, Huimin Cheng, Wenxuan Zhong, Ping Ma

entry.summary: This review provides a unified Bayesian formulation of knowledge distillation, treating teacher predictions as prior information and connecting KD to uncertainty quantification. It covers foundations, classical methods, and extensions relevant to distilling large language models, elevating KD from engineering trick to statistical principle.

entry.title: Faster Block-Diffusion Serving with Distribution-Free Risk Guarantees

author.name: Jungseob Lee, Dongyub Jude Lee, Chanjun Park, Sugyeong Eo, Heuiseok Lim

entry.summary: This work analyzes serving configurations for block-diffusion language models, showing that mean benchmark accuracy is a poor guide for choosing speed-risk trade-offs. The authors characterize how commit rules, static skip rules, and self-distillation contribute speedups, and propose Redline, a finite-sample, distribution-free guarantee that lets operators choose faster configurations with bounded per-prompt regression risk. This brings principled risk management to a fast-moving serving area.

entry.title: Certified Multi-Source Integrity for Structured Agent Actions

author.name: Anmol Pandey, Aditya Jain, Liang Chen, Carsten Maple, Christo Panchev

entry.summary: The paper addresses integrity of LLM agents' privileged structured actions (such as paying an invoice) assembled from corruptible document and tool fields, characterizing when such policy-bound actions are safely certifiable under a corruption budget with shared upstream sources. It gives a maximally live safe certifier that admits an action only when each field clears the rule its evidence structure supports, including against indirect prompt injection.

entry.title: ReScraper: Unified Scraping and Cleaning of Web Data for Effective LLM Pretraining

author.name: Zichun Yu, Jiarui Yan, Shlok Sanghvi, Nihar Atri, Chenyan Xiong

entry.summary: ReScraper replaces the typical hand-written heuristic pipeline for web scraping and corpus cleaning with a single 0.6B-parameter language model. Distilled from three teacher models, it extracts main page content and then applies one of four operations per page: keep, edit out noise, delete, or rewrite low-quality but informative text. The approach directly targets pretraining data quality, which is a key lever for LLM performance at a fraction of the cost of larger models.

entry.title: RoPE is Dead, Long Live RoPE: Towards Scalable Data-aware Positional Encodings

author.name: Jarod L\'evy, Mathurin Videau, Jad Yehya, Jean-R\'emi King, St\'ephane d'Ascoli, Thomas Moreau

entry.summary: This paper identifies a specific weakness of RoPE: its slow frequency bands, whose wavelengths exceed the training context, expose models to unseen angles during extrapolation. The authors introduce DaRoPE, a data-aware positional encoding that preserves standard RoPE on fast bands while adapting the problematic slow bands. The work brings order to a fragmented positional-encoding literature and proposes a scalable drop-in alternative.

entry.title: Two-Timescale Fine-tuning Provably Learns New Features for Two-Layer ReLU Networks

author.name: Etienne Boursier, Nicolas Flammarion

entry.summary: This theory paper analyzes fine-tuning in a Gaussian multi-index setting where the teacher has m+1 features, m learned at pre-training and one new during fine-tuning. For two-layer ReLU networks, it proves that two-timescale training (outer weights updated much faster than hidden weights) learns the new task-specific feature while preserving pre-trained ones, requiring only O(d) fine-tuning samples. This provides one of the first provable accounts of feature learning during fine-tuning.

entry.title: Statistical Benefits of Fine-Tuning from Pretrained Initialization in Diagonal Linear Networks

author.name: Alexandre Decl\`eves, Etienne Boursier, Nicolas Flammarion
