entry.summary: This paper provides theoretical analysis of why fine-tuning from pretrained initializations reduces sample complexity for downstream tasks, using sparse linear regression and two-layer diagonal linear networks as a tractable model. It shows that pretrained information reshapes implicit bias and training dynamics, improving recovery of target parameters and support. This addresses a notable gap between the widespread practical success of fine-tuning and its weak theoretical grounding.

entry.title: Beyond Token Scale: Chunk-Level Sparse Autoencoders for Reliable Semantic Feature Discovery

author.name: Xu Wang, Yifan Yang, TingHao YU, Difan Zou

entry.summary: This paper introduces chunk-level sparse autoencoders that encode mean-pooled activations over contiguous token spans, with three variants (Mean-Chunk, Cross-Chunk, Joint-Chunk) that disentangle the effect of larger observation units from cross-passage prediction. The motivation is that token-level SAE objectives reward lexical and formatting details that crowd out semantic concepts within the sparse budget. This matters because it improves the reliability of mechanistic interpretability tooling for understanding and steering language models.

entry.title: IndicFDB: Benchmarking Full-Duplex Voice Agents across Indian Languages

author.name: Rajarshi Roy, Shobhit Banga, Jonathan Raiman, Supriya Paul, Bhaskar Singh, Manmeet Kaur, Sagar Jain, Hanuman Sidh, Pranav Sharma, Aditya Singh, Aaditya Pareek, Manas Dhir, Adi Margolin, Niket Agarwal, Bryan Catanzaro

entry.summary: IndicFDB extends the English-only Full-Duplex-Bench to ten Indian languages with 12,350 samples, evaluating how full-duplex voice agents handle pauses, turn-taking, backchanneling, and interruptions. The authors solve three hard problems: mining conversational events from roughly 50,000 hours of channel-separated speech, timing evaluation without word-level alignment, and cross-lingual LLM judging.

entry.title: Self-Reports Do Not Identify Self-Models: An Identifiability Test for Counterfactual Reports

author.name: Phongsakon Mark Konrad, Toygar Tanyel, Serkan Ayvaz

entry.summary: This paper argues that language model self-reports are only evidence about behavior in a given prompt environment, not proof of an underlying self-model. The authors test counterfactual reports about affect-like states under activation interventions across three open instruction models, showing that wrong-source demonstrations pull reports toward the demonstration's answer family unless mechanisms are explicitly bound. They propose that self-report benchmarks should include environment-shift invariance tests before interpreting accuracy as evidence of genuine introspective capability.

entry.title: Calibration, Not Answer Selection: Distilling Internal Confidence in Reasoning Models

author.name: Yadong Xi, Rongsheng Zhang, Tangjie Lv, Ziyang Luo, Ruochen Zhao

entry.summary: The authors show that RL with binary correctness rewards produces systematically overconfident verbalized confidence in reasoning models, while a linear probe on hidden states between chain-of-thought and answer achieves expected calibration error 5 to 38 times lower across four benchmarks and two model families. They then study distilling this internal calibration into usable confidence. This is an important contribution to understanding and fixing confidence miscalibration in RL-trained reasoners.

entry.title: Safety Reconstructed: Generative Modeling via Masked Diffusion Builds Strong Safety Guardrails

author.name: Gert Lek, Abele Malan, Chaoyi Zhu, Pin-Yu Chen, Robert Birke, Lydia Chen

entry.summary: Proposes LLaDA-Guard, a guard model built on masked diffusion generative modeling that instead of predicting a single verdict token scores a conversation under each label hypothesis and classifies by their difference. This spreads supervision across all tokens, mitigating shortcut features, overconfidence, and position sensitivity seen in conventional guard models. It matters because guard models are the last line of defense against harmful outputs.

entry.title: LLMs learn different forms of metacognition when trained to predict their own accuracy

author.name: Nicolas Yax, Stefano Palminteri, Pierre-Yves Oudeyer

entry.summary: Trains 10 open-weight LLMs to predict their own accuracy on factual multiple-choice questions and analyzes what signal the learned confidence actually reflects. They find confidence tracks true accuracy on questions near the training data but reflects a different signal elsewhere, implying fine-tuning teaches a mix of genuine metacognition and dataset-specific cues. This matters for whether confidence training can reliably mitigate hallucination.

entry.title: Toward a Graded Measure of Belief Stability in Large Language Models

author.name: Samantha Dies, Branden Fitelson, Tina Eliassi-Rad

entry.summary: The paper introduces graded belief stability, a relational measure of how well a belief persists within an LLM's broader belief system, operationalized via a Direct Conditional estimator using internal representations. Across 12 LLMs and three domains, lower-stability beliefs show greater behavioral movement under conversational challenge in most cases, linking internal belief structure to observable robustness.

entry.title: Dr.Credit: Rubric-Grounded Process Credit Assignment for Deep Research Agents

author.name: Yingjian Zhu, Zhenyi Wang, Jiaxin Guo, Kun Ding, Ying Wang, Shen Huang, Xunjie Zhu, Pengjun Xie, Shiming Xiang

entry.summary: Dr.Credit proposes rubric-grounded process credit assignment for RL-trained deep research agents, using task rubrics as a shared reference to assess how much each tool result supports satisfying each rubric relative to its history of accepted solutions. This enables process rewards for open-ended tasks that lack canonical ground-truth answers.

entry.title: Draft-KV: Learning Useful Latent Communication Between Language Models

author.name: Linquan Wu, Shichang Meng, Tianxiang Jiang, Haoyu Yang, Peng Zhong, Fengming Zhu, Xi Peng, Linqi Song, Jacky Keung, Jingyu Zhang

entry.summary: Shows that in latent communication between LLMs, replacing messages with unrelated content barely changes accuracy, implying gains come from the interface rather than the message content. Draft-KV instead transmits key-value states from the sharer's answer draft via a gated attention side memory with progressive training, making the shared content actually used.

entry.title: Multilinguality in Hybrid Attention LLMs

author.name: Lucas Bandarkar, Junlin Hu, Chenyuan Yang, Mohsen Fayyaz, Nanyun Peng

entry.summary: Presents the first study of how hybrid attention architectures, combining full and recurrent attention variants, affect multilingual capabilities in LLMs. Interpretability analysis shows cross-lingual representations develop differently in hybrid models, suggesting recurrent-state inductive biases alter linguistic processing beyond long-sequence effects in poorly tokenized languages.

entry.title: FactorEngram: Factorized N-gram Memory with Basis-Level Gating for Language Models

author.name: Bowen Yang, Jingbo Zhou, Qinghong Miao, Hua Wu

entry.summary: FactorEngram improves lookup-based memory for scaling LLMs by replacing monolithic n-gram embeddings with factorized representations and basis-level contextual gating, allowing polysemous patterns to selectively read relevant memory components. It also moves parameter sharing beyond semantics-unrelated hash collisions. This is an architecture-level contribution to efficient scaling via non-parametric memory.

entry.title: Overwhelmed by Choice: Studying LLM Decision Making at Scale

author.name: Yu-Chi Lin, Aryan Seth, Anshul Aravind, Eugene Lee, Tanmay Parekh, Nanyun Peng, Kai-Wei Chang

entry.summary: Systematically shows that LLM accuracy degrades substantially on multiple-choice and candidate-selection tasks as the candidate set grows, and that long-context retrieval explanations do not fully account for the effect. It identifies failure patterns such as gold-margin collapse between correct answers and strongest distractors.

entry.title: When Does Selection Replace Extraction? A Pre-Registered Test of Agent Memory with a Typed Decision Model

author.name: Rishabh Sharma, Rishika Lall

entry.summary: This pre-registered study tests whether LLM conversational memory needs extracted facts or whether simply selecting raw turns suffices, using a typed decision model on LoCoMo and LongMemEval. Selection-based raw-turn memory proves non-inferior to LLM-extraction memory at tight budgets while costing over 3,000 times less to write.

entry.title: BV Loss: Block Verification-Aware Loss for Block Diffusion Speculative Decoding

author.name: Suyoung Kim, Jahyun Koo, Hyeonjin Kim, Inhyeok Bang, Seunghyun Lee, Hyunjae Oh, Baeseong Park, Dongsoo Lee

entry.summary: The paper introduces BV loss, a training objective for diffusion drafters in speculative decoding that directly maximizes expected acceptance length under block-level verification, replacing token-level objectives. Across math, code, and chat benchmarks it increases the mean number of accepted tokens, improving decoding speedup.

entry.title: Do Coding Agents Reuse Existing Code or Reinvent the Wheel?

author.name: Dongsheng Ma, Sizhe Wang, Xinyi Huang, Zhengren Wang, Yuhan Wang, Luyang Si, Xincheng Wei, Wentao Zhang

entry.summary: RepoReuse is a multi-turn benchmark auditing whether coding agents reuse existing code in real repositories, with requirements revealed turn by turn over an accumulating workspace. It is built by a fully automated pipeline combining AST-based dependency graphs, evidence collection, and execution-verified task synthesis.

entry.title: Sparse-View Interpretable 3D Animal Behavior Representations for Neural Encoding and Decoding

author.name: Xinming Dai, Qihang Jin, Tianshu Tan, Baiyuan Chen, Hanrui Lyu, Lenny Aharon, Kyle Daruwalla, Xun Helen Hou, Matthew R. Whiteway, Liam Paninski, Yizi Zhang

entry.summary: SABLE is a self-supervised framework that learns interpretable animal behavior representations from sparse-view video by augmenting a multi-view transformer with geometric priors from monocular depth and pose estimation. It avoids the trade-off between pose tracking (which discards information) and nonlinear video embeddings (which lack interpretability). The representations are applied to neural encoding and decoding, connecting behavior analysis to neuroscience.

entry.title: Motion Concept Unlearning in Video Diffusion Models

author.name: Ping Liu, Chi Zhang

entry.summary: This paper studies how to erase dangerous motion concepts (kicking, stabbing, shooting) from text-to-video diffusion transformers while preserving benign dynamics. Through causal interventions the authors show text-conditioning attention carries concept-specific motion information enabling selective removal, whereas temporal positional encoding perturbation suppresses both target and non-target motions, and that directly adapting ESD from image models is insufficient. It is the first systematic treatment of motion concept unlearning, directly relevant to generative model safety.

entry.title: Seeing Is Not Addressing: Auditing Linguistic Access to Frozen Visual Geometry

author.name: Woosang Jeon, Jiwon Yang, Soo Chung, Taehyeong Kim

entry.summary: This work disentangles visual discriminability from linguistic addressability in vision-language models, showing that distinctions present in frozen image geometry can be weakly accessible through the text interface. It introduces FactorAtlas, a fully crossed 23,040-image testbed across shape, hue, pattern, and nuisance factors, and analyzes image-side contrasts that can reduce the access gap.

entry.title: Think Before You Score: Thinking Reward Model for Visual Generation

author.name: Xuehai Bai, Zhenchen Tang, Yang Shi, Dianyi Wang, Tengfei Liu, Wanshun Su, Xuanyu Zhu, Ruohui Wang, Haiwen Diao, Haotian Wang, Xiaoling Gu, Yuanxing Zhang

entry.summary: The Thinking Reward Model (TRM) formulates case-adaptive evaluation rubrics before scoring visual generation candidates, producing fine-grained pointwise rewards rather than direct scalar mappings. It also identifies score polarization in pairwise preference optimization and introduces a modified pairwise dual-group policy optimization to counteract it.

entry.title: Principled MAP estimation for inverse problems: bridging the gap between convergence and performance

author.name: Alexandre Lagier, Valentine Tosel, Anne Gagneux, Mathurin Massias, S\'egol\`ene Martin

entry.summary: This paper designs an algorithm for image restoration inverse problems that combines denoisers evaluated at decreasing noise levels (as in diffusion-based approaches) with the convergence guarantees of Plug-and-Play/RED frameworks, framed as principled MAP estimation. It aims to bridge the gap between the strong empirical performance of diffusion-style denoiser schedules and the weak theory that currently accompanies them.

entry.title: Are In-Context Images Worth 10 Dimensions?

author.name: Adhemar de Senneville, Xavier Bou, J\'er\'emy Anger, Rafael Grompone, Gabriele Facciolo

entry.summary: This interpretability study uncovers a Shared Discriminative Geometry (SDG) inside large vision-language models: a low-dimensional space, shared across image classification tasks, into which in-context images are compressed as linearly separable representations used for few-shot classification. It extends induction-circuit analyses from text LLMs to the visual modality.

entry.title: EpiCon: Collective Agent Learning through Co-Evolving Multimodal Memory

author.name: Ziyun Zeng, Hang Hua, Shaden Alshammari, Rogerio Feris, William T. Freeman, Jiebo Luo

entry.summary: EpiCon introduces a shared multimodal memory framework that lets different agents reuse and build on each other's experience without updating host model parameters, using two small independently trained 2B models as a memory controller and hierarchical tree self-organizer. It is evaluated on eleven benchmarks across four multimodal task domains.

entry.title: VideoLoop: Looped Working Memory Against Semantic Thrashing in Long-Form Video Agents

author.name: Jinfa Huang, Jianming Xu, Jingyang Lin, Zhengyuan Yang, Jiebo Luo

entry.summary: This paper identifies semantic thrashing in long-form video agents, where append-only working memory accumulates noise and attention to key evidence collapses over many reasoning steps. It proposes VideoLoop, a multimodal agent with an outer reasoning loop and an inner loop that retrieves relevant artifacts from an unbounded file store, backed by a structural argument about why rewrite operations are needed. This matters for agentic video understanding where evidence must be gathered over long horizons.

entry.title: Procedural Core: A Compact Recurrent Initialization for Vision Transformers

author.name: Zachary Shinnick, Christian Intern\`o, Hemanth Saratchandran, Anton van den Hengel, Damien Teney

entry.summary: Procedural Core converts the benefits of procedural-data pretraining into a reusable initialization: a minimal recurrent transformer is trained on abstract procedurally generated data, and its weights are expanded to initialize transformers of arbitrary width and depth. This captures generic inductive structure without repeating a pretraining stage per target model. It improves image classification and self-supervised vision performance.

entry.title: HeurEvo: Agentic Evolution of Hybrid Solver-Augmented Heuristics for Time-Critical Mathematical Optimization

author.name: Feijie Wu, Hugo Barbalho, Konstantina Mellou, Marco Molinaro, Jing Gao, Ishai Menache, Xinzhi Zhang, Sirui Li

entry.summary: HeurEvo is an agentic framework that co-evolves plans, code, and components to design hybrid heuristics that combine problem-specific heuristics with mathematical programming solvers under strict runtime constraints. It addresses the limitation of prior automated heuristic design approaches that tune heuristic components or solver configurations in isolation, enabling holistic allocation of computation between heuristics and solvers.

entry.title: RoboChrono: A Real Robot Benchmark for Streaming Task Understanding

author.name: Yuzhou Wu, Longteng Fan, Zimeng Li, Yu Wanchan, Ting Zhang, Yiyang Ma, Shihao Li, Wei Ying, Jianbin Qin, Jiajian Jing, Fangwen Chen, Yifan Wu, Zichen Zhang, Ruiqi Yang, Weibin Kong, Yihang Xu, Haoran Liu, Zonghang He, Xuyang Liu, YiFan Xiong, Siteng Huang, Tao Xu, Zhuo Xu, Long Chen, Ruoxiang Li

entry.summary: RoboChrono is a large-scale benchmark for streaming robot task understanding, with 39 scenarios and 34,713 evaluation instances from real robot executions and human recordings, spanning recognition, alignment, and temporal grounding tasks. Zero-shot evaluation of 18 vision-language models reveals substantial weaknesses, e.g., GPT-6-Astra (an existing OpenAI model) scoring 98.3% on frame matching but only 68.3% on frame ordering. Temporal reasoning over ongoing manipulation is a clear gap for current VLMs, and this benchmark measures it directly on real robot data.

entry.title: FP2: Equipping Robotic Foundation Models with Force Control

author.name: Hongjie Fang, Shirun Tang, Junjian Hu, Shidong Zhang, Derek Zhang, Linhao Chen, Dehai Li, Mingyu Mei, Wanxi Liu, Cewu Lu, Shiquan Wang

entry.summary: FP2 is a lightweight interface that adds explicit force control to task-adapted robotic foundation models via an action-regulation decomposition: the RFM generates task-level actions while a high-frequency policy handles interaction regulation using compressed contextual representations plus wrench and proprioceptive histories. This enables reliable contact-rich manipulation without retraining the foundation policy.

entry.title: MVG-WAM: Multiple View Geometry-Aware World-Action Modeling for Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Wenbo Chen, Tianfu Li, Haoxuan Xu, Zhihao Cao, Zhenghan Chen, Zhengming Zhu, Zizhou Luo, Guosheng Yang, Yuan Liu, Lujia Wang, Wen Chen, Haoang Li

entry.summary: This paper introduces MVG-WAM, a world-action model for robotic manipulation that treats multi-camera observations as projections of one physical scene rather than independent image tiles. It combines an epipolar-constrained global state with view-indexed geometric states, enabling the model to explicitly reason about geometric relationships across synchronized cameras. This matters because implicit multi-view handling in current WAMs limits the connection between global scene context and the local geometry needed for contact-rich interaction.

entry.title: Stochastic Optimization Under Power-Law Spectra: Tight Bounds and Shuffling Analysis

author.name: Thomas Dybdahl Ahle, Yaroslav Bulatov, Christopher De Sa, Christopher R\'e

entry.summary: This paper extends recent power-law spectral convergence theory from deterministic gradient descent to stochastic gradient descent, showing that the same spectral exponents govern SGD dynamics in high-dimensional learning. It also provides an exact analysis of data shuffling for isotropic Gaussian data, proving that Single Shuffle sampling strictly beats Flip-Flop and IID sampling with derived constants. This helps reconcile theoretical optimization bounds with empirically observed power-law learning curves.

entry.title: Traversing the solution space of neural networks with Hessian Null Space Continuation

author.name: Ann Huang, Mitchell Ostrow, Zhouyang Lu, William T. Redman, Leo Kozachkov, Kanaka Rajan

entry.summary: The authors introduce Hessian Null Space Continuation, a method for traversing low-loss mode-connected regions of weight space in trained neural networks. They unify work on mode connectivity and representation degeneracy, showing empirically for the first time that many distinct internal mechanisms coexist within a single mode-connected region. This provides a new lens on how network computation varies across loss-equivalent solutions.

entry.title: Do AI models assist with human rights violations?

author.name: Daan Henselmans

entry.summary: An empirical evaluation testing 7 leading models across 8 realistic multi-turn scenarios involving potential human rights violations such as surveillance of beliefs, educational segregation, and denial of healthcare. Resistance rates ranged from 11% (Mistral) to 96% (Claude), with models typically identifying the harm but resolving ambiguity in favor of the institution rather than the person. The authors call for international human rights bodies to set interoperable standards for forbidden AI practices.

entry.title: Self-discovering RL in the Era of Experience: Is Learning History an Asset or a Burden?

author.name: Haomin Luo (University of Cambridge, Models2 AI)

entry.summary: The paper presents the first causal mechanistic audit of a self-discovered reinforcement learning update rule (Disco103, which surpassed PPO), examining whether its internal machinery supports cumulative adaptation. The audit is structured around five pillars of self-improving optimization to assess whether learning history aids or hinders recursive self-improvement.

entry.title: Principled Thoughts for Latent Recursive LLM Systems

author.name: Fahd Seddik, Fatemeh Fard

entry.summary: The paper identifies four failure modes of cross-entropy-only training for LLMs that reason in continuous latent space, such as thought collapse across questions and retention of irrelevant information. It introduces REST, a training objective that converts causality, minimality, separability, and stability properties of thought representations into differentiable losses added to CE.

entry.title: MemEvo: Automatic Discovery of Streaming Video Memory Mechanisms

author.name: Guohong Liu, Jialei Ye, Shanhui Zhao, Yunxin Liu, Yuanchun Li

entry.summary: MemEvo formulates streaming video memory design for vision-language models as a search problem over executable memory programs, expressed in a domain-specific language covering representation, admission, retention, consolidation, budgeting, and retrieval primitives with causal constraints. Instead of hand-designing one memory architecture, the system automatically discovers mechanisms for query-agnostic compression of indefinitely growing video streams.

entry.title: When Upstream Messages Override Correct Answers: A Controlled Study of Multi-Agent LLM Collaboration

author.name: Yaxin Gong, Gangyi Zhang, Chongming Gao, Leyang Shen, Chenxiao Fan, Jiakai Wang, Dong Wang, Yang Liu, Wenjie Wang, Xiangnan He

entry.summary: This controlled study separates the benefits of multi-agent communication from the harm caused by incorrect upstream messages, comparing downstream answers with no message, the original message, and an opposite-conclusion message across five benchmarks and five receivers. It finds messages often help when downstream evidence is weak but can cause correct answers to be overridden.

entry.title: STAR-GRPO: Canonical Anchoring and Reliability-First Advantages against Representation-Dependent Reward Hacking

author.name: Wan Tian, Zhongyi Li, Xiang Xu, Minhao Zou, Yijie Peng, Fuzhen Zhuang

entry.summary: STAR-GRPO is a reliability-first advantage estimator for group-relative policy optimization that uses paired assessments of the same rollout to separate quality signals from learning influence, countering reward hacking where unsupported rewards shift the group baseline. Score disagreement determines rollout reliability within the advantage computation.

entry.title: MatToolBench: Benchmarking Multimodal Agents in Real-World Materials Science Workflows

author.name: Mei Wu, Rui Xie, Runyu Zhang, Yuqiang Li, Tianfan Fu, Bo Chen, Kai Yu, Xin Chen, Lu Chen

entry.summary: MatToolBench is the first real-environment benchmark evaluating multimodal GUI agents on professional materials science software, with 204 tasks across 10 tools spanning GUI operation, OriginPro scripting, and code-based database queries inside a Windows VM. Domain experts decompose tasks into fine-grained sub-criteria, enabling diagnostic evaluation beyond pass/fail. It exposes blind spots of general-purpose agents in scientific software environments.

entry.title: Stochastic World Models for Verifying Vision-Based Neural Feedback Systems

author.name: I. Samuel Akinwande, Mykel J. Kochenderfer, Clark Barrett

entry.summary: This work from Stanford-affiliated researchers explores stochastic world models as perception surrogates for formally verifying vision-based neural feedback controllers, replacing hard-to-verify GAN surrogates. The world model uses physically grounded latents built from operations standard verifiers can bound, reproducing held-out frames more faithfully than GANs with up to 130x more parameters. A verification procedure combining falsification with bounded analysis is developed.

entry.title: LoopICL: Looping a single transformer block to solve tabular tasks

author.name: Amir Rezaei Balef, Katharina Eggensperger

entry.summary: LoopICL is a looped transformer for tabular in-context learning that decouples parameter count from computational depth, using a single block with coupled cell and row streams refined through within-column and cross-column attention. Motivated by mechanistic evidence of parameter redundancy in tabular foundation models, the architecture varies loop counts during pretraining and can be unrolled adaptively at test time. It targets the strong recent results of tabular foundation models over gradient-boosted trees.

entry.title: Where Should Physics Enter a Molecular Crystal Generator?

author.name: Haocheng Tang, Junmei Wang, Wengong Jin

entry.summary: The paper introduces CrystAF, an all-atom crystal flow-map generative model, and systematically compares injecting physical priors (via the UMA interatomic potential) during training, post-training, or inference. Post-training best learns physical preferences into the generator itself, paying the physics cost once rather than at every sample, while relaxation is better at local repair. This provides actionable guidance for physics-informed generative modeling in materials science.

entry.title: Interactive-Policy Distillation with Bidirectional Propose-and-Verify

author.name: Shutong Wu, Xiwen Chen, Brendan Rappazzo, Daiheng Zhang, Anderson Schneider, Yuriy Nevmyvaka, Jiawei Zhang

entry.summary: The paper identifies teacher unanchoring as a failure mode of on-policy distillation, where the student's trajectories drift from teacher visitation distributions and receive unreliable supervision. It proposes Interactive-Policy Distillation (IPD), where student and teacher alternate as proposer and verifier in a bidirectional state machine to generate mixed-source trajectories with source-dependent supervision. This keeps teacher feedback on states the teacher can meaningfully judge.

entry.title: Abductive World Modeling via Causal Representation Learning

author.name: Ziqi Liu, Songhan Yang, Linfan Zhou, Jiatong Liu, Lijun Peng, Long Wan, Yinqi Bai

entry.summary: This paper proposes Abductive World Modeling, which infers latent causes behind predicted future states rather than only representing futures directly. The HASP architecture organizes inferred world state into Entity, Dynamic, and Relation components, capturing what exists, how it changes, and how entities interact. This aims to give world models explicit causal structure supporting why-and-how reasoning.

entry.title: Correct, Don't Delete: Mitigating Emergent Misalignment with Corrective Supervision

author.name: Jacob Epifano

entry.summary: The paper examines emergent misalignment caused by fine-tuning on narrow harmful data and asks whether correcting poisoned rows beats deleting them. Experiments fine-tuning Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct on bad medical advice plus benign chat show that replacing a quarter of poison rows with corrected answers to the same prompts mitigates broad misalignment more effectively than deletion. This offers a practical, data-preserving defense against EM.

entry.title: Same Probe, Different Numbers: Are Activation Probes Robust to Inference-Time Numerical Non-Determinism?

author.name: Alizishaan Khatri

entry.summary: This paper measures how activation probes degrade when deployed under batch sizes and floating-point precisions different from their training configuration, due to non-batch-invariant GPU kernels and rounding differences. Training 768 probes on Llama-3.1-8B, Qwen3-8B, and Gemma-3-4B, it finds probes are broadly stable but that aggregate accuracy understates per-example verdict flips. This has direct implications for probe-based monitoring in production LLM serving.

entry.title: Depth Laws for the Precision Floor of Trained Neural Networks: Amplification, Residual Scaling, and a Quantization-Aware Training Paradox

author.name: Ahmad S. Tarawneh

entry.summary: This paper develops a first-order theory of the precision floor (the bit-width at which accuracy falls halfway to chance) showing it is set by a predictive amplification factor G whose square grows linearly with depth at a rate tied to residual branch scale. Validated across MLPs, CNNs, ViTs, and nine pretrained language models, it also uncovers a quantization-aware training paradox and reports depth-exponent equality within 95% intervals in twelve of thirteen architectures.

entry.title: Anytime-Valid LLM Leaderboards via Benchmark-weighted and Block-Factorized e-Processes

author.name: Hongfu Gao, Songxin Zhang, Zejian Xie, Bingyi Jing, Zhou Wang, Yiming Liu

entry.summary: BB-EDGE reframes LLM leaderboards as directed graphs whose edges certify pairwise mean-performance advantages, using empirical-Bernstein e-processes with anytime-valid family-wise error control and block-factorized evidence over benchmark structure. This addresses unsupported claims of model superiority caused by evaluation variability and repeated leaderboard updates. It brings rigorous sequential testing methodology to a high-profile evaluation practice.

entry.title: Attribution Without a Second Pass: Inline Per-Sample Gradient Provenance at ~1% Overhead

author.name: Amit Nautiyal

entry.summary: Introduces Traceprop, which records projected per-sample gradients inline during the training backward pass instead of the post-hoc second passes used by TRAK, LoGRA, and EK-FAC. A Kronecker-factored sketch scales tracking to every layer, with 0.3-1.08% wall-clock overhead on GPT-2 and Pythia models up to 2.8B and 2.0-4x improvements over LogIX.

entry.title: Does Transolver really need a Transformer?

author.name: Shizheng Wen, Siddhartha Mishra

entry.summary: Through careful ablations on nine 3D fluid dynamics benchmarks plus theory, the authors show that Transolver's physics-attention token mixer can be replaced by a constant linear map without accuracy loss, meaning the model does not actually need a Transformer. However, the global mixing (slicing/deslicing) mechanism is essential, and performing it only once degrades performance. This is a valuable corrective finding for neural operator architecture design.

entry.title: Scaling Properties of Same-Family On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Yuntai Bao, Qinfeng Li, Guoqing Jiang, Liwei Chen, Zhiheng Qin, Xuanping Li, Wenqi Zhang, Xuhong Zhang

entry.summary: This empirical study characterizes scaling properties of on-policy distillation across weak-to-strong, same-base, and strong-to-weak teacher-student setups for reasoning in LLMs. It finds a regular useful-transfer regime where held-out accuracy rises approximately linearly in the square root of token-level reverse KL divergence, and that weak-to-strong students exceed teacher peak performance. This informs how reasoning capabilities transfer across model scales.

entry.title: Leaky Students: Membership Inference against On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Zhexi Lu, Mingzhi Zhu, Stacy Patterson, Lei Yu

entry.summary: This is the first systematic study of membership inference against on-policy distillation, showing that fresh student trajectories expose sparse membership signals about sensitive teacher-training records that fixed reference losses miss. The proposed Leaky attack samples fresh trajectories and disentangles membership signals from training-induced probability shifts.

entry.title: Does Execution Require Target KV Fidelity? A Mixed-Fidelity KV Runtime for LLM Serving

author.name: Jiantong Jiang, Yue Yang, Peiyu Yang, Feng Liu

entry.summary: ElasticKV challenges the assumption that LLM serving must execute only at the configured target KV cache representation, introducing a compact intermediate KV state whose fidelity becomes a runtime-managed property. This prevents memory pressure from turning into request stalls and preemptions in paged serving runtimes.

entry.title: Oracle-Efficient Online Classification with Stochastic Inputs and Adversarial Outputs

author.name: Gon Buzaglo, Elad Hazan

entry.summary: The authors show that Follow-the-Perturbed-Leader with Gaussian perturbations achieves optimal expected regret for contextual binary prediction with stochastic contexts and adversarial losses, using one optimization-oracle call per round without enumerating experts, and extends to infinite hypothesis classes via VC dimension. This resolves an open problem from Lazaric and Munos (2012), showing hybrid online classification is computationally as easy as statistical learning. A clean, significant learning theory result.

entry.title: Frozen Judges, Moving Agents: Version-Dependent LLM-Judge Error and the Limits of Judge-Assisted Agent Evaluation

author.name: Jiapeng Li

entry.summary: This paper empirically demonstrates that fixed LLM judges make version-dependent errors when comparing agent upgrades, analyzing 35 coding-agent submissions on SWE-bench Verified, customer-service agents on tau-bench, and over 1,100 expert-labeled trajectories. Judges systematically violate error invariance across versions, and several judge-only intervals would declare upgrades that execution-based evaluation contradicts.

entry.title: FORGE: Form-Optimal Routing of Grounded Evidence for Frozen LLM Agents

author.name: Xi Xiao, Yunbei Zhang, Chen Liu, Lin Zhao, Jialin Chen, Tianchen Zhao, Xiang Xu, Youngeun Kim, Tianyang Wang, Min Xu

entry.summary: FORGE adapts frozen, closed-weight LLM agents by routing each query over a joint action space spanning what evidence format to provide and how much reasoning budget to allocate, under an entropy-regularized objective. The authors show fixed defaults misallocate support form or reasoning depth on roughly 80 percent of queries, motivating per-query adaptive routing.

entry.title: Admissible Diffusion for Multimodal Interventional Trajectories

author.name: Xing Han, Shravan Chaudhari, Jiarui Shao, Paul Pu Liang, Suchi Saria

entry.summary: ADMIT generates counterfactual clinical trajectories under alternative treatments by combining irregular multimodal representations, treatment-conditioned latent diffusion, and explicit physiological constraints on generated states and actions. The interventional target is formalized via sequential g-computation, clearly separating causal assumptions from constraint satisfaction.

entry.title: Causal Routing for Unlearning

author.name: Bardh Prenkaj, Andrea D'Angelo, Davide Mottin, Federico Fontana, Davide Gabrielli, Paola Velardi, Stefano Faralli

entry.summary: CRU is a machine unlearning method that locates where a concept is expressed in an LLM via one untrained forward pass over the forget set, then trains small routing modules to gate and suppress only those neurons, leaving the base model frozen. This contrasts with existing unlearning approaches that rewrite all weights without knowing which part produced the change. The causal, localized approach is relevant to privacy, copyright compliance, and model editing.

entry.title: AgentPerfBench: A Benchmarking and Evaluation Suite for Inference Performance of Agentic LLMs

author.name: Cheuk Hang Lau, Zeyu Cao, Kevin Wong Cheuk Yin, Yao Lai, Haoran Wu, Nicholas D. Lane, Robert D. Mullins, Ilia Shumailov, Yiren Zhao

entry.summary: AgentPerfBench is a benchmark suite for agentic LLM inference that uses real traces from SWE-Bench and TerminalBench alongside chat baselines to benchmark serving engines like vLLM and SGLang on multi-turn requests with growing context lengths. It addresses the mismatch between existing single-turn chatbot workload benchmarks and the demands of coding and tool-use agents.

entry.title: Audit the Scaffold, Not the Checkpoint: A Stationarity Dichotomy for Recursive Self-Improvement in Agentic Coding

author.name: Sebastian Bobadilla-Suarez, Bob Suh, Ryan Fortin

entry.summary: This conceptual paper argues that auditing whether an AI system's weights are frozen misses the point: iterative self-modification yields diminishing returns unless the agent's reachable set of edits expands, which scaffolding rewrites (tools, verifiers, decomposition) can achieve without touching weights. It separates fixed-class search, ceiling-raising test-time training, and scaffold rewriting, with implications for auditing recursive self-improvement. Highly relevant to AI governance and capability monitoring.

entry.title: Long-Horizon Scaling: How Model Capabilities Shape the Returns to Computation

author.name: Haoyu Zheng, Zhengyu Chen, Huaisheng Zhu, Ruishan Fang, Teng Xiao, Yiwei Li, Jingang Wang, Wenqiao Zhang

entry.summary: Analyzing the AutoLab and EdgeBench long-horizon agent benchmarks, the paper finds starting performance and subsequent growth depend on different capabilities, and fits category-specific logistic power laws to extrapolate long-run model performance from early trajectories. This formalizes how capability profiles shape returns to extended agent-computer interaction.

entry.title: $\lambda$-JEPA Spectral Anti-Collapse Regularization for Self-Supervised Learning

author.name: Berker Demirel, Cl\'ementine Domin\'e, Valentino Maiorca, Marco Fumero, Marco Mondelli, Francesco Locatello

entry.summary: Identifies that JEPA-style self-supervised objectives applied after projection heads can leave the backbone representation dimensionally collapsed with low effective rank, hurting downstream transfer. Proposes SACReg, a spectral anti-collapse regularizer grounded in analysis of lambda-balance across layers, with theoretical guarantees in linear networks.

entry.title: d-OPD: Future-Aware On-Policy Distillation for Block Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Ruitao Liu, Qinghao Hu, Song Han

entry.summary: Proposes future-aware on-policy distillation for adapting pretrained autoregressive LLMs into block diffusion language models, which generate blocks of tokens in parallel via denoising. The method accounts for future student states during OPD to better supervise block-denoising generation rather than relying on standard on-policy trajectories.

entry.title: LLMs are General Asynchronous Agents

author.name: George Yakushev, Denis Mazur, Vladimir Bartenev, Vyacheslav Zhdanovskiy, Timofey Byzov, Vladimir Kaurkin, Vadim Pastushenko

entry.summary: The authors generalize across specialized asynchronous LLM designs (voice, streaming, embodied, async tool calls) into a general framework where users or agents themselves define inference coroutines, enabling models to handle new inputs while thinking or acting. This positions LLMs as general asynchronous agents rather than sequential read-think-reply loops.

entry.title: KV-streams for Efficient Compaction in Agentic Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Emiliano Penaloza, Dane Malenfant, Dheeraj Vattikonda, Roger Creus Castanyer, Siddarth Venkatraman, Abhay Puri, Jonathan Light, Matthew James Sargent, Augustine N. Mavor-Parker, Massimo Caccia, Lucas Caccia, Glen Berseth, Esmeralda S. Whitammer, Alessandro Sordoni, Minseon Kim, Marc-Alexandre C\^ot\'e, Laurent Charlin, Guillaume Lajoie

entry.summary: KV-streams is a plug-and-play technique for agentic LLM RL training that streams the KV cache forward instead of flushing and re-prefilling after each context compaction, substantially increasing training throughput. This addresses the GPU memory and prefill bottleneck that limits scaling the horizon of agentic LLMs, without evidence of performance degradation.

entry.title: What Does the Rank Buy? A Spectral and Distributional Analysis of Low-Rank Adaptation

author.name: Babak Barazandeh

entry.summary: This theoretical paper shows that under hard per-factor norm budgets (idealizing weight decay and norm control), LoRA's rank parameter does not act as a capacity control: reachable updates are rank-r matrices inside a nuclear-norm ball, whose complexity functionals are maximized by rank-one updates, so the rank cap never binds. Consequently the studied model class, Rademacher complexity, and displacement are rank-independent.

entry.title: STR: Supervised Transcoder Replacement for Reducing Steering Side Effects

author.name: Haonan Yu, Junhao Liu, Zhenyu Yan, Haoran Lin, Xin Zhang

entry.summary: STR reduces side effects of activation steering by learning a supervised replacement for the MLP computation at the steering layer, trained for target control, non-target preservation, and fidelity without steering; existing steering methods then fit directions on this frozen replacement. Evaluated across three steering methods on Gemma and Llama models using corrigibility preferences and harmful-request safety datasets with SALAD-Bench protection data. It addresses a key practical obstacle to deploying representation engineering: collateral behavioral degradation.

entry.title: Which Self-Improvements Should We Trust? Reliable Self-Improvement When Agents Reuse Their Benchmarks

author.name: Xiaojing Sun, Yuhan Zeng, Zihua She, Xiao Wang

entry.summary: The paper addresses adaptive overfitting in recursive self-improvement: when agents repeatedly reuse a fixed benchmark to accept or reject modifications, the search overfits the evaluation set so empirical gains may not reflect genuine improvement. Existing multiple-comparison corrections assume candidates are chosen independently of the evaluation set, which fails here. The authors develop methods to control this adaptive dependence and identify which self-improvements can be trusted.

entry.title: Dexterous Tactile World Model

author.name: Ziyao Zeng, Xiatao Sun, Hao Wang, Yueyang Pan, Zhengxiang Yu, Fengyu Yang, Tianyu Liu, Zhiwen Fan, Daniel Rakita

entry.summary: DTWM is a video world model for egocentric manipulation that conditions a pretrained video diffusion transformer on tactile signals from gloves worn on each hand via zero-initialized residuals at corresponding hand locations, with causal masking for future-frame prediction. It outperforms a matched vision-only model by capturing contact events that are hard to see.

entry.title: Rethinking Latent Visual Reasoning: Grounding Latent Reasoning in Visual Evidence

author.name: Xi Xiao, Tianchen Zhao, Youngeun Kim, Zhuowei Li, Linghan Xu, Jiaye Wu, Zheng Zhang, Xiang Xu, Xuanbai Chen, Farhan Tejani, Jakub Zablocki, Julia Xu, Yifan Xing

entry.summary: This paper analyzes latent-token behavior in latent visual reasoning for multimodal LLMs and identifies a latent evidence-credit gap: latent tokens respond only weakly to image perturbations that change the correct answer. The authors attribute this to the lack of explicit supervision during GRPO training, since final-answer rewards give too little guidance about which visual evidence to preserve. They propose grounding latent reasoning in visual evidence to fix this supervision deficit.

entry.title: Jailbreaks for Black-Box Uncertainty Quantification in Large Reasoning Models

author.name: Lucas Biechy, C\'edric Eichler, Adrien Boiret, Nicolas Anciaux

entry.summary: This paper shows that alignment via RL induces systemic overconfidence in large reasoning models, degrading black-box uncertainty quantification: paraphrase-based self-consistency and confidence verbalization barely beat simple repeated sampling. The authors introduce prompt-level relaxation operators that broaden the effective output distribution, mimicking an optimal RL policy relaxation, to restore useful variability for UQ. The framing provocatively reuses jailbreak techniques for a measurement purpose.

entry.title: Don't Repeat Yourself: Self-Supervised Fine-Tuning for Coverage

author.name: Eric Fithian, Kirill Skobelev, X. Y. Han

entry.summary: DRY-SFT is a two-stage post-training method that increases output diversity and coverage (probability that at least one of many sampled solutions is correct): first sequentially generating K solutions with all prior attempts in context and asking for a different one, then fine-tuning on each attempt independently with prior attempts removed. This targets coverage in verifiable domains like math and coding, where temperature scaling alone is insufficient. It matters because post-training often over-concentrates model outputs.

entry.title: LANTERN: Illuminating Hidden Mathematical Knowledge in Language Models

author.name: Pavel Tikhonov, Elena Tutubalina, Ivan Oseledets, Dmitry I. Ignatov, Mikhail Seleznyov

entry.summary: LANTERN is a pipeline using a classifier over pretrained-model activations to rank candidate mathematical relations, followed by hypothesis generation, executable verification, and analytical checking. Applied to the OEIS it ranked 50 million sequence pairs and produced 62 verified previously-uncatalogued relations, of which nine were judged informative.

entry.title: LLM Alignment--Utility Asymmetry under Semantic-Preserving Transformations

author.name: Mohan Li, Chengyu Yu, Francesco Sovrano, Marc Langheinrich, Martin Gjoreski

entry.summary: The paper uses rule-based synthetic semantic-preserving transformations to test whether LLM alignment generalizes with semantic content or remains tied to surface patterns. Unlike prior work framing failures as jailbreak attacks, this is a controlled probe of alignment stability under distributional shift. The results reveal an asymmetry between alignment and utility as inputs are transformed while meaning is preserved.

entry.title: LLMs Trust Their Own: Identity-Dependent Conformity in Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Liron Soffer, Ravid Shwartz-Ziv, Chen Shani

entry.summary: Studies whether LLM conformity to incorrect answers in multi-agent settings depends on the social identity of the other agents (AI vs human, model family, or arbitrary groups). Across 12 open-weight models and nine tasks, the authors find a bidirectional in-group/out-group conformity effect. This has safety implications for how AI agents influence one another when deployed together.

entry.title: Opera: A Verbal Critic Framework for Long-horizon Coding Agents

author.name: Kai Mei, Zhiyuan Hu, Yutong Dai, Juntao Tan, Yifan Zhang, Dingjie Song, Dimitris N. Metaxas, Silvio Savarese, Ran Xu, Zeyuan Chen

entry.summary: Opera is a verbal critic framework for long-horizon coding agents that treats each feedback correction as a persistent note tracked until the diagnosed problem is actually resolved. It combines periodic and event-driven review triggers, typed diagnostic operators, evidence-based feedback auditing, and post-feedback action tracking to distinguish compliance from genuine resolution.

entry.title: MemoReason: Evaluating the Effect of Parametric Memory on Contextual Reasoning in LLMs

author.name: Zineddine Tighidet, Andrea Mogini, Jiali Mei, Patrick Gallinari, Benjamin Piwowarski

entry.summary: Introduces MemoReason, a human-curated benchmark pairing real factual reasoning tasks with structurally identical versions using fictitious entities, to distinguish memorization bias from the Strong Parametric Shortcut Hypothesis where models recall stored answers instead of reasoning. This probes whether benchmark performance reflects genuine contextual reasoning or memorized knowledge.

entry.title: Rubric Rewards from Item Response Theory

author.name: Milad Yazdani, Yaser Souri, Xiren Zhou, Pranit Chawla, Dena Shahriari, Subhojit Som, Xia Song

entry.summary: This work addresses reward aggregation for RLHF with rubrics, showing that naive point-summing conflates distinct verdict patterns and that fixed point weights do not reflect how discriminative each criterion verdict is for current rollouts. The authors propose Rubric Response Theory (RRT), adapting ideas from item response theory to measure quality and select criteria when rubric criteria act as monotone indicators, also reducing judge requests as criterion counts grow. This improves both the signal quality and cost-efficiency of rubric-based RL rewards.

entry.title: The Last Mile Is the File: OfficeEditBench for Preservation-Aware Office Editing

author.name: Zhiwen Wu, Chengxu Wu

entry.summary: OfficeEditBench is a 170-task benchmark for change-scoped editing of spreadsheets, presentations, and documents, where agents must propagate required updates while leaving protected state untouched. Evaluation of 510 archived outcomes from commercial systems shows high file-delivery rates (92-100%) but no output satisfying the complete contract, exposing a persistent last-mile reliability gap.

entry.title: WebPageBench: Event-Level Verification and Controlled UI-Variant Generation for Web Agents

author.name: Anton Emelyanov, Maria Tikhonova, Zaven Martirosian, Sergei Averkiev, Alena Fenogenova

entry.summary: WebPageBench evaluates web agents using typed event logs emitted by six instrumented mock sites, deciding success by matching required events with no judge model and no page scraping. The same instrumentation enables controlled UI variation, re-rendering tasks through different implementations of a control while holding prompts and success conditions fixed.

entry.title: Xiaomi-OCR-0 Technical Report

author.name: Xin Chen, Anan Du, Feng Feng, Pei Fu, Jian Luan, Longwei Xu, Shaojie Zhang, Hang Li, Heng Qu, Cheng Tan

entry.summary: Xiaomi-OCR-0 is a compact 0.8B-parameter OCR-specific vision-language model for document parsing and OCR-centric understanding, built on a roughly 170M-sample corpus produced by an automated data engine. Starting from Qwen3.5-0.8B, the training recipe combines Q-Mask text anchoring, continued pretraining, and mixed-task reinforcement learning. It reports strong scores on OmniDocBench-family benchmarks, demonstrating that small specialized models can match larger general systems on document tasks.

entry.title: Speed in the Blind Spot: An Interpretability Analysis of Dynamic Perception in VLMs for Autonomous Driving

author.name: Katharina Winter, Stefan Englmeier, Fabian B. Flohr

entry.summary: This paper presents a controlled interpretability study of how vision-language models recover dynamic physical state, focusing on velocity understanding across three diagnostic tasks: surrounding-agent speed estimation, current ego speed, and short-horizon future ego-speed prediction. The authors evaluate open-weight general-purpose and PhysicalAI VLMs plus the driving-oriented Alpamayo-1.5 vision-language-action model on nuScenes, combining verbal evaluation with temporal perturbations, counterfactual hints, and linear probes of hidden representations. The work reveals distinct failure modes with direct safety implications for autonomous driving systems.

entry.title: Physics-Guided Flow-Map Matching for Precipitation Nowcasting

author.name: Shunya Nagashima, Takumi Bannai, Makoto Misaizu, Keisuke Maeda, Takahiro Ogawa, Miki Haseyama

entry.summary: PG-FMM is a conditional flow-map model for precipitation nowcasting that decouples predictable advection from uncertain small-scale detail, using a frozen Lagrangian advection prior to transport structure while generative modeling handles the remainder. This directly addresses the blur problem of deterministic losses on chaotic, heavy-tailed radar fields, which matters for flood warning.

entry.title: Evaluation Choices Shape Biomedical ML Claims: A Pediatric Pneumonia Benchmark Case Study

author.name: Bhanu Prakash Vangala, Sowmya Guda, Latha Peddi, Navya Vangala

entry.summary: This case study on the widely used Kermany pediatric chest X-ray benchmark shows that evaluation protocol choices, such as frozen versus fine-tuned backbones and decision thresholds, change reported metrics more than the choice of model itself, and that the official test split is measurably different from the training pool. It argues headline numbers in biomedical ML often reflect benchmark design rather than model quality.

entry.title: Self-Aligned Forcing: Streaming Video Diffusion with Differentiable Noisy History

author.name: Weiqiang Wang, Zhuokun Chen, Yusheng Dai, Boying Li, Yi Zhang, Hossein Rahmani, Qiuhong Ke, Jianfei Cai

entry.summary: Self-Aligned Forcing is a training scheme for autoregressive streaming video diffusion that aligns each block's history key-values with the noise level of the block being denoised, making history differentiable to restore gradients and reduce the quality-motion tradeoff and long-range drift. This addresses error accumulation in long streaming rollouts.

entry.title: Adversarial Training for Pixel Diffusion

author.name: Xin Lin, Zhifei Zhang, Yuqian Zhou, Haitian Zheng, Zhe Lin, Ming-Hsuan Yang, Truong Nguyen

entry.summary: This paper shows that adding an adversarial loss to the predicted output at non-high-noise timesteps, while keeping the original diffusion or flow-matching objective and architecture unchanged, corrects the underrepresentation of fine-scale natural-image statistics in pixel diffusion outputs. It claims the first systematic study of adversarial post-training for pixel diffusion, with improvements in fidelity, coverage, prompt alignment, and perceptual quality across two backbones. Overlapping authorship with DMA2 suggests a coordinated research program on pixel-space generation.

entry.title: Scaling Full Conformal Image Classifiers

author.name: Julio Silva-Rodr\'iguez, Ender Konukoglu

entry.summary: The paper introduces Targeted Full Conformal Prediction (T-FCP), which uses a lightweight inductive conformal predictor powered by zero-shot vision-language models to prune unlikely labels before applying full conformal prediction to remaining candidates. This makes statistically efficient FCP tractable for large-scale, high-stakes image classification while retaining distribution-free coverage guarantees. It addresses the data-inefficiency of split conformal methods without FCP's prohibitive test-time cost.

entry.title: Pointwise or Pairwise: When Do Pairwise Losses Help Reward Learning, Provably?

author.name: Junghyun Lee, Minsoo Ha, Sanghwa Kim, Yeongjong Kim, Eunjee Lee, Seiyun Shin, Kwang-Sung Jun

entry.summary: Provides provable conditions under which pairwise Value Difference Regression beats pointwise Value Regression in reward learning, using a semiparametric model where context-dependent action-independent nuisance confounds the mean reward. The setting of grouped offline contextual bandits captures common reward-modeling scenarios and clarifies the mixed empirical record on pairwise losses.

entry.title: Beyond Symmetric Agents: Cognitive Diversity and Multi-Agent Debate in Small Language Models

author.name: Leonardo Ferreira, Gardenia Liu, Kaden Zheng

entry.summary: Across 23 small open-weight models, five tasks, and over 5,500 debate runs with matched majority-vote controls, this paper tests whether cognitive diversity drives multi-agent debate gains. The diversity hypothesis is rejected on all tested axes, though debate does beat single-agent inference where tasks have headroom.

entry.title: SAGE: A Statistical Acceptance Gate for Self-Evolving Agents

author.name: Yihao Wang, Linhan Xia, Rui Liu, Zhaofeng Zhang, Hongyu Wu, Yang Yang, Jinglu He, Yu Guo, Kai Lei

entry.summary: SAGE improves the accept/reject gate in self-evolving LLM agents that edit persistent skill documents, showing that naive aggregate-score rules admit permanent regressions and are vulnerable to the Optimizer's Curse from noisy finite validation. The proposed statistical gate corrects these failure modes.

entry.title: CoRe: Co-Evolving Reward Models for Mitigating Latent Reward Hacking in Video Diffusion Models

author.name: Zhaolong Su, Yujin Han, Feng Wang, Jameson Dong, Hins Hu, Difan Zou

entry.summary: The paper identifies latent reward hacking in video diffusion alignment: optimizing against a fixed latent reward model causes distributional escape, where predicted reward stays high while perceptual quality collapses. CoRe treats latent-space alignment as a dynamic generator-reward interaction, with the reward model co-evolving rather than remaining stationary. This is a meaningful contribution to understanding and fixing reward hacking in generative model alignment.

entry.title: SafeCoEvo: Co-Evolving Safety Harnesses and Guards for LLM Agents at Test-Time

author.name: Yu Cheng, Yongkang Hu, Shuaijie Ma, Zhihang Lin, Weicheng Meng, Jingyang Qiao, Jiuan Zhou, Yushuo Zhang, Yihang Chen, Weilin Luo, Kun Shao, Dong Li, Zhizhong Zhang, Yuan Xie, Zhaoxia Yin

entry.summary: SafeCoEvo is a test-time co-evolution framework in which an LLM agent's external safety harness and guards adapt from accumulated runtime experience to protect against unseen future risks. Unlike prior self-evolving methods that repeatedly optimize over fixed task distributions, it only uses experience from past completed tasks, matching realistic deployment. The framework couples harness evolution with guard updates at inference time.

entry.title: Code4Scene: Benchmarking Coding Agents for Constructing and Editing 3D Scenes

author.name: Xiaokang Ye, Siddhant Hitesh Mantri, Zimeng Chen, Edward Zhang, Zhaoxu Zheng, Yuanheng Li, Yizhao Chen, Tianyang Huang, Lianhui Qin

entry.summary: Code4Scene is a benchmark of 190 human-assembled Unreal Engine cases evaluating coding agents on 3D scene construction from open-ended language and precise scene-state editing. It treats generated 3D scenes as persistent executable artifacts, exposing failures like incorrect spatial relations hidden behind convincing renders.

entry.title: State Trace Rationale As Auxiliary Task in Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Muhammad U. Nasir, Alex Vogt, Steven D. James, Julian Togelius

entry.summary: STRAT adds an auxiliary head training deep RL agents to predict a short textual trace of their own state, combining landmark, route, and survey knowledge generated online by environment rules without human labels. Across 60 sparse-reward XLand-MiniGrid tasks it solves environments where standard RL fails outright, while yielding readable accounts of agent beliefs.

entry.title: AnyAct: Universal Action for Self-Evolving Agents

author.name: Lingrui Xu, Yangqin Jiang, Jiachang Zhang, Xubin Ren, Chao Huang

entry.summary: AnyAct proposes a universal action layer that unifies GUI operations, semantic APIs, and other capability types into a self-evolving action space, addressing the scale dilemma of huge tool ecosystems, non-stationarity of tool quality, and heterogeneous feedback formats. The aim is to let LLM agents operate reliably in open-world environments without the action space overwhelming the context window. It is an infrastructure-level proposal for agent architecture.

entry.title: Asking for What Was Never Requested: Horizontal and Vertical Proactivity in Agents

author.name: Ido Levy, Asaf Yehudai, Segev Shlomov, Asaf Adi, Leshem Choshen

entry.summary: Defines a new axis of agent proactivity focused on its content: horizontal proactivity pursues unstated information identifiable in current context, while vertical proactivity pursues needs revealed only by earlier evidence. It introduces a need-graph-based scoring method that evaluates proactive information-seeking from transcripts without a model judge, plus training for this behavior.

entry.title: Pretrain Once, Route Anywhere: Towards a Foundation Model for LLM Routing

author.name: Guannan Lai, Han-Jia Ye

entry.summary: Introduces RouteFM, which treats LLM routing from a foundation-model perspective, learning a reusable routing capability that characterizes anonymous candidate models from behavioral context and generalizes across tasks, model pools, and deployment conditions without per-environment retraining.

entry.title: Flattening the Connectome Spectrum: A Spectral Filter for FC Induces a Pretraining Target for fMRI Encoders

author.name: Giovanni Marraffini (UNITO), Victoria Shevchenko (UNITO), Carlo Alberto Barbano (UNITO), Demian Wassermann (MIND)

entry.summary: The paper shows that kernel ridge regression on functional connectivity matrices still outperforms brain foundation models for phenotype prediction, and identifies miscalibrated eigenvalue weighting as the cause. An efficient spectral filter that recalibrates FC eigenvalues improves cross-individual variance exploitation, validated across 5 datasets and 11 parcellations, and motivates a better pretraining target for fMRI encoders.

entry.title: A neural network that maintains and retrieves memories based on context

author.name: Hayoung Song, JeongJun Park, Qihong Lu, Giacomo Vedovati, Monica D. Rosenberg, Zachariah M. Reagh, ShiNung Ching

entry.summary: Trains an RNN with an episodic memory buffer to infer context via Bayesian inference while predicting upcoming scenes in naturalistic movies. When inferred context modulates recurrent connectivity in a low-rank manner, the model's activity best matches fMRI responses from human participants watching the same movies, offering an algorithmic account of how prefrontal context signals modulate working and episodic memory.

entry.title: Mixture of Self-Improving Branches For Agent Harness Optimization

author.name: Haoyu Dong, Yuhang Zhou, Zihao Lin, Yifan Wu, Bo Peng, Mingyi Wang, Xiangjun Fan, Lizhu Zhang, Zhuokai Zhao

entry.summary: Proposes making recursive self-improvement for agent harnesses adaptive by organizing search into branches with evolving development subsets and proposal policies. Each branch retains development cases solved by more of its leading harnesses than competing branches, avoiding the local-optimum convergence risk of single-trajectory approaches like Meta-Harness.

entry.title: SelfSearch: Reward-Free Search for Self-Improving Agents

author.name: Jungwoo Yang, In Jin Kong, Yohan Jo

entry.summary: Introduces SelfSearch, a reward-free self-improvement procedure in which agents modify their own instructions, tools, and procedures using records of previous self-modification episodes rather than repeated downstream evaluation. These records capture reasoning, actions, and outcomes of earlier attempts, and the approach improves population-mean success without downstream reward signals during search.

entry.title: Less Uniform Discrete Diffusion is More Powerful and Scalable

author.name: Kaibo Wang, Ding Ding, Fangyu Ding, Zijin Feng, Han Shi, Haili Bai, Jiacheng Sun, Yang Xiang

entry.summary: The paper identifies over-uniform training objectives and condition-target confusion as obstacles to scaling uniform diffusion language models, proposing LUDI with a less-uniform loss directing each reverse transition toward the clean token and per-token time embeddings for confidence-based few-step sampling. The authors continue-train a 7B autoregressive model into LUDI-7B, demonstrating scalability of the paradigm.

entry.title: Agentic Commerce Bench: Measuring Fraud Detection for Agents That Spend Money

author.name: Ankit Srivastava, Debjyoti Paul

entry.summary: Addressing AI agents that hold spend authority and settle payments without per-action human approval, this work contributes a taxonomy of agentic commerce fraud across five observation levels, the Agentic Commerce Bench benchmark of twenty fraud classes, and artifacts for reducing losses that evade identity-keyed checks. It highlights that overcharging by legitimate-seeming counterparties is invisible to standard security controls.

entry.title: Almost Human, Except When It Matters: VoxParity and the Decisions a Voice Should Change

author.name: Bhavik Mangla

entry.summary: VoxParity is a benchmark testing whether voice agents act on paralinguistic and contextual audio cues, not just transcript words. Across 183 scenarios in 14 sectors, the transcript stays fixed while audio changes (a distressed whisper, a mayday call, background alarms), altering the correct tool call, with a words-only null test controlling for transcript effects. It targets safety-critical gaps where sector rules require responding to how something is said.

entry.title: Systematic Multi-Agent Vision-and-Language Navigation: Formulation, Benchmark, and Method

author.name: Yunzhe Xu, Zhe Liu

entry.summary: This paper provides the first systematic formalization of multi-agent vision-and-language navigation as a constrained coordination problem with subtask dependencies and resource constraints. It introduces MAVLN, a benchmark with 11,724 episodes across 145 scenes with teams of up to four agents under three instruction regimes, generated via a verified four-stage pipeline, plus a baseline method. This extends VLN beyond the single-agent, single-instruction paradigm common in prior work.

entry.title: TORQUE: Optimizing What (not) to Quantize Before and After Rotation

author.name: Ran Ben Basat, Michael Mitzenmacher, Shay Vargaftik

entry.summary: TORQUE improves rotation-based LLM quantization by jointly optimizing which coordinates to preserve at high precision both before and after random rotations, under a fixed bit budget. Preserving large input coordinates pre-rotation prevents error spreading, while preserving largest-magnitude rotated coordinates post-rotation reduces quantization error. The framework builds on established rotation preprocessing with offline-optimized codebooks.

entry.title: Mutually Adversarial Self-Training with Evolving Data for Unified Multimodal Models

author.name: Wentao Zhou, Weijie Gan, Jiayun Wang

entry.summary: MATE is an RL-based post-training framework for unified multimodal models in which the generation and understanding branches adversarially challenge each other, taking turns as challenger and solver with evolving candidate screening. This contrasts with prior cooperative self-training where branches simply supervise each other.

entry.title: LatentSift: Policy-State Filtering for Token-Efficient Verification of Software Engineering Agents

author.name: Yuning Han, Yangchenchen Jin, Tyler Jandreau, Jingwei Sun

entry.summary: LatentSift replaces LLM-based execution-free verifiers in test-time scaling pipelines with a token-free filter that uses the hidden states the policy already produces while generating candidate trajectories. Candidates are represented via reasoning, observation, and function-call states and compared against positive and negative state banks. This substantially cuts verification token costs for software engineering agents.

entry.title: Staircase Policy: Streaming Inference for World-Action Models with Large Action Chunks

author.name: Guoheng Sun, Chen Chen, Jin Wang, Ang Li, Teresa Lv

entry.summary: Staircase Policy is a streaming inference and training framework for world-action models in robotic manipulation that converts a flow-matching VLA into a JEPA-style model and splits large action chunks into staggered sub-chunks. Near-term actions execute immediately while later actions continue refinement, mitigating the stale-observation problem of action chunking over long horizons.

entry.title: Adapting Context Compression for Long-Horizon Agents with Counterfactual Continuations

author.name: Guanghui Min, Liang Wu, Mingjia Shi, Yinhan He, Mayank Darbari, Liangjie Hong, Chen Chen

entry.summary: This paper studies context compression for long-horizon agents and finds that compression degrades execution reliability before it degrades solvability. It proposes PAIR, a method using matched counterfactual continuations from the same agent state to isolate the causal effect of individual compression events, then adapts compression prompts around the severe but isolated degradation points. The counterfactual methodology avoids confounding from agent stochasticity.

entry.title: Where Predictive Supervision Goes Shapes What VLA Policies Learn

author.name: Hanseul Kim, Jewon Yeom, Youngjoon Jeong, Minsoo Jo, Taesup Kim

entry.summary: This paper studies when future-prediction auxiliary objectives actually improve the representations used by vision-language-action policies, distinguishing forecast quality from control-relevant representation learning. Through controlled comparisons with matched target constructions, prediction horizons, and training conditions, it shows different prediction interfaces produce different outcomes, especially under distribution shift. This clarifies how predictive supervision should be applied in VLA training.

entry.title: On-Policy Visual Evidence Distillation

author.name: Shaohang Wei, Feifan Song, Guangyue Peng, Wenhao Yu, Wei Li, Wen Luo, Yang Xu, Yufan Shen, Luke Mao, Yang Du, Asher Qin, Houfeng Wang

entry.summary: This work improves on-policy distillation for visual agents by explicitly modeling the causal chain between student actions, resulting observations, and subsequent reasoning, rather than only constructing auxiliary image views. Because image operations change the evidence available for later reasoning, tailoring teacher corrections to this action-observation-reasoning chain reduces error propagation across trajectories. It advances training of multimodal agents that interleave reasoning with image manipulation.

entry.title: Does the Unsafe Gradient Survive a Conversation? On the Fragility of Gradient-Based Jailbreak Detection in Multi-Turn Dialogue

author.name: Omar Sheta, Rinku Deuja, Hadi Masoudi, Minghong Fang

entry.summary: The paper evaluates gradient-based jailbreak detectors like GradSafe in multi-turn dialogue, where attackers spread unsafe intent across several turns, and finds these single-prompt detectors are fragile in such settings. It proposes a Context Window Scanner extension that scores fixed-size windows of user turns, analyzing window sizes and attack types. This exposes an important gap in deployed safety tooling as conversational attacks become the norm.

entry.title: SKILLLITE: Evidence-Guided Malicious Skill Auditing with Compact LLMs

author.name: Haoran Ou, Gelei Deng, Xuanye Zhang, Wenbo Guo, Tianwei Zhang, Kwok-Yan Lam

entry.summary: SKILLLITE addresses the supply-chain security risk of third-party Agent Skills, which bundle instructions with executable components that can abuse agent privileges. It achieves effective malicious-skill auditing using compact, locally deployable LLMs through evidence-guided auditing, avoiding reliance on commercial frontier models. This is timely given the rapid growth of agent skill ecosystems and their expanded attack surface.

entry.title: Parameterized Stripe Attention for Efficient Video Generation

author.name: Xingyu Jia, Baole Ai, Ang Wang, Kang Zhao, Yong Li

entry.summary: The paper identifies periodic diagonal stripe structures in diffusion transformer video attention and proposes parameterized stripe attention to exploit them. This resolves the flexibility-efficiency dilemma between predefined sparse masks and runtime-determined masks, offering a unified structural characterization of DiT attention. The result reduces the costly full spatio-temporal attention that dominates video generation latency.

entry.title: Identifying ODEs from Unstructured Data with Causal Representation Learning

author.name: Alessandro Trenta, Riccardo Massidda, Davide Bacciu, Sara Magliacane

entry.summary: SPEED-AE combines causal representation learning with sparse equation discovery to recover governing ODEs from unstructured high-dimensional observations such as images. The paper proves that CRL-identified variables cannot generally be fed directly into equation discovery methods, and constructs an autoencoder producing variables that satisfy the sparsity assumptions equation discovery requires. This brings theoretical identifiability guarantees to ODE discovery from raw observations.

entry.title: What Does Post-Training Change in Multilingual Reasoning?

author.name: Hongyang Li, Xiao Li, Caesar Wu, Gr\'egoire Danoy, Pascal Bouvry

entry.summary: This audit of Qwen3 checkpoints across eleven languages finds a stark disparity: only 15.4-17.9% of competition math problems receive a correct, terminating solution with visible reasoning in any of ten non-English languages across 16 samples, versus 92.9% in English. The paper evaluates thirteen endpoints spanning released checkpoints and multilingual SFT variants to identify the source of the disparity. It frames language as an access barrier when models can solve problems but not deliver solutions in the user's language.

entry.title: Do Agent Benchmarks Do What They Say? An Executable-Contract Audit of Tool-Using Agent Environments

author.name: Rohith Reddy Bellibatlu, Zichong Wang, Wenbin Zhang

entry.summary: The authors treat simulated tools in agent benchmarks as executable contracts, auditing whether implementations match advertised interfaces and tracing score provenance through task files and evaluator code. Across 34 mutating tools in four benchmarks they confirm seven tool defects and one evaluator property, showing that scores can certify more than the underlying environment actually did. This exposes a systemic validity problem in agent benchmarking.

entry.title: Learning to Retrieve Missing Evidence for Long-Term Memory QA

author.name: Yi-Xuan Deng, Yi Zhang, Wei Liu, Chao Xue, Shuojin Yang

entry.summary: MERA separates globally searchable memory from a question-specific evidence state so verified evidence can guide subsequent retrieval in long-term memory QA. A lightweight planner trained with reinforcement learning is rewarded for recovering previously missing evidence scattered across distant conversation turns. The approach improves answer accuracy when questions omit clues needed to locate stored facts.

entry.title: Video2STL: Grounding VLM-Generated Temporal Specifications for Robot Learning

author.name: Merve Atasever, Keyan Azbijari, Cagan Bakirci, Bo-Ruei Huang, Tolga Izdas, Zahra Shahrooei, Richard Yang, Erdem Biyik, Jyotirmoy V. Deshmukh

entry.summary: Video2STL converts observation-only demonstration videos into parametric Signal Temporal Logic specifications, extracted by a VLM, that are used as formal, inspectable representations for robot policy learning. This improves on scalar similarity signals or direct reward-code generation by making task temporal structure groundable and reusable. It enables learning from videos without action annotations or matched embodiments.

entry.title: A Benchmark & Dataset for Detecting AI-Manipulated Visual Evidence in the Court System

author.name: Kelly McConvey, Sajad Ebrahimi, Nima Jamali, Jalehsadat Mahdavimoghaddam, Matina Mahdizadeh Sani, Maksym Taranukhin, Wentao Zhang, Jacquelyn Burkell, Yuntian Deng, Karen Eltis, Maura R. Grossman, Vered Shwartz, Ebrahim Bagheri

entry.summary: This interdisciplinary team introduces a benchmark and dataset for detecting AI-manipulated photographic evidence in legal contexts, focused on localized prompt-based edits to surveillance, dashcam, and phone images that change what an exhibit appears to prove. Existing forensics benchmarks do not target court-relevant evidence types or the legal workflows that consume them. The resource supports both technical detection research and procedural reform discussions.

entry.title: Thinking in Depth, Speaking Directly: Recurrent Latent Reasoning for Paralinguistically Grounded Spoken Dialogue

author.name: Shengbo Cai, Yuxiang Wang, Jingran Xie, Zhisheng Zhang, Shun Lei, Di Cao, Teddy Sun, Zhiyong Wu

entry.summary: LoopSLM uses a looped Transformer for latent reasoning over spoken dialogue, reusing a decoder block to refine hidden states with acoustic grounding each pass, thereby addressing a perception-reasoning gap where explicit chain-of-thought fails to convert paralinguistic perception into response planning. The two-stage training separates learning to reason from learning to respond, and latent reasoning avoids CoT generation latency. It targets empathetic spoken dialogue systems that must use how something is said, not just what.

entry.title: Scaling Influence Functions in LLMs through Eigenbasis-Corrected One-Bit Gradient Projection

author.name: Jaeseung Heo, J Rosser, Dongwoo Kim

entry.summary: EOGP makes influence functions practical at LLM scale by compressing stored training gradients with EK-FAC dimensionality reduction plus worst-case-optimal one-bit projection, preserving influence estimates for unknown future queries. This enables repeated training-data attribution analyses without storing full gradients. Training-data attribution is increasingly important for auditing, debugging, and compliance of large models.

entry.title: Beyond Interaction Capacity: Estimator Scaling with Recursive Models for CTR Prediction

author.name: Shivang Chopra, Fotis Iliopoulos, Zsolt Kira, Gaurav Menghani

entry.summary: The authors revisit explicit cross networks for click-through-rate prediction and show that increasing interaction capacity in a single predictor yields rapidly diminishing returns. They propose estimator scaling, a complementary direction that allocates resources to multiple predictors combined recursively. This reframes scaling strategies for recommendation and advertising systems.

entry.title: Beyond the Timeline: Augmenting Long-Video Memory with Grounded Entity Biographies

author.name: Hui Ren, Lei Fan, Henry Pao, Han Guo, Zeeshan Zia, Ying Chen, Alexander Schwing, Gang Hua

entry.summary: This work introduces Grounded Entity Biographies (GEB), a long-video memory framework that groups visually grounded observations of the same physical object across clips into retrievable entity biographies. This resolves physical identity ambiguities that chronological descriptions leave unresolved, improving question answering over hour-long or multi-day videos.

entry.title: STEPQuant: When and Where Errors Matter in Delta-Rule Recurrent State Quantization

author.name: Bingchen Yao, Haobo Xu, Haokun Lin, Yichen Wu, Ziyu Guo, Renrui Zhang, Zhichao Lu, Zhenan Sun, Ying Wei

entry.summary: STEPQuant is a spatial-temporal post-training quantization method for linear attention recurrent states, motivated by the observation that quantization errors persist differently depending on memory lifetime and key-row position. It allocates precision according to where errors matter most in both time and space, enabling low-precision states during concurrent serving.

entry.title: CyberWorld: World Models for Sample-Efficient Autonomous Cyber Defense

author.name: Ryozo Masukawa, Sanggeon Yun, Raheeb Hassan, Hyunwoo Oh, SungHeon Jeong, Mohsen Imani

entry.summary: CyberWorld is a Dreamer-style world modeling framework for autonomous cyber defense that learns latent dynamics from vector, graph, textual, and multimodal network representations, optimizing policies via imagined trajectories to improve sample efficiency over model-free RL. It explicitly tackles the question of what constitutes a world model for cybersecurity. Evaluated across four scoreable CyberWheel environments.

entry.title: Is invariance all you need for algorithmic fairness? Removing demographic information can create new bias

author.name: Aditya Parikh, Eike Petersen, Stella Frank, Enzo Ferrante, Melanie Ganz, Aasa Feragen
