It offers a practical route to better reasoning distillation without discarding data or adding intermediate models.

entry.title: Shared Experience, Separate Learning: Companion Confidence Calibration for LLMs

author.name: Shiyu Ni, Keping Bi, Jiafeng Guo, Yilong Xu, Jingtong Wu, Zengxin Han, Xueqi Cheng

entry.summary: Studies concurrent confidence calibration during RLVR training, arguing that existing methods couple capability and confidence learning in shared policy parameters. The proposed approach decouples the two: shared experience from RL rollouts but separate learning of a confidence companion. This targets the persistent problem of LLMs remaining highly confident when wrong.

entry.title: USA: Update-aware SAM for Cross-domain On-Policy Disitllation of Language Agents

author.name: Qiyong Zhong, Mao Zheng, Mingyang Song, Huwei Ji, Houcheng Jiang, Jiajie Su, Li Zhang, Gengsheng Li, Junfeng Fang

entry.summary: This paper studies multi-domain on-policy distillation for agentic reasoning, showing that model merging benefits polarize across domain pairs and falls below single-domain references under negative transfer. The proposed update-aware SAM approach addresses cross-domain conflicts during distillation while avoiding full retraining when one domain's data changes.

entry.title: Reciprocal Guidance: Orchestrating Draft and Verify Budgets for Advancing the Diffusion-AR Self-Speculation Frontier

author.name: Linye Wei, Shutian Zheng, Haoyu Zeng, Meng Li

entry.summary: The paper optimizes diffusion drafting with autoregressive verification for self-speculative decoding, exploring the Pareto frontier between aggregate and per-request throughput across concurrency regimes. Reciprocal guidance dynamically orchestrates draft and verify budgets to mitigate the two-forward-pass cost at low concurrency and expensive long drafts at high concurrency.

entry.title: LongPuzzleBench: Evaluating GUI Agents on Long-Horizon Visual Puzzles

author.name: Bingo Zhang, Haochuan Lu, Zongjie Li, Genjian Li, Ari Yu Zhang, Chaozheng Wang

entry.summary: Introduces a benchmark of 114 levels across six puzzle games played through native GUI actions, designed to test whether GUI agents maintain coherent multi-step plans where early moves can silently make the puzzle unsolvable. Strongest agents struggle to complete objectives that take humans over a thousand actions.

entry.title: Scaling Long-Form Story Generation via Narrative State Tracking

author.name: Zhennan Wan, Jianfei Chen

entry.summary: The authors present NstAgent, a training-free agentic framework that maintains a structured narrative state (characters, past events, future requirements) to scale LLM story generation to full-length novels. They extend an existing benchmark to test narrative consistency across lengths and evaluate both consistency and writing quality. This addresses a known scaling pain point in creative generation that existing ~10k-word methods do not handle.

entry.title: InfoEdit: Probing Global Layout Reasoning in Infographic Editing

author.name: Cheng Yang, Chufan Shi, Huijuan Wang, Bo Shui, Yaokang Wu, Muzi Tao, Yibo Yan, Xuezhe Ma, Taylor Berg-Kirkpatrick

entry.summary: Introduces InfoEdit, a benchmark of 1,000 infographics with 4,000 editing instructions across eight logical-relation families, designed to test reflow: the global layout reasoning needed when editing one element requires adapting surrounding elements. Across eight frontier editors, models struggle with this structured visual content unlike natural photos.

entry.title: Representation Alignment as a Bottleneck in LLM-Based Retrosynthesis Planning

author.name: Hyunwoo Yoo, Cassie Huang, Haebin Shin, Li Zhang, Gail L. Rosen

entry.summary: The authors show that direct SMILES-to-PDDL retrosynthesis planning fails in LLMs, and hypothesize the cause is missing intermediate abstractions rather than model capacity. Decomposing the task into molecule mapping, reaction mapping, and PDDL generation achieves high success where end-to-end approaches fail, indicating a representation-alignment bottleneck.

entry.title: What Makes High-Magnification Knowledge Transferable? A Study of Cross-Resolution Distillation in Whole-Slide Imaging

author.name: Zhiyuan Yang, Jiahao Cheng, Mahdi S. Hosseini

entry.summary: This paper develops a decomposition-based analysis of cross-resolution knowledge distillation in pathology, separating teacher access, representation loss, and model excess to determine when high-magnification knowledge transfers usefully to low-magnification whole-slide analysis. Controlled experiments across ten pathology cohorts covering classification, grading, and survival prediction show that providing teacher regional means alongside native low-magnification features improves downstream performance. The study clarifies the conditions under which distillation helps in computational pathology.

entry.title: Seeing What Should Be Heard: Diagnosing and Repairing Cross-Modal Shortcuts in Omni-Modal LLMs

author.name: Yueran Ma, Ronghao Lin

entry.summary: The paper uncovers a pervasive cross-modal shortcut in omni-modal LLMs: audio questions are answered using visual evidence as much as or more than audio, because training data provides redundant cross-modal evidence. A Factorized Modality Diagnostic independently swaps audio and images between samples to isolate each modality's causal contribution, and the authors propose repairs. This is a significant robustness and faithfulness finding for multimodal systems.

entry.title: RoXDrive: Closed-Loop Reinforcement Learning for End-to-End Autonomous Driving via Action-Faithful Rollouts

author.name: Hongbin Lin, Chaoda Zheng, Yiming Yang, Xiangyu Li, Shijia Chen, Jinhao Deng, Kangjie Chen, Dongbin Zhang, Jie Feng, Yu Zhang, Xianming Liu, Shuguang Cui, Boyang Wang, Zhen Li

entry.summary: RoXDrive uses RL post-training in video world models to train end-to-end autonomous driving policies with action-faithful rollouts, addressing causal confusion from imitation learning that never observes consequences of its own actions. It positions itself between reconstruction-based simulators with limited counterfactual interaction and synthetic simulators with a large sim-to-real gap. This matters because closed-loop training of driving policies is a central open problem.

entry.title: HaPRL: Human-Anchored Process Reinforcement Learning for Visual Search Agent

author.name: Zhangquan Chen, Yaoxin Niu, Xiang An, Mingze Sun, Zhumei Wang, Chih-Ting Liao, Hongkun Cao, Ruqi Huang

entry.summary: HaPRL is the first framework to reinforce the search process of multi-turn visual search agents using human search behavior rather than only final-answer rewards. The authors collect 1K+ human-annotated behavioral signals and train a judge to score rollouts with task-adaptive weights, aiming to prevent scaling along faulty reasoning paths that reach correct answers.

entry.title: When to Retrieve, When to Stay: Uncertainty-Aware Temporal Evidence Allocation for Streaming Video-LLMs

author.name: Xiang Hu, Jiazuo Yu, Lu Zhang, Yunzhi Zhuge, Huchuan Lu

entry.summary: WRWS is a training-free framework for streaming Video-LLMs that adaptively allocates a bounded visual-processing budget between retrieving historically relevant evidence and retaining recent context, using normalized entropy from a lightweight relevance encoder to gauge uncertainty. It addresses failure modes of both recency-only and semantic-only selection.

entry.title: Complementary Retrieval-Augmented Prompting for Consistent Long-Form Video Generation

author.name: Xianghan Wei, Xiaoda Yang, Zhi Wang, An Pan, Daoan Zhang, Huayi Zhang, Yan Zhang, Wei Xu, Zishun Liao, Jianwen Lou

entry.summary: The paper introduces an agentic, training-free framework for long-form video generation that strategically aggregates multiple complementary retrieved references to condition each new shot, mitigating the informational mismatch of single-reference retrieval. The goal is preserving character, scene, and object consistency across a story.

entry.title: HeadGuard: Selective Head Protection for Low-Bit VLM KV-Cache Quantization

author.name: Nenad Banfic

entry.summary: HeadGuard augments base KV-cache quantizers with a fixed high-precision mask that protects the roughly one-eighth of physical KV heads selected offline by image-sensitivity and output-sensitivity scores, keeping their image keys in BF16. Across eight VLMs, three base quantizers, and eight benchmarks, it recovers substantial lost accuracy at low bit-widths, especially for Qwen and InternVL. This is a practical efficiency technique for VLM deployment.

entry.title: Rethinking Multimodal Fake News Detection in the Generative AI Era

author.name: Wenbin Shen, Guoxuan Qin, Guangxu Yao, Baodong Wang, Yuanbo Rui, Zhichao Lian

entry.summary: This work addresses the gap between multimodal fake news detection and AIGC detection as generative content increasingly mixes with native news material. The authors construct Weibo26, a multimodal benchmark that explicitly characterizes how generativity differences affect evidence reliability in news verification. It reframes fake news detection for a setting where real and generated content jointly appear.

entry.title: When to Adapt: Multi-Signal Domain Shift Detection for Efficient Training-Free Adaptation in Open-Vocabulary Segmentation

author.name: Michele Antonazzi, Alejandra C. Hernandez, Jos\'e Araujo, Olov Andersson, Patric Jensfelt

entry.summary: This work tackles when to trigger training-free adaptation of visual foundation models for open-vocabulary segmentation on resource-constrained robots, replacing impractical per-frame adaptation with multi-signal domain shift detection. The approach adapts online via lightweight adapters only when the environment genuinely changes. This is aimed at long-term robotic missions with shifting conditions.

entry.title: Reactive Real-Time Flow Policies via Asynchronous Distribution Alignment

author.name: Moritz Zoellner, Reece O'Mahoney, Ioannis Havoutis, Rohan Paleja

entry.summary: The paper studies whether asynchronous execution of vision-language-action policies, which avoids pauses by predicting the next action chunk during execution of the previous one, preserves the original action distribution. It shows that for non-Markovian demonstrations asynchronous execution yields a fundamentally different distribution limiting reactivity, and proposes aligning the asynchronous action distribution with the synchronous one to restore responsiveness.

entry.title: PreferenceFlow: Test-Time Guidance of Flow-Matching Robot Policies from Human Interventions

author.name: Yiqi Tang, Diyuan Shi, Runze Li, Donglin Wang

entry.summary: PreferenceFlow improves pretrained flow-matching robot policies at test time using human interventions: intervention chunks are paired with policy-generated chunks from the same initial state to train a preference model, whose gradient guides the flow sampling without reward functions or base-policy updates. A gradient-cap loss prevents harmful drift. This offers a reward-free, deployment-time path to policy improvement, akin to RLHF but on-robot.

entry.title: Disentangling Spurious Correlations in Vision-Language-Action Models via Predicting Domain-Invariant Latent Lookahead

author.name: Junghyun Kim, Ngseo Kim, ChungWoo Lee, Seoyeon Lee, Woo-Jeong Baek, Adam Zhou, Chip Huyen, Jun-Ki Lee, Gi-Cheon Kang, Byoung-Tak Zhang

entry.summary: DILL is a representation-learning framework that reduces shortcut learning in VLA policies by supervising them with domain-invariant future latents learned from domain-transformed trajectories. A contrastively trained Task-Domain Encoder with disentanglement regularization separates task-relevant structure from domain-specific visual variation.

entry.title: High-Dimensional Simulation-Based Inference in Latent Spaces

author.name: Lars K\"uhmichel, Stefan T. Radev, Bhanu Prasanna Koppolu, Masoumeh Davoudi, Jerry M. Huang, Paul-Christian B\"urkner

entry.summary: Merges neural simulation-based inference with latent generative modeling by learning a low-dimensional representation of simulator parameters and performing posterior inference directly in that latent space. This complements prior SBI work that compressed only observations, enabling inference over increasingly high-dimensional parameter spaces.

entry.title: Memory Is a Derivation: The Distributed-Evidence Paradox in Long-Term Agents

author.name: Hongjun Liu, Chen Zhao

entry.summary: The paper characterizes a derivation problem in long-running LLM agents whose persistent memories may not follow from the interaction histories that support them, formalized via evidence scope, compositional validity, and admission reliability. It highlights how compression can introduce unsupported relations while valid memories may appear unsupported due to omitted citations.

entry.title: From Surfaces to Volumes: Registered Geometry for Protein Representation Learning

author.name: Siyuan Chen, Cai Zhou, Jinrui Zhang, Zhaokang Liang, Taku Komura, Wojciech Matusik, Stephen Bates, Tommi Jaakkola, Wengong Jin, Peter Yichen Chen, Minghao Guo

entry.summary: Protein-TetSphere introduces a registered residue-wise volumetric representation for proteins, tetrahedralizing each chain into residue-associated volumetric regions and registering them to a shared fixed-topology reference in a common Laplacian basis. This goes beyond surface-only geometric features to model volumetric structure with a consistent coordinate system. The work strengthens geometric deep learning for structural biology with potential downstream uses in protein function prediction and design.

entry.title: RankBuffer: Efficient Ranking-Based Rewards for Open-Ended Generation

author.name: Zixuan Yang, Yiqun Chen, Qi Liu, Wei Yang, Erhan Zhang, Liyi Chen, Qimeng Wang, Yan Gao, Jiaxin Mao

entry.summary: RankBuffer addresses the cost of ranking-based rewards in group-based RL for open-ended generation by maintaining an ordered, query-specific buffer of previously judged responses as a reusable quality scale. New rollouts are coarsely assigned to an anchor interval, then only same-interval rollouts receive local fine ranking, with boundary expansion and anchor pruning controlling cost. The complete order converts to bounded rank rewards.

entry.title: The Default Trap: Rethinking Plan Evaluation in Tool-Using LLM Agents

author.name: Xueqi Li, Jingjie Ning, Yibo Kong

entry.summary: This paper identifies the default trap: misreading an agent's weak sensitivity to removal of a default-aligned plan as unresponsiveness to alternative priorities, using paired plans and a shared no-plan reference with an accounting identity relating the contrasts. Experiments across thousands of decision windows on Retail, Airline, and AgentDojo tasks quantify how priority switches and list-order reversals redirect agent choices.

entry.title: How Can Recommendation Feedback Evolve Agent Memory?

author.name: Shanwen Mao, Mingming Li, Hao Zhang, Zhiheng Li, Yige Wang, Penghua Yu, Junxiong Zhu

entry.summary: TIDE (Trajectory-Informed Directed Memory Evolution) is a framework for evolving agent memory using delayed, noisy recommendation feedback such as impressions, clicks, and conversions, which are confounded by audience composition and placement. The method addresses the attribution problem of mapping real-world outcome signals to memory fitness, moving beyond immediate-feedback or purely semantic-retrieval approaches.

entry.title: HARISSA: Inference-Time Self-Checks for Efficient and Safe Local Language Model Deployment

author.name: Kenan Alkiek, Moontae Lee, David Jurgens, V. G. Vinod Vydiswaran

entry.summary: Addresses local deployment of small language models by framing two decisions for hard queries: whether to spend extra computation before answering, and whether to defer to a human rather than deliver a wrong answer. HARISSA uses inference-time self-checks to navigate the efficiency-safety tradeoff without escalating to cloud models, preserving privacy and cost advantages.

entry.title: Learning Meta-Skills for Agent Harness Design in Test-Time AI4AI

author.name: Cheng Qian, Kunlun Zhu, Beibin Li, Zhenhailong Wang, Heng Ji

entry.summary: The paper studies test-time AI-for-AI, where a frozen Builder model learns meta-skills - reusable principles about when support is needed and what resources to provide - to construct better execution environments (harnesses) for a frozen Target model. Learned skill banks improve macro-average performance by 8.95 points over no-skill construction and 12.02 points over direct task delivery on Harness-Bench and NewtonBench.

entry.title: Mnemon: Raw Records, Fast Judgments, Slow Thoughts

author.name: Guangren Wang

entry.summary: Mnemon is a memory agent for LLM assistants that separates memory work into fast System 1 judgments (many small yes/no decisions about raw dated records, handled by a small decision model) and slow System 2 composition (search query writing and answer composition by an LLM). Unlike systems that rewrite conversations into facts or graphs at write time, it preserves conversations as raw records. This cognitive-architecture-inspired division aims for more reliable long-term memory.

entry.title: ATLAS: Aligned Transport of Latent Structure for Reliable World Model Planning

author.name: Ke Fang, Yupu Yao, Lu Cheng

entry.summary: ATLAS is a training objective that preserves relational geometry in latent world models while calibrating the global latent distribution, transferring normalized pairwise structure from an informative encoder to the planning latent via Wasserstein embedding matching. This prevents planning-relevant novelty structure from degrading during representation learning.

entry.title: Reliability Testing of Medical Model Performance under Distributed Deployment

author.name: Yifei Wang, Xiaohan Zhang, Youtao Ding, Tianlin Li, Xiaoyu Zhang, Yida Yang, Li Pan

entry.summary: The authors identify an evaluation-deployment mismatch where medical models that pass centralized HuggingFace evaluation can produce different outputs when served via distributed inference stacks using tensor parallelism, mixed precision, and kernel fusion. They propose a testing framework and a distributed-execution-sensitive medical benchmark comparing the same checkpoint under centralized versus distributed execution. This matters because silent output changes in medical settings carry patient-safety risk.

entry.title: ER-JEPA: Experience Replay Improves Joint-Embedding Predictive Learning in Language Models

author.name: Jingnan Pu, Zi-En Fan, Feng Lian

entry.summary: ER-JEPA augments LLM-JEPA, a joint-embedding predictive architecture for language model training, with an episodic replay memory that stores training pairs and retrieves relevant ones for additional supervision. This stabilizes token prediction and representation alignment beyond what strong view alignment alone achieves. The work connects JEPA-style objectives with classic continual-learning machinery for improved semantic learning in LLMs.

entry.title: VStress: Correlation-Aware Auditing and Adaptive Budget Allocation for Repeated Verifiers

author.name: Miaobo Hu, Shuhao Hu, Xiaobo Guo, Xin Wang, Bokun Wang, Peng Zhang, Daren Zha, Jun Xiao

entry.summary: VStress proposes an auditable replay contract and a correlation-aware allocation policy for repeated verifier calls in LLM pipelines. It estimates conditional marginal information of unqueried verifiers on a sealed calibration split, normalizes by call cost, and abstains when calls are uninformative. Controlled experiments quantify when majority voting over verifiers degrades under corruption.

entry.title: Lucid Dreaming for World Models: Learning to Doubt Imagination and Decide by Trust

author.name: Ziqi Wen, Ting Xu, Lianyu Wang, Xian Lin, Yanda Meng, Huazhu Fu, Meng Wang, Ching-Yu Cheng

entry.summary: The Lucid World Model (LucidWM) integrates Subjective Logic into categorical latent transitions so agents can distinguish predicted outcomes from their evidential support, assigning each imagined transition a degree of doubt. Trust accumulates multiplicatively along imagined trajectories to reweight returns for policy learning and guide action selection. This addresses overconfident model-based rollouts in unfamiliar states, a core failure mode of world models.

entry.title: Hierarchical Compression of Vision-Language Model Benchmarks

author.name: Hyunjong Ok, Seunggu Kang, Jaeho Lee

entry.summary: PRIMEBench is a vision-aware hierarchical framework for compressing VLM benchmarks in four stages: data cleaning, category representative selection, and further pruning, to preserve model rankings at a fraction of the cost. It extends benchmark compression, well studied for LLMs, to the underexplored multimodal case. This makes frequent VLM evaluation more affordable as benchmarks and model releases proliferate.

entry.title: AS$^2$D: Accelerating On-Demand Audio Understanding on Mobile Devices

author.name: Yunzhe Li, Kyoungjun Park, Hongzi Zhu, Lili Qiu

entry.summary: AS2D introduces target-decoupled drafting for speculative decoding of audio language models: an audio-conditioned drafter generates candidates following its own history while the target verifies independently, removing the serialization between drafting and verification. This exploits the observation that input audio and the user request can provide useful speculative candidates without tracking the target text prefix. It targets on-demand audio understanding on resource-constrained mobile devices.

entry.title: When Keywords Drop but Classifiers Hold: Soft Refusals under KV Cache Compression

author.name: Kang Chen, Xiuze Zhou, Hong Chen, Yuanguo Lin

entry.summary: This study examines whether KV cache compression, which preserves task accuracy, also preserves agreement between lightweight lexical refusal monitors and stronger refusal classifiers on harmful prompts. Using a paired protocol on 200 harmful prompts with long filler contexts, it finds keyword-based monitors diverge under compression while learned classifiers hold. The finding has direct safety-monitoring implications for deployed long-context systems.

entry.title: Interactive Distributionally Robust Multi-Agent Learning with General Function Approximation

author.name: Debamita Ghosh, George K. Atia, Yue Wang

entry.summary: The paper studies online learning in general-sum distributionally robust Markov games with general function approximation and phi-divergence uncertainty sets. It proposes RoMEX-phi, a model-free framework combining equilibrium-based exploration with dual fitted learning via a functional dual representation of the robust multi-agent Bellman operator, addressing scalability limits of prior methods.

entry.title: DP-Rec: Towards Dynamic Patching for Efficient Long-Sequence Recommendation

author.name: Dwipam Katariya, Thomas Caputo, Akshat Shreemali, Juan Manuel Origgi, Nikita Seleznev, Pranab Mohanty, Kalanand Mishra, Nam Nguyen, James Montgomery

entry.summary: DP-Rec applies dynamic latent patching, inspired by the Byte Latent Transformer, to sequential recommendation transformers so that computation is allocated adaptively across items in a user history rather than uniformly. This targets the inefficiency and noise sensitivity of fixed-rate architectures on long sequences, avoiding lossy truncation or staged modeling. The work connects recent efficient-transformer ideas to an industrially important application area.

entry.title: Continual Data Unlearning in Diffusion Models via Transition-based Regularization

author.name: Sunbeom Jeong, Sehwan Kim, Sangwoo Hong, Jungwoo Lee

entry.summary: Proposes a continual data unlearning framework for diffusion models that handles sequential deletion requests by recording changes in denoiser responses before and after each unlearning step and applying a one-sided penalty to prevent reversal along recorded directions. This regularizes future updates to avoid degrading earlier deletions or generative utility.

entry.title: Neural Dynamics as the Composition of Quantized Units

author.name: Jacopo Minniti, Aravinth Kulanthaivelu, Richard Sproat

entry.summary: The paper builds an intermediate abstraction between scaling-law-level and circuit-level views of deep learning, describing training as ordered acquisition of quanta: reusable computations that activate binary across examples. By approximating population-gradient updates, the authors derive quanta acquisition dynamics governed by demand for computations. This connects interpretability microstructure to macroscopic loss behavior.

entry.title: Prioritizing Repeated LLM Evaluation for Hidden Failure Discovery

author.name: Keita Broadwater, Akin Broadwater

entry.summary: The paper formulates LLM reliability evaluation as a budget-constrained discovery problem where each prompt has an unknown per-generation failure probability, proposing a framework that first performs shallow evaluation and then adaptively reallocates budget to prompts likely to hide rare failures. This addresses the problem that shallow stochastic sampling can miss operationally important low-probability failures. It is relevant to responsible LLM deployment testing.

entry.title: Quantization-Aware Pre-Training with Constrained Empirical Weight Distribution

author.name: Ningfeng Yang, Tor M. Aamodt

entry.summary: This work addresses rounding boundary weight oscillation during quantization-aware pre-training, proposing CEWT, a hyperparameter-free optimizer post-update step that projects weights to suppress oscillation without extra memory overhead. It claims consistent improvements in quantization-aware pre-training accuracy and convergence speed. Quantization efficiency is highly relevant to reducing LLM inference costs.

entry.title: Derivative-Informed Training of Neural Operators On-the-Fly via Sketched Tangent Consistency

author.name: Xinhan Yang, Lu Lu, Shancong Mou

entry.summary: The paper proposes sketched tangent consistency loss (sTCL), an on-the-fly method for derivative-informed training of neural operators that enforces sensitivity consistency directly from PDE residuals, eliminating offline derivative label generation. This matters for using neural operators as differentiable surrogates in inverse problems, optimization, and control.

entry.title: A Function-Level Vulnerability Score Measures Flag Rate More Than the Model: Protocol Effects on Paired Benchmarks

author.name: Maciej Cicho\'n, Bart{\l}omiej Dmitruk

entry.summary: This paper measures how much evaluation protocol choices (metric, verdict extraction, output budget) explain the wide variance in reported LLM vulnerability-detection scores, with model outputs held fixed across 68 models and six benchmarks. Findings indicate function-level F1 largely reflects flag rate rather than discriminative ability.

entry.title: Generative Priors Conditioned on Natural Language for Bayesian Inversion in PDEs

author.name: Pengyu Zhang, Mark Girolami, Arnaud Vadeboncoeur

entry.summary: The paper learns natural-language-conditional Bayesian priors from paired text descriptions and quantitative quantities of interest, enabling Bayesian inversion in PDE problems to exploit qualitative expert knowledge alongside noisy sensor or simulation data. This bridges linguistic and numerical modalities for scientific machine learning.

entry.title: D-JEPA: Design-Recoverable JEPA Representation with Swappable Physics Decoders

author.name: Nitin Nagesh Kulkarni, Aashwin Anand Mishra, Yin Yu, Peter Lyu

entry.summary: D-JEPA is a geometry-centric joint-embedding predictive architecture that computes compact representations from geometry alone and reuses them across operating conditions and physical response spaces via lightweight physics-specific decoders. An explicit design-recoverability objective keeps the latent informative about underlying design variables, preventing entanglement.

entry.title: RMB: Reward Model Boosting Mitigates Reward Hacking

author.name: Jiabin Fan, Dezhi Ye, Yongchang Hao, Lili Mou

entry.summary: Reward Model Boosting (RMB) addresses reward hacking in RLHF by training an ensemble of reward models with a diversity-promoting regularizer so each captures complementary aspects of the reward landscape, then learning a lightweight booster-style aggregator. The aggregated reward signal is claimed to be more robust and reliable than individual proxy reward models.

entry.title: SMAT: Simple and Efficient Merge-Aware Training

author.name: Yanggan Gu, Yuanyi Wang, Zhen Li, Shuo Cai, Yuhang Liu, Junzhuo Li, Zihao Wang, Hongxia Yang

entry.summary: SMAT improves model merging by training experts to be merge-aware: it abstracts common merging operations as Scale, Mask, and Perturb, then jointly optimizes expert loss and expected loss at simulated merged parameters. This accounts for merging operations without the extra training cost of prior merge-aware methods.

entry.title: TerMeZO: Ternary Sparse Zeroth-Order Optimization for Fine-tuning BitNet Models at the Edge

author.name: Houssem Sifaou, Prabodh Katti, Bipin Rajendran, Osvaldo Simeone

entry.summary: TerMeZO enables memory-efficient zeroth-order fine-tuning of BitNet models with ternary weights, addressing the problem that sparse ZO methods either ignore ternary structure or require first-order gradients for masking. It aims to keep fine-tuning memory footprint at inference levels for edge deployment.

entry.title: Dynamic Kuramoto-Hodge Operators for PDEs on Complex Geometries and Topologies

author.name: Xiang Li, Yue Song

entry.summary: The paper introduces the Dynamic Kuramoto-Hodge Operator (DKHO), a neural operator that encodes conditions on their native cochain supports, evolves Kuramoto-inspired relation states via Dirac operators, and decodes responses in orthogonal Hodge subspaces for PDE learning on complex geometries. It explicitly respects topology and condition-dependent coupling among vertex, edge, and face fields. This is a mathematically principled advance for neural PDE solvers on irregular domains.

entry.title: Rethinking Contextualization by Reinterpreting Attention Head Channels

author.name: Hakaze Cho, Haolin Yang, Zhun Sun, Naoya Inoue, Benjamin Heinzerling, Kentaro Inui

entry.summary: Proposes a global principle for how transformer contextualization works: words carry different amounts of information, and less-informative words tend to absorb more contextual information, with fine-grained selectivity routing information between matched words. The work reinterprets attention head channels to give a global account of contextualization beyond word-by-word or head-by-head analyses.

entry.title: Future Information-Directed Sampling for Bayesian Nonstationary Bandits

author.name: Yichen Song, Alessio Russo, Aldo Pacchiano

entry.summary: Proposes Future Information-Directed Sampling, an algorithm for Bayesian nonstationary bandits that explicitly explores to gather information about future optimal arms rather than only reducing current uncertainty. FIDS matches Thompson Sampling regret up to a small constant factor while exploiting predictive structure of the nonstationarity.

entry.title: PReCache: Efficient KV Cache Sharing for Multi-LoRA Agents via Low-Rank Precomputation and Neutral Reconstruction

author.name: Hyesung Jeon, Hyeongju Ha, Jae-Joon Kim

entry.summary: PReCache is a training-free framework for sharing KV caches across multiple LoRA agents that repeatedly prefill a growing shared trajectory. It uses low-rank precomputation and neutral reconstruction so cache reuse does not erode the role-specific behavior encoded by each agent's own adapter, reducing memory and compute redundancy in long-horizon tasks.

entry.title: Learning to Optimize through Solver-Grounded Self-Play

author.name: Xia Jiang, Yaoxin Wu, Chenyu Zhou, Mengzhu Xu, Wim P. M. Nuijten, Yingqian Zhang

entry.summary: OPT-Zero is the first fully self-play training framework for LLM-based optimization modeling requiring zero external training data, using one LLM in a dual-role loop where a Proposer synthesizes problems and a solver learns from solver-grounded verification. It aims to overcome the generalization ceiling and capability anchoring of annotation-dependent training paradigms.

entry.title: Q-learning Penalized Transformer for Safe Offline Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Shengchao Hu, Peng Wang, Jifeng Hu, Qiyang Zhou, Anning Hu, Li Shen, Ya Zhang, Dacheng Tao

entry.summary: QPT is a training-inference consistent framework for safe offline RL that combines conditional sequence modeling with constraint-aware value estimation, balancing safety constraints, reward maximization, and behavior regularization. A Transformer policy generates actions conditioned on trajectory context and target return and cost, retaining constraint awareness from training through inference.

entry.title: Learn Here, Move Less Elsewhere: Input-Conditioned Plasticity from Retained-Domain Activation Atlases

author.name: Jiangtao Lin, Bangyang Wei, Yihang Ding, Siyi Liu, Yuhan Dong

entry.summary: ATLAS turns retained-domain representations into an input-dependent plasticity rule for task fine-tuning: an activation atlas provides local reference centers and directional filters to a shared low-rank residual, so updates concentrate on the target task while preserving existing behavior. On Qwen3-8B it achieves lower retained-output KL divergence than seven published baselines at matched coding performance. This addresses the problem of task-specific fine-tuning rewriting model behavior beyond the training task.

entry.title: GenMem: Generative Symbolic Memory for Self-Evolving Harness

author.name: Xinke Jiang, Tao Feng, Weixuan Xu, Zhixin Zhang, Zhibang Yang, Wentao Zhang, Runchuan Zhu, Xu Chu, Junfeng Zhao, Yasha Wang

entry.summary: GenMem addresses long-term memory for self-evolving LLM agents, proposing generative symbolic memory that supports retention, retrieval, reuse, and revision of sparse, hierarchical, redundant experience across long-horizon tasks. It tackles sparse delayed feedback across the memory lifecycle and the tension between continual memory evolution and invariance of stored content.

entry.title: Minimax Last-Iterate Convergence in Matrix Games with Observed Actions

author.name: Yuheng Zhang

entry.summary: The paper develops an algorithm for two-player zero-sum matrix games with bandit payoff feedback and observed opponent actions achieving a duality gap of O(sqrt(d/t)) with high probability simultaneously at every round, improving prior dimension dependence by d^(3/2) and matching a standard bandit lower bound. The algorithm uses only O(d) time and memory per round.

entry.title: No Pain, More Gain: Iterative Merging for Effective Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Seonghyeon Kim, Chaeyun Jang, Noah Lee, Boseop Kim, Juho Lee

entry.summary: The paper studies multi-teacher on-policy distillation where domain teachers share a reference model but differ in post-training, showing that student initialization strongly affects whether teacher capabilities are recovered. It finds that benchmark performance is a poor predictor of good initialization and proposes iterative weight merging of teachers as a better starting point. This informs practical model distillation pipelines.

entry.title: TIDE: Teacher-Student Transition via Informative Distillation and Exploration for Agentic RL

author.name: Yibin Huang, Xinming Xu, Conghui Zhu

entry.summary: TIDE improves agentic RL by adaptively scheduling on-policy distillation from a stronger teacher alongside reward optimization, arguing a fixed mixture fails both globally (distillation pressure caps the model below teacher capability) and locally across interaction turns. It targets multi-turn agents trained with GRPO under sparse trajectory rewards.

entry.title: Small transformers track Bayesian evidence for latent common causes via a context-invariant mechanism

author.name: Amir Mohammadpour, Michael Franke

entry.summary: This interpretability-style study shows how Bayesian reasoning about latent common causes can emerge in small transformers as cross-contextual generalization. It disentangles model mechanisms from data-generating causal structure and examines whether Bayesian evidence accumulation is implemented in mechanisms that generalize to novel test cases.

entry.title: Collaborative Principle Evolution via Evidence Transfer for Scientific Discovery

author.name: Yingming Pu, Hongyu Chen, Tao Lin

entry.summary: Presents COEVOLVE, a framework where parallel LLM-driven principle-evolution branches collaborate by transferring evidence through value-of-information-gated routing and context-discounted likelihood injection, while keeping their principle posteriors separate. This parallelizes and broadens hypothesis-space exploration for automated scientific discovery.

entry.title: Interference Beyond Geometry in Concept Extraction

author.name: Val\'erie Costa, Bahareh Tolooshams

entry.summary: Proposes effective interference, combining feature geometry with code statistics to distinguish constructive from destructive interference in learned representations. Characterizes four mechanisms by which architectural constraints shape interference and shows sparse autoencoders selectively reduce overlap among co-active features while preserving constructive cross-contributions.

entry.title: Manifold-Stable Flow Matching

author.name: Amirhossein Nazerian, Ali Pezeshki, Jianguo Zhao

entry.summary: MSFM enables flow matching to start from an arbitrary ambient prior not supported on the data manifold by combining learned tangential transport with prescribed normal contraction from contraction theory, ensuring generated samples adhere to the data manifold. This removes the need for prior knowledge of the manifold geometry required by geometric flow matching variants.

entry.title: Attention Graphons: A Graph Limit Perspective on Graph Transformers

author.name: Caio F. Deberaldini Netto, Moshe Eliasof, Luana Ruiz

entry.summary: The authors ask whether attention-induced graphs in graph transformers converge to a stable limit object as graph size grows, answering affirmatively via dense graph limit theory: each attention matrix is a finite sample of an underlying attention graphon. They derive variance bounds under cut-distance and propose a canonicalize-then-build pipeline to operationalize the theory.

entry.title: X-Reset: Scaling Object-Centric Reinforcement Learning via Cross-Embodiment Resets

author.name: Prithwish Dan, Chenyang Ma, Wei Zhan

entry.summary: X-Reset addresses the exploration problem in training generalist dexterous manipulation policies by using human hand-object demonstrations not for imitation but to kinematically retarget states for environment resets. By resetting the robot near informative hand-object states filtered for feasibility, it enables task-agnostic reward training without per-task reward shaping or heavy robot demonstrations.

entry.title: PalmLeaf-VQA: A Multi-Script Visual Question Answering Benchmark for Historical Palm-Leaf Manuscript Understanding Across Diverse Regions

author.name: Nimol Thuon, Jun Du, Panhapin Theang

entry.summary: PalmLeaf-VQA is a visual question answering benchmark of 923 historical palm-leaf manuscript images and 7,384 QA pairs across eight South and Southeast Asian scripts including Balinese, Grantha, Khmer, Sundanese, and Tamil. It targets manuscript-aware visual reasoning about preservation-relevant cues rather than simple recognition, probing how multimodal LLMs handle culturally diverse, degraded, non-Latin documents. This fills a genuine gap in VLM evaluation coverage of underrepresented scripts and cultural heritage.

entry.title: Statistical Testing for Multiple Instance Learning via Selective Inference with Applications to Computational Pathology

author.name: Noriaki Hashimoto, Shuichi Nishino, Teruyuki Katsuoka, Tomohiro Shiraishi, Daiki Miwa, Hiroyuki Hanada, Jun Sakuma, Hidekata Hontani, Hiroaki Miyoshi, Ichiro Takeuchi

entry.summary: The authors formulate evaluation of high-attention instances in attention-based multiple instance learning as a statistical hypothesis testing problem using selective inference. This determines whether selected high-attention whole-slide image regions in computational pathology are significantly different from normal instances, addressing the unreliability of attention scores as explanations. The work adds statistical rigor to a widely used weakly supervised paradigm.

entry.title: Clarify the User or Verify the World? Uncertainty Routing for Proactive Agents

author.name: Zhaofeng Li, Xuan Zhang, Xiaokui Xiao, Yang Deng

entry.summary: PROUR addresses a decision LLM agents face beyond whether to seek information: which source can resolve the uncertainty, routing among acting, clarifying with the user, and verifying the environment. It decomposes action uncertainty into disagreement over user-goal interpretations versus residual entropy within interpretations, with queries generated for the routed source.

entry.title: Train4Merge: A Controlled Single-Teacher Study of RL vs. SFT Teachers for OPD-Based Model Merging

author.name: Jingyuan Huang, Zuming Huang, Yucheng Shi, Zhongzhi Li, Xiaoming Zhai, Wei Chu, Ninghao Liu

entry.summary: The paper asks whether experts trained via RL versus SFT, though equally strong, are equally good teachers for on-policy distillation during model merging. In controlled experiments from a shared 9B checkpoint across agentic, reasoning, and perception domains, RL-guided students outperform SFT-guided students at their best checkpoints.

entry.title: What Should the Reflector See? An Empirical Study of Evidence in Reflective Prompt Optimization

author.name: Xiaofan Zhou, Lu Cheng

entry.summary: This empirical study systematically examines which evidence a reflector should receive in reflective prompt optimization, varying evidence composition, example visibility, candidate selection, and domain-knowledge policy within a single-parent Pareto-guided search. Using Qwen3.5-9B as both task model and reflector across nine strategies and five datasets, it finds failures-only evidence yields the largest mean test gain (+8.0 points), while balanced-mix and no-examples configurations rank best overall. It provides practical guidance for the fast-moving area of automatic prompt optimization.

entry.title: MixBench-TS: A Multivariate Time Series Forecasting Benchmark Where Channel Mixing Pays Off

author.name: Ibram Abdelmalak, Mischa Putzke, Jungmin Choi, Tom Hanika, Vijaya Krishna Yalavarthi, Lars Schmidt-Thieme

entry.summary: MixBench-TS interrogates whether standard multivariate time-series forecasting datasets actually contain the cross-channel coupling that channel-mixing models assume, testing Granger causality, transfer entropy, lagged mutual information, and a new model-based CD-gain measure on synthetic data with planted coupling. It then builds a benchmark where channel mixing demonstrably helps.

entry.title: Revisiting AdaGrad in Stochastic Convex Optimization: Last Iterates, High Probability, and Lower Bounds

author.name: Weiming Ou, Xiao Wang

entry.summary: The paper proves that AdaGrad and AdaGrad-Norm admit no universal last-iterate rate even under sub-Gaussian noise, that bounded variance alone cannot yield high-probability average-iterate rates, and establishes tight Omega(log T / sqrt T) lower bounds showing the log factor in known upper bounds is unavoidable.

entry.title: An Empirical Study on What Matters for Viewpoint-Generalizable Policies in Visual Imitation Learning

author.name: Mino Nakura, Sriram Krishna, Yufei Wang, Shubham Tulsiani, Zackory Erickson, David Held

entry.summary: A controlled empirical study of design choices enabling visuomotor manipulation policies to generalize across camera viewpoints, finding that retaining dense visual tokens and letting the action head participate in geometric reasoning substantially improves viewpoint robustness in simulation across a wide range of camera poses.

entry.title: Scoring the Wrong Question: Readout Failures in Constrained-Option Evaluation

author.name: Jiaxuan Guo, Kejia Zhang, Shuo Xin, Jingxin Yang, Youran Sun, Haizhao Yang

entry.summary: The paper studies failures of constrained-option (multiple-choice log-probability) evaluation: models can start answering a quoted embedded question instead of the requested meta-question, and on Qwen3 checkpoints the answer letter is the most probable token on nearly every passage, making correctness forecasts indistinguishable from chance. The authors contribute a label-free diagnostic measuring the support and first-token mass of declared options. This exposes systematic measurement errors in a widely used LLM evaluation protocol.

entry.title: Beyond One-Step Accuracy: State-Affine Latent Transition for Reliable Visual Planning

author.name: Boyuan Zhang, Yingjun Du, Xiantong Zhen, Ling Shao

entry.summary: The paper analyzes error propagation in joint-embedding world models under recursive rollout, decomposing multi-step error into per-step and propagation terms, and proves state-affine dynamics eliminate the nonlinear propagation residual. It leverages this to train latent transitions that yield more reliable visual planning over long horizons.

entry.title: Autonomous phase discovery

author.name: Shiyu Zhou, Yuxuan Zhang, Sebastian Wetzel, Roger Melko, Xiu-Zhe Luo

entry.summary: A fully autonomous system combining differentiable programming and unsupervised learning to discover quantum phases of matter, adaptively selecting evaluation trajectories through Hamiltonian space rather than fixed grids. It is demonstrated with three solvers and benchmarked against random sampling, including on a cluster chain hosting many phases.

entry.title: 3D Point Tracking with State Space Models

author.name: Masahiro Ogawa, Qi An, Atsushi Yamashita

entry.summary: This paper presents a metric 3D point tracker that composes frozen front-ends (dense optical flow for 2D correspondence and a monocular metric-depth network) with a learned residual state space model, exploiting the observation that depth along a point's pixel ray governs metric accuracy once its 2D trajectory is fixed. The method runs on a single commodity GPU in a pose-free monocular setting with absolute-meter accuracy. This supports 4D reconstruction, robot navigation, and autonomous driving applications.

entry.title: ReplayLens: Auditing Agents' Use of Outcomes

author.name: Dong Xu, Zhangfan Yang, Jiantao Wu, Shipeng Zhang, Zexuan Zhu, Jiangqiang Li, Jun Zhang, Junkai Ji

entry.summary: ReplayLens is a black-box audit framework that isolates which relationship (recorded score, action name, storage position, or score attachment) drives changes in an agent's decisions when it reuses logged experience, via targeted single-variable interventions. A constructive separation shows the interventions are distinguishable.

entry.title: P2P: Cross-View Population Denoising for Unpaired Single-Cell Perturbation Response Prediction

author.name: Haojie Yang, Ran Su

entry.summary: P2P addresses perturbation response prediction for AI Virtual Cells by using stochastic cell-set views as the supervision unit rather than individual cells, exploiting the fact that two views from the same condition share a reproducible population effect. This handles the unpaired nature of Perturb-seq data and denoises heterogeneous, noisy cell populations. The approach targets the reproducible population effect rather than per-cell variation.

entry.title: On Temporal Binding in Large Audio Language Models

author.name: Paul Primus, Gerhard Widmer

entry.summary: Using mechanistic interpretability, this study examines how temporal information is represented and bound to sound events in three open-source large audio language models. It finds event-specific positions concentrate in event name representations at intermediate modality integration layers, encoded along a low-dimensional curved relative-time trajectory, and demonstrates steering along this direction. This offers the first mechanistic account of temporal grounding in LALMs.

entry.title: A Hierarchy of Entropy-Shapley Games for Multivariate Predictive Uncertainty

author.name: Niklas Koenen, Claudia Battistin, Jeriek Van den Abeele, Martin Jullum

entry.summary: The paper proposes a hierarchy of Shapley-value-based games to attribute multivariate predictive uncertainty to input features without collapsing outputs to scalars. Existing aggregation or component-wise approaches obscure whether features affect marginal uncertainty versus dependence structure; this framework disentangles both. It targets risk-aware decisions and diagnostics for models producing complex dependent outputs like multi-step forecasts.

entry.title: TopoEP: Topology-Aware Load Balancing for Expert-Parallel MoE Training

author.name: Jiacheng Zhu, Xie Zhao, Gongming Zhao, Hongli Xu, Yao Fei, Jin Fang

entry.summary: TopoEP is a GPU-native, topology-aware load-balancing system for expert-parallel Mixture-of-Experts training, addressing stragglers caused by dynamic routing to hot experts. It computes balancing plans on GPUs to avoid device-host transfers and cross-rank synchronization, and its planning formulation accounts for hierarchical scale-up and scale-out communication costs of modern clusters. This targets a real bottleneck in large-scale MoE training efficiency.

entry.title: RIDE: Reference-Anchored Inference-Time Diffusion Editing for Scaffold Hopping

author.name: Ruoxi Gao, Frazier N. Baker, Trieu Nguyen, Xia Ning

entry.summary: RIDE is an inference-time diffusion editing framework for scaffold hopping in drug discovery that recovers the reference diffusion noise trajectory conditioned on the binding pocket and functional groups, then selects an optimal trajectory segment for editing to jointly enforce 2D structural novelty and 3D shape preservation. This addresses a gap in prior conditional-generation approaches to molecular design. It matters for AI-accelerated drug discovery where shape preservation is critical.

entry.title: Using LMs to Model the Effects of Context and Coreference during Sentence Comprehension

author.name: Kohei Kajikawa, Lin Ai, Tatsuki Kuribayashi, Ethan Gotlieb Wilcox

entry.summary: By systematically varying GPT-2 context window size across four large naturalistic English reading-time datasets, the authors find a U-shaped relationship: very restricted contexts capture local memory limits, but expanded contexts of 500-1,000 tokens yield the best overall fit to human data. This challenges the view that strict memory decay is the right way to model human sentence processing with LMs.

entry.title: How to Reduce Whisper Hallucination

author.name: Husein Zolkepli

entry.summary: This paper quantifies Whisper's speech hallucination problem, showing whisper-large-v3 emits words on 61.9% of 42 clips of pure room tone and emits something on all of them. It critiques distillation approaches that filter hallucinated pseudo-labels, arguing they hide the failure mode from the student's training data, and notes that adding non-speech audio teaches suppression without discrimination. The work is analysis of the existing Whisper model rather than a new release, proposing a better checkpoint selection approach.

entry.title: Beyond Memory Construction: Rethinking Memory Access for LLM-based Conversational Agents

author.name: Donghua Cai, Yongheng Deng, Yifei Wang, Zijun Shen, Ju Ren

entry.summary: The paper shows that LLM-based memory construction pipelines become lossy, unstable, and costly in long-horizon, high-entropy conversations, and proposes Threader, a system shifting from memory construction to efficient structure-aware access over raw interactions. This reframes a common architectural assumption in conversational agent memory design. Its relevance is high given the rapid growth of long-context and agent applications.

entry.title: Grounding Memory Summarization in Utility Intent

author.name: Zhenyu Lei, Mingjia Shi, Xingbo Fu, Haoyu He, Qi R. Wang, Jundong Li

entry.summary: The authors show that memory summarizers optimized for human-facing faithfulness misalign with their real objective of supporting future queries, and that conditioning summarization on query-answer pairs substantially improves answer quality. MemSuit is a self-distillation framework where a utility-conditioned teacher produces memory entries that a student learns to reproduce from raw conversation, with safeguards against collateral erasure of evidence. This reframes memory summarization around downstream utility.

entry.title: Reset Is Not Recovery: Evaluating Recoverability from False Conversational Context via Sycophancy Hysteresis

author.name: Adi Shnaidman

entry.summary: Introduces a recovery-after-pressure protocol measuring sycophancy hysteresis: the residual bias toward a user-advocated wrong answer after the user withdraws pressure, relative to a clean-context counterfactual. Across seven instruction-tuned open-weight models and two factual benchmarks, ordinary reset reduces but does not erase pressure-induced bias. This matters for safe deployment of assistants in contaminated multi-turn conversations.

entry.title: In-Context Adaptation of Encoder-Decoder Models in Speech Recognition

author.name: Yen Meng, Sharon Goldwater, Hao Tang

entry.summary: This paper investigates whether in-context learning, previously shown to enable adaptation of LLM-based speech models to new speakers, accents, and domains, is an inherent capability of encoder-decoder speech recognition models more broadly. The authors evaluate two demonstration formats (collated and interleaved speech-text pairs) across six encoder-decoder architectures, covering both conventional cross-attention-based and LLM-based designs, and find that all tested models can perform in-context adaptation out of the box. This suggests ASR adaptation may not require prompting-heavy LLM hybrids, broadening the design space for speaker- and domain-adaptive speech systems.

entry.title: On the Token Value Inequality in Efficient Reasoning

author.name: Runjia Zeng, Hang Hua, Yiyang Liu, Zhiqiang Tao, Ruixiang Tang, Qifan Wang, Cheng Han, Dongfang Liu

entry.summary: Presents a diagnostic and optimization framework showing that token value in chain-of-thought reasoning is highly non-uniform and can be characterized by normalized log-probability signals that separate core structural tokens from redundant filler. This enables pruning or allocating budget within CoT traces for efficient reasoning. It contributes both an empirical insight and a practical optimization path for reasoning-cost reduction.

entry.title: Evaluating Machine Unlearning in ASR

author.name: Diogo Dinis, Francisco Teixeira, Bhiksha Raj, Alberto Abad, Isabel Trancoso

entry.summary: The paper investigates machine unlearning for automatic speech recognition, motivated by right-to-be-forgotten compliance. Applying several MU techniques to an ASR model, the authors find gradient ascent-based methods achieve the best privacy-utility trade-offs, while complex approaches over-unlearn and make unlearned samples easier to detect, suggesting standard privacy evaluations overstate effectiveness.

entry.title: When Harness Beats Scale, and When Reading Beats Both

author.name: Ivan Bondarenko, Nikolay O. Nikitin

entry.summary: This system paper describes the DocSem entry for document-grounded quantitative reasoning, combining hybrid block retrieval, sandboxed Program-of-Thoughts execution, self-consistency, and knowledge-graph entity enrichment. The analysis shows architecture mattered far more than scale: PoT added 0.282 joint accuracy to a 7B model versus at most 0.005 to a 72B model, and a 27B model with the full harness matched the 72B at lower cost and carbon footprint.

entry.title: Using LLMs to Detect LLM-Generated Texts: A Cross-Generation Analysis

author.name: Haiyue Yuan, Jie Guo, Weidong Qiu, Zheng Huang, Ruizhe Li, Shujun Li

entry.summary: A large systematic study of 15 LLMs across three generations acting as both generators and detectors of machine-generated text, using over 233,000 classifications on a benchmark of 1,000 human texts per model. Findings show detection efficacy is driven mainly by detector capability rather than self- versus cross-detection relationships.

entry.title: Distributional Metrics for Evaluating Spoken Conversational Systems

author.name: Shree Harsha Bokkahalli Satish, Erica Cooper, Patr\'icia Schmidtov\'a, Maike Z\"ufle, \'Eva Sz\'ekely, Nicholas Sanders, Ond\v{r}ej Klejch

entry.summary: This work proposes the Conversational Distribution Score (CDS), which evaluates spoken conversational systems by comparing distributions of conversational behavior (speech rate, rhythm, turn interaction, plus a semantic baseline) against human reference conversations. Using listener judgments from goal-oriented dialogues, the composite CDS recovers five of six listener system rankings. It addresses the persistent, unresolved problem of evaluating conversational systems beyond turn-level metrics.

entry.title: Do Audio LLMs Listen Before They Act? Diagnosing Acoustic-Context Gating in Voice Agents

author.name: Yanjie Zhang, Nanchen Hu, Yushi Sun

entry.summary: The paper introduces VGBench, a 1,018-item diagnostic benchmark testing whether voice agents correctly withhold action when audio context (side-talk, self-talk, speaker switches) does not warrant it. Across six raw audio LLMs and three training-free adaptations, models often identify the target tool but rarely withhold action, with a maximum switch mute rate of only 14%. This exposes a significant safety-relevant gap in deployed voice agents.

entry.title: MassAlloc Attention: Let Attention Allocate Its Own Compute

author.name: Jingze Shi, Zhangyang Peng, Xianduo Li, Yanlin Qi, Xiaotian Lin, Haoxian Chen, Liangdong Wang, Guang Liu, Yuyu Luo

entry.summary: Presents MALA, a fused attention primitive that uses the online-softmax normalizer to adaptively skip low-contribution post-score computation while retaining access to all causal interactions, with a shared tolerance governing training and inference. Matched-work experiments at 8K context show benefits from distribution-adaptive compute allocation.

entry.title: One Readout, Many Repairs: Diffusion-Guided Hierarchical Search for Tool-Agent Repair

author.name: Xiang Xia, Cheng Yan, Wuyang Zhang, Fan Xu, Zhijun Fan, Shuyuan Zhang, Yanyong Zhang

entry.summary: The authors formulate tool-agent repair as hierarchical search over operation supports, using diffusion guidance to explore alternative realizations without re-selecting operations unnecessarily. This reduces the cost of complete-sequence regeneration while preserving exploration when failures stem from how operations are realized.

entry.title: From Sharp Eyes to Expert Mind: Internalizing Expert Knowledge in MLLMs for Tampered Text Detection

author.name: Kaiqing Lin, Songze Li, Shen Chen, Yunfei Guo, Xiaoye Qiu, Haodong Li, Taiping Yao, Bo Wang, Youchang Xiao, Bin Li, Shouhong Ding

entry.summary: This work internalizes expert forensic perception into multimodal LLMs for tampered text detection, rather than accessing expert models as external modules. The authors identify a Double Mismatch problem — spatial precision mismatch between coarse visual tokens and tiny tampered regions, and a perceptual mismatch — and design mechanisms to bridge them. This combines the semantic transferability of MLLMs with the fine-grained forensic sensitivity of expert models for document security.

entry.title: S4VY: Segment Anything in Feed-Forward 4D Visual Geometry

author.name: Jingdong Zhang, Xin Li, Jan Kautz, Wenping Wang, Chris Choy

entry.summary: S4VY extends the Segment Anything paradigm to promptable 4D instance segmentation built on feed-forward visual geometry, converting shared visual-geometric features from RGB observations into class-agnostic 4D instance masks via a space-time query decoder. Persistent object queries bind one entity across all observations, removing reliance on sequential memory for identity tracking. This is significant for robotics and autonomous driving, which need consistent dynamic-scene instance segmentation.

entry.title: TaoFlowForge: Progressive Native Mesh Generation via Cascaded Flow Matching

author.name: Xianze Fang, Qiyuan Feng, Dongfang Sun, Yan Zhang, Xiuchao Wu, Jingnan Gao, Jiangjing Lyu, Chengfei Lyu, Gang Yu

entry.summary: TaoFlowForge is an artistic mesh foundation model that generates production-ready 3D meshes by decomposing generation into coarse-to-fine vertex generation and a separate connectivity (edge) prediction stage, formulated with cascaded flow matching. It targets lightweight, editable, topologically clean outputs for design, 3D printing, and gaming.

entry.title: FLASH: A "Generate Once, Synthesize Many" Framework for Synthetic Anomaly Generation in Industrial Anomaly Detection

author.name: Abhay Kumar Das, Rajesh Gangireddy, Ashwin Vaidya, Samet Akcay

entry.summary: FLASH decouples defect generation from anomaly synthesis for industrial inspection: a VLM-guided image generation model produces a small bank of reusable, validated defect patches from normal images, which are then recombined cheaply via Object Boundary Suppression. This bridges fast procedural methods and costly per-sample generative approaches.

entry.title: MotionMaestro: Masked Tokenization for Unified Motion Generation

author.name: Yun Chen, Munchurl Kim, Jeonghyeok Do

entry.summary: MotionMaestro unifies human motion generation tasks (text-to-motion, pose-conditioned generation, trajectory control) under a single masked-tokenization framework, observing that different conditioning types correspond to different masking strategies over motion sequences. This provides a common representation that simplifies otherwise fragmented motion generation systems.

entry.title: CHOQOLATE: Organizing Concept Bottleneck Latent Spaces with Choquet Integrals

author.name: R\'emi Kazmierczak, Johanne Cohen, Marianne Clausel

entry.summary: CHOQOLATE is an interpretable-by-design layer for concept bottleneck models built on CLIP, using 2-additive Choquet integrals to merge correlated concepts into compact, semantically coherent nodes with sparse weights. A closed-form gradient derivation explains why Choquet layers organize concept spaces without explicit supervision, and Choquet weights map directly to Shapley values.

entry.title: ReCAP: Retrieval-Guided Capability Reuse for Multimodal Continual Instruction Tuning

author.name: Tao Hu, Zhinuo Zhou, Xialiang Tong, De-Chuan Zhan, Da-Wei Zhou

entry.summary: ReCAP enables multimodal large language models in continual instruction tuning to reuse external knowledge by retrieving reusable domain concepts and reasoning patterns rather than only constraining parameter updates. The approach composes retrieved capabilities to solve diverse sequential multimodal instructions while mitigating forgetting.

entry.title: Losing the name before the box: measuring and repairing what narrow fine-tuning costs a detector outside its deployment vocabulary

author.name: Trung Minh Bui, Jongsul Moon, YoungOuk Kim, Jung-Hoon Hwang, Dongin Shin

entry.summary: The paper gives a longitudinal protocol tracking held-out top-K proposal coverage as a pretrained detector is fine-tuned on narrow domains, showing that open-world coverage of categories omitted by the fine-tuning vocabulary falls while in-domain accuracy rises, across four architectures and multiple datasets. It both measures and proposes repairs for this silent loss of open-world capability in safety-critical settings like obstacle detection. This exposes a real deployment risk in standard fine-tuning practice.

entry.title: RAEGNet: Relation-Aware Evidence Graph Network for Harm-Aware Multimodal Fake News Detection

author.name: Wenbin Shen, Guoxuan Qin, Guangxu Yao, Baodong Wang, Yuanbo Rui, Zhongjie Ba, Zhichao Lian

entry.summary: RAEGNet combines an event-level evidence retrieval framework (ELERF) with a relation-aware evidence graph network that models news-evidence stance relations and evidence-evidence interactions, reducing noise from entity-level retrieval. It also introduces harm-awareness, accounting for differing degrees of damage caused by different fake news instances. This targets both detection accuracy and practical prioritization of harmful misinformation.

entry.title: One from Infinity: Actualizing Futures from Pretrained World Models into Robot Actions

author.name: Bang Du, Yichen Xie, Shuqi Zhao, Yuxin Chen, Menglin Wu, Masayoshi Tomizuka

entry.summary: The paper argues that expensive video world model pretraining already encodes diverse plausible futures, so converting world models into robot policies should not require heavy fine-tuning. It formalizes task-conditioned selection and realization of one specific future as an actualization problem, learning a lightweight selection and action-readout mechanism on top of a frozen prior.

entry.title: OTRetarget: Joint Robot and Object Motion Retargeting via Optimal Transport

author.name: Guillaume Besset, Erwann Carn, Timoth\'ee Carecchio, Valentin Tordjman-Levavasseur, Fabian Schramm, Yann de Mont-Marin, Justin Carpentier, Ajay Suresha Sathya

entry.summary: OTRetarget jointly retargets human demonstrations to humanoid robots while adapting both robot and multi-object motions, representing interactions via signed distances and closest surface points and solving the correspondence with optimal transport. This avoids the common limitation of fixing object trajectories during retargeting. The joint formulation is significant for scaling humanoid loco-manipulation learning from human video/mocap data.

entry.title: BlenDAgger: Blended Shared Control for Interactive Imitation Learning

author.name: Cailyn Smith, Geoffrey Sun, Henny Admoni, Zackory Erickson

entry.summary: BlenDAgger blends the policy's and demonstrator's actions during interventions in interactive imitation learning, using shared control to reduce the teleoperation burden of human-gated correction schemes like DAgger. Across five manipulation tasks, it improves autonomous performance by 30 or more percentage points on two real-world tasks versus typical human-gated correction.

entry.title: A QCQP-Representable IMU Pre-Integration Factor for Certifiable State Estimation

author.name: Utkarsh Rai, Zhexin Xu, Bang-Shien Chen, David Rosen

entry.summary: The authors derive a QCQP-representable form of IMU pre-integration, enabling certifiable (globally optimal, verifiable) state estimation with inertial measurements for the first time. The key challenges are obtaining a polynomial algebraic structure despite the exponential map in standard pre-integration and achieving a tight semidefinite relaxation with auxiliary lifting variables. This broadens certifiable estimation from vision-only settings to the inertial modality central to most robotic systems.

entry.title: Learning from the Gap Between Pass@K and Pass@1

author.name: Xuan Liu, Jingbin Qian, Haosheng Chen

entry.summary: GapFT is a post-training recipe for RLVR-trained LLMs that distinguishes problems solved on the first decode from those only recovered within K samples, using the pass@K minus pass@1 gap to allocate training examples under a fixed budget. This avoids wasting budget on behavior the deployed single-sample policy already exhibits, and aims to absorb search-exposed behavior into the model itself. It speaks directly to efficient use of verifiable rewards in single-sample decoding regimes.

entry.title: Finite-Sample Theory for Fitted Q-Iteration When Actions Are Functions

author.name: Gefei Lin, Rui Miao, Xiaoke Zhang

entry.summary: Develops finite-sample guarantees for fitted Q-iteration in discounted infinite-horizon offline RL where actions are entire functions, such as radiation therapy fluence maps or robot trajectories. The work tackles coverage without Lebesgue densities on functional action spaces, relaxes conventional coverage requirements, and handles greedy optimization over function spaces.

entry.title: The Price of Token Boundaries: Compression Certificates and Prediction

author.name: Yuhao Du, Shunian Chen

entry.summary: The paper quantifies the compression cost imposed by pre-tokenization boundary rules, providing lower and upper bounds on optimal token counts with and without regular-expression constraints. On English Wikipedia, boundaries increase optimal token count by roughly 28-37%, and BPE sits measurably above the unrestricted bound.

entry.title: MERID: Multimodal Exploration via Recursive Self-Improvement Agents for Major Depression Analysis

author.name: Lei Liu, Zhaokang Liang, Qingcheng Zeng, Chenda Duan, Lu Mi, Zhen Tan, Tianyu Liu

entry.summary: MERID uses recursive self-improvement agents to autonomously build and revise multimodal prediction pipelines for detecting major depressive disorder from interview recordings and sensor data. The key contribution is the ability to revise pipelines from experimental feedback and carry verified improvements forward across design iterations. This matters for both clinical ML and the broader goal of autonomous experiment-driven agent improvement.

entry.title: PILLAR: Private Inverted-Index Lexical Lookup for Augmented Retrieval

author.name: Truong Son Nguyen (Arizona State University), Daniel Blackley (George Mason University), Ni Trieu (Arizona State University), Evgenios M. Kornaropoulos (George Mason University)

entry.summary: PILLAR is a privacy-preserving RAG system where a client retrieves the k most similar documents from a server-held corpus without revealing the query or its access pattern, using private information retrieval. It combines a sparse stage with a fixed number of PIR queries plus dense retrieval, avoiding the high latency and quality costs of prior dense-only PPRAG constructions. This matters for enabling RAG over sensitive corpora with strong query privacy guarantees.

entry.title: Semantic Projection for Continual Self-Evolution of Language Agents

author.name: Ziyu Liu, Jun Chen, Lixu Wang

entry.summary: SSPE transfers the functional principle of Orthogonal Gradient Descent from continual learning to natural-language skill libraries, projecting new skill revisions onto a semantic subspace that preserves procedures needed by earlier tasks. This prevents improvements for new tasks from overwriting shared natural-language skills when agents evolve on non-stationary task streams. It extends gradient-projection ideas to settings with no gradients or canonical vector space.

entry.title: Distinguish or Homogenize: Last-Chance Policy Identification and Risk-Budgeted Recovery under Irreversible Resource Depletion

author.name: Yibo Guo, Xiaodan Wang

entry.summary: This paper formalizes Last-Chance Policy Identification (LCPI), a planning framework for scenarios with irreversible resource depletion where an agent must choose between spending resources to diagnose latent fault models or homogenizing the system state so all remaining hypotheses admit a common safe continuation. It reframes correctness as being evaluated at the state the agent actually reaches, rather than at the initial state.

entry.title: ImbalancE: Inference-Time Latent Search Against Degree Imbalance in Link Prediction

author.name: Alberto Bernardi, Luca Costabello, Christophe Gueret

entry.summary: This paper shows that poor knowledge-graph-embedding link prediction quality correlates with degree imbalance in test triples: predicting low-degree target entities anchored to high-degree entities is especially problematic, which matters for recommender-system corner cases. The authors propose an inference-time latent search method to mitigate this bias without retraining. The diagnosis reframes prior loose attributions to relation type or degree bias.

entry.title: Seek Before You Move: Evidence Seeking for Progress Grounding in Vision-Language Navigation

author.name: Zhimin Wang, Meiyuan Zhu, Duo Wu, Linjia Kang, Yajun Wang, Yuan Ni, Xiaohang Wang, Tianlu Pan, Jingyan Jiang, Yaowei Wang, Zhi Wang

entry.summary: Identifies Progress Myopia in VLM-based navigation agents, which act confidently on insufficient evidence when task-relevant landmarks are outside view, and proposes SeekVLN, which couples semantic progress reasoning with active acquisition of missing evidence. This addresses a concrete safety-relevant failure mode in embodied navigation.

entry.title: Direct Experience World-Model Optimization: Learning the World Beyond Action Imitation

author.name: Xiangcheng Zhan, Zirui Chen, Yicheng Zhao, Ziteng Gao, Shuo Yang

entry.summary: This paper proposes DEWO, a post-deployment learning paradigm for World-Action Models (WAMs) that refines world representations using real visual experience in addition to action imitation. It focuses on dexterous manipulation, where small execution errors compound in high-dimensional action spaces and push interactions outside the world model's training distribution. The method identifies interaction turning points to better condition action generation on updated world predictions, addressing a key limitation of current post-deployment improvement approaches.

entry.title: XU-RS: Explaining Credal Width in Random-Set Language Models

author.name: David Achara, Maryam Sultana, Alexander D. Rast, Fabio Cuzzolin

entry.summary: XU-RS attributes the credal width (epistemic uncertainty, the gap between lower and upper probabilities) of answers in random-set language-model classifiers to input tokens, addressing the question of which input features drive a model's uncertainty. This extends explainability beyond point-estimate uncertainty to imprecise-probability models.

entry.title: WISE-ATTA: When to Ask for Labels in Budgeted Active Test-Time Adaptation

author.name: Muhammad Huzaifa, Lea Sch\"onherr, Thorsten Eisenhofer

entry.summary: The paper introduces budgeted active test-time adaptation, where labels can be requested for only a fraction of test batches, shifting the challenge to deciding when to query supervision over a long stream. WISE-ATTA allocates a labeling budget over time, improving robustness under distribution shift at lower annotation cost than per-batch ATTA methods.

entry.title: DIET: Deletion-response Expert Trimming for Video Diffusion Transformers

author.name: Jiachang Zhang, Teng Hu, Bohao Feng, Songhang Shen, Wenqiang Wang, Hongqian Deng, Ran Yi

entry.summary: DIET is a training-free framework for pruning mixture-of-experts in video diffusion transformers based on deletion responses rather than static activation statistics. A single all-expert calibration pass caches outputs and router states, so candidate deletions can be replayed without extra forward passes, capturing layer-level re-routing effects after expert removal.

entry.title: Do LLM Agents Execute the Plans They Declare? From Planning-Mode Declaration to Pattern-Specific Execution

author.name: Subba Reddy Oota, Francisco Herrera, Jordi Cabot Sagrera, Marcos L\'opez de Prado, Shadab Khan

entry.summary: The paper identifies a Plan Declaration-Execution Gap in LLM agents, distinguishing plan-selection failures from plan-execution failures that final task success cannot separate. It proposes Planning-as-Routing, where an LLM declares one of four planning modes and a deterministic router dispatches to a pattern-specific executor. Experiments across four benchmarks and three LLMs characterize when declared plans are faithfully executed.

entry.title: When Should LLMs Trust Their Own Revisions? A Risk-Aware Study of Intrinsic Self-Correction

author.name: Tianzhu Zhang

entry.summary: This paper studies intrinsic self-correction in 29 open-weight LLMs across BoolQ, GSM8K, and Corr2Cause, tracking whether revisions fix errors or flip correct answers to wrong ones. It shows aggregate accuracy masks divergent revision behavior, such as large GSM8K gains for Llama-3.1-8B alongside a notable rate of correct-to-incorrect flips, and compares runtime policies for when a model should accept its own revisions.

entry.title: UNBIND: UNlearning By INference-time Directional Steering for Code LLMs

author.name: Zhengyang Shan, Jiayun Xin, Yanjun Lin, Xu Qian, Zhiang Liu, Minghui Xu, Yue Zhang, Qin Hu, Kun Li, Xiuzhen Cheng

entry.summary: This arXiv paper introduces UNBIND, a machine unlearning framework for code large language models that removes memorized code implementations without retraining. It disentangles two objectives - identifying hidden states corresponding to target code and suppressing their reproduction - using separate directional steering at inference time while keeping model weights frozen, addressing the tension between forgetting specific implementations and retaining general programming ability. This matters for copyright and security compliance as code LLMs are increasingly deployed in production.

entry.title: Normative Loss Landscape Navigation: A Trajectory-Based Approach to Mitigating Forgetting in Incremental Learning

author.name: Isabelle Aguilar, Zayn Andre Zainal, Luis Fernando Herbozo Contreras, Zhaojing Huang, Omid Kavehei

entry.summary: TMLN formalizes continual learning as an optimal control problem over a curved loss landscape, using a memory-efficient diagonal empirical Fisher information metric to navigate gradients along trajectories rather than applying rigid scalar penalties. The aim is to reduce catastrophic forgetting in sequential training on non-stationary data. It moves beyond myopic gradient preconditioning and Euclidean regularization.

entry.title: Intrinsic Associative Memory on Riemannian Manifolds: Curvature, Capacity, and Emergent Modes

author.name: Krishnakumar Balasubramanian, Zhaoyang Shi

entry.summary: This paper develops dense associative memory models on Riemannian manifolds by framing memory retrieval as kernel-density mode seeking with Epanechnikov kernels. It proves that curvature fundamentally shapes memory behavior: positive curvature can erase memories in high dimensions while negative curvature reinforces them, with explicit capacity scalings derived. This connects associative memory theory to differential geometry, potentially informing how geometric structure affects memory in neural systems.

entry.title: PADM\'E: Preference Alignment Data Synthesis for Meta-Evaluation of LM Agent Evaluators

author.name: Cheng Chang, Yining Mao, Peng Qi

entry.summary: This paper addresses the problem of validating LM-based evaluators that score agentic behaviors across multiple criteria, a task the authors call meta-evaluation. Because collecting human judgment data is costly and absolute scores are hard to align, the authors reformulate meta-evaluation as a preference judgment problem and introduce PADM'E, a data synthesis method that generates reliable criterion-based preference data for assessing whether LM evaluator decisions align with human preferences. This matters for the reliability of LLM-as-a-judge pipelines increasingly used to evaluate AI agents.

entry.title: CineSubBench: Evaluating LLMs on Long-Form Narrative and Cultural Understanding from Multilingual Movie Subtitles

author.name: Mir Tafseer Nayeem, Susmoy Chakraborty, Davood Rafiei
