A small context reservoir modulates the output weights of the main reservoir, analogous to hypernetworks in deep learning, while preserving the simple training procedure of standard reservoir computing. This matters because it addresses a well-known failure mode of reservoir models on heterogeneous, regime-switching data.

entry.title: Inspector: Conversational and Lightweight Analyzer of Analog Circuit Layouts Using LLM and CNNs

author.name: Abril Cano Castro, Giuseppe Chiari, Michele Piccoli, Federico Viola, Davide Zoni

entry.summary: Inspector combines fine-tuned LLMs and CNNs to analyze GDSII layout files of analog integrated circuits, enabling a conversational interface between designers and CAD tooling. It targets the shift from manual/algorithmic analog design flows to AI-assisted paradigms.

entry.title: Large Language Models for Automated Cross-Domain Machine Learning Task Type Identification: A Benchmark Dataset and Evaluation

author.name: Petros Tsialis, Steffen Limmer, Tobias Rodemann, Martin Heckmann

entry.summary: Investigates whether LLMs can infer data domain and downstream prediction task from dataset-level information in AutoML pipelines, releasing an annotated benchmark of 625 public tabular and time-series datasets. Evaluates against AutoML heuristics, in cross-domain settings, and with smaller local models for deployment.

entry.title: One Proposal for Every Margin: Zero-Shot Amortized Sequential Importance Sampling for Binary Matrices

author.name: Ruishuo Chen, Weijia Li, Xun Wang, Yu Chen, Leheng Cai, Longbo Huang

entry.summary: For counting and uniform sampling of binary matrices with fixed row and column margins, the authors characterize the ideal SIS proposal and train an amortized neural proposal that approximates it zero-shot for new margins. This yields efficient, low-variance estimation across ecology, psychometrics, and network analysis applications.

entry.title: DR-net-Mamba: Selective State-Space Modeling for Long-Range ECG Time-Series Denoising

author.name: Basile Morel, Samuel Ruiperez-Campillo, Andreas P. Streich, Julia E. Vogt, Thomas Hofmann

entry.summary: The authors propose a Mamba-augmented denoising model that inserts selective state-space blocks into a convolutional bottleneck for ECG recordings, combining local feature extraction with linear-complexity long-range temporal modeling. They evaluate reconstruction fidelity, noise robustness, scaling to long recordings, and downstream diagnostic performance.

entry.title: Bidirectional Neural Networks for Global Nucleon-Nucleus Optical Model Calculations

author.name: Jin Lei

entry.summary: This work introduces a differentiable neural emulator based on Bidirectional Liquid Neural Networks mapping optical potential parameters to scattering wave functions in nuclear physics. A phase-space coordinate normalization allows one network to generalize across projectile energies from 1 to 200 MeV. The differentiability enables gradient-based uncertainty quantification and parameter optimization for nuclear data evaluation.

entry.title: Evasion Attacks on Cost-Utility-Based Adversarial Training for Online AutoML in IoT Networks

author.name: Chukwunonso Henry Nwokoye, Wajiha Zaheer, Khalil El-Khatib, Li Yang

entry.summary: The study evaluates black-box evasion attacks against a cost-utility adversarial training defense in an Online AutoML setting for IoT security, applying attacks to streaming learners including Hoeffding Trees, Leveraging Bagging, Streaming Random Patches, and Hoeffding Adaptive Trees. It assesses whether adversarial training holds up in resource-constrained online learning regimes.

entry.title: All On-Board: Fully On-Chip Neuromorphic Q-Learning with Embedded CartPole Simulation

author.name: Steven C. Nesbit, Giovanni T. Michel, Gerd J. Kunde, Edward Kim, Andrew T. Sornborger

entry.summary: The authors implement a fully on-chip closed-loop RL system on Loihi 2, embedding both a Q-learning algorithm and an on-chip simulation of CartPole in neuromorphic hardware. This demonstrates low-power neuromorphic training and control suited to resource-constrained environments, targeting energy sustainability concerns of growing AI systems.

entry.title: De-biasing Skeleton-based Action Recognition with Convex Hull Adaptive Shift

author.name: Mengyuan Liu, Yuhang Wen, Yi Zhang, Songtao Wu, Hong Liu, Junsong Yuan, Beichen Ding

entry.summary: The paper identifies entity bias in skeleton-based action and interaction recognition, caused by the initial configuration of the world coordinate system where origin choice skews representations, violating the i.i.d. assumption behind weight-shared entity encoders. It proposes Convex Hull Adaptive Shift, a preprocessing approach to remove this bias before fusion. This improves recognition across bodies, hands, objects, and robots in skeleton sequences.

entry.title: Flat-Consensus Diffusion for Robust Data Reshaping under Noisy Evaluator

author.name: Hongyu Cao, Kunpeng Liu, Fei Xie, Sandip Ray

entry.summary: The paper casts feature-centric data reshaping as reward-guided diffusion generation and proposes flat-consensus sampling that searches for robust regions of the latent reward landscape rather than isolated high-reward transformations, mitigating dual instability from noisy evaluators and stochastic trajectories.

entry.title: CollisionGAT: Controller-Agnostic One-Step Collision Screening for Multi-Agent Motion

author.name: Alan Debbas, Edwin Meriaux, Gregory Dudek

entry.summary: Presents a graph-attention network that scores collision risk per agent from current and proposed multi-agent states plus nearby obstacles, usable as a modular safety screen by any controller or planner. Exact geometric checks provide training labels and audit executed steps, demonstrated on path-following control and an obstacle-blind D* Lite planner.

entry.title: Notes on Generative Modeling for Feedback Control and Planning

author.name: Karthik Elamvazhuthi

entry.summary: These lecture-style notes frame control as dynamically constrained sampling on a system's state space and extend generative modeling tools — flow matching, normalizing flows, and diffusion — to control problems such as steering to target states or distributions and sampling from reachable sets. Controllability and optimal control concepts guide well-posedness of the algorithms. The notes are an accessible synthesis for control-theory and robotics readers.

entry.title: Mask-Induced Displacement in Audio XAI via Logit Trajectory Decomposition

author.name: Nico Garc\'ia-Peguinho (School of Electronic Engineering and Computer Science, Queen Mary University of London), David Kelly (Department of Informatics, King's College London), Fabrizio Smeraldi (School of Electronic Engineering and Computer Science, Queen Mary University of London), Anna Xamb\'o Sed\'o (School of Electronic Engineering and Computer Science, Queen Mary University of London)

entry.summary: The authors propose logit-space trajectory decomposition to audit perturbation-based audio XAI methods, separating on-axis output change along the occluded-to-retained line from off-axis displacement. Across three fills, three classifiers, and 1,100 AudioSet clips, they show no fill is acoustically neutral under full occlusion, questioning a core assumption of masking-based audio explanations.

entry.title: CLIMB-flow: Coupled Linear Inverse posterior sampling via Multiscale-Based flow

author.name: Zeqiu Yu, Ruizhi Yuan, Mathews Jacob

entry.summary: CLIMB-Flow is a posterior sampling algorithm for Bayesian imaging inverse problems customized to pyramidal/cascaded diffusion architectures, generating in pixel domain via coarse-to-fine hierarchy. It alternates end-point estimation, data-consistent updates, and flow-based steps, avoiding the spatial-detail loss of latent-diffusion autoencoder compression.

entry.title: Curating Merchant-Matching Training Data with Two Confidence-Gated Local LLM Judges

author.name: Donghao Huang, Jinling Pei, Zhaoxia Wang

entry.summary: This paper studies pseudo-label curation for merchant matching, where a key difficulty is distinguishing teacher abstention from genuine no-match evidence. The authors use agreement between two local LLM judges with separate ordered confidence thresholds for selections and abstentions, guaranteeing disjoint positive and negative label sets. Retrospective replay on 2,000 expert-annotated queries shows thresholding trade-offs between purity and coverage.

entry.title: AlphaPareto: Formulaic Alpha Discovery with LLM-Guided Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Yingbo Zhao, Zeyu Yang, Zhoufan Zhu

entry.summary: AlphaPareto formulates formulaic alpha discovery for quantitative trading as an RL problem, addressing pool-evolution non-stationarity by augmenting the state and using multi-objective optimization over properties of the alpha pool rather than only predictive power. LLM guidance is incorporated into the search process.

entry.title: Query Expansion and Key Specialization in Transformer Attention Geometry

author.name: Vidit Gupta, Siddhesh Nadkarni, Mihik Chaudhari, Vinaya Sawant, Prachi Tawde

entry.summary: This empirical study trains small GPT-like Transformers (3 depths, 3 query/key initializations, 4 seeds, 36 runs) on character-level WikiText-103 and tracks effective dimensionality of query and key projections via participation ratios. It finds that the mathematically symmetric query and key projections develop distinct geometric roles during training.

entry.title: Accelerator Choice Is Not Enough: AlphaFold2 Inference on Cloud TPUs

author.name: Lorenzo Pazienza, Ihab El Bani

entry.summary: This systems paper benchmarks AlphaFold2 inference across a Colab CPU runtime, an NVIDIA T4 GPU, and an eight-chip Cloud TPU v5e slice, showing large raw hardware advantages for TPUs but also that software-layer choices determine realized gains. The default path uses only one of eight TPU chips, and idle capacity erodes the cost advantage at list prices. It offers practical guidance for deploying JAX scientific workloads on cloud accelerators.

entry.title: GUIDE-FBO: Guidance via Uncertainty Intervention and Distributional Exchange for Federated Bayesian Optimization

author.name: Jintao Wei, Chenxi Li, Songhao Wang

entry.summary: GUIDE-FBO enables federated Bayesian optimization agents to exchange compact distributions over optima locations inferred from local Gaussian process posteriors instead of raw observations or surrogate parameters. A server merges and reweights these distributions, and agents construct a Federated Interventional GP preserving local posterior means while incorporating peer information. It targets knowledge transfer under communication constraints and task heterogeneity.

entry.title: Coordinated Lane-Level Variable Speed Limits and Ramp Metering for Successive Weaving Segments Considering Merging/Diverging Risks: A Hybrid Model Predictive Control and Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Approach

author.name: Guodong Ma, Baofeng Sun, Wenyu Yang, Zhihong Yao

entry.summary: The paper proposes a hybrid MPC and multi-agent reinforcement learning framework for coordinating lane-level variable speed limits and ramp metering across successive weaving segments on urban expressways. It introduces L-METANET, a lane-level macroscopic traffic model capturing forced lane changes, and combines XGBoost-SHAP with a random-parameters logit model to derive analytical collision-risk equations. The goal is balancing adaptive data-driven control with model-based resilience and transferability.

entry.title: Elicitation and Decision Geometry in Single-Index Bandits

author.name: Sakshi Arya, Cheng Soon Ong

entry.summary: The paper studies two-arm contextual bandits with arm-specific single indices and a shared unknown monotone link, introducing Natural Boundary Learning, a greedy procedure using a sequential Stein contrast to learn the optimal decision boundary directly without estimating rewards or the link. It characterizes local dynamics through a decision stability coefficient tied to the elicitation geometry of the underlying convex potential. This is a theoretical contribution to bandit decision-making.

entry.title: From Granular Revision Operations to Meaningful Revision Units: Evaluating LLMs for Revision Boundary Detection

author.name: Yu Tian, Andrew Potter, Katerina Christhilf, Motahareh Darvishpour Ahandani, Jessica Early, Steve Graham, Danielle S. McNamara

entry.summary: Evaluates whether LLMs can detect meaningful revision-unit boundaries in structured writing-revision data, using 113 undergraduate draft-revision pairs and 4,344 expert-annotated candidate boundaries. It compares zero- and few-shot GPT-5.5, base and fine-tuned Qwen3-32B, and baselines for learning-analytics purposes. The work improves how automated writing-process analytics are represented for education research.

entry.title: Reference-Grounded Data Curation for Instruction-Following Thai-English Machine Translation

author.name: Thodsaporn Chay-intr, Krittapad Harnchang, Mahannop, Thabua, Kobkrit Viriyayudhakorn, Thanaruk Theeramunkong

entry.summary: Proposes a two-phase data curation pipeline for instruction-following machine translation that extracts constraints directly from reference translations, guaranteeing feasibility by construction. Applied to Thai-English, it yields a 1.97M-instance dataset balancing rule compliance and translation quality.

entry.title: How Well Can LLMs Simulate Real Learner Evaluations of Educational Feedback?

author.name: Momoka Furuhashi, Kouta Nakayama, Takashi Kodama, Saku Sugawara, Kyosuke Takami

entry.summary: Evaluates how well six LLMs simulate real learner evaluations of biology feedback at group and individual levels, testing whether learner profiles and example evaluations improve simulation. Results show limited simulation ability, with profiles improving individual-level calibration but rarely group-level correspondence.

entry.title: Retrieving Biblical Intertextual References in Karen Blixen's Seven Gothic Tales

author.name: Andr\'as Kov\'acs, Alexander Conroy, Daniel Hershcovich, Jens Bjerring-Hansen

entry.summary: This paper builds a benchmark of 189 expert-annotated biblical references in Karen Blixen's tales and evaluates retrieval methods (TF-IDF, BM25, multilingual and Danish sentence encoders, plus fine-tuning with hard negatives) against all 31,170 verses of historically plausible Danish Bible translations. It tackles the computational literary scholarship problem of detecting allusion under paraphrase, historical language, and translation. The work is valuable as a careful humanities-facing NLP study with a novel benchmark.

entry.title: Attribution Gaps in Zero-Training LLM+OVOD Pipelines: A Fine-Grained Analysis of the CAAP--SNAP Discrepancy

author.name: Yu-Feng Yen

entry.summary: This paper analyzes why class-agnostic localization accuracy (CAAP) and semantic naming accuracy (SNAP) diverge in zero-training LLM plus open-vocabulary-detector pipelines, evaluating the full 5,000-image COCO-Val split with 27,273 detections. It finds vocabulary novelty, not visual complexity, drives the gap: localization accuracy falls from 80.9% to 31.6% when the LLM's wording falls outside the detector's native category set. This diagnostic insight can guide fixes for modular vision-language pipelines.

entry.title: Beyond Legibility: Benchmarking Visual Text Rendering and In-Place Editing in Unified Video Generation

author.name: Ziying Zhang, Litao Li, Junchao Liao, Tianyi Zeng, Siyu Zhu, Long Qin, Zhenghao Zhang

entry.summary: VidScribe is a diagnostic benchmark for visual text in video generation, covering four regimes: text-to-video writing, reference-based text transfer, sustaining text under motion, and localized text editing. It provides 803 human-verified samples across a 12-axis evaluation design, going beyond static OCR-style metrics. It matters because text legibility is a common failure mode that existing benchmarks ignore.

entry.title: EGSD: Event-Grounded Self-Distillation for Streaming Video Understanding

author.name: Yuwei Miao, Xuesheng Zhang, Wenhao Zou, Jixia Zhang, Jianwei Lv, Bo Yuan, Junfeng Wang, Shiao Xie

entry.summary: EGSD adapts on-policy self-distillation to streaming video understanding, fixing a preference misalignment where the teacher scores memory written before the question arrived using question-and-answer privilege, and preventing collapse of effective-entity memory. This supplies dense token-level training signals for real-time video models with incrementally maintained memory. It targets training methodology for a growing real-time video understanding niche.

entry.title: GlassFormer: Learning Real-time Glass Segmentation using Radar-Depth Fusion

author.name: Suhani Grover, Astik Srivastava, Viswas Dinesh, Avinash Sharma, K. Madhava Krishna

entry.summary: GlassFormer tackles the persistent failure of robotic perception on transparent surfaces by fusing radar with depth sensing for real-time glass segmentation. Optical sensors see through or fail on glass, so RGB-only approaches break down in low light, and the multimodal fusion approach targets safe navigation around glass walls, doors, and mirrors. It matters for reliable robot operation in built environments.

entry.title: Structured Visual Target Learning For Cross-Subject eeg-to-image retrieval

author.name: Salini Yadav, Taveena Lotey, Micka\"el Coustaty, Pravendra Singh, Partha Pratim Roy

entry.summary: This work addresses cross-subject EEG-to-image retrieval from the visual-target side, preserving spatial structure of a Perception Encoder, converting patch grids into learned visual views aggregated by a content-dependent router, and training with contrastive learning plus MMD regularization across subjects. A training-free refinement aligns frozen embeddings for unseen-subject deployment. It advances brain-signal-to-vision alignment generalization.

entry.title: RBF-GNN: Rational Basis Functions for Pseudo-Coordinate based Graph Convolutions

author.name: Pawe{\l} Batorski, Abtin Pourhadi, Paul Swoboda

entry.summary: RBF-GNN replaces SplineCNN's B-spline kernels with rational Pade basis functions for pseudo-coordinate based graph convolutions over Euclidean, spherical, or angular coordinates. The authors add spline-subspace initialization and variance-preserving rescaling, showing improved results including semantic keypoint matching.

entry.title: Task-Oriented Visual Feature Compression via Residual Vector Quantization for Device-Edge Multimodal Inference

author.name: Luning Pang, Cheng Yuan, Jiawei Shao, Mingtao Huang, Yuan Shen

entry.summary: Q-TOFC uses query-guided residual vector quantization to compress visual features for device-edge multimodal inference, encoding merged features as compact quantized sequences to reduce uplink bandwidth. This preserves task-relevant local evidence that query-agnostic aggregation would discard.

entry.title: ByteTraX: Enhancing the ByteTrack Architecture with Optimised Thresholding

author.name: Thomas A. O'Shea-Wheller

entry.summary: This paper proposes ByteTraX, an enhancement of the widely used ByteTrack multi-object tracking algorithm that uses a single unified matching threshold and stricter track initiation criteria to reduce identity switches and erroneous track reclassification. It is a simple, computationally lightweight modification targeting a well-known weakness in confidence-based association priority.

entry.title: Cropland PAtteRNS: Parallel Dimensional Attention Networks and Attention to Dataset Disparity for Crop Segmentation in Satellite Imagery Time Series Data

author.name: Joseph Metcalfe, Sara Sharifzadeh, Fabio Caraffini

entry.summary: Cropland PAtteRNS is a hybrid transformer-convolutional model applying self-attention separately along temporal, spectral, and spatial axes of Sentinel-2 multispectral time series for cropland segmentation, using a parallel factorized attention architecture. The paper also critiques dataset disparity trends in the field. It is a domain-specific application contribution in remote sensing.

entry.title: Degeneracy-Orthogonal Geometric Constraints for LiDAR SLAM

author.name: Minseo Kim, Yina Kim, Jinhwa Hwang, Alex Junho Lee

entry.summary: DeCOD introduces a structure-aligned geometric descriptor for cross-sectional landmarks (pipe joints, structural rings) that provides metric constraints along the degenerate axis in feature-poor corridors like tunnels and pipelines, where LiDAR odometry otherwise drifts. The descriptor distinguishes individual landmarks to anchor the unconstrained travel direction. This addresses a well-known structural failure mode of SLAM in axially uniform environments.

entry.title: Towards Spatial Perception for Heterogeneous Robot Collaboration in Subterranean Mining Environments

author.name: Mario Alberto Valdes Saucedo, Akash Patel, Christoforos Kanellakis, George Nikolakopoulos

entry.summary: The paper presents an onboard perception pipeline for the PERSEPHONE autonomous mining mission, pairing a lightweight Explorer robot that builds 3D scene graphs of a mine using zero-shot vision-language segmentation with an Inspector robot that characterizes ore bodies. It demonstrates heterogeneous multi-agent collaboration for exploration of abandoned underground mines.

entry.title: Ornstein-Uhlenbeck Is Hard to Beat, Yet Superlinear Drift Ships Lower Transport Costs

author.name: Attila Lovas, L\'or\'ant Nagy

entry.summary: Responding to a recent theory result that Ornstein-Uhlenbeck diffusion is hard to beat for forward convergence, this paper empirically tests superlinear Langevin diffusions for score-based image generation with scores computed from the Fokker-Planck equation. Superlinear drifts beat the OU baseline on empirical Wasserstein distance across nearly the whole test grid with lower variation across horizons. The result shows the theoretical hardness verdict is not universal in practice.

entry.title: Interpretable intrinsic dimension estimation through componentwise calibration of distance and angle

author.name: Chih-Hsuan Huang, Chih-Wei Chen, Szu-Chi Chung

entry.summary: Reformulates the DANCo intrinsic dimension estimator componentwise, keeping separate distance and angular discrepancy curves so the source of an estimate can be diagnosed. It derives closed-form KL divergences for the Gride distance component and shows DANCo reduces to Gride under matched angular parameters, improving robustness to noisy neighborhoods and amplitude heterogeneity.

entry.title: Superintelligence ban, but then what?

author.name: Milly Medén

entry.summary: The post analyzes what a global superintelligence ban would actually entail, arguing that enforcement would require restricting inference of existing frontier models, not just new training runs, and that a comprehensive ban creates an unstable equilibrium with pressure to reopen development. It proposes verifiable, carefully selected use cases as a mechanism for safely relaxing a ban. It cites concrete policy developments including proposed US and UK superintelligence ban legislation and recent UN and EU statements.

entry.title: The Case Against Slowing Down AI

author.name: CAC

entry.summary: A lengthy steelman of AI accelerationism, drafted by an author who favors slowing frontier AI, engaging seriously with arguments from Ege Erdil and Matthew Barnett about why AI development should not be slowed. The exercise of steelmanning made the author more confident in slowing down while slightly lengthening their timelines. It serves partly as a demonstration that AI safety advocates have stress-tested their own views.

entry.title: Optimal Networks for Agentic Information Aggregation

author.name: MohammadHossein Bateni, Zahra Hadizadeh, MohammadTaghi Hajiaghayi, Mahdi JafariRaviz, Shayan Taherijam

entry.summary: The paper extends the Kearns-Roth-Ryu networked learning model, where agents on a DAG learn linear predictors from features and parents' predictions, studying which network topologies optimally aggregate information toward the global predictor. It builds on the prior result that sufficiently deep paths with feature coverage drive output error to the global optimum.

entry.title: Interpretable Physics Informed WiFi Indoor Localization: Learning an Effective Access Point Geometry and Using It to Prune

author.name: Arshia Eftekhari zadeh, Rezvan Nasiri, Hadi Moradi

entry.summary: The paper proposes a hierarchical deep learning framework for WiFi fingerprint-based indoor localization that jointly predicts user location and learns an effective geometry of surrounding access points via physics-informed decoders, without requiring true AP coordinates during training. The learned geometry is used to rank and prune APs, and on UJIIndoorLoc the chained model achieves 7.07 m mean 3D error, a 26-36% reduction over baselines. It improves both interpretability and accuracy in a widely deployed positioning technology.

entry.title: Graph-Based Learning for Multi-Horizon Martian Atmospheric Forecasting

author.name: Gary Myler, James Holmes, Manish Patel, Amel Bennaceur

entry.summary: MaGMA is a graph-based data engineering framework that transforms OpenMARS Mars reanalysis fields into structured learning objects for multi-horizon Martian atmospheric forecasting, linking atmospheric patches through spatial, temporal, and dynamical-similarity edges. It integrates atmospheric history and engineered physical descriptors to handle Mars's dust-driven, multi-scale atmospheric behavior. Martian forecasting supports future exploration missions.

entry.title: Multi-Granularity Language-Guided Imitation Learning via Instruction Decomposition

author.name: Yi-Pei Chiu, Wei-Ta Chu

entry.summary: This work improves language-guided robot imitation learning by decomposing an overall task description into fine-grained subtask-level instructions, so different execution stages receive distinct language guidance. This addresses the ambiguity when a single description must cover multi-stage manipulation trajectories.

entry.title: ProAct-VLM: Pre-Failure Vision-Language Task Replanning with Continuous Perception Feedback

author.name: Ahmed Nader Ahmed, Omar Moured, Mughni Irfan Mohammed Abdul, Muhayy Ud Din, Irfan Hussain

entry.summary: ProAct-VLM embeds VLM-based task planning into a closed loop with continuous perception feedback, enabling robots to detect environmental changes as they occur and replan before failures happen in long-horizon tasks. The framework aims to overcome the brittleness of rule-based pipelines in open-world conditions by leveraging VLM world knowledge.

entry.title: More Features Are Not More Evidence: Limits of Training-Free Human Activity Recognition with Jev

author.name: Orhan Konak

entry.summary: This study evaluates Jev, a fixed general-purpose probabilistic decision model, for training-free human activity recognition on 1,800 accelerometer windows across three standard datasets. Comparing 5,400 decisions against generative and supervised baselines, it finds richer feature representations do not translate into better zero-shot sensor decisions.

entry.title: Information Bottleneck-Guided Adaptive Hypergraph Transformer for Brain Disease Diagnosis

author.name: Jingxi Feng, Xudong Chen, Yifan Zhang, Heming Xu, Hongcheng Han, Xijing Wang, Dong Zhang, Shaoyi Du

entry.summary: Proposes IBAHGT, a hypergraph transformer with information bottleneck guidance that adaptively learns high-order correlations and short/long-range dependencies in brain networks while suppressing redundancy. Applied to brain disease diagnosis, it offers a unified framework relevant to clinical neuroscience.

entry.title: BrainNet Studio: A Unified Toolkit for Brain Network Construction, Intelligent Analysis, and Visualization

author.name: Xiwei Zeng, Shengrong Li, Yiheng Liu, Chunwei Tian, Daoqiang Zhang, Qi Zhu

entry.summary: Presents BrainNet Studio, an integrated toolkit for static and dynamic brain network analysis covering network construction, feature extraction, predictive modeling, biomarker identification, visualization, and interpretation. It aims to fill the gap left by tools focused on static connectomes without modern graph and sequence learning integration.

entry.title: TRACE: Deployable Tree-Relational Structure Enhancement for Oncology LLMs

author.name: Jizheng Lai, Yingyun Li, Ying Qin, Haiyang Qian

entry.summary: TRACE enhances oncology LLMs by separating offline structure learning of medical concepts and relations from lightweight online retrieval of compact prompt evidence at inference time. The tree-relational structure is refined using LM-loss-derived evidence and supports task-adaptive, label-free evidence selection, improving results across ten oncology classification tasks and a medical QA benchmark.

entry.title: VISTA-Bench: Benchmarking Multilingual Image Translation with Image-Specific Rubrics

author.name: Bo Lv, Mao Zheng, Zheng Li, Fangxu Liu, Mingrui Sun, Tao Chen

entry.summary: VISTA-Bench evaluates multimodal image translation across 22 languages and 10 domains using image-specific rubric evaluation, with model-assisted but human-verified annotations grouping text into coherent semantic units. It addresses limited language coverage and missing image-specific criteria in prior benchmarks. This supports systematic assessment of a core multimodal capability for multilingual applications.

entry.title: No Scale Left Behind: Multi-Scale Autoencoder with Bi-directional Attention for Time Series Anomaly Detection

author.name: Jiaheng Guo, Haochen Zhang, Yu-Chao Huang, Jinhao Duan, Nicholas Konz, Tianlong Chen

entry.summary: MSCAD is a semi-supervised time series anomaly detection framework using parallel autoencoder branches with cross-scale bidirectional attention, designed to capture anomalies spanning from sub-second spikes to multi-hour drift patterns that single-granularity methods miss. It matters because time series anomaly detection underpins monitoring in healthcare, finance, and industry, where multi-scale interactions are commonly mishandled.

entry.title: From Phase Transition to Systemic Failure: A Decoupled Analytics Framework for GNN Robustness

author.name: Shuai Yan, Dan Peng, Jie Li, Ke Wang

entry.summary: This paper constructs a synthetic homophilic graph regression benchmark that independently manipulates label noise and feature distribution shift, running 410 evaluations of representative GNNs. It identifies distinct failure patterns, including relative robustness under additive label corruption versus abrupt systemic failure under shift, framing GNN robustness through a phase-transition lens.

entry.title: 3-D Emissions Mapping and Social Cost Estimation for US Domestic Aviation at West Coast Hubs

author.name: Hesam Shafiei Nia, Don MacKenzie

entry.summary: This work reconstructs 3-D flight trajectories at US west coast hubs from ADS-B records using a physics-informed autoencoder (CNN, Bi-GRU, 3-D CNN encoder with a TCN decoder), then maps emissions via BADA and ICAO tables to estimate regional environmental and near-airport health impacts. It addresses the gap that existing aviation emissions inventories lack trajectory-level resolution. Useful for policy analysis on aviation social costs.

entry.title: FARE: Deep Reinforcement Learning For Fair Exposure Constrained Uncertainty Aware Financial Content Personalization

author.name: Arundeep Chinta, Lucas Vinh Tran, Jay Katukuri

entry.summary: FARE frames Share-of-Voice-constrained content ranking in financial services as a deep RL problem analogous to constrained trade execution, ensuring fair exposure across offerings and preventing rich-get-richer dynamics. It combines SOV constraints with uncertainty awareness for personalization. The novelty lies in transplanting algorithmic-finance constrained execution machinery into recommender ranking.

entry.title: HyperLabel: Multi-Label Classification via Hypergraph-Based Label Correlation Modeling

author.name: Peiyu Zhang (University of Southern California), Heng Ping (University of Southern California), Nikos Kanakaris (Amazon Web Services), Yucheng Zhao (University of Tennessee, Knoxville), Shixuan Li (University of Southern California), Wei Yang (University of Southern California), Xiongye Xiao (University of Tennessee, Knoxville), Paul Bogdan (University of Southern California)

entry.summary: HyperLabel is an encoder-decoder framework for multi-label classification that explicitly models label dependencies via hypergraph neural networks, constructing a label hypergraph whose sample-defined hyperedges encode multi-way co-occurrence patterns. This provides explicit structural priors beyond the pairwise attention or contrastive approaches used in prior MLC methods.

entry.title: FUND: Density Flow for Sampling Unnormalised Distributions

author.name: Vikas Kanaujia, Vipul Arora

entry.summary: FUND learns Boltzmann distributions without true samples, targeting limitations of MCMC such as critical slowing down and poor mode mixing, and of Boltzmann Generators such as costly training. Departing from sample-trajectory matching in flow matching, it matches distribution trajectories, iteratively reshaping the target using model-geometric information.

entry.title: Compositional Objectives: Learning Structure in Structure

author.name: Pranavchandra Vivekananda, Sumukh Bettadapura, Ajan Subramanian

entry.summary: Building on the notion of epiplexity, a measure of learnable structure in data via a bounded observer, the paper develops a closed-form spectral approximation and shows that a fixed-trace constraint leads the objective to prefer uniform spectral mass. The authors then extend toward compositional objectives so learned structures can be composed for goal-directed action. This ties into open-endedness and intelligence-as-novelty-pursuit research programs.

entry.title: Logic Gate Networks and Lookup Table Networks as Lightweight Hardware Classifiers for Inter-patient ECG Arrhythmia Classification

author.name: Wout Mommen, Lars Keuninckx, Siddharth Patil, Paul Detterer, Achiel Colpaert, Piet Wambacq

entry.summary: The authors generalize differentiable logic gate networks to N-input lookup table networks using a multiplexer-based Boolean formulation, applying them to low-power ECG arrhythmia classification on MIT-BIH. They achieve up to 94.41% accuracy with a kappa of 0.683 in an inter-patient setting.

entry.title: TwinS-GCN: Spectral conjugate for Spectral Graph Convolutional Networks

author.name: Chun Hei Michael Chan, Flavia Petruso, Dimitri Van De Ville

entry.summary: This work addresses oversmoothing and long-range dependency limits in graph convolutional networks by extracting pure directionality via the skew-symmetric part of a directed shift operator. It introduces a spectral conjugate construction that preserves shift-invariance of filters, enabling attenuated long-distance information transport.

entry.title: CalibHyper: Chance-Corrected Relational Hypergraphs for Few-Shot Molecular Property Prediction

author.name: Linyu Li, Zhi Jin, Yuanpeng He, Dongming Jin, Huanyu Liu, Huanyao Zhang, Haoran Duan, Heng Tian, Gadeng Luosang, Nyima Tashi

entry.summary: CalibHyper improves few-shot molecular property prediction by replacing label-agreement supervision with chance-corrected relational hypergraphs built from joint label distributions, subtracting an independence baseline and shrinking residuals by observation count. A swap-equivariant relation head estimates these dependence-corrected relations to condition context-aware prediction.

entry.title: A Light Bilevel Refinement Aligns Self-Supervised Representations for Stronger Task-Specific Learning

author.name: Gustav Wagner Zakarias, Zheng-Hua Tan

entry.summary: The authors refine the BiSSL framework, which uses a bilevel optimization transition stage to align self-supervised representations with downstream objectives before fine-tuning, by replacing costly implicit hypergradient approximations with a lighter bilevel refinement. This makes alignment between pretraining and fine-tuning objectives cheaper and more scalable.

entry.title: Geometric Inductive Biases for Semi-Supervised Equalization: The Constellation-Aware Transformer

author.name: Avi Caciularu

entry.summary: This paper proposes the Constellation-Aware Transformer (CAT) for channel equalization in communications, injecting known constellation geometry as an inductive bias via custom TransFIRmer blocks with an early interaction paradigm. The goal is decoding over unknown channels with minimal pilot overhead, addressing agnostic estimation gaps in generic deep learning encoders. It targets next-generation communication systems where data is scarce.

entry.title: RICE-Alpha: Reliability-Informed Correction with Event Graphs for LLM-Agent Stock Forecasting

author.name: Tong Liu, Lanmiao Liu, Xiang Hu

entry.summary: RICE-Alpha is a point-in-time stock-scoring framework that separates a history-aware multi-view base scorer from a reliability-calibrated residual correction built on event graphs of temporally dependent corporate events. It targets preservation of issuer-specific chronology under point-in-time constraints in LLM-agent financial forecasting.

entry.title: Bounding Retraining Equivalence and the Deletion Floor in Materials Machine Unlearning

author.name: Can Polat, Mustafa Kurban, Erchin Serpedin, Hasan Kurban

entry.summary: This paper addresses ambiguity in evaluating machine unlearning for materials ML, defining a deletion floor as the expected target loss under retraining at the deleted request and deriving sharp intervals bounding an update's loss around this baseline. It provides theoretical bounds linking deletion floor to retained fit, prediction regularity, and local label agreement using ridge-regression identities.

entry.title: Learning Steadily: Accumulating Relative Point Margin Scores for Face Image Quality Assessment

author.name: Guray Ozgur, Tahar Chettaoui, Eduarda Caldeira, Marco Huber, Jan Niklas Kolf, Naser Damer, Fadi Boutros

entry.summary: CARPM-FIQA addresses temporal instability in face-recognition-integrated face image quality assessment, where single-epoch quality estimates fluctuate as the feature space evolves during training. It accumulates relative point margin measurements across the entire training trajectory rather than relying on single-epoch estimates, with theoretical justification for the cumulative averaging. This yields more reliable quality prediction for biometric systems.

entry.title: Period Segmentation in Transition Network Analysis: A Topological Data Analysis Approach

author.name: Hitoshi Inoue, Koichi Yasutake

entry.summary: The paper applies Zigzag Persistent Homology change points in connected components (beta_0) to segment courses into data-driven periods in Transition Network Analysis, using 22 Open University courses. The topological segmentation captures greater between-period variation than time-based segmentation (median variance ratio 4.10), helping identify intervention windows in learning analytics.

entry.title: Prediction Limits and Koopman Closure of Geometry-Induced Soft State Abstractions

author.name: Mohit Kumar, Somayeh Kargaran

entry.summary: The paper analyzes when simplex-valued soft state abstractions from class-specific Kernel Affine Hull Machine reconstruction scores admit accurate finite-dimensional linear (Koopman-style) dynamics, deriving a computable lower confidence bound on the minimum achievable prediction error. The bound is evaluable from independent state-successor pairs without fitting a prediction matrix.

entry.title: Sliced Orlicz-Wasserstein

author.name: Binh Thuan Tran, Khai Nguyen

entry.summary: Introduces the sliced Orlicz-Wasserstein distance, generalizing sliced Wasserstein by replacing the Lp norm with a Luxemburg norm induced by an Orlicz function. The paper proves metric and topological properties, derives sample complexity bounds, and shows the sliced Wasserstein case is recovered for phi(x)=x^p.

entry.title: Decentralized Optimization with Cross-Coupled Mixed Affine Constraints

author.name: Ewsey Obzherin, Ilya Khomchenko, Natalia Shelegeda, Nhat Trung Nguyen, Demyan Yarmoshik, Alexander Rogozin, Alexander Gasnikov

entry.summary: Studies decentralized optimization where local and shared variables interact through two affine channels, showing that the Friedrichs angle between channels governs intrinsic difficulty via a cross-coupling factor that preconditioning cannot remove. The authors develop an accelerated method with matching minimax guarantees and extend it to nonsmooth convex settings.

entry.title: A Visual Classification Dataset and Model Evaluation for Historical Manuscript Illustrations

author.name: Yoav Evron, Michal Bar-Asher Siegal, Michael Fire

entry.summary: The authors introduce a manually labeled dataset of 15,000 illustrations from centuries-old manuscripts spanning 22 categories, enabling large-scale exploration of digitized historical collections. They benchmark modern vision models on this challenging classification task characterized by stylistic diversity and degradation.

entry.title: Calibrated Derivative-Process Sensitivity for Gaussian-Process Variable Selection

author.name: Jia Cai

entry.summary: The paper develops a calibrated selection rule for the derivative sensitivity statistic in Gaussian-process regression, showing standard Wald and bootstrap cutoffs are anti-conservative at null inputs and proposing a studentized multiplier correction. This provides a principled alternative to inverse-lengthscale ARD rankings with explicit error control.

entry.title: The Price of Peeking: Anytime-Valid Leakage Detection on ML-KEM EM Traces

author.name: Georgios Feretzakis, Alexandros Papaspyridis

entry.summary: This paper applies anytime-valid testing by betting (SKIT-type swap-pair e-processes) to electromagnetic side-channel leakage detection on ML-KEM, giving uniform false-alarm control while inspectors monitor acquisition in real time. Empirically, first-crossing detection needs roughly 1.7-2.4 times the traces of fixed-horizon tests, quantifying the price of anytime validity.

entry.title: Non-Adaptive Learning of Sparse Erd\H{o}s--R\'enyi Graphs via Affine Splitting

author.name: Hoang Ta

entry.summary: The paper studies reconstructing sparse Erdos-Renyi graphs from non-adaptive edge-detecting queries, giving a scheme with O(k log n) queries and fast decoding, improving on worst-case quadratic lower bounds that hold for general graphs. It is a theoretical contribution in group testing on random graphs.

entry.title: High-Level Text Preprocessing for Semantic Similarity Analysis of Discursive Texts: A Framework and Empirical Demonstration

author.name: Mehmet Murat Albayrakoglu, Mehmet Nafiz Aydin

entry.summary: This paper identifies semantic diffusion: standard preprocessing fails on discursive documents because similarity scores are inflated by vocabulary acquired through critiquing and contextualizing other positions rather than substantive agreement. The authors propose high-level text preprocessing that accounts for a passage's discursive function, with an empirical demonstration on semantic textual similarity analysis. This is a useful conceptual critique with practical preprocessing implications.

entry.title: Word Similarity Datasets for Indian Languages: Annotation and Baseline Systems

author.name: Syed S. Akhtar, Arihant Gupta, Avijit Vajpayee, Arjit Srivastava, M. Shrivastava

entry.summary: This paper introduces manually annotated monolingual word similarity datasets for six major Indian languages (Urdu, Telugu, Marathi, Punjabi, Tamil, Gujarati) built via translation and re-annotation of English datasets, plus baseline scores for word representation models in three of the languages.

entry.title: Pre-registered tests of solid-state-physics-inspired LLM compression: a cluster-level negative result at small-language-model scale

author.name: Jun-qiang Lu

entry.summary: This paper reports a three-month autonomous research-agent program that pre-registered tests of five solid-state-physics-inspired compression mappings on pretrained LMs with predictions committed before data collection and a 3-sigma PASS/SHELVE gate; most hypotheses were falsified, with attention-versus-distance best fit by stretched exponentials in GPT-2-medium heads.

entry.title: SincDPNet: Interpretable Raw-Waveform Bathroom Activity Recognition for Assistive Living

author.name: Debolina Chowdhury, Suman Samui, Sujoy Saha

entry.summary: The paper presents a seven-class bathroom acoustic-event dataset of 21,387 annotated clips across five environments, plus SincDPNet, a compact raw-waveform classifier using a learnable sinc filter bank with inspectable frequency parameters for privacy-preserving assistive living. It addresses robustness to room changes and interpretable learned passbands in hertz. Acoustic monitoring offers an alternative to undesirable video surveillance in care settings.

entry.title: Simulation-Based Inference for Plate Reverb System Identification

author.name: Dylan Sechet, Marc Evrard, Matthieu Kowalski

entry.summary: The authors apply simulation-based inference to Task A of the first DAFx Parameter Estimation Challenge, retrieving physical parameters of a plate reverb model from impulse responses. A neural network amortizes parameter-density estimation using simulator-generated data, with per-observation fine-tuning rounds that resample and resimulate to specialize the posterior. This demonstrates SBI in an audio signal processing system identification setting.

entry.title: A literature-guided descriptor-based framework for filtering composition search spaces

author.name: Lei Zhang, Markus Stricker

entry.summary: This paper presents a literature-guided framework for materials discovery that selects descriptors from a vocabulary in a literature-trained word embedding model and uses them to construct Pareto-based filters reducing candidate composition search spaces. It demonstrates how latent knowledge in scientific corpora expressed through words and associations can be operationalized for practical materials problems. This matters for AI-driven scientific discovery.

entry.title: CHI: A Composite Hallucination Index Unifying Entity, Relation, and Quantity Dimensions for Summarization Evaluation

author.name: Praveenkumar Katwe, Rakesh Chandra Balabantaray, Kali Prasad Vittala

entry.summary: CHI is a unified hallucination metric for abstractive summarization that decomposes faithfulness errors into entity, relation, and quantity hallucination dimensions using a shared softmax-normalized architecture over Venn-derived factors. It aims to capture interactions between hallucination types that existing isolated metrics miss. This improves evaluation tooling for summarization faithfulness.

entry.title: MM-VeriRec: Failure-Guided Fusion for Verifiable Agentic Multimodal Recommendation

author.name: Yufeng Wang

entry.summary: MM-VeriRec is a verifiable multimodal recommendation protocol that handles hidden visual constraints, image-text mismatch, and abstention on impossible tasks, building tasks from real movie-poster and product-image datasets. Recommendations are verified with deterministic visual attributes, and failures are converted into actionable training labels. It highlights an important trust dimension of multimodal recommenders: knowing when visual evidence is decisive and when to refuse.

entry.title: Beyond Binary Preferences: Graded Preference Optimization for Limb-Motion Captioning

author.name: Yanan Wang, Tingsong Li, Kaixun Jiang, Chongyang Zhong, Chenwei Xoe, Zhaohe Liao

entry.summary: This paper targets a fine-grained failure of vision-language models: misidentifying which person performs an action or which limb is involved, especially across camera cuts. It introduces FlexBench (3,105 shots, 18,161 queries) with checklist-based graded scoring that distinguishes missing information from fabricated assertions, plus a graded preference optimization method. This advances more reliable physical-action understanding in video captioning.

entry.title: Causal-EVC: Breaking Emotional Spurious Causality via Spatiotemporal Grounding and Counterfactual Intervention

author.name: Cheng Ye, Weidong Chen, Peipei Song, Zhendong Mao

entry.summary: Causal-EVC targets emotional video captioning, using spatiotemporal grounding and counterfactual intervention to break spurious causal links such as mislabeling sadness as joy on a sunny beach, and introduces EVC-CauseGround, a benchmark that verifies genuine causal reasoning rather than background confounder exploitation. It exposes shortcut learning in emotion-aware captioning. This brings causal inference tools to multimodal emotion understanding.

entry.title: End-to-End Self-Supervised RGB-T Tracking without Modality Misleading

author.name: Shenglan Li, Rui Yao, Kunyang Sun, Hong Jia, Yong Zhou, Javen Qinfeng Shi, Xinyu Zhang

entry.summary: ESMTrack is a fully end-to-end self-supervised RGB-T tracking framework that avoids offline pseudo-labeling and dense bounding-box annotation, learning discriminative, temporally consistent representations from only initial-frame annotations. It aims to prevent modality misleading in fusing visible and thermal infrared inputs.

entry.title: Learning from synthetic photorealistic raindrop for single image raindrop removal

author.name: Zhixiang Hao, Shaodi You, Yu Li, Kunming Li, Feng Lu

entry.summary: The authors present the first physics-based photorealistic synthetic dataset of adherent raindrops, modeling water dynamics, geometry, and photometry, to train deep networks for single-image raindrop removal relevant to autonomous driving. The dataset addresses the lack of large, realistic training data for this degradation.

entry.title: Passive-Dynamic-Walking-Inspired Dynamics Guidance for Energy-Efficient Humanoid Locomotion

author.name: Hyeonjin Choi, Joongheon Kim, Daekyum Kim

entry.summary: The authors propose a reinforcement learning framework for energy-efficient humanoid locomotion inspired by passive dynamic walking, using a temporary tilted-gravity field during early training to bias learning toward mechanically economical gaits. All PDW-specific guidance is removed before nominal-dynamics optimization, and the approach requires no reference trajectories.

entry.title: Trajectory-Level Mode Guidance for Controllable Diffusion-Based Multi-Robot Motion Planning

author.name: Tianyou Yu, Shengze Cai, Chao Xu

entry.summary: The authors propose a guidance mechanism for diffusion-based multi-robot motion planning that incorporates coarse or partial trajectory priors without collapsing the multimodal solution distribution. Guidance operates in clean trajectory space with timestep-dependent strength, integrating priors at each reverse diffusion step while preserving diverse feasible coordination modes.

entry.title: NIDAR: NIR-Guided Intrinsic Decomposition for Scalable Scene-Agnostic LiDAR Intensity Reconstruction

author.name: Junjie Zhang, Jie Yin, Kefei Qian, Jie Li, Mengpei Jia, Yajuan Dun, Wenbo Chu, Guofa Li

entry.summary: NIDAR is a feed-forward framework that synthesizes dense LiDAR intensity-like observations from RGB appearance and simulator geometry, using pretrained pseudo-NIR translation, hierarchical intrinsic decomposition, and geometry-aware modulation without per-scene optimization or real intensity supervision. This lowers the cost of adding intensity cues to simulation pipelines for robotic perception and state estimation. Scalable intensity simulation supports better sim-to-real transfer for LiDAR-based systems.

entry.title: From Sky to Soil: A Morphing Aerial-Ground Robot for Seed Deployment

author.name: Namai Chandra, Lining Yao

entry.summary: This paper presents a tri-functional morphing robot combining aerial flight, wheeled ground locomotion, and controlled-depth seed embedding for reforestation, reusing propulsion motors for drilling via a clever mechanical coupling. After landing, the platform folds into a four-wheeled planter that drills, dispenses a seed, and repositions. It matters as a novel hardware design for scalable ecological restoration.

entry.title: Recompositional Robotics: Cross-Domain, Open-set, and Lifelong Modularity Beyond Morphology

author.name: Steven Swanbeck, Jonathan Salfity, Corrie Van Sice, Robert Blake Anderson, Mitch Pryor

entry.summary: This position/systems paper argues that modular robotics should target changeable robot capabilities rather than only changeable morphology, spanning kinodynamics, perception, compute, and coordinating behaviors. It proposes a reconfiguration framework across these domains supporting open-set and lifelong capability adaptation.

entry.title: Exact Regret Frontiers and Externality Scheduling in Centralized Serial-Dictatorship Bandits

author.name: Lishang Xu, Guodong Ma, Pengcheng Weng, Zixuan Xia

entry.summary: This paper characterizes the exact attainable set of logarithmic regret coefficients in centralized serial-dictatorship matching bandits, where learning one player-arm pair imposes regret externalities on others. Matching-level Graves-Lai constraints reduce to finitely many pairwise exploration quotas, and at top-choice-separated instances the exact frontier follows from a polynomial-size linear program. The work also shows the usual upper-closed Graves-Lai region can be strictly larger than the attainable set.

entry.title: Serverless gossip training of LSTM failure detectors: A matched-protocol comparison with federated, local and centralized learning on NASA C-MAPSS

author.name: Yusuf \"Ozt\"urk, Enes G\"oktekin, Bengisu Atl{\i}, Ak{\i}n \"Ozt\"urk, Zhixiang Wang, Ulas Bagci

entry.summary: This paper compares synchronous ring gossip learning against federated averaging, isolated local, and centralized training for stacked LSTM failure detectors on the NASA C-MAPSS turbofan benchmark under a fully matched protocol (shared implementation, architecture, split, and budget). It provides the first controlled measurement of gossip learning for recurrent failure-detection models, informing serverless options for predictive maintenance where sensor data cannot be pooled. The matched design isolates the effect of the learning topology.

entry.title: Alignment Is to a Virtual Governor: A Theory of Coordination in Diverse Intelligence

author.name: Samuel Knoche

entry.summary: Summarizing a paper by Lyons, Pio-Lopez, and Levin, the post argues that in decentralized systems alignment is necessarily to a virtual governor: an abstract entity embodied in coordinating relationships, such as bioelectric networks or the price system, that is causally instructive despite being non-physical. It connects biological morphogenesis to multi-agent AI alignment questions raised by the recent Hugging Face swarm behavior. The framing suggests alignment targets in multi-agent systems should be understood at the level of coordinating structure.

entry.title: Collecting Differential Data for Automated Safety Research

author.name: lachlan on a boat

entry.summary: A SPAR Fall 2026 project proposal to collect process artifacts from AI safety research — documents showing deliberation, idea modification, and direction choices — into a centralized repository for training models to be better safety researchers. The thesis is that such data can differentially improve safety-research capability without boosting general capabilities. The post solicits feedback and data-contributing organizations.

entry.title: Cross-Organizational SysML Model Integration: A Survey of Challenges and AI-Supported Tasks

author.name: Zirui Li, Torsten Brix, Stephan Husung

entry.summary: This survey reports a questionnaire study with 29 MBSE stakeholders on challenges in cross-organizational SysML model integration and expectations for LLM-assisted tasks. Respondents rated eight challenge categories and six AI-supported task types, revealing persistent integration difficulties and tempered enthusiasm given reliability and oversight concerns. It maps where AI could realistically help systems engineering workflows.

entry.title: Bathtubs, Boundaries, and Sandboxes: AI Regulatory Learning under Legal Uncertainty

author.name: Tom Deckenbrunnen, Alessio Buscemi, Marco Almada, Alfredo Capozucca, German Castignani

entry.summary: This governance paper uses Coleman's bathtub framework to analyze the regulatory learning space under the EU AI Act, arguing that legal uncertainty cannot be fully eliminated but can be structurally managed. It addresses the gap between abstract legal principles and verifiable technical requirements that developers, companies, and auditors must operationalize.

entry.title: Estimation of Room Impulse Responses from Handclaps

author.name: Shih-Yu Lai, Kyung Yun Lee, Nils Meyer-Kahlen, Eloi Moliner, Bing-Yu Chen, Vesa V\"alim\"aki

entry.summary: The authors introduce an anechoic dataset of 2,540 handclaps from 17 participants and investigate estimating room impulse responses directly from handclaps, which lack a known source waveform. They establish a deconvolution upper bound with known excitation and propose a learned approach to estimate RIRs without it, relevant to equipment-free acoustic measurement.

entry.title: InterBias-SV: Compound Conditions in Speaker Verification

author.name: Kamel Kamel, Hridoy Sankar Dutta, Keshav Sood, Sunil Aryal

entry.summary: InterBias-SV investigates whether combined degradations in speaker verification (noise, channel distortion, speech changes) have additive effects, using a four-term comparison of joint error, marginal errors, and a common reference. The artifact spans 4,068 scored records, 12 encoders, and six corpora totaling 12 million trial evaluations, with small positive mean EER contrasts suggesting mostly sub-additive or near-additive behavior.

entry.title: State Transport Routing for Short-horizon Adaptation in Multi-horizon Photovoltaic Forecasting

author.name: Xu Yuqing, Zhou Liguo, Sun Ze, Yu Lei, Jiang Mingming

entry.summary: The paper proposes state transport routing (STR), a lightweight adapter that refines predictions from a frozen photovoltaic power forecasting model by blending the original forecast with trajectories derived from the latest measured power level and its recent trend. A horizon-conditioned router adjusts contributions over the first 120 minutes of the forecast horizon. Experiments on four public PV datasets show consistent gains over a parameter-matched residual adapter.

entry.title: Multichannel Audio Quality Assessment: Extending Pretrained Perceptual Models to Spatial Audio

author.name: Gouthaman KV, Shiv Gehlot, Vishnu Raj, Lars Villemoes, Arijit Biswas

entry.summary: The authors study how pretrained perceptual quality models can be reused for multichannel spatial audio, using 5.1-channel audio to compare four integration levels (signal, prediction, latent, and feature). They propose two learned approaches, including latent-level aggregation and a feature-level Feature-Band method. This matters for evaluating and optimizing immersive audio systems where subjective testing is expensive.

entry.title: Codebook-Guided Cross-Modal Knowledge Distillation for Structurally Heterogeneous Features

author.name: Dae Ung Jo, Jongin Lim, YoungJoon Yoo, Daeho Um

entry.summary: This work proposes a cross-modal distillation framework for structurally heterogeneous feature spaces, such as 2D spatial visual grids and 1D temporal audio sequences, where unit-level correspondence is absent. Teacher features are discretized into a vector-quantized codebook that serves as an intermediate bridge for transferring knowledge to the student modality. The codebook mechanism enables feature-level alignment where direct matching fails.

entry.title: BITEM at the NTCIR-19 R2C2 Task: Predicting Confidence from Agentic RAG Pipeline Signals

author.name: Julien Knafou, Luc Mottin, Alexandre Flament, Paul van Rijen, Esteban Gaillac, Patrick Ruch

entry.summary: The BITEM team describes an agentic RAG pipeline for the NTCIR-19 R2C2 shared task in which an orchestrator admits claims only after entailment-cascade verification against cited passages and computes answer confidence from pipeline signals rather than asking the model to self-rate. The system-design lesson of deriving confidence from verifiable pipeline state is relevant to making agentic retrieval systems more trustworthy.

entry.title: Energy-aware frugal Bayesian optimization

author.name: Gaston Plat, Paul Saves, Nathalie Bartoli, Thierry Lefebvre, Joseph Morlier

entry.summary: This paper introduces an energy-footprint metric within Bayesian optimization that guides model parameter settings toward configurations balancing predictive performance and computational frugality. Experiments show tradeoffs between optimum convergence and energy use, and in some cases simultaneous improvements in both.

entry.title: Measure Learning at Steady State: A BIRD-SQL Formula 1 Case Study

author.name: Manoj Bajaj

entry.summary: This single-author study critiques continual learning benchmarks that score short-horizon gains, proposing steady-state evaluation on a late window of BIRD-SQL Formula 1 questions and decomposing performance into exploration efficiency, task reward, and delivery cost. Testing gpt-5.6-luna, an OpenAI model released months earlier, it finds short-horizon metrics understate late-stage savings and miss cost inversions as in-context learning context grows to roughly 95k tokens.

entry.title: Medium-Term Multi-Resolution Electric Load Forecasting using Economic Data and Foundation Model

author.name: Lindas Eloi, Goude Yannig, Ciais Philippe

entry.summary: This paper investigates whether socioeconomic indicators help medium-term electricity load forecasting (months to years), a regime between weather-driven short-term and economics-driven long-term forecasting, using foundation models across multiple resolutions. It identifies at which horizons and resolutions economic data add value. Relevant to power plant maintenance scheduling, dispatch, and price settlement.

entry.title: Self-Reconstruction Dynamics for Autoencoder Reconstruction Refinement

author.name: Hitoshi Iyatomi

entry.summary: The paper studies what happens when a frozen, trained autoencoder is repeatedly applied to its own reconstruction, producing trajectories in image and latent space termed Self-Reconstruction Dynamics. Although iteration degrades fidelity, these trajectories carry sample-specific information that can be used to train a refinement module predicting latent corrections without per-sample test-time optimization.

entry.title: STRIDE: State-Transition Representation via Increment Dynamics and Evolution

author.name: Yuchen Xiong, Siming Huang, Jianfeng Sun

entry.summary: Proposes STRIDE, which defines states through derivative fingerprints, estimates local joint-transition frequencies via trailing convolution windows, and uses proper orthogonal decomposition with sparse dynamics to jointly forecast coordinate paths. Sampled state paths select local functions to generate continuous forecasts, recasting continuous forecasting as transition prediction.

entry.title: AnchorMixGAN: Anchor-Aligned Generative Semi-Supervision for DDoS Detection in Cloud-Integrated IoT Networks

author.name: Jin Yang, Xufeng Liu, Yong Hu, Xueyang Wang, Honglu Yang, Gang Li

entry.summary: AnchorMixGAN is a generative semi-supervised framework for DDoS detection in IoT networks that treats each real unlabeled flow as an anchor and builds alternative views by replacing field groups with generated values, using a frozen reference classifier to produce stable soft targets. It tackles label scarcity while avoiding prediction shifts from synthetic views. This is a domain-specific security application of semi-supervised learning.

entry.title: Optimizing H-Graph Hybridization for Diffusion-Guided RRT

author.name: Omer Talmi

entry.summary: The paper presents two inference-time diversification strategies (factorial seed/bias sweeps and refinement-only diversity) for a fixed pretrained DiTree diffusion planner, combined via H-Graph hybridization and evaluated on a holonomic robot across 15 maze scenarios. It exploits stochastic diversity at inference rather than retraining.

entry.title: Low-Rank Single-Index Bandits with Unknown Links: From Matrices to Tensors

author.name: Zhongxuan Liu, Yue Kang, Thomas C. M. Lee

entry.summary: This paper studies stochastic matrix and tensor bandits with an unknown shared Lipschitz reward link and low-rank index structure, proposing T-ESTOR, which combines rank-adaptive Stein estimation with epoch-based greedy selection. For monotone links it achieves square-root regret with dimension dependence governed by the low-rank structure.

entry.title: MTLiquid: Enabling Efficient Multi-Task Learning using Liquid Neural Networks for Lightweight Healthcare Monitoring Systems

author.name: Rachmad Vidya Wicaksana Putra, Fahad Abdul Rauf, Muhammad Shafique

entry.summary: MTLiquid applies continuous-time liquid neural networks to healthcare monitoring with a multi-task architecture that handles irregularly sampled physiological signals and solves multiple detection/prediction tasks in one network. The goal is efficient, lightweight continuous-time processing for comprehensive patient monitoring.

entry.title: Structure-Adaptive Tree Field Integrators

author.name: Millend Roy, Soham Samal, Ivan Zelich, Krzysztof Marcin Choromanski

entry.summary: STAD-TFIs are near-linear algorithms for integrating tensor fields on trees with distance-dependent kernels, exploiting path-backbone and vertex-separator decompositions plus 2D FFTs to compute interactions jointly. The paper provides theoretical analysis and extensive empirical speed evaluations against prior efficient tree field integrators.

entry.title: From Preference to Reciprocity: Decentralized Matching with Empirically Grounded LLM-agent Based Modeling

author.name: Wangxuan Fan, Xiaoyu Nie, Zhoutian Shi, Xiangcheng Meng, Shipei Zeng, Pin Gao, Yan Hu, Zhongxiang Dai

entry.summary: The authors combine LLM agents with contextual bandits in a dynamic bipartite matching framework applied to a simulated Chinese marriage market, where economically grounded agents evaluate candidates and Logistic-UCB models learn reciprocal acceptance from realized outcomes. The mechanism separates preference formation from learned reciprocity in decentralized, asynchronous matching.

entry.title: A Multimodal Autonomic Sensing Framework for Objective Assessment of Patient Responses to Dental Pulp Stimulation

author.name: Youngsun Kong, Yubin Choi, Dongjin Song, Dong-Guk Shin, I-Ping Chen, Ki Chon

entry.summary: This study integrates ECG-derived skin nerve activity, R-R intervals, and electrodermal activity using temporal convolutional network encoders with attention to objectively classify patient responses during cold dental pulp testing. Data from 49 patients spanned no-response, mild-response, and intense-response conditions.

entry.title: Physics-Guided Conditional Diffusion Model for Rare Event Synthesis and Diagnosis for the Water-Gas Shift Reaction

author.name: Md Abrar Rafid Siddique, Bibek Aryal, Qiugang Lu

entry.summary: The authors propose a physics-guided conditional diffusion model to generate realistic rare-event trajectories for the water-gas shift hydrogen production process, addressing the scarcity of abnormal-condition data such as fouling and thermal runaway. The synthesized data supports fault diagnosis for process safety and yield maintenance.

entry.title: Accurate Sampling from Diffusion Models

author.name: D\'enes Sexty

entry.summary: This paper proposes DM-SMC, combining diffusion models with sequential Monte Carlo to accurately sample lattice field theory ensembles even when the diffusion model and numerical stepsize are approximate. Improved update strategies are explored and results shown for 2D Z2 scalar field theory near its second-order phase transition. It connects generative modeling to accurate sampling in computational physics.

entry.title: Radiomap Blind Prediction under Incomplete Observation: Error Characterization and Correctable Propagation-Prior Learning

author.name: Xiaojie Li, Yu Han, Han Fang, Shangqing Liu, Guangxu Zhu, Shi Jin, Chao-Kai Wen

entry.summary: Establishes a population-level theory for blind radio-map prediction under incomplete environmental observation, identifying the conditional mean as the optimal target and separating reducible approximation error from irreducible uncertainty. The framework also characterizes train-test risk gaps and motivates learning a correctable propagation prior.

entry.title: VCRE-Fib: View-Conditioned Regional Evidence for Fine-Grained Ultrasound Grading of Schistosoma japonicum-Associated Liver Fibrosis

author.name: Ziyang Xu, Shuli An, Hao Zhou, Haitian Zhong, Tingting Wu, Tao Wang, Kun Yang, Tieyong Zeng

entry.summary: Presents a view-conditioned regional evidence framework for fine-grained ultrasound grading of schistosomiasis-associated liver fibrosis, integrating anatomical context, local echogenic patterns, and global assessment. The method retains spatial information for inspection while incorporating acquisition views into the grading process.

entry.title: Modelling non-linear aeroelastic loads in long-span bridges with extreme learning machines

author.name: Gledson Rodrigo Tondo, Samir Chawdhury, Sergio Andres Castro Giraldo, Guido Morgenthal

entry.summary: The paper applies extreme learning machines — single-hidden-layer feedforward networks — to model nonlinear aerodynamic self-excited forces on bridge decks, trained on forced-oscillation data from CFD or wind-tunnel experiments. The learned model predicts self-excited loads for arbitrary motions within the training envelope, capturing nonlinear behavior missed by semi-analytical approaches. This improves aeroelastic stability analysis for long-span bridge design.

entry.title: Local LMO is Secretly a Projection Method!

author.name: Peter Richt\'arik, Ammar Mahran

entry.summary: This theory paper proves that the local linear minimization oracle (Local LMO) step for constrained convex optimization is equivalent to a Euclidean projection onto the feasible set intersected with a separating half-space, computable by a linear oracle alone. It situates Local LMO within a family of projection methods indexed by the depth of the localizing half-space.

entry.title: E-CONAN (Entailment, CONtradition And Neutral) Diagnostics Dataset Investigating Linguistic Phenomena in Arabic Natural Language Understanding

author.name: Khloud AL Jallad, Nada Ghneim, Ghaida Rebdawi

entry.summary: This paper introduces E-CONAN, a diagnostics dataset for fine-grained error analysis of Arabic natural language understanding, built around entailment, contradiction, and neutral labels. It aims to standardize macro and micro linguistic categories so researchers can systematically probe model weaknesses from lexical ambiguity to higher-level reasoning, addressing a gap in Arabic-language NLU benchmarking.

entry.title: Forecast-Necessary Causal Discovery for Nonlinear Political Panel Data: Feedback, Functional Form, and the Dynamics of Democratization

author.name: Michael Coppedge, Dmitry Zaytsev, Valentina Kuskova

entry.summary: The authors develop an inferential workflow for political panel data combining flexible autoregressive estimation, forecast-necessity testing, and functional characterization to disambiguate non-significant coefficients caused by heterogeneous effects, reciprocal dynamics, or omitted covariates. It is applied to the dynamics of democratization.

entry.title: Hierarchical Clustering and Signal Denoising on Digraphs

author.name: Yi Wang, Sippanon Kitimoon, Hrushikesh N. Mhaskar, Xiaosheng Zhuang

entry.summary: This paper represents directed graphs as Hermitian matrices derived from their adjacency matrices, capturing both connectivity and edge orientation, and uses spectral decomposition with k-means for digraph clustering. A recursive bottom-up application yields hierarchical spectral digraph clustering producing consistent nested partitions, and in/out-degree-based cluster statistics enable a hierarchical signal denoising scheme. It is a mathematically principled extension of spectral graph methods to directed graphs.

entry.title: Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Depth-Averaged Avalanche Dynamics

author.name: Pradyumn Singh Sikarwar, Vishal Sharma, Gaurav Bhutani

entry.summary: The authors develop a PINN framework for the Savage-Hutter model of depth-averaged granular flow relevant to avalanche hazard assessment, progressing from 1D analytical verification to 2D experimental validation. Decoupled tests reconstruct individual fields accurately, and the coupled conservative formulation learns both height and velocity fields. It demonstrates a systematic verification path for PINNs in geophysical flow problems.

entry.title: LLM-Guided Ontology-Driven Knowledge Graph Construction from Unstructured Text

author.name: Abdelhadi Belfadel, Maxence Gagnant, Joseph Kattan, Sana Tmar

entry.summary: The paper presents an ontology learning pipeline combining compact open-source LLMs (7B to 32B parameters), reusable prompting strategies, and open knowledge bases for extracting and structuring knowledge from a private French corpus of power-grid incident reports. It targets the difficulty of domain-specific ontology engineering with scarce annotated resources. The locally deployable design matters for industrial settings with privacy constraints.

entry.title: SinBrief: A Hybrid Framework for Abstractive Text Summarisation of Sinhala Legal Documents

author.name: Minduli Lasandi, Nevidu Jayatilleke

entry.summary: SinBrief is a hybrid abstractive summarization framework for Sinhala legal documents that requires no human-annotated training data, combining domain-aware word graphs with neural sentence scoring. It evaluates five scoring models, including a Sinhala-legal-domain-adapted Llama, using reference-free metrics.

entry.title: BaatCheet: A Multilingual Corpus for Dialogue Translation in Indian Languages

author.name: Priyanka Dasari, Yuvrajsinh D. Bodana, Vandan Mujadia, Arafat Ahsan, Dipti Misra Sharma, Parameswari Krishnamurthy

entry.summary: BaatCheet introduces roughly 49,000 dialogues for dialogue translation across five Indian-language translation directions, filling a gap left by sentence-level and formal-text translation resources. The authors fine-tune five open-source LLMs under seven data configurations to establish baselines. It matters for improving conversational machine translation in underserved Indic languages.

entry.title: Quantitative Measurement of Language Distance among Closely Related Indo-European Languages Using Pretrained Language Models: A Case Study on the North Germanic Branch

author.name: Yiping Bai

entry.summary: This paper proposes a three-metric computational framework for measuring language distance among Danish, Norwegian Bokmal, and Swedish using multilingual pretrained models, combining semantic distance from LaBSE and mBERT embeddings of parallel sentences with an orthographic fragmentation rate and a third complementary metric. It aims to replace qualitative linguistic distance judgments with a unified quantitative framework.

entry.title: Deep Learning Methods in Neuroscience: From Modeling Molecular Mechanisms to Classifying States of Consciousness

author.name: Elena Benderskaya, Anastasiia Alifanova, Svetlana Batalova, Vasilisa Zhuk, Anna Kovalenko

entry.summary: A critical review of deep learning methods for studying conscious states, covering EEG/fMRI-based classification of consciousness, modeling brain dynamics under anesthesia, and detecting neurophysiological correlates of consciousness level. It consolidates a cross-disciplinary research area at the intersection of neural networks and neuroscience.

entry.title: Agentsensus: Consensus-Compressed Shared Memory for Multi-Agent Story Worlds

author.name: Yu Pan

entry.summary: Agentsensus is a story-world simulation framework with unified long-term memory in which records of the same event witnessed by multiple characters are merged and linked, reducing duplication versus per-character private memories. Across four simulated worlds (including Hamlet and classical Chinese novels), it writes 22-44% fewer entries than three per-character memory baselines under equal-granularity evaluation. It targets storage and consistency issues in multi-agent narrative simulation.

entry.title: CrossTimeEdit: A Decade-Spanning Cross-View Dataset and Reward-Guided Editing for Historical Street-View Generation

author.name: Hanwen Lu, Jun He, Mingjia Yang, Hao Wei, Jinhao Huang, Yi Lin, Xiang Zhang

entry.summary: The authors build VIGOR-his, a dataset of 43,653 location-level quadruplets across 11 cities on three continents linking recent street views, satellite imagery, and historical change descriptions, and propose CrossTimeEdit, a reward-guided editing model for generating plausible past street appearances. This enables urban evolution reconstruction from sparse historical records. It is a substantial dataset-plus-model contribution for a new task.

entry.title: S2T-Unet: A Structure-to-Style Framework for Inter-Modality MRI Translation

author.name: Yichao Liu

entry.summary: S2T-Unet is a structure-to-style framework for synthesizing missing MRI modalities, explicitly separating modality-invariant structure from modality-specific appearance using vector quantization at the bottleneck with a learned discrete codebook. This addresses structural information loss in existing translation methods that learn only intensity mappings. The work could reduce the need for additional clinical scans while preserving anatomically relevant content.

entry.title: Context without Commitment: Robust Dense Correspondence under Non-Rigid Deformation

author.name: Yuzhen He, Sara Homscheid

entry.summary: CoCo-Reg improves non-rigid point-cloud registration by using regional patches to enrich dense point features while preventing patch-level predictions from restricting the final point-level search. It combines farthest-point-sampled patches with identity-supervised patch similarity to handle ambiguous local geometry.

entry.title: Adaptive Rotation for iSOMA: Geometry, Benchmarking, and Noise Robustness in Variational Quantum Objectives

author.name: Vojt\v{e}ch Nov\'ak, Ivan Zelinka

entry.summary: The paper introduces iSOMA-AR, a variant of the improved Self-Organizing Migrating Algorithm that learns a basis from successful migration displacements to reduce coordinate dependence. It outperforms baseline iSOMA on the noiseless BBOB benchmark suite, especially on rotated ill-conditioned landscapes, and is evaluated in variational quantum objective contexts. Ablations confirm robustness to gate-threshold and rotation-cap settings.

entry.title: Hybrid Joint-Selective Optimization: Reduced-Space Levenberg-Marquardt Refinement of Low-Dimensional Parameters of Interest

author.name: Muhammad Luthfi Shahab, Gabriella Alfa Indahsari, Imam Mukhlash, Hadi Susanto

entry.summary: The paper proposes HJSO, a hybrid optimization framework for large-scale problems where a small subset of parameters of interest matters most.
