entry.title: Refinement Symmetry in Multimodal Transformers

author.name: Yuhao Du, Shunian Chen

entry.summary: Defines refinement symmetry for attention: splitting a representation while preserving content, position, visible context, and total mass should preserve its contribution. The authors prove split invariance forces a linear local mass factor for nondecreasing attention kernels, and demonstrate in Qwen2.5-Omni-7B that duplicating visual tokens changes 255 of 3,586 MVBench answers under standard attention, while their measure weighting preserves every answer. Qwen2.5-Omni-7B is an existing open model, so this is analysis of established behavior rather than a new release.

entry.title: World Agent: Can Language Models Keep a World Running?

author.name: Weixing Chen, Weipeng Zhang, Nan An, Yang Liu, Liang Lin

entry.summary: Proposes the world agent task: rather than generating a playable world, a model must keep one running over time, coordinating events and carrying forward their consequences. Existing evaluations of generative worlds stop at generation, delivery, or single-step transitions, and correct local transitions do not guarantee coherent causal event flow. This reframes world-model evaluation around sustained operation.

entry.title: Counterfactual Self-Evolving Agents for Evidence-Grounded Reasoning

author.name: Xing Han, Yuxin Wang, Chen Chen, Wei Dai, Gautham Krishna Gudur, Shijun Li, Hsing-Huan Chung, Gregory D. Hager, Joydeep Ghosh, Paul Pu Liang, Suchi Saria

entry.summary: This paper introduces counterfactual self-evolution for self-play proposer-solver systems on evidence-identifiable tasks, where a trainable Proposer generates targeted counterfactual context edits with causal explanations so answers can be independently verified. The method is supported by an expert-verified counterfactual instruction-tuning dataset. It matters because it addresses a core bottleneck in self-play: generating plausible but verifiable training cases.

entry.title: Trust and Task Completion in the World of Consumer AI Agents

author.name: Jeroen Olieslagers, Eduardo Pujol, Gal Zahavi, Lukas Ingemarsson, Shivani Poddar

entry.summary: The authors built a simulation-based evaluation scoring trust and completion on the same runs for action agents that email, spend money, and call businesses on a user's behalf, in a world of simulated businesses with websites, inboxes, phone lines, and responsive people. They distinguish trust failures (acting without consent or failing to act when told) from completion failures (giving up on hard errands), both heavily dependent on the harness. This is a valuable benchmark for consumer agent deployment safety.

entry.title: CodeSkill: Latent Skill Abstraction for Long-Horizon Code Agents

author.name: Song-Li Wu, Jingyi Wang, Zhaocheng Du, Weinan Gan, Weiwen Liu

entry.summary: CodeSkill adapts hierarchical latent skill modeling to code agents, using a teacher model to distill recurring multi-step behavioral patterns from large trajectory datasets into skill abstractions. This addresses the mismatch between token-level RL optimization and high-level behavioral reasoning, improving exploration and credit assignment under sparse rewards.

entry.title: Reasoning on the Simplex: Geometric Fixed-Point Models

author.name: Talgat Daulbaev, Ilya Glazkov, Maxim Rakhuba, Ivan Oseledets

entry.summary: Proposes Geometric Fixed-Point Reasoning (GFPR), a looped-reasoner formulation where the iterated state is a categorical belief field on products of simplices, so the argmax is always a valid answer and task structure can be imposed via convex relaxations. With roughly 7M parameters, GFPR achieves 95.1% exact match on Sudoku-Extreme and 92.0% on Maze-Hard, competitive with far larger looped reasoning models.

entry.title: R$^2$ Flow: Recursive Self-Improvement via Recursive Skill Evolution

author.name: Mingda Zhang, Qiang Huang, Yanjin Li, Zijia Wang, Qika Lin, Xiaoying Tang, Tiesunlong Shen

entry.summary: R2 Flow is a recursive self-improvement framework for LLM agents that alternates policy learning, independent verification, and versioned skill-library updates, fixing three failure modes of flow-based training: strategy collapse, credit for frequent use rather than benefit, and unverified library edits. It uses flow-based reward sampling to credit skills in library revisions.

entry.title: GUITAR: Structured Failure Diagnosis of GUI Agents via State Transitions

author.name: Shaoqing Zhang, Kehai Chen, Xuefeng Bai, Zhuosheng Zhang, Pengfei Zhang, Yang Xiang, Min Zhang

entry.summary: GUITAR is a state-centric diagnostic framework that analyzes GUI agent failures across states and transitions rather than per-screen step accuracy, addressing blind spots like functionally equivalent screens and long-tailed failure distribution. This matters because current evaluation metrics hide systematic failure patterns critical for building reliable GUI agents.

entry.title: AdaGuard: An Adaptive Guard Model with User-defined Policies

author.name: Yunhao Feng, Yifan Ding, Yuxiang Xie, Zheng Li, Mingrui Lao, Zeyuan Wang, Yanming Guo

entry.summary: AdaGuard introduces guard models that judge agent behavior against user-defined policies rather than fixed risk taxonomies, supported by AdaptiveSafety, a dataset of 10,939 training and 1,000 test examples with 1-100 rule policies, behavioral counterfactuals, and explanations identifying violated rules. This enables policy-dependent judgments of identical actions.

entry.title: Dynamical Parameters: An Interpretability Framework for Time-Series Foundation Models

author.name: Kang Yang, Gaofeng Dong, Liying Han, Mani Srivastava

entry.summary: This paper introduces Dynamical Parameters — properties like trend slope, oscillation frequency, and autoregressive dependence — as a formal framework for interpreting time-series foundation models. The authors compare how well these dynamical properties are accessible in hidden states versus how much forecasts actually respond to changes in those properties, finding across nine frozen TSFMs that representation accessibility is high (42 of 63 cells above 0.95) while forecast response is poor (median 0.46), revealing a representational-use gap.

entry.title: When Does Structured Knowledge Help Neural Theorem Proving?

author.name: Sareh Nabi, Roland Vogl, Marzieh Nabi

entry.summary: MathAgent builds MathKG, a knowledge graph connecting 364 Mathlib theorems and definitions via 9,434 typed semantic edges inferred by LLM relation extraction, to augment LLM theorem provers in Lean 4. A controlled ablation across four augmentation modes examines when structured semantic knowledge actually helps automated proving.

entry.title: TULIP: Targeted LLM Unlearning at Layers Identified Per-Input

author.name: Yejin Kim, William F. Shen, Seokwon Jung, Daeun Park, Seong Joon Oh

entry.summary: TULIP shows through a hidden-state hijacking experiment that forget answers are formed at intermediate layers whose location varies per input, so fixed-layer unlearning is insufficient. It proposes per-input identification of the formation layer for targeted representation-level unlearning.

entry.title: RSI-Router: Evolving Subtask-Level LLM Routing and Skills for Cost-Efficient Agents

author.name: Hao Li, Hangfan Zhang, Zhiyao Cui, Chunjiang Mu, Yiqun Zhang, Bo Zhang, Danyang Jia, Shuyue Hu

entry.summary: Introduces RSI-Router, a framework that assigns large and small LLMs to subtasks within long-horizon agent tasks and learns model-specific skills through recursive self-improvement over accumulated experience. Each iteration mines subtasks from trajectories, evolves routing strategies, and refines assignments to improve the performance-cost trade-off of agent deployments.

entry.title: RISE: Red-teaming via Iterative Strategy Evolution for Modern Text-to-Image Models

author.name: Dmitrii Kharlapenko, Sergei Bratchikov, Konstantin Korolev, Aleksandr Nikolich

entry.summary: This paper identifies two core weaknesses in automated red-teaming of production text-to-image systems: unreliable VLM-based judges that miss true violations or reward borderline images, and poor exploration on hardened guardrails. It proposes RISE, an iterative strategy-evolution framework with strict category-specific success criteria and calibrated judges. The work matters because policy-violation detection on hardened commercial APIs is a real safety bottleneck as image generators scale.

entry.title: Sol-H3: Recursive Self-Improvement for MiniMax-H3 Inference Acceleration on Sol-Engine across Cloud and Edge

author.name: Yitong Li, Jincheng Yu, Junsong Chen, Haopeng Li, Shuchen Xue, Haozhe Liu, Ping Luo, Song Han, Enze Xie

entry.summary: The paper presents a full-stack inference acceleration pipeline for MiniMax-H3, a 33-billion-parameter open-source video diffusion model, targeting both cloud (NVIDIA GB200) latency and edge (DGX-Spark) memory constraints. It integrates algorithmic design with optimized operator implementations and uses a recursive self-improvement loop on a Sol-Engine for tuning. This tackles the practical deployment bottleneck of multi-step iterative denoising in production video generation.

entry.title: Imprint Reader: From Weight-Update Readout to Behavioral Intervention

author.name: Guanxu Chen, Qihao Lin, Jing Shao

entry.summary: Imprint Reader is a model trained with Semantic Mount-and-Read Tuning (SaRT) to describe frozen weight updates in natural language, giving models a way to decode parameter-level traces of their own learning. The work points toward self-reflection over training history and using the resulting readout for behavioral intervention.

entry.title: MechBench: Can AI Scientific Agents Discover Mechanisms Beyond Phenomenal Laws?

author.name: Zihan Yu, Jiadong Zhang, Jialin Cheng, Jingtao Ding, Yong Li

entry.summary: MechBench is a benchmark that explicitly separates recovering observable phenomenal laws from identifying the underlying mechanisms that generate them, defining each task via structured mechanistic models and evaluating recovery through mechanism probes that query consequences not visible in the data. It matters because existing symbolic regression benchmarks only test surface-law fitting, so the field currently cannot measure whether scientific agents understand mechanisms at all.

entry.title: ARISE: Adapting to Evolving Capability Gaps in Agentic Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Kun Feng, Yuchen Fang, Yiyang Tan, Shuqi Gu, Yongxiang Zhao, Yu Liu, Xingyu Lu, Lintao Ma, Kan Ren

entry.summary: ARISE is a reinforcement learning framework for long-horizon agents that uses rollout evidence to continually update behavioral rubrics and training priorities as the agent's capability gaps evolve, addressing the misalignment between static training criteria and changing weaknesses. It matters because fixed rubrics and sparse task feedback are known failure modes in agentic RL, and co-evolving rubrics with skills is a plausible general remedy.

entry.title: Signatures of semantic search in the activations of large language models

author.name: Luke Leckie, Peter M. Todd, Jacob G. Foster

entry.summary: Applying mechanistic interpretability to the semantic fluency task, this paper finds that LLMs, like humans, organize output into clusters punctuated by switches and that their internal states show distinguishable signatures for within-cluster exploitation versus between-cluster exploration, using techniques including a Jacobian lens over intermediate layers. It matters because it provides evidence that LLMs internally represent search regimes analogous to human semantic foraging, bridging cognitive science and interpretability.

entry.title: Failure-Transparent Agents: Benchmarking Post-Failure Reporting in Tool-Using Language Models

author.name: Junru Zhu, Shiming Xie, Aime Lu Fan Chen, Xiaoqing Ding, Chunxin Tang, Ruoyu Qi, Yulang Fei

entry.summary: FTA is a controlled benchmark that isolates whether tool-using agents honestly report failure versus claiming unsupported success, by fixing failed observations and required evidence before generation. It spans 100 tasks across five failure families, includes user-pressure conditions, and evaluates 3,600 human-annotated responses across six models. This targets a safety-relevant honesty failure mode that existing benchmarks confound with tool-selection ability.

entry.title: MaD-RL: Matching Distributions for Calibrating LLMs with Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Sourabh Kulkarni, Ksheeraj Sai Vepuri, Basar Demir, Jason Bohrer, Emily Shen, Jianfa Chen, Nan Jiang, Ankit Jain, Harihar Subramanyam, Mannat Singh, Chirag Nagpal

entry.summary: MaD-RL proposes a general RL-based distribution-matching framework for LLM post-training that controls the distribution of a latent categorical attribute of outputs against a target distribution, beyond mere expected-reward maximization. The authors show dominant recipes like GRPO are ill-suited for such distributional control in applications like synthetic data generation, fairness constraints, and exploration. This extends post-training from scalar reward optimization to full output-distribution shaping.

entry.title: Active Causal Discovery Benchmark: Evaluating LLM Agents Under Budgeted Interventions

author.name: Sagar Deb, Devam Shah, Ashwanth Krishnan

entry.summary: ACDB is a new SCM-grounded benchmark evaluating whether LLM agents can recover causal graph structure using budget-constrained interventions, with a three-layer scoring contract separating skeleton recovery, DAG recovery, and intervention efficiency. Results show classical PC with an active heuristic outperforms raw LLM agents like Claude Sonnet 4.6 and GPT-5.4 on directed F1. The benchmark exposes significant gaps between LLM agents and classical causal discovery methods.

entry.title: A Large-Scale Benchmark and Risk Assessment of Traffic Analysis Attacks on Cloud LLM Services

author.name: Shahrooz Pouryousef, Jesus Lopez, Saeefa Rubaiyat Nowmi, Md Mahmuduzzaman Kamol, Moinul Hossain, Muoi Tran, Mohammad Saidur Rahman

entry.summary: This is the first unified measurement study and public benchmark of network-level traffic analysis attacks on encrypted cloud LLM services, showing that a passive observer can infer the serving model, prompt category, and multi-agent task behavior from packet sizes, timing, and burst structure alone. The benchmark covers 60,000 user-LLM interactions across 10 models and 6 prompt categories, plus multi-agent executions. This is a significant security contribution highlighting a real privacy side channel in deployed LLM infrastructure.

entry.title: Is invariance all you need for algorithmic fairness? Removing demographic information can create new bias

author.name: Aditya Parikh, Eike Petersen, Stella Frank, Enzo Ferrante, Melanie Ganz, Aasa Feragen

entry.summary: This paper challenges the assumption that demographic-invariant representations are always desirable for fairness, showing mathematically and empirically that enforcing invariance can hinder bias mitigation or even create new biases when demographics correlate with labels. It distinguishes marginal from class-conditional invariance and connects them to demographic parity and equalized odds. This is a useful corrective to a widely held fairness heuristic.

entry.title: DS-VLA: A Dendritic-inspired Vision-Language-Action Model for Robust Action Control

author.name: Yaxing Lyu, Jingyi Li, Mingkun Xu, Yujie Wu

entry.summary: DS-VLA is a vision-language-action model that incorporates dendritic spiking dynamics into action control, using sparsely connected dendritic branches with learned decay factors to modularize feature processing and integrate temporal information, plus mechanisms to suppress unreliable state updates. The work targets robustness under transiently corrupted actions, a gap between nominal evaluation and closed-loop behavior. It is a novel bio-inspired architectural contribution to robust robot manipulation.

entry.title: What Can a Leaderboard Certify? Compositional Controllability for Fair Evaluation and Training of Biomedical Literature-Review Agents

author.name: Zhaowei Han, Xiang Zhang, Lingxiao Guan, Danqi Hu, Kai Liu, Kevin Chang, Jie Liu

entry.summary: This paper introduces compositional controllability, a formal framework for certifying comparisons of long-horizon agents on leaderboards despite unequal evidence, inputs, or budgets. Its central result bounds the gap between observed and controlled score differences using only nuisance factors outside the comparison window, yielding an admissibility test applied before scores are inspected, with certification only when the score gap exceeds the bound. It is applied to biomedical literature-review agents.

entry.title: DRAM: Delta-rule Recurrent Associative Memory for Robot Manipulation Policies

author.name: Xinyu Zhao, Yixiang Shan, Tao Yang, Runyu Lei, Yiming Zhao, Jiaxin Fan, Zongbao Feng, Peng Jia

entry.summary: DRAM is a plug-and-play memory module that attaches to pretrained robotic manipulation policies, giving them long-horizon memory without modifying the backbone or retraining it. It uses delta-rule recurrent associative memory to avoid the inference cost of multi-frame observation windows and the task-limitations of predefined semantic features. This tackles a genuine gap, since most manipulation policies are memoryless or use short temporal windows.

entry.title: Do Audio LLMs Listen Before They Act? Diagnosing Acoustic-Context Gating in Voice Agents

author.name: Yanjie Zhang, Nanchen Hu, Yushi Sun

entry.summary: VGBench is a 1,018-item diagnostic benchmark for action-level addressedness in audio LLM agents, covering side-talk, self-talk, and speaker-switch scenarios with a shared action space of silence, tool call, or natural-language answer. Six raw audio LLMs and three training-free adaptations often identify the target tool but rarely withhold action under speaker shifts, with the highest raw switch mute rate only 14 percent. This reveals a critical safety gap in voice agents acting on speech not directed at them.

entry.title: Timestep Weighting: A Hidden Key to Effective ELBO-Based Flow-Matching RL

author.name: Qinwei Ma, Jingzhe Shi, Simin Fan, Ling Li, Mengdi Wang, Alex Lamb

entry.summary: The paper studies timestep weighting in ELBO-based reinforcement learning for fine-tuning flow-matching models with reward feedback, showing that effective weighting depends on both the reward landscape and learning stage. It provides a unified view explaining prediction-loss heuristics in prior work through controlled CIFAR image generation and robotics experiments. This reveals an under-explored knob that strongly affects fine-tuning performance.

entry.title: Transfer Learning for Edge Classification on Dynamic Text-Attributed Graphs

author.name: Tyler Bonnet, Marek Rei

entry.summary: This paper establishes a leave-one-domain-out transfer learning protocol for edge classification on dynamic text-attributed graphs, showing that state-of-the-art self-supervised dynamic graph methods transfer poorly across domains and can underperform a simple Bag of Events baseline. The findings expose overfitting to domain-specific structural, temporal, and semantic patterns. This matters because it challenges the robustness claims of an entire line of dynamic graph learning research.

entry.title: Multimodal LLMs Outperform Pathology Foundation Models in Cross-Domain Histological Similarity

author.name: Yishu Zhang, Yun Li, Daiwei Zhang

entry.summary: This paper introduces MOSAIC, a benchmark for relative histological similarity assessment across institutions and cohorts, and evaluates 17 models on 6 datasets. It finds that specialized pathology foundation models can rank tiles from the same institution but different disease as more similar than same-disease tiles from different institutions, a failure mode with clinical risk. Notably, general-purpose multimodal LLMs, without pathology-specific training, consistently outperform the specialized encoders on these cross-domain similarity judgments.

entry.title: When Less Compute Is More: Adaptive Early Exit Improves Pretrained Outlier Detection

author.name: Tianyang Zhou, Leman Akoglu

entry.summary: The paper presents the first study of depth-adaptive early exit for pretrained tabular foundation models in outlier detection, finding that exiting at the optimal intermediate layer improves detection performance by 4.7-7.3% on average across benchmarks and three foundation models. It identifies context pollution — outliers among in-context samples — as the key mechanism driving the gains. This inverts the usual efficiency framing of early exit into an accuracy win.

entry.title: Vision-Language Agents for Active Perception in Optics Laboratories

author.name: Ryan Lopez, Sachin Vaidya, Seou Choi, Serena Landers, Marin Solja\v{c}i\'c

entry.summary: This work tests whether general-purpose vision-language models can perform closed-loop control of laboratory experiments, using experimental optics as a testbed where informative signals are sparse, intermittent, or visually ambiguous. Agents must interpret visual observations, take actions to acquire useful feedback, and adapt behavior based on consequences. It extends VLM agent evaluation beyond simulation into real experimental science.

entry.title: CAPEX: Efficiently Distilling Foundation Model Behavior into Deployable Robot Policies through Experience-Adaptive Reasoning

author.name: Shivam Aarya, Zhang Xi-Jia, Chengyue Huang, Junhyun Kim, Huishu Xue, Hrishit Leen, Roman Yakunin, Animesh Garg, Zsolt Kira

entry.summary: CAPEX distills behavior from general-purpose multimodal foundation models into deployable robot policies by using the foundation model as an autonomous demonstrator, with an experience-conditioned frame that avoids repeatedly invoking the slow, expensive model during execution. This replaces human teleoperation with foundation-model-generated demonstrations. It addresses a key bottleneck in scaling robot learning data collection.

entry.title: Beyond the Training Horizon: Mechanisms and Limits of Length Generalization in Looped Transformers

author.name: Jia Liang, Xi Jin, Liangming Pan

entry.summary: Mechanistically compares Matched-Recurrence and Decoupled-Recurrence looped transformers on polynomial iteration, finite-state composition, and knowledge-graph traversal, using attention analysis, intermediate-state decoding, and causal interventions to reveal distinct learned mechanisms under final-answer supervision. Explains how and to what extent looped transformers generalize to longer reasoning chains than seen in training.

entry.title: Beyond Calibration: Do a Typed-Decision Model's Probabilities Obey the Probability Axioms?

author.name: Keyi Li, Yihao He, Quanyi Li

entry.summary: This paper tests probabilistic coherence of typed-decision models like TypeSafe's Jev, checking whether probabilities assigned to logically linked questions (e.g., whether a label is X, is not X, or is one of two alternatives) fit together consistently. Using label-free batteries of related questions on ChaosNLI and PubMedQA, it finds coherence failures beyond standard accuracy and calibration metrics. This matters because systems acting on model probabilities need internally consistent beliefs, not just well-calibrated marginals.

entry.title: From Position Risks to Block Survival: Faster Generation for Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Siwei Chen, Yuxiang Wan, Yifan Yu, Fan Lai

entry.summary: BRISK-DLM fixes a mismatch in diffusion language model decoding where parallel proposals cannot condition on earlier tokens in the same block, causing early rejections under proposal-verification decoding to invalidate all subsequent progress. It trains on self-generated sequences optimizing proposal learning and selection toward verified block survival. This directly improves dLM generation speed and reliability.

entry.title: Evaluating System One Models for Agent Security Decisions: Reliability, Calibration, and Selective Automation

author.name: Yixuan Liu

entry.summary: This paper evaluates four System One models (Jev, Laya, Decider, Bespoke Nimble) used as model-based judges for agent security tasks like prompt injection detection and harmful request screening, comparing them against specialized classifiers and LLM judges. It finds that strong average performance and calibration can mask systematic failures on specific attack groups, with important implications for selective automation of security decisions.

entry.title: Decoupling Token Roles in Autoregressive Pretraining

author.name: Suqin Yuan, Runqi Lin, Kevin Qinghong Lin, Junchi Yu, Lei Feng, Chris Russell, Tongliang Liu

entry.summary: This arXiv paper analyzes how tokens contribute to autoregressive pretraining by distinguishing between two roles a token plays: as a prediction target and as context for subsequent tokens. Using controlled corruption experiments, the authors find a surprising reversal — making a noisy token easier to predict reduces its harm as a target but increases its damage as context — and they connect this decoupling to an explanation of how generation can go wrong in language models, since a generated token's contextual role is never validated against an independently determined continuation. The work matters because it refines the standard next-token loss attribution framework and could inform data curation and pretraining objectives for heterogeneous datasets.

entry.title: Learning to Learn from Context: Synthetic Training from Perturbed Public Documents

author.name: Haoyi Wu, Yang Xiao, Yusong Sun, Wenyang Hui, Zhaokai Luo, Chengyue Jiang, Mu Chuan

entry.summary: The authors generate synthetic training data by perturbing high-quality public documents so that LLMs must learn from in-context task information rather than rely on memorized pretraining knowledge, then distill these context-dependent reasoning traces into a student model. This addresses the costly human annotation bottleneck for training in-context learning ability. It offers a scalable recipe for improving a known LLM weakness.

entry.title: PI-NOMT: Physics-Informed Neural Optimal Mass Transport for Brain Fluid Dynamics

author.name: Mehmet Emin Acar, Vahit Bugra Yesilkaynak, Helene Benveniste, Gozde Unal

entry.summary: This paper proposes PI-NOMT, a physics-informed neural optimal mass transport framework that treats the transport velocity field itself as the primary object of inference for brain tracer imaging from DCE-MRI. It represents density, velocity, and source terms as continuous neural fields to recover hidden transport mechanisms from sparse spatiotemporal observations. The work matters because it bridges optimal transport theory, scientific machine learning, and a concrete neuroscience application with clinical relevance.

entry.title: Maat: Independent Deterministic Contract-Based Governance for Multi-Agent LLM Workflows

author.name: Uliana Elina

entry.summary: Maat is a runtime governance layer for multi-agent LLM systems that validates agent-to-agent handoffs against a versioned workflow contract using a deterministic seven-check rubric with no LLM in the validation path. Evaluated across six controlled workflows with injected data-level defects over 522 trials, it aims to stop contract-detectable defects from propagating. It offers a deterministic alternative to probabilistic LLM-based judges for multi-agent reliability.

entry.title: JET: Judge-Guided Evolution at Test Time for Agent Programs

author.name: Yao Long Teng, Jiayi Cai, Bo An

entry.summary: JET evolves an executable judge on labeled source trajectories, then freezes and transfers it to guide test-time evolution of agent programs on new tasks, providing scores and diagnostic feedback without target-side evaluators or weight updates. On unseen WebShop tasks it achieves strong adaptation, addressing the problem of deciding which agent-program changes to retain when true rewards are unavailable. Relevant to the growing area of agent self-improvement at inference time.

entry.title: Bayesian Active Learning for Intent Disambiguation in Interactive Robot Planning

author.name: Huao Li, Carson Sobolewski, Augustinos Saravanos, William Tan, John Karigiannis, Chuchu Fan

entry.summary: This paper proposes a Bayesian framework that treats clarification dialogue in robot planning as active learning over grounded Signal Temporal Logic task specifications. LLMs initialize candidate formal specs and translate informative contrasts into natural-language clarification questions, while Bayesian optimization maintains uncertainty over user intent. It matters because it reduces systematic multi-turn conversation failures when robots interpret ambiguous instructions.

entry.title: Coding Agent Memory Post-training: Unlocking the Memory Potential of Pre-trained File Operations for Long-Horizon Tasks via Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Lirui Luo, Kelong Mao, Heming Xia, Rongqing Li, Xinwei Yang, Luyu Chen, Kieran Wong, Yudong Guo, Xinrui Wang, Jiayin Zhu, Simiu Gu, Sulong Xu, Cong Fang

entry.summary: This paper introduces CAMG, a suite of long-horizon agentic-RL environments spanning Shopping, Coding, DeepResearch, and AutoResearch, built on pre-trained file operations so memory behavior does not need to be learned from scratch. RL post-training on these environments makes memory control part of the policy and transfers better to long-horizon tasks than domain-specific memory tools. It tackles the key limitation of agent context overflow.

entry.title: Precise Editing and Flexible Referencing for Interactable Worlds

author.name: Xinyao Liao, Xianfang Zeng, Zhu Liang, Zhoujie Fu, Qianxun Xu, Jiachi Liu, Gang Yu, Guosheng Lin

entry.summary: EditWorld is a video world model that extends world modeling from exploration to precise modification, supporting streaming editing instructions and reference images during autoregressive generation. It introduces Gated Causal Attention for temporally varying editing conditions and a Sparse Context mechanism for bounded long-horizon inference, trained with joint autoregressive and bidirectional objectives. This advances controllable, interactive world generation.

entry.title: SEAD: A State-Based Perspective on Attack and Defense in Tool-Using Agents

author.name: Xinjie Shen, Junran Wang, Rongzhe Wei, Pan Li

entry.summary: SEAD formulates attack and defense in tool-using agents as partially observed state control, recognizing that earlier actions alter hidden system state making later routine-looking actions harmful. It derives DART, an attacker that decomposes harmful goals into locally plausible steps guided by real tool-execution feedback, and SAGE, a defender that decides before execution with incomplete state evidence. This shared formulation yields design requirements for both sides.

entry.title: Sufficiency of Zeroth-Order Reward Shaping for Policy Gradient in Stabilization Control

author.name: Yisheng Zhang, Tao Wang, Sicun Gao

entry.summary: The paper theoretically and empirically shows that policy gradient methods can solve stabilization control tasks using only zeroth-order (configuration-based) reward terms, without velocity-based (first-order) terms, and that adding such terms can sometimes hurt. This challenges heuristic reward-design practice in deep RL for robotics and clarifies which reward components are intrinsic to the control objective.

entry.title: Beyond Verbalized Confidence: Calibrating Reasoners with Differentiable Readouts

author.name: Chenxiao Fan, Chongming Gao, Gangyi Zhang, Leyang Shen, Yaxin Gong, Jiamin Wang, Jiakai Wang, Dong Wang, Yang Liu, Fuli Feng, Xiangnan He

entry.summary: The paper observes that RLVR-trained reasoning models are systematically overconfident and that existing in-loop calibration methods sample confidence as text, introducing variance, value collapse, and non-differentiability. CREDO replaces sampled confidence with a deterministic differentiable readout, enabling direct calibration losses alongside RLVR training.

entry.title: Audit the Scaffold, Not the Checkpoint: A Stationarity Dichotomy for Recursive Self-Improvement in Agentic Coding

author.name: Sebastian Bobadilla-Suarez, Bob Suh, Ryan Fortin

entry.summary: This arXiv paper proposes a stationarity dichotomy for recursive self-improvement in agentic coding systems: iterative self-modification yields strictly diminishing returns when the agent's reachable set of edits is fixed, and can only escape that ceiling if the set expands. The authors argue that auditing whether model weights are frozen is the wrong criterion; instead, one should audit the scaffold (tools, verifiers, task decomposition), since scaffold rewriting expands an agent's reach without modifying weights. The framework distinguishes three often-conflated regimes: search within a fixed class, test-time training that raises the ceiling itself, and scaffold rewriting between them, and extends the argument to best-of-k orchestration.

entry.title: Semantic Uncertainty Quantification Needs Factual Equivalence

author.name: Joseph Hoche, Quentin Guimard, Gianni Franchi

entry.summary: Formalizes semantic uncertainty quantification for LLMs into an answer-comparison operator and an aggregator, showing that the off-the-shelf comparison operators (NLI models, sentence encoders) are the primary bottleneck because they poorly measure factual equivalence among sampled answers. It proposes a simple recipe to build operators that measure factual equivalence, improving the whole UQ template.

entry.title: Learning to Re-Draft: A Variational Stackelberg Game for Discrete Diffusion

author.name: Dmitrii Moor, Federico Tomasi, Paul N. Bennett, Alice Wang, Mounia Lalmas

entry.summary: VSDD learns a semantically aware corruption process for discrete diffusion models via a leader-follower Stackelberg game, replacing fixed masking or uniform substitution schemes. The learned forward process trains a denoiser that can meaningfully revisit and correct earlier tokens during generation.

entry.title: "Nothing to See Here'': Unintended Disclosure through Revision Traces of LLM Deliverables

author.name: Yage Zhang, Yukun Jiang, Yang Zhang

entry.summary: The paper identifies revision traces: cases where an LLM assistant removes sensitive content from a document but reveals it in an edit note, e.g., mentioning a deleted password in a comment. An in-the-wild analysis of three public conversation corpora surfaced 26,753 revision requests, exposing a previously unnamed privacy leak channel in LLM-assisted drafting.

entry.title: Almieyar: A Culturally Grounded Benchmark for Multi-Dialect Arabic Speech Recognition

author.name: Omid Ghahroodi, Anas Madkoor, Dima Faris Al Saudi, Fagr Tahir, Malak Annan, Talha shahid javad allah rakha, Omar Al-Busaidi, Zineb El Kahla, Iheb Zouari, Essa Ahmed Abou Jabal, Ahmed Ezzat, Hind AL-Merekhi, Aisha Hamad M A Al-Naimi, Hadi Wazni, Bushra Alnajjar, Omar Amin, Haya Al-Thani, Houssam Eddine-Othman Lachemat, Marwa Elwakedy, Sundus Abdulmalik Al Nahari, Elahe Zahiri, Osamah Sarraj, Raghad Mousa, Mckeen Assi, Ahd Al Jumah, Heyam Salman, Alhanouf Abdulraqib, Sara Benoumhani, Alia Hamwi, Ayaat Al-Yasseri, Rim Ibrahim Ghazal, Lamia Ben hiba, Mohamed Eltabakh, Fatima Al-Raisi, Yassine El Kheir, Mohammed Abdulrahman, Hamdy Mubarak, Ayah Hashem, Lefkir Meriem, Ehsaneddin Asgari

entry.summary: Introduces ALMIEYAR, a new ASR benchmark covering 17 Arabic dialects across six dialect families, built from freshly recorded speech with culturally relevant prompts selected by dialect-community coordinators. The authors evaluate 12 zero-shot ASR systems, including GPT-4o-transcribe and Whisper-based models, and find overall underperformance on living dialects relative to Modern Standard Arabic.

entry.title: On-Policy Attention Linearization

author.name: Arian Raje, Anupam Nayak, Anthony Fei, Akaash Parthasarathy, Mohamed Abdelfattah, Gauri Joshi

entry.summary: Addresses collapse of distilled hybrid linear-attention transformers on long-context retrieval and reasoning by arguing that off-policy distillation never teaches the student to recover from error drift inherent in fixed-size state compression. Proposes on-policy attention linearization so that linear attention layers are trained on the model's own distributions, improving long-context behavior where hybrid efficiency matters most.

entry.title: Representation Learning for Exact Preimages

author.name: Konstantin Hess, Stefan Feuerriegel

entry.summary: This paper introduces TRIO, a representation learning framework for computing preimages: given a target performance or safety level for a neural predictor, TRIO characterizes and optimizes over the complete set of inputs meeting that target. It addresses the three-way tradeoff between expressive forward prediction, accurate preimage approximation, and tractable downstream optimization. The problem is important for safety verification and inverse design in science and engineering.

entry.title: A Journey to the Edge of Stability

author.name: Jaerin Lee, Kyoung Mu Lee

entry.summary: The paper studies what happens before deep learning trajectories reach the edge of stability regime by tracking loss, sharpness, and gradient alignment across dense learning-rate sweeps with multiple optimizers. It reports a striking empirical finding: learning-rate traces scaled by the dc gain of the optimizer almost perfectly overlap across a wide learning-rate range. This suggests a unifying normalization principle for optimizer dynamics.

entry.title: Does Transolver really need a Transformer?

author.name: Shizheng Wen, Siddhartha Mishra

entry.summary: Through careful ablations on nine 3D fluid dynamics benchmarks, the authors show that Transolver's physics-attention can be replaced by a constant linear map with no accuracy loss, meaning the architecture does not need a Transformer. Performance instead hinges on the global slicing/deslicing mixing step, which must be applied repeatedly.

entry.title: Permutation-Equivariant Flow Matching for Alignment-Free Neural Weight Generation

author.name: Arkadi Piven, Yam Eitan, Guy Bar-Shalom, Fabrizio Frasca, Daniel Cremers, Thomas Dag\`es, Ron Kimmel, Haggai Maron

entry.summary: The authors parameterize a flow-matching velocity field with a permutation-equivariant Graph Meta Network to generate neural network weights, handling the permutation symmetry that makes independently trained networks appear distant in parameter space. This removes the need for a common base model or costly approximate neuron alignment used by prior weight-generation methods.

entry.title: Last-Iterate Guarantees for Online Reinforcement Learning in Structured Constrained MDPs

author.name: Nam Phuong Tran, Trinh Ha Mai Huynh, Tuyen Pham Le, Van-Truong Nguyen, Quan Nguyen, Long Tran-Thanh

entry.summary: This paper provides a statistically efficient framework for last-iterate convergence guarantees in structured Constrained MDPs, ensuring that the single deployed policy satisfies both performance and safety constraints rather than only an average over training policies. The analysis separates contraction of regularized primal-dual dynamics from actor approximation and statistical errors under online exploration. This addresses an open scalability gap in safe constrained RL for large-state problems.

entry.title: Cost-free Spectral Estimation for Adaptive Newton--Schulz in Matrix Optimizers

author.name: Kristi Topollai, Anna Choromanska

entry.summary: Focusing on matrix optimizers like Muon that use Newton-Schulz iterations for approximate orthogonalization, the paper shows the spectral information needed to adapt the polynomial routine can be extracted for free from Gram matrices formed inside the iterations. This enables per-layer, per-timestep adaptive orthogonalization without additional matrix multiplications, potentially improving quality and cost of optimizer updates.

entry.title: SketchSSM: Write to the Full State, Read from a Compact Sketch

author.name: Omin Kwon, JoongWon Shin, Minseo Kim, Kurt Keutzer, Sehoon Kim, Jae W. Lee

entry.summary: SketchSSM accelerates hybrid-attention models where recurrent state reads become a decode bottleneck: it preserves full-state updates while approximating reads using a low-rank, state-weighted query approximation with offline-fixed basis vectors, reading the full state only at updates. This builds on and improves ReplaySSM's amortization strategy. The result targets larger decode batches and reduced KV-cache pressure in efficient LLM inference.

entry.title: CARVE: Breaking Data Barriers in Chip Placement by Harnessing Reusable Expertise

author.name: Jiefu Zhang, Haixiang Sun, Yang Xu, Vaneet Aggarwal, Zishen Wan

entry.summary: CARVE is a continual learning framework for macro-placement of chip circuits that stores accumulated expertise as a frozen base policy plus immutable specialist checkpoints and task-specific validation credentials. For new tasks, it reuses qualifying specialists or trains a new one from the frozen base, avoiding catastrophic overwriting of earlier improvements even when original training data are unavailable.

entry.title: When an Evaluation Rule Writes Training Labels: Measuring Human-Reference Forgiveness in NAVSIM

author.name: Jiaxuan Guo, Jingxin Yang, Jiaqi Ye, Youran Sun, Shuo Xin, Kejia Zhang, Haizhao Yang

entry.summary: The paper audits NAVSIM driving-benchmark label generation, showing that the human-reference forgiveness rule sets entire columns of 16,384 candidate trajectories to passing whenever the human reference scores zero. Re-running the generator with the overwrite disabled reveals the rule erases candidate distinctions used by the training loss on 10.88 percent of navtrain scenes.

entry.title: Two Heads Are Better Than One: Aggregating Weaker LLMs for Better Forecasts

author.name: Cheng Peng, Ruixi Luo, Zhi Chen, Wei Tang

entry.summary: Using ForecastBench, the paper evaluates 70 LLM forecasters and shows that ensembles of individually weaker forecasters, with weights learned on separate training data, can outperform the strongest individual forecaster in their comparison groups. It provides substantial evidence of weak-to-strong improvement in real-world event forecasting.

entry.title: Direct Hidden-State Alignment: Mapping and Controlling Preference Expression in LLMs

author.name: Fansheng Zhang, Shengran Guo, Zexiao Wang, Liang Yuan, Jiyuan Chen, Ruikun Luo

entry.summary: The paper introduces Residual Competition Maps, which map a behavioral preference onto signed causal effects of native residual computation in LLMs, revealing coexisting target-supporting and target-competing components and input-dependent roles. This structure directly guides control, reframing part of post-training alignment from capability acquisition to reliably expressing behavior the base model already supports.

entry.title: When to Evict, Not What to Keep: Draft-Guided Eviction for Training-Free KV-Cache Compression

author.name: Haeyong Kang, Chang D. Yoo

entry.summary: This paper identifies two failure modes (compensation and selection) in existing training-free KV-cache compression methods like SnapKV, H2O, and PyramidKV, arguing they fail because eviction happens before answer-determining queries exist. It proposes Draft-Guided Eviction (DGE), which defers eviction until after a draft phase, improving long-context inference quality without training.

entry.title: Quantifying Behavioral Tails in Black-Box Language Models

author.name: Elsayed Eshra, Ali Al-Lawati, Dongwon Lee, Suhang Wang

entry.summary: RareTrap is a framework for estimating the probability of severe behaviors in black-box LLMs, using a surrogate model and a geometry-aware mapping from a latent reference space to token-embedding space to induce an explicit, reproducible prompt distribution. Sequential rare-event simulation then concentrates evaluations on increasingly severe behaviors while preserving probability estimates.

entry.title: Oracle-Efficient Online Classification with Stochastic Inputs and Adversarial Outputs

author.name: Gon Buzaglo, Elad Hazan

entry.summary: Shows that Follow-the-Perturbed-Leader with Gaussian perturbations achieves optimal regret for contextual binary prediction with stochastic contexts and adversarial losses, using one optimization-oracle call per round without enumerating the expert class. This resolves an open problem from Lazaric and Munos (2012), establishing that hybrid online classification is computationally as easy as statistical learning.

entry.title: Learning to Optimize through Solver-Grounded Self-Play

author.name: Xia Jiang, Yaoxin Wu, Chenyu Zhou, Mengzhu Xu, Wim P. M. Nuijten, Yingqian Zhang

entry.summary: OPT-Zero is a fully self-play training framework for LLM-based optimization modeling that requires zero external training data, using a single LLM in a dual-role loop where a Proposer synthesizes problems and a Solver grounds learning via executable optimization-solver feedback. It aims to overcome the generalization ceiling and capability anchoring of human-annotated or teacher-generated datasets.

entry.title: SleuthBench: Benchmarking Statistical LLM Evaluation Using Tabular Hidden Signals

author.name: Jingyun Jia, Antoine Remond-Tiedrez, Aaron Alvarez, Joshua Shunk, Rich Caruana, Ben Lengerich

entry.summary: This paper introduces SleuthBench, a benchmark for evaluating LLM agents on statistical discovery tasks over tabular data. It injects controlled data-quality problems and feature effects into public datasets so that ground-truth answers can be computed automatically and memorization of the original tables cannot inflate scores, with 17 question templates modeled on real-world analytical phenomena.

entry.title: Emergence, Not Bandwidth: Physical Coupling and the Limits of Learned Multi-Agent Communication

author.name: Mihir Chauhan, Aniket Bera

entry.summary: The paper derives theoretical answers to what rate-limited messages should encode, what compression costs over horizons, and when learned protocols are decodable, for rate-limited Dec-POMDPs, fixing what is achievable independent of any learner. Experiments on MuJoCo arenas spanning zero, partial, and rigid physical coupling at exactly 2 bits per decision show where reinforcement learning falls short of these optima, separating optimization limits from information-theoretic limits.

entry.title: Admissible Diffusion for Multimodal Interventional Trajectories

author.name: Xing Han, Shravan Chaudhari, Jiarui Shao, Paul Pu Liang, Suchi Saria

entry.summary: ADMIT is a framework for generating counterfactual clinical trajectories under alternative treatments, combining irregular multimodal representations, treatment-conditioned latent diffusion, and explicit physiological constraints. It grounds the interventional target in sequential g-computation and distinguishes genuine causal assumptions from mere constraint satisfaction, an important rigor step for clinical generative models.

entry.title: Universality and Generalization of Causal Transformers Across Context Lengths

author.name: Takashi Furuya, Maarten V. de Hoop, Gabriel Peyr\'e

entry.summary: Proves that a single masked transformer with length-independent parameters can uniformly approximate causal token-to-token maps over sequences of arbitrary length drawn from compact classes of alpha-Holder sequences, extending results to an infinite-length mean-field limit with continuous token curves. This is a strong expressivity/universality result directly motivated by long-context transformer systems. It characterizes the continuity conditions under which such uniform approximation holds.

entry.title: Cross-Rollout Bellman Closure for Long-Horizon Agentic Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Yangyang Ren, Haodong Zhu, Linlin Yang, Sheng Xu, Peichao Lai, Baochang Zhang

entry.summary: The paper improves credit assignment in group-based RL methods like GRPO for long-horizon LLM agents by exploiting shared anchor states across rollouts. It introduces a method that propagates step-level evidence across rollouts recursively, avoiding both the local limitations of visit-local averaging and the frequency bias of shortest-path estimators.

entry.title: On-Policy or Off-Policy Learning? A Systematic Study of Distillation Dynamics

author.name: Julianna Piskorz, Antonin Berthon, Mihaela van der Schaar

entry.summary: A controlled study of strong-to-weak distillation across Llama3 and Qwen2.5 families that independently varies rollout policy, KL direction, and learning rate. The authors find that rollout policy is not necessarily the central driver of distillation outcomes, complicating the common on-policy vs off-policy narrative. This matters because it clarifies which design choices actually matter when compressing reasoning models.

entry.title: An RL View of OPD: Least Square Policy Distillation for Sample-Efficient LLM Reasoning

author.name: Shangzhe Li, Yuxiao Yang, Tianrun Yu, Kaixiang Zhao, Xiaoyun Wang, Taylor W. Killian, Weitong Zhang

entry.summary: The paper connects on-policy distillation (OPD) for LLM reasoning to KL-regularized policy optimization and introduces Least-Square Policy Distillation (LSPD), which imports optimistic exploration and off-policy data reuse from value-based RL into distillation. The authors prove a sharp O(log K) regret bound under online exploration and report improved sample efficiency for reasoning distillation.

entry.title: Recipe-Matching, Not Equivalence

author.name: Ali Habibullah, Mohammad Alshiekh, Yazan Alshoibi, Salman Khan, Naeemullah Khan

entry.summary: This paper examines MathNet-Retrieve, a benchmark where a retriever must find documents stating the same math problem, and asks how much of the measured performance comes from matching the benchmark's construction recipe rather than genuine retrieval ability. Using two models from the same base trained on either LLM-generated pairs following the benchmark's published prompt or computer-algebra-verified pairs with no LLM involved, the authors show the LLM-built pairs lead by 45 R@1 points on the easy tier, with half to two-thirds of that gap attributable to paraphrase leakage rather than the skill the benchmark claims to test. This is a benchmark-validity critique with practical implications for how retrieval benchmarks should be constructed.

entry.title: Evolving Dexterous Robots from Scratch

author.name: Zihan Guo, Shuzhe Zhang, Muhan Li, Peiyang Li, Sam Kriegman

entry.summary: Evolves freeform robots from scratch, without presupposing any body part's presence, articulation, or geometry, to pick up, hold, rotate, and use diverse objects. Familiar grasping forms like paws, claws, beaks, and tails can emerge spontaneously, offering insights relevant to both robotics and evolutionary biology.

entry.title: Identifying Temporal Features within Transcoders for Time Sensitive Factual Recall

author.name: Sanjay Govindan, Yang Song, Maurice Pagnucco

entry.summary: This mechanistic interpretability paper provides the first feature-level map of time-sensitive factual recall in LLMs, using transcoder circuit tracing to isolate MLP features rather than just attention heads or layers. The authors identify three node categories that jointly form a temporal filter, analyzed on Gemma 2, an existing model. This offers a more granular alternative to fine-tuning or RAG for addressing temporal misalignment.

entry.title: A Statistical Perspective on Knowledge Distillation: Foundations, Classical Methods, and Large Language Model Extensions

author.name: Luyang Fang, Haoran Lu, Jiazhang Cai, Tao Wang, Huimin Cheng, Wenxuan Zhong, Ping Ma

entry.summary: This review develops a unified Bayesian formulation of knowledge distillation, interpreting teacher predictions as prior information and connecting KD to uncertainty quantification. It surveys classical methods and extends the statistical framing to large language model distillation, elevating KD from an engineering trick to a principled statistical procedure.

entry.title: Autonomous phase discovery

author.name: Shiyu Zhou, Yuxuan Zhang, Sebastian Wetzel, Roger Melko, Xiu-Zhe Luo

entry.summary: This work builds a fully autonomous system for discovering quantum phases of matter, combining differentiable programming and unsupervised learning to evaluate ground-state data along adaptive trajectories rather than fixed parameter grids. It is demonstrated with three solvers and benchmarks favorably against random sampling on a generalized cluster chain hosting up to 200 sites.

entry.title: One Attack to Fool Them All: Highly Transferable Black-Box Adversarial Attacks on Frontier MLLMs

author.name: Sen Nie, Jie Zhang, Zhongqi Wang, Shiguang Shan, Xilin Chen

entry.summary: The authors propose O-Attack, a black-box adversarial framework in which a single crafted image can consistently mislead diverse frontier multimodal LLMs without access to model internals. The method exploits a broad, cross-modally aligned semantic space within surrogate models that existing attacks underutilize, achieving unusually high transferability across heterogeneous MLLMs.

entry.title: Prospective Interpretation Risk: Principled Communication Control Between LLMs

author.name: Wanrong Yang, Rehan Deen, Julian Ma, Yuheng Fan, Yaoyu Jin, Taher Jafferjee, Ziquan Liu, Dominik Wojtczak, Yalin Zheng, David Henry Mguni

entry.summary: The paper defines prospective interpretation risk (PIR), the probability that an LLM receiver reconstructs a task other than the sender's intent, modeling agent-to-agent communication as a sender-receiver problem with a latent receiver type. Black-box probes over message, intended task, and receiver-specific reconstructions enable scalable estimation and principled communication control before a message is sent.

entry.title: RewardExplainer: Learning Reward Model Explanations from Counterfactual Preference Feedback

author.name: Jingyi He, Nier Wu, Shuang Liu, Xin Wang, Mengnan Du, Xia Hu

entry.summary: RewardExplainer is a framework that trains a reusable explainer for reward models by obtaining feedback from the target RM via counterfactual rewriting of responses, forming a closed loop that identifies which response behaviors drive scoring decisions. This addresses the opacity of scalar-output discriminative reward models used in LLM post-training, where prior interpretation methods required predefined attributes and repeated manual interventions.

entry.title: Unbiased Top-$k$ Estimation for On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Linjian Meng, Siyuan Gan, YuHan Li, Xiran Wang, Ziyang Ding, Ditang Gou, Yiming Wu, Zhen Zhao

entry.summary: The paper tackles gradient estimation of the reverse KL divergence in on-policy distillation, where sampled-token supervision is cheap but weak and full-vocabulary supervision is accurate but expensive. It proposes an unbiased Top-k estimation method that interpolates between these extremes, providing better distributional supervision than biased Top-k approaches at reduced cost.

entry.title: Rethinking Latent Visual Reasoning: Grounding Latent Reasoning in Visual Evidence

author.name: Xi Xiao, Tianchen Zhao, Youngeun Kim, Zhuowei Li, Linghan Xu, Jiaye Wu, Zheng Zhang, Xiang Xu, Xuanbai Chen, Farhan Tejani, Jakub Zablocki, Julia Xu, Yifan Xing

entry.summary: The paper studies latent visual reasoning in multimodal LLMs, where intermediate computation happens in continuous latent tokens rather than text. The authors identify a latent evidence-credit gap: latent tokens respond weakly to image perturbations that change the correct answer, and attribute this to lack of explicit supervision in GRPO training where final-answer rewards give little guidance on what visual evidence to preserve. The work diagnoses an important failure mode and motivates supervision methods grounded in visual evidence.

entry.title: Two-Timescale Fine-tuning Provably Learns New Features for Two-Layer ReLU Networks

author.name: Etienne Boursier, Nicolas Flammarion

entry.summary: The paper provides theoretical guarantees for fine-tuning in a Gaussian multi-index setting where a teacher network has m+1 features, m learned during pretraining and one that must be learned during fine-tuning. For two-layer ReLU networks, it proves that two-timescale training (updating outer weights much faster than hidden ones) learns the new task-specific feature while preserving pre-trained ones, requiring only O(d) fine-tuning samples. This gives one of the cleaner formal accounts of how fine-tuning acquires new features.

entry.title: Simulation-Based Quantum System Inference with Neural Posterior Estimation

author.name: Hang Zou, Anton Frisk Kockum, Martin Rahm, Simon Olsson

entry.summary: The paper introduces simulation-based quantum system inference, a likelihood-free framework that learns parameter posteriors directly from classical simulation data by pairing polynomial-cost classical simulators (Pauli propagation, tensor networks) with normalizing flows and other neural density estimators. A single trained model maps any new measurement record to its posterior in one forward pass, sidestepping intractable likelihoods from the exponentially large Hilbert space. This turns quantum parameter inference into an amortized simulation-based inference problem.

entry.title: Don't Repeat Yourself: Self-Supervised Fine-Tuning for Coverage

author.name: Eric Fithian, Kirill Skobelev, X. Y. Han

entry.summary: DRY-SFT is a post-training method that increases output diversity and coverage, meaning the probability of at least one correct solution among many attempts, in verifiable domains like math and coding. It sequentially generates K solutions while showing the model all prior attempts and asking for a different one, then fine-tunes on each attempt independently with the prior attempts removed from context. This counteracts mode collapse that higher sampling temperature cannot fix.

entry.title: Solving Every Step Is Not Enough: Milestone Oracles Reveal a Composition Gap in LLM Math Reasoning

author.name: Zhuohan Wang, Haoran Ma, Tianyu Wu, Yuanlin Duan, Zichun Liao, Jieming Yu

entry.summary: OracleLadder is a diagnostic evaluation that gives LLMs increasing levels of oracle help on multi-step math problems — roadmap of subgoals, roadmap plus milestone answers, or each milestone alone — with a symbolic verifier grading answers, sorting failures into five reasoning gap types. Across 354 NuminaMath problems and six models from 8B to 671B parameters, it shows models can solve every intermediate step yet still fail the composed problem. This composition gap is a valuable contribution to understanding why chain-of-thought performance does not translate into end-to-end multi-step success.

entry.title: LLMs learn different forms of metacognition when trained to predict their own accuracy

author.name: Nicolas Yax, Stefano Palminteri, Pierre-Yves Oudeyer

entry.summary: Training ten open-weight LLMs to predict their own accuracy on factual multiple-choice questions before answering, this paper finds trained confidence reflects two distinct signals: it tracks true accuracy on questions near the training distribution but apparently behaves differently further away. The work clarifies what fine-tuning actually teaches when improving confidence estimates, warning that metacognition learned this way may not generalize. This has direct implications for calibration and hallucination mitigation.

entry.title: When Words Fall Short: Iterative Synergy Between Verbalized Reasoning and Hidden Features for LLM Confidence Estimation

author.name: Yekun Xu, Ante Wang, Jingyi Ren, Xuanyi Chen, Weizhi Ma, Yang Liu

entry.summary: The authors challenge the assumption that verbalized self-reported confidence is the best approach, showing empirically that a dedicated estimator leveraging internal representations substantially outperforms verbalized confidence. They propose IPoET, an iterative training framework that combines verbalized reasoning traces with hidden-state features for better confidence estimation.

entry.title: Measuring Collapse and Correction in Homogeneous-Panel LLM Debate

author.name: Xin Li, Mengbing Liu, Chau Yuen

entry.summary: The authors introduce an auditable protocol recording each homogeneous multi-agent LLM debate as a transition ledger over collapse, correction, onset, and signed intervention utility, applied to 6,925 MMLU-Pro debates. This separates cases where debate rescues a wrong majority from cases where it destroys a correct one, revealing tradeoffs in probe-gated interventions.

entry.title: Epistemic Policy Divergence in Multi-Turn LLM Contamination: A Protocol-Gradient Investigation

author.name: Fahrell Giovanny, Geby Bayuningtyas, Sahrul Mukharom, Hafiz Budi Firmansyah

entry.summary: This paper studies session-level contamination, where false premises injected into earlier conversation turns are adopted as fact by LLMs. The authors introduce five contamination protocols along a source-authority gradient and evaluate GPT-5.4 Mini, Gemini-3.1 Flash-Lite, and GLM-4.5-Air across ten knowledge domains at temperature zero over 22,500 turns, with a human-validated automated judge (Cohen's kappa 0.901). Notably, GPT-5.4 Mini showed zero premise adoptions across all 500 sessions, suggesting a content-independent refusal policy, with token-level probing used to examine the underlying decision margins.

entry.title: InfoEdit: Probing Global Layout Reasoning in Infographic Editing

author.name: Cheng Yang, Chufan Shi, Huijuan Wang, Bo Shui, Yaokang Wu, Muzi Tao, Yibo Yan, Xuezhe Ma, Taylor Berg-Kirkpatrick

entry.summary: Introduces InfoEdit, a benchmark of 1,000 infographics with 4,000 editing instructions designed to test reflow, the ability of image-editing models to globally adapt surrounding elements when one element is edited. Evaluates eight frontier image editors and finds they struggle with structured visual content compared to natural photographs.

entry.title: Explainable and Generalisable LLM-based Cognitive Decline Detection with Spontaneous Speech

author.name: Ziyun Cui, Wen Wu, Chuan Shi, Shuguang Yang, Xueying Gui, Yan Zheng, Qiong Yang, Haiyan Zhao, Wei-Qiang Zhang, Ji Wu, Yelei Li, Nan Li, Chao Zhang

entry.summary: Builds a bilingual speech LLM framework for explainable screening of Alzheimer's disease and mild cognitive impairment from spontaneous speech, processing raw audio directly rather than relying on error-prone ASR to preserve prosodic cues. Uses a newly collected PUTH-AD hospital dataset alongside open-source corpora.

entry.title: Double-Edged Sword of Mediated Visibility: How Visual Framing Undermines Congresswomen's Perceived Competence

author.name: Bryce J. Dietrich (Purdue University), Hyein Ko (Case Western Reserve University), Myriam Shiran (The Ohio State University)

entry.summary: Analyzing 695,464 image-text segments from CNN and Fox News (2011-2021) with facial recognition, the study finds congresswomen appear disproportionately in split-screen rather than solo shots. Two pre-registered experiments with 6,220 participants show split-screen framing reduces perceived competence of congresswomen in static frames but not congressmen, with the penalty disappearing in dynamic video.

entry.title: SGA-Flow-GRPO: Spatial Gradient-Guided Credit Assignment for Flow-GRPO

author.name: Yunkai Yang, Yudong Zhang, Xinying Chen, Bin Luo, Jienan Lyu, Kunquan Zhang, Weitao Wan, Runmin Dong

entry.summary: This work improves Flow-GRPO reinforcement learning for flow-based generative models by reformulating transition-level log-likelihood into token-wise representations aligned with Diffusion Transformer latents, enabling spatial gradient-guided credit assignment. Standard Flow-GRPO applies a uniform scalar advantage across denoising steps and spatial dimensions, which the authors show leads to sub-optimal policy updates.

entry.title: OmniSmartHome: A Multimodal Reasoning Benchmark for Smart-Home Agents

author.name: Jihoo Jung, Suho Yoo, Jeongsoo Choi, Hyebin Cho, Tae Wook Haam, Hyeonggon Ryu, Sumin Park, Joon Son Chung

entry.summary: OmniSmartHome is a multimodal benchmark for smart-home agents in which each spoken user request is paired with surrounding visual and spatial-audio context, since real users leave requests underspecified in language alone. It includes 1,360 synthetic and 272 real-world episodes, moving beyond existing text-only smart-home benchmarks. This addresses a real gap for evaluating embodied and ambient assistants that must disambiguate instructions using what the user sees, hears, or points at.

entry.title: RCVLA: 4D Radar-Grounded Semantic Reasoning and Trajectory Arbitration for Autonomous Driving

author.name: Lianqing Zheng, Xiaokai Bai, Yixuan Luo, Runwei Guan, Minghao Liu, Zhiqiang Wei, Hui-liang Shen, Xichan Zhu, Zhixiong Ma

entry.summary: Proposes a radar-camera vision-language-action framework for autonomous driving with two stages: radar-grounded semantic reasoning (RCVLA-Sem) and trajectory arbitration (RCVLA-Plan). It contributes two large datasets, Cap4DR with 86,016 radar-image-text samples for alignment pretraining and OmniHD-QA with 520,161 QA pairs for instruction tuning.

entry.title: Progressive Risk Estimation for Accident Anticipation

author.name: Samet Hicsonmez, Eray \c{C}akar, Nermin Samet, Fatma G\"uney

entry.summary: PRE-ACT reformulates accident anticipation from binary classification into modeling a continuously evolving risk signal that rises as a crash approaches, enforcing temporal ordering and distance-to-accident awareness to suppress false alarms. It also introduces a Separation Score metric for evaluating global behavior of predicted risk curves, showing gains on MM-AU and Nexar benchmarks.

entry.title: Structured Residual Connectivity Matters for Diffusion Transformers

author.name: Yuhe Liu, Xinyin Ma, Gongfan Fang, Songhua Liu, Xinchao Wang

entry.summary: The paper analyzes residual connections in diffusion transformers, finding latent preferences for early-layer feature reuse and symmetric layer guidance, and transforms the uniform residual stream into an active retrieval mechanism with structured connectivity optimized for denoising. This contrasts with the hand-crafted skip connections of U-Net diffusion models.

entry.title: Relevance Does Not Imply Applicability: Experience Activation for Personal GUI Agents

author.name: Fuyao Zhang, Xuan Wang, Zherui Li, Jiaming Zhang, Longtao Huang, Wei Yang Bryan Lim

entry.summary: Shows that retrieved interaction history in personal GUI agents strongly helps only the first decision in an episode, offering little benefit across the remaining 90% of steps and weak guidance on proactive suggestions. It proposes experience activation, distinguishing task-relevant experience from action-applicable knowledge on the current screen. This is an insightful empirical finding with implications for memory-augmented agent design.

entry.title: Concept Score Relearning: A Unified Cross-Architecture Attack on Concept Erasure

author.name: Hong Xi Tae, Jiaming Zhang, Wenwen He, Xuan Wang, Wei Yang Bryan Lim

entry.summary: This paper introduces Concept Score Relearning (CSR), a parameter-level attack that reactivates erased concepts in text-to-image models across both U-Net noise-prediction and flow-matching Transformer paradigms, using each model's native prediction space and requiring no external target-concept dataset. It demonstrates that concept erasure defenses evaluated only against architecture-specific relearning attacks are not robust.

entry.title: ForeFly: A Dual-Horizon World Action Model for Aerial Vision-Language Navigation

author.name: Kunhui Wang, Xintong Zhang, Junyu Gao, Changsheng Xu

entry.summary: ForeFly is a dual-horizon latent world action model for aerial vision-language navigation that predicts both a proximal future for local continuity and a route-critical far future for long-range guidance, with horizon-specific foresight queries primed from visual memory. This addresses long UAV trajectories where reactive single-horizon policies fail. It combines world modeling with instruction following for UAVs.

entry.title: SCOPD: Sparse-Context On-Policy Self-Distillation for Efficient Vision-Language Models

author.name: Ahmadreza Jeddi, Enming Zhang, Jasper Gerigk, Hakki Karaimer, Mozhgan Nasr Azadani, Jiayun Luo, Minh Ngoc Le, Gholamali Aminian, Hugo Buurmeijer, Yongchao Chen, Leonid Sigal, Igor Gilitschenski, Konstantinos G. Derpanis, Marco Pavone, Babak Taati

entry.summary: This paper challenges the common explanation that token pruning in vision-language models fails because task-relevant visual information is irreversibly lost. Through a Pass@K analysis on pruned representations, the authors show useful evidence often remains accessible but is used unreliably, a phenomenon they call the representation-utilization gap, and propose SCOPD, an on-policy self-distillation framework that trains models to better exploit sparse visual contexts.

entry.title: MaLiang-Harness: A Programmable Path to Image and Video Generation

author.name: Haoyu Zhao, Zihao Zhang, Xudong Wang, Jiaxi Gu, Zuxuan Wu, Yu-Gang Jiang, Shuicheng Yan

entry.summary: Introduces the Program-to-Visual (P2V) gap, where generated code executes correctly but fails to satisfy the requested visual composition, appearance, or motion, and presents MaLiang-Harness, a framework organizing MLLM-driven visual generation into a persistent loop of construction, inspection, and revision. The framework defines a Persistent Executable Generation (PEG) state that keeps programs, history, and verification aligned to a common revision reference.

entry.title: Preference-Guided Adaptation for Open-Vocabulary Semantic Segmentation via Prompt Disagreement

author.name: Hyun-Kurl Jang, Jihun Kim, Kuk-Jin Yoon

entry.summary: This paper proposes adapting open-vocabulary semantic segmentation models to specialized domains (medical, remote sensing, industrial) using only binary preferences instead of costly dense pixel masks. The key insight is that different prompt templates yield systematically different segmentations for the same image, and this prompt disagreement can be harvested as free preference supervision for adaptation.

entry.title: What Visual Generators Need from Teachers: Rethinking Representation Alignment

author.name: Yongcong Wang, Hingchin Chen, Mingyu Fan, Shuo Jiang, Teer Zhang, Yucong Sun, Zijia Wang, Yiming Lu, Chengchao Shen

entry.summary: This work analyzes representation alignment for diffusion transformer training, finding that alignment helps where the student cannot linearly recover the teacher's features rather than where features already match. It reveals a hierarchy-filling dynamic where the student fills the teacher's feature hierarchy bottom-up and stalls near the top even after 400K steps, informing which teacher layer to align and for how long.

entry.title: What Makes World Action Models Generalize? An Empirical Study of Test-Time Future Modeling

author.name: Renping Zhou, Zanlin Ni, Zihao Fan, Guohao Fu, Zeyu Liu, Hao Shi, Jie Zhang, Chi Bene Chen, Yang Yue, Xueyang Fu, Gao Huang

entry.summary: This empirical study dissects whether world action models must generate future predictions at inference time, comparing explicit WAMs that denoise future frames with latent WAMs that discard them for speed. Using matched backbones, data, and budgets, it finds latent WAMs match explicit ones in-distribution but lose the generalization benefits (environmental perturbation robustness, data efficiency, task generalization) that motivated WAMs in the first place. This is a valuable clarifying result for the rapidly growing world-model-for-robotics literature.

entry.title: Beyond Saying Less: Fine-Grained Alignment for Informative and Faithful Vision-Language Models

author.name: Xingming Long, Jie Zhang, Yuecong Min, Shiguang Shan, Xilin Chen

entry.summary: The authors identify a failure mode of on-policy RL for reducing object hallucination in VLMs: without fine-grained rewards, models cheat by saying less, dropping valid claims. They propose a fine-grained alignment framework coupling dense object-presence/absence reward signals with precise algorithmic credit assignment. Directly diagnosing and fixing a reward-hacking shortcut makes this valuable for VLM alignment methodology.

entry.title: ReSS: Residual-Restoring Sparse Attention for 3D Vision Transformers

author.name: Yongsung Kim, Jaehoon Lee, Minjun Park, Wooseok Song, Hun Hwangbo, Sungroh Yoon

entry.summary: ReSS targets the computational bottleneck of global attention in 3D vision transformers like VGGT. The authors show that attention probability poorly predicts behavioral change when a block is removed — the cause of performance collapse under sparsification — and propose recasting block selection as restoring residuals, improving sparse attention quality at high sparsity.

entry.title: Residual Transferability in Neural Image Watermarking

author.name: Ziping Dong, Qi Li, Xinchao Wang

entry.summary: The paper formalizes residual transferability (RT), a metric quantifying how easily watermark-bearing residuals extracted from watermarked images can be forged onto unrelated content. Through controlled interventions, the authors show that architectural design, not training-side variations, is the dominant factor in a watermarking system's vulnerability to this attack. This provides security-relevant design guidance for building watermarking systems resistant to transfer attacks.

entry.title: Revision, Not Restart: Revisable Visual Plans for Closed-Loop World-Action Models

author.name: Pengyiang Liu, Junbo Niu, Wenhao Zheng, Xinchen Chen, Canyu Li, Zhongyue Shi, Jiahao Xie, Si Liu

entry.summary: RTP (Revisable Temporal Planning) maintains predicted visual futures as persistent action conditions for world-action models and revises them after execution feedback instead of replanning from scratch. Its learned revision bridge resumes an intermediate state from visual generation and adapts the continuation to current observations, with an adaptive policy choosing among retention, bridge revision, or fresh replanning.

entry.title: HapticWorld: an Interactive World Simulator with Real-time Torque Feedback

author.name: Shaoting Peng, Litian Liang, Yixuan Wang, Ming Yang, Katherine Driggs-Campbell, Mark Cutkosky, James Jingxi Xu

entry.summary: HapticWorld is an interactive world simulator that predicts joint torques alongside observations and renders them back to a human operator in real time, closing the haptic loop during data collection for contact-rich manipulation. It addresses the scalability gap between vision-only learned world simulators and force-annotated data scarcity.

entry.title: MemTransfer: Benchmarking Memory Beyond Matched Experience in Embodied Decision-Making

author.name: Haiming Tang, Xianjie Dai, Gujie Shao, Zuyi Guo, Jingguang Li, Kailang Ma, Yihong Tang, Heye Huang

entry.summary: A benchmark comparing six memory representations under a shared frozen VLM policy across 100 navigation cases in a simulated warehouse, with three controlled comparisons varying start pose, route availability, and history relevance. Shows large success drops when test conditions differ from demonstration starts.

entry.title: Towards Kinematic Actionable Infeasibility Detection in Motion Planning

author.name: Aayush Rath, Lakshya Jindal, Antony Thomas

entry.summary: A geometry-driven framework for certifying motion-planning infeasibility via resolution-dependent analysis of configuration-space topology, using signed distance fields to trace obstacle-induced separating manifolds, enabling both infeasibility detection and identification of why plans fail.

entry.title: Beyond State-as-Action: Exploiting Command-State Discrepancy for Robot Imitation Learning

author.name: Peiyan Li, Yueran Tao, Enhao Zhang, Zhixuan Zhao, Chenghao Yue, Hao Wang, Lei Lv, Wentao Zhao, Jiahao Chen, Xin Liu, Kangyao Huang, Yu Luo, Huaping Liu

entry.summary: Investigates when command-state discrepancy in imitation learning carries control demands not captured by measured motion, and proposes Command-State Discrepancy Weighting (CSDW), which combines subsequent progress, persistent unmet demand, and demand changes into continuous weights for command supervision across three real-robot tasks.

entry.title: Beyond Retrieval Relevance: Scene-Grounded Risk Entailment for Vision-Language Driving

author.name: Jiaxin Liu, Ruilin Yu, Liang Peng, Jingkai Wang, Chengxiang Zhao, Zhenxin Zhu, Bing Wang, Guang Chen, Hangjun Ye, Hong Wang, Jun Li

entry.summary: This paper addresses the gap between retrieving a relevant safety rule and verifying that it actually applies to the current driving scene. The authors introduce a Driving-Risk Knowledge Graph and an SWRL logical reasoning stage that derives events and directed risk relations from structured perception facts before a vision-language model makes driving decisions. This makes the justification for risk conclusions explicit and verifiable rather than implicit in the VLM.

entry.title: Model-Informed Safe Reinforcement Learning for Bipedal Locomotion via Step-to-Step Prediction

author.name: Victor Paredes, Ayonga Hereid

entry.summary: The authors propose a model-informed reinforcement learning framework for humanoid bipedal locomotion anchored to the analytical ALIP (Angular Momentum Linear Inverted Pendulum) template. They derive a step-to-step safety certificate via a discrete exponential control barrier function, used both as a training-time shaping signal and a runtime action filter that minimally adjusts swing-foot placement. This combines the interpretability of model-based gait generation with the adaptability of RL, with full-order safety claims.

entry.title: DexWeave: Learning Dexterous Humanoid Loco-Manipulation from Human Demonstrations

author.name: Naichuan Sun, Haotian Shen, Yizhang Zhang, Luying Feng, Haoze Wang, Yuanbo Xiangli, Yaochu Jin, Peidong Liu

entry.summary: DexWeave is a unified framework for learning dexterous humanoid loco-manipulation from human demonstrations, combining interaction-consistent motion retargeting with anatomy-aware whole-body policy learning. It uses a two-stage retargeting procedure to handle embodiment differences that distort coupling between body motion, wrist placement, and finger articulation. The work addresses a key gap in transferring not just motion but interaction structure from humans to humanoid robots.

entry.title: Agent Priors-guided Policy Learning

author.name: Puming Jiang, Tianrun Hu, Haozhe Du, Yibo Li, Zhiwei Xue, Xinhu Li, Harold Soh

entry.summary: This paper targets few-demonstration robot learning that requires both compositional generalization (recombining skills) and skill generalization (policies working in new situations). Its key idea is to use each skill policy's structural prior, which states what a behavior depends on, as part of the interface between the composition layer and the skills, closing an information gap that arises when skills are referenced only by names or symbolic descriptions. From Harold Soh's group, it offers a principled fix for skill composition failures.

entry.title: Humanoid Loco-Manipulation With Discrete VLA Model

author.name: Wenxin Shao, Siqi Chai, Kun Li, Kerou Zhang, Xinzhou Jiang, Wei Xu, Qiang Liu
