entry.summary: Revamps scene coordinate regression for outdoor LiDAR localization, replacing scene-classification-based global embeddings that fail to discriminate nearby locations and fixing uniform feature sampling that propagates features from dynamic objects and unstable regions. The result is map-free, robust localization without explicit 3D maps. Relevant to autonomous navigation and SLAM systems.

entry.title: TC-ADA: One-Shot Active Domain Adaptation for Semantic Segmentation

author.name: Weihao Yan, Yeqiang Qian, Yueyuan Li, Tao Li, Chunxiang Wang, Ming Yang

entry.summary: TC-ADA studies a practical one-shot image-level active domain adaptation setting for driving-scene semantic segmentation, selecting and densely annotating a fixed target subset in a single round before uninterrupted adaptation. It uses vision-foundation-model representations in stage 1 for complete-image acquisition and a target-calibrated adaptation stage.

entry.title: Fill2SR: Repurposing Inpainting Diffusion Transformers for Real-World Super-Resolution

author.name: Xingfu Yi, Xiaoxue Yu

entry.summary: Fill2SR repurposes a masked-inpainting diffusion transformer for real-world super-resolution by writing the low-quality observation into the native masked-image slot under a full-image mask, avoiding extra ControlNet-style branches and using LoRA-only tuning. A companion offline pipeline (RCDT) distills degradation descriptors from unpaired real images. It reduces memory and compute versus spatial-conditioning approaches.

entry.title: VastMAT: A Large-Scale Multi-Category Benchmark for Multi-Animal Tracking

author.name: Zhizhen Li, Zan Wang, Huidong Peng, Bohan Tan, Shimin Shan, Yu Liu, Liang Peng

entry.summary: VastMAT is a large-scale multi-animal tracking benchmark with 2,947 videos, over one million annotated frames across 27.85 hours, covering 337 animal categories with 3.66 million bounding boxes and extensive within-video instance associations. It fills a gap left by pedestrian- and vehicle-focused MOT benchmarks.

entry.title: ECHO: Event-Augmented Context with Hindsight and Outlook for Wrist-Only Manipulation

author.name: Xinyue Wang, Yicheng Jiang, Zesen Gan, Junhao He, Jiaxu Wang, Junhao Li, Jingtao Zhang, Tianlun He, Jianan Wang, Isabel Guan, Qiming Shao

entry.summary: ECHO is a wrist-only latent world action model that fuses event camera signals with RGB for robotic manipulation, encoding wrist-mounted event data into compact motion representations providing temporal and spatial context. It addresses placement limits of fixed cameras and the loss of static scene content in wrist-mounted views using hindsight and outlook mechanisms. Event cameras offer high dynamic range that mitigates RGB degradation under extreme exposure.

entry.title: Lagrangian--Hamiltonian Flows for Video Prediction and Image Generation: A Symplectic Perspective

author.name: Jiawei Hu

entry.summary: LHFM is a geometric framework for image dynamics grounded in symplectic geometry and geometric quantization, representing images as exact Lagrangian graphs evolving via image-dependent Hamiltonian flows. LHFM-V achieves the lowest reported FLOP count among comparable recurrent video prediction models, and LHFM-I shows compatibility with flow matching for image generation.

entry.title: Inertia-Corrected Newton Method For Generalized Nash Equilibria in Dynamic Games with Optimality Verification

author.name: Zhiyuan Zhang, Panagiotis Tsiotras

entry.summary: The paper proposes an efficient numerical method to verify second-order sufficient conditions for local Generalized Nash Equilibria by connecting the inertia of the agent KKT matrix with positive definiteness of the reduced Hessian. An inertia-corrected update step helps Newton solvers avoid converging to non-Nash saddle points, supporting reliable multi-agent MPC.

entry.title: Repair Before You Fuse: Frozen-Host Adaptation for Corrupted-but-Present Sensors

author.name: Gia-Huy Thai, Quang-Thinh Ly, Anh-Minh Phan, Tuan Dang

entry.summary: This paper introduces Boundary Feature Repair (BFR), a frozen-host adaptation framework that learns task-supervised residual corrections at the modality interfaces of camera-LiDAR detectors when sensors are present but unreliable. Variants repair camera features, align LiDAR candidates, or compose both, with zero-initialized per-channel scales guaranteeing an exact identity before optimization so only repair modules train. It addresses robustness to degraded sensing without retraining the host detector.

entry.title: AI Harness: Certification under Proposal-Conditioned Information for Foundation-Model Agents

author.name: Hailin Zhong, Shengxin Zhu

entry.summary: The paper formalizes foundation-model agents as emitting semantic proposals that are both action candidates and history-conditioned observations, showing that collapsing this structure into a state-only model can preserve proposal coverage while destroying certifiability of safe interventions. It characterizes when the collapse is lossless via viability-kernel analysis in finite robust interfaces.

entry.title: PINNMorph: Evolving Online Adaptation Policies for Physics-Informed Neural Networks

author.name: Xu Yang, Mingyang Yu, Jun Zhang, Keqian Li, Jing Xu

entry.summary: Proposes PINNMorph, an online adaptation framework for physics-informed neural networks that uses LLM-guided policy evolution over a population of state-conditioned adaptation policies mapping execution diagnostics to interventions on network topology, representation, and training. This addresses the fact that PINN training behavior changes substantially during optimization while architectures are usually fixed beforehand. It connects evolutionary search with LLM reasoning for scientific ML.

entry.title: Overwhelmed by Choice: Studying LLM Decision Making at Scale

author.name: Yu-Chi Lin, Aryan Seth, Anshul Aravind, Eugene Lee, Tanmay Parekh, Nanyun Peng, Kai-Wei Chang

entry.summary: This systematic study evaluates LLMs as the number of competing candidates in multiple-choice-style decisions grows, finding substantial accuracy degradation across tasks, prompting strategies, and model scales that long-context retrieval limitations cannot fully explain. Two failure patterns are identified: gold-margin collapse, where the score gap between correct answer and strongest distractor shrinks, and a second pattern not fully described here. The results question whether conclusions from small-candidate benchmarks generalize to large candidate spaces.

entry.title: Precision As You Need: Stochastic Computing Is a Dense Adaptive Quantizer

author.name: Haoran Jin, Kangqi Zhang, Jirong Yang, Barry Lyu, Qiuyi Ding, Ruijie Gao, Nathan Bleier

entry.summary: This paper revisits stochastic computing as a dense adaptive quantizer for transformer inference, where precision is controlled by bit-stream length and each multiplication is a single AND/XNOR gate, circumventing the fixed-width format limits of accelerators. The authors build a GPU library emulating SC matrix multiplication and evaluate end-to-end on vision tasks. The work offers a hardware-level path to fine-grained precision control beyond INT4/INT8 quantization.

entry.title: LiveOption: Evaluating LLM Agents in Structured Option Trading with Nonlinear Payoffs

author.name: Haochen Luo, Yifan Li, Binh Minh An, Xiaolong Luo, Zhengzhao Lai, Yuan Zhang, Chen Liu

entry.summary: LiveOption is an evaluation framework for LLM agents in option trading, formulated as structured sequential decision-making with nonlinear payoffs, multi-leg strategy construction, execution and capital constraints, and a reproducible environment with standardized interaction protocols. It moves beyond equity directional prediction to capture the structural complexity of derivative markets. This fills a genuine evaluation gap in financial agentic AI.

entry.title: OpenFC: Learning Verification Policies towards Open-Search Fact Checking

author.name: Xinming Wang, Kaixiang Qiu, Yansong Lin, Chunji Lv, Yi Chen, Boran Wang, Hong-Ming Yang, Xu-Yao Zhang

entry.summary: Frames open-search fact checking as a sequential decision problem and trains Qwen3-8B as a unified next-action controller over reasoning, evidence acquisition, and stopping, using a two-stage pipeline with a stepwise-calibrated cold start. This replaces scattered, hand-pipelined modules with a learned task-specific verification policy.

entry.title: Robust Biomolecular Complex Design Across Protein Conformational Landscapes

author.name: Qingyuan Zeng, Zongqi Xu, Anglin Liu, Ziqi Gong, Pengxiang Cai, Zixin Guan, Yunan Chen, Sen Gao, Min Zhou, Jintai Chen

entry.summary: Introduces FlexEvo, a model-agnostic inference-time evolutionary framework that adapts structure-based design candidates from a single target conformation to improve compatibility with alternative natural conformations, cast as geometry-constrained bi-objective optimization balancing input-state interactions against cross-state robustness. No retraining or conformational ensemble is required.

entry.title: Large Language Models for Structured Clinical Data Analysis: Dual-Agent Grounding and Validation

author.name: Erfan D. Dehkalani, Seetha Shankaran, Abbot R. Laptook, C. Michael Cotten, P. Ellen Grant, Yangming Ou

entry.summary: CLEAR-Med is a dual-agent framework for natural-language analysis of structured clinical data: one agent translates questions to SQL and drafts answers, while deterministic checks plus a cross-provider Validation Agent accept, request one bounded repair, or abstain. Evaluated as a bounded selective pipeline on a 25-query benchmark over a harmonized 21-site neonatal database.

entry.title: CoeF-SFL: Preserving Collaborative Server-Client Learning with Enhanced Communication Efficiency

author.name: Junwoo Bae, Jin-Hyun Ahn

entry.summary: The paper identifies a fundamental flaw in communication-efficient split federated learning: auxiliary client-side networks make clients optimize a local objective that diverges from the end-to-end objective. CoeF-SFL retains the end-to-end objective while cutting communication overhead, using compensated feedback without auxiliary networks.

entry.title: Does Model Uncertainty Track Human Ambiguity? Evidence from Multi-Annotator Vision Benchmarks

author.name: Manya Singh, Arjun Pakrashi

entry.summary: Using FER+ and CIFAR-10H with multiple human annotations, the study tests whether vision model uncertainty (softmax confidence, entropy) and predictive multiplicity correlate with human disagreement on ambiguous instances. Eight pretrained models across three architectures are evaluated to assess human-model alignment on genuinely ambiguous data.

entry.title: SkillRubric: Co-Evolving Actor Guidance and Evaluator Rubrics for Multimodal Agents

author.name: Bingqing Jiang, Guoxi Zhang, Jasper Wang, Auric Wang, Bingning Wang, Tianyi Lin, Zichao Yu, Yujin Han, Ziye Ma, Difan Zou

entry.summary: SkillRubric represents each distilled skill through aligned actor guidance and evaluator rubrics that co-evolve during training, providing dense intermediate supervision for multimodal agent policy optimization instead of sparse outcome rewards. The insight is that a well-structured skill specifies both how to act and what success looks like.

entry.title: Simulating Respondents, Not Single Questions: Coherent Survey Generation with Large Language Models

author.name: Ji Huang, Mengfei Li, Shuai Shao

entry.summary: Proposes FR-LLM, which fine-tunes two specialized LLMs to simulate survey respondents: a marginal model for per-item response distributions and a respondent-level autoregressive model capturing dependencies across answers. A marginal-constrained joint approach ensures coherent preferences across a full questionnaire rather than accurate but incoherent single-item distributions.

entry.title: VD-DeepStack: Bridging Visual Comparison and Language Reasoning for Few-Shot Anomaly Detection

author.name: Mengyang Zhao, Zhuolin He, Haiyang Yu, Yuxuan Liang, Yifang Xu, Yuchuan Wu, Xiaolei Chen, Zhengtao Yao, Fan Shi, Yang Liu, Bin Li, Xiangyang Xue

entry.summary: VD-DeepStack conditions language reasoning in large vision-language models on explicit query-reference visual differences, fusing DINO features into the LVLM visual hierarchy and constructing dense difference representations. This addresses the gap where abstract chain-of-thought descriptions underrepresent fine-grained visual differences in few-shot anomaly detection. The approach is relevant to industrial inspection and multimodal reasoning.

entry.title: TermJudge: A Document-Level Metric Judging, Not Counting, Terminology in Machine Translation Evaluation

author.name: Nicolas Dahan (ISIR, ALMAnaCH), Fran{\cc}ois Yvon (MLIA, ISIR), Rachel Bawden (ALMAnaCH)

entry.summary: TermJudge is a document-level terminology metric for machine translation that assigns interpretable verdicts per term occurrence: glossary-conforming terms are handled deterministically while divergences are assessed via a two-step LLM-as-judge procedure distinguishing genuine errors from valid human-like variation. It is validated against expert error annotations and MQM scores. This fixes a real flaw in reference-counting terminology metrics.

entry.title: Towards Reliable AI Data Scientists: Data Agents with Workflow Harnesses

author.name: Huachi Zhou, Yujing Zhang, Jiahe Du, Jiacheng Cai, Zijin Hong, Chuang Zhou, Zheng Yuan, Qinggang Zhang, Qing Li, Xiao Huang

entry.summary: A survey offering a harness-centric taxonomy of Data Agents for the end-to-end data science lifecycle, organized around five functional stages: perception, planning, execution, verification, and repair. It identifies 15 distinct technical approaches, from data structure probing to data state reconstruction, and discusses reliability challenges.

entry.title: Hyper Algorithm Design Agent: Evolving Learnable Optimizer from Zero

author.name: Zipei Yu, Yue-Jiao Gong, Zeyuan Ma, Yuncheng Jiang, Zhiguang Cao

entry.summary: This work treats MetaBBO (meta black-box optimization) design loops as open-ended coding tasks, using an agent to evolve learnable optimizers from zero rather than handcrafting them case by case. This aims to remove human subjectivity from optimizer design and improve both performance ceilings and practical usability.

entry.title: Representation Alignment as a Bottleneck in LLM-Based Retrosynthesis Planning

author.name: Hyunwoo Yoo, Cassie Huang, Haebin Shin, Li Zhang, Gail L. Rosen

entry.summary: The paper argues that LLM failures at SMILES-to-PDDL retrosynthesis planning stem from missing intermediate abstractions rather than insufficient model capacity, and shows that decomposing the task into molecule mapping, reaction mapping, and PDDL generation achieves high success rates where end-to-end approaches fail. This is evidence that representation alignment is a primary bottleneck for LLM symbolic planning in chemistry. It matters because it redirects effort from scaling toward interface design for scientific planning tasks.

entry.title: ChestPheNoT: Deployable, Auditable Label-Status-Evidence Extraction from Radiology Reports

author.name: Kai Yu, Chenyu Zhu, Zaifu Zhan, Meijia Song, Min Zeng, Xiaoyi Chen, Mingquan Lin, Rui Zhang

entry.summary: ChestPheNoT is a compact 0.5-3B parameter language model that jointly extracts finding labels, three-class assertion status, and verbatim supporting evidence spans from chest radiology reports, enabling fully local inference for privacy-constrained clinical settings. It uses hybrid CheXbert-plus-72B silver supervision followed by supervised fine-tuning to overcome scarce expert annotations. The system targets deployability and auditability in real clinical workflows.

entry.title: ROTE: Benchmarking Neural Memorization on Complexity-Controlled Symbolic Sequences

author.name: Xinye Chen, Stefan G\"uttel, Mohammad Mozaffari

entry.summary: ROTE is a benchmarking protocol evaluating symbolic memorization in neural sequence models using sequences whose complexity is regulated by Lempel-Ziv-Welch compression, comparing teacher-forced one-step prediction and closed-loop rollout on withheld symbols. It evaluates gated recurrent, minimal recurrent, attention-based, and hybrid architectures under a shared prediction-and-rollout routine. This provides a principled complexity-controlled instrument for studying memorization versus rule extension, relevant to generalization and copyright-style memorization debates.

entry.title: Communication between Frozen Large Language Models via Prompt Optimization in a Referential Game

author.name: Vivek Anand, Muthu Chandrasekaran, Shiva Chaitanya

entry.summary: This paper studies emergent communication between two frozen LLMs from different providers with different tokenizers playing a referential game, where isolated prompt optimizers rewrite each agent's prompts based on scored interactions. Optimized prompts develop a shared code that generalizes to held-out objects above a no-codebook baseline, including without a shared memory window, and the paper probes the limits of this setting. This extends emergent-communication research to modern frozen LLMs communicating purely through prompts, which is methodologically interesting and low-cost.

entry.title: Presence Is Not Faithfulness: Figurative Vehicle Intrusion in Text-to-Image Generation

author.name: Xiaoyu Ma, Chen Yang, Hao Chen

entry.summary: The paper identifies Figurative Vehicle Intrusion in text-to-image models: a figurative vehicle meant to guide depiction of a tenor instead appears as a visible object, showing that visual presence is not faithfulness and that presence-oriented evaluation misses such errors. It introduces VISTA, a multilingual benchmark of figurative prompts organized by figurative form and mapping mechanism, plus V-Score, a diagnostic QA-based metric. This exposes a systematic failure mode of TTI models on figurative language.

entry.title: EyeVQA: Benchmarking Ophthalmic Vision-Language Models from Recognition to Spatial Grounding

author.name: Gujie Shao, Zixun Xie, Xuechun Xing, Ruixiang Wang, Ziyun Lan, Yanlin Qi, Gangyi Zhang, Yuxin Yang, Dawei Li, Haiming Tang

entry.summary: EyeVQA is a unified visual question answering benchmark for ophthalmic VLM evaluation, built from 21 existing ophthalmic datasets with 20,000 question-answer pairs spanning six disease groups and seven question types, moving beyond disease recognition toward comparative reasoning and fine-grained spatial grounding. It fills a gap in systematically characterizing VLM capabilities in a medical imaging specialty.

entry.title: Shared Worlds, Private Minds: Structured Memory for Long-Form Writing as World Creation

author.name: Qiuyu Tian, Xiaowen Gu, Hang Su, Jianghan Chao, Haojie Yin, Fan Guo, Xin Zhang, Jinjing Shen, Ewing Luo, Youyong Kong, Yingce Xia, Zequn Liu

entry.summary: NarraWorld is a structured memory system for LLM long-form fiction writing that treats memory construction as world creation, deriving four connected views from a shared evidence-grounded graph: world facts, per-character beliefs, open developments, and hypothetical branches. Hierarchical aggregation with atomic closure consolidates events into scenes, plotlines, and plots to keep new writing consistent with established facts. It addresses persistent consistency and implicit dependency recovery in story generation.

entry.title: Adapting Nonstationary Multi-output Gaussian Processes to Bayesian Optimization

author.name: Zikai Xie

entry.summary: The paper examines a mismatch in multi-objective Bayesian optimization where expressive nonstationary multi-output GPs fit training data well but produce unreliable acquisition decisions. MOLRN-BO combines a regularized shared-spectral surrogate with residuals, prequential mean correction, tempered covariance scaling, and Pareto-local qLogEHVI optimization. This bridges the gap between expressive surrogate models and trustworthy BO decisions.

entry.title: Getting Motif-ated: Controllable AI Compositions from Injected Motif Prompts

author.name: Chao Peter Yang, Cynthia Rudin, Yue Jiang, Simon Mak, Stephen Ni-Hahn

entry.summary: MotiGen is a recipe for retrofitting pretrained symbolic music models (like NotaGen) to accept new instruction prompts that inject user motifs, providing control handles without training a foundation model from scratch. This enables musicians to steer classical score generation with specific musical material. It addresses the lack of control in current LLM-style music generation systems.

entry.title: Optimizing H-Graph Hybridization for Diffusion-Guided RRT

author.name: Omer Talmi

entry.summary: This work develops two inference-time diversification strategies for a fixed pretrained DiTree diffusion-based motion planner — factorial diversity over seeds and Diffusion Goal Bias, and refinement-only diversity over refinement strength — combined via H-Graph hybridization on a holonomic AntMaze robot. It exploits the stochastic diversity of diffusion planners at inference time to improve trajectory quality. The approach requires no retraining of the underlying model.

entry.title: \L{}ukasiewicz Neural Networks Extended: Residual Architectures and Crystallization Strategies for Interpretable Rule Extraction

author.name: Carlos Leandro

entry.summary: The paper extends Lukasiewicz many-valued logic neural networks — integer-weight feed-forward networks whose neurons exactly implement logical connectives — with residual architectures and improved crystallization strategies to overcome limitations to shallow networks and small datasets. Training produces interpretable logical formulas rather than black-box models. This advances the exact neural-symbolic correspondence program.

entry.title: SemReward-VL: Semantic Reward-Guided Video-Language Adaptation for Developmental Behavior Assessment

author.name: De Jiang, Shuo Zhang, Kehong Yuan, Hongen Liao

entry.summary: Presents SemReward-VL, which trains a vision-language model to describe item-specific child behaviors from clinical outcomes using a frozen language model as a semantic reward scorer covering agreement, relevance, abstention, and clarity, with GRPO updating LoRA adapters. Evaluated on 13,379 videos across 41 items, it improves aggregate accuracy and per-item recall.

entry.title: Learning Transferable Reaction Mechanisms from Visual Chemical Knowledge

author.name: Yujian Yuan, Jiaxin Xu, Xin Cai, Yufan Chen, Zhichao Tan, Ziqi Zhou, Hanyu Gao

entry.summary: MechaVLM is a visual framework for reaction mechanism prediction that combines transferable chemical representations with external mechanistic knowledge, learning reusable visual features via multiscale chemical grounding and cross-rendering contrastive objectives. It targets transfer to unseen chemistry where familiar mechanisms must apply to unfamiliar molecular structures.

entry.title: From Distributions to Stochastic Processes: Neural Approximation of Measure-Valued Maps

author.name: Yichen Wang, Ziyi Wang, Wenlian Lu, Chenghuang Shen, Jianfeng Liu, Zhengdong Xiao, Longjiu Luo, Qianrong Wang

entry.summary: This work builds an approximation-theoretic framework for learning mappings between probability distributions and extends it to stochastic processes, proving uniform neural approximation guarantees in the 2-Wasserstein metric. It uses finite law statistics, simplex-valued neural maps, and shared atomic output supports to guarantee valid probability measures, with extensions to Hilbert-space laws. It provides theoretical foundations for distribution-to-distribution learning.

entry.title: DEALS: Decentralized Expertise-Aware Load Serving for Multi-Agent LLM Systems

author.name: Jingjuan Huang, Wenbin Wang, Yanchuan Yin, Alvaro Velasquez, Jia Liu

entry.summary: DEALS provides decentralized, expertise-aware load serving for multi-agent LLM systems where agents self-organize and self-evolve on heterogeneous task streams without centralized controllers or LLM-based routers. It avoids the computational cost and coordination overhead of dedicated routing models. This addresses scalability of emerging multi-agent LLM deployments.

entry.title: Augmenting Visual Anomaly Detection with Automated Interpretability

author.name: Antonio De Santis, Arsenio Leo, Marco Brambilla

entry.summary: The paper decomposes PatchCore nearest-normal residuals into sparse features using Sparse Autoencoders, has a multimodal LLM label each feature as anomaly, distractor, or uncertain, and then intervenes in the SAE latent space to suppress distractors and amplify anomaly signals. This improves the precision of visual anomaly detection while adding interpretability. It connects interpretability tooling to industrial inspection.

entry.title: EEG-Fusion: Failure-Informed Source-Free Expert Routing for Robust Motor Imagery EEG Decoding

author.name: Abdul Basit, Saim Rehman, Muhammad Shafique

entry.summary: EEG-Fusion frames source-free motor-imagery EEG decoding as label-free reliability estimation over heterogeneous experts, routing each target subject to a neural, covariance-based, or physiological-feature expert using failure-informed decision-level fusion. It addresses the problem that subject-shifted decoders can become overconfident near-one-class predictors even when average performance looks acceptable. This improves robustness of brain-computer interfaces under source-free deployment.

entry.title: ADPTNet: Adaptive with Prescriptive Timescales Non-Linear SSM for Sequence Modelling

author.name: Matei-Ioan Stan, Oliver Rhodes

entry.summary: ADPTNet is a state-space model inspired by fixed timescales in the auditory cortex, designed to simultaneously satisfy four properties: data adaptivity, long-range dependency capture, GPU parallelizability, and non-linear recurrence for complex reasoning. It is motivated by neuromorphic computing's goal of providing an energy-efficient alternative to Transformers. The work contributes a new architecture in the SSM/alternative-architecture space.

entry.title: Coherence-Aware Distributional Evaluation of Open-Ended Text Generation

author.name: Jinnuo Liu, Junhao Zhu, Weifeng Jiang, Haoming Liu, Hongyi Wen

entry.summary: The paper identifies global coherence as a blind spot in existing open-ended generation metrics, since locally fluent text can be globally contradictory or topically disconnected while preserving token-level statistics, and introduces CHORD, a coherence-sensitive distributional metric operating in hidden-state space. Better evaluation of open-ended generation is a persistent unsolved problem. Contributes both an analysis of metric blind spots and a practical new metric.

entry.title: When Harness Beats Scale, and When Reading Beats Both

author.name: Ivan Bondarenko, Nikolay O. Nikitin

entry.summary: This system paper for the DocSem shared task shows that pipeline architecture mattered far more than model scale for document-grounded quantitative reasoning: Program-of-Thoughts added large gains to a 7B model but almost none to a 72B model, and a 27B model with the full harness matched the 72B at 2.7x fewer parameters and a quarter of the CO2. The authors also honestly analyze why the system succeeded on labeled data but failed on the test set. It offers practical evidence that scaffolding can substitute for scale.

entry.title: SPACE-LoRA: Allocating Activation-Subspace Protection for Continual Learning

author.name: Seunghyun Yoo, Kiseok Kim, Hyeontae Joo, Junyeop Bang, Hwangnam Kim

entry.summary: SPACE-LoRA addresses catastrophic forgetting in LoRA-based sequential task learning by explicitly suppressing additive interference, where new residual adapters produce non-zero responses along input directions critical to old tasks. It allocates activation-subspace protection with bounded capacity for efficient continual adaptation. This refines prior approaches that only constrained parameter updates or learning subspaces.

entry.title: Triangular Resampling for Long-Horizon Motion Generation

author.name: Kunhang Li, Yiyi Cai, Xiangyue Zhang, Fangyuan Tu, Yuhan Wu, Zhixiang Wang, Kaipeng Zhang, Haiyang Liu

entry.summary: Triangular Resampling (TR) is a post-training method for motion diffusion models that mitigates long-horizon error accumulation by extending rollout-based training to partially denoised states, using ground-truth clamping and shared denoising thresholds on replayed samples. It builds on FloodDiffusion's triangular denoising schedule and addresses the train/inference state mismatch in autoregressive motion generation.

entry.title: EviSplat: Preserving Multi-View Evidence in 3D Gaussian Splatting for Open-Vocabulary Segmentation

author.name: Sungho Moon, Kota Shimomura, Junwoo Park, Wonhyeok Choi, Seunghun Lee, Takayoshi Yamashita, Sunghoon Im

entry.summary: EviSplat improves open-vocabulary 3D segmentation on Gaussian Splatting scenes by preserving individual multi-view observation features as evidence rather than consolidating them into language features before a query is known, since pre-query consolidation can suppress query-relevant cues. Evidence is retained for later text-conditional retrieval and segmentation.

entry.title: PEAR: Progressive Evidence-Based AutoResearch for Industrial Search Systems

author.name: Yifan Wang, Shipeng Zhu, Fei Xiong, Yuqin Yang, Yonghui Huang, Kunyao Wu, Yue Wang, Weichao Meng, Yu Gong

entry.summary: Proposes PEAR, an AutoResearch framework for industrial search systems in which agents propose, evaluate, and stack candidate modifications. It addresses non-stationary traffic (where keep-if-better rules mistake transient gains for persistent ones) and combines multiple evaluation fidelity levels from cheap proxies to online validation with evidence-based accumulation.

entry.title: QAM: Quadratic-Accurate Checkpoint Merging via Sequential Consistency

author.name: Shihao Wang, Rui Kong, Xinran Chen, Hui Wu, Qipeng Qian, Jinman Zhao, Jiashu Zhao, Yuchen Li, Jimmy Huang, Dawei Yin

entry.summary: This paper studies how saved training checkpoints can reconstruct the endpoint of a sequential reference schedule, characterizing all convex merges that are second-order accurate via two moment conditions. It also proves an information-theoretic lower bound showing no algorithm using fixed-length gradient-descent history can achieve better than cubic step-size scaling in endpoint error.

entry.title: Semantic Prefix Oracles for LLM Decoding: Contracts and Differential Validation

author.name: Paul Kronlund-Drouault

entry.summary: The work proposes semantic grammar specifications, a declarative formalism attaching semantic constraints (scope, typing, declaration effects) to a context-free grammar executed during Earley parsing for constrained LLM decoding. It introduces safe pruning and dead-end freedom properties with sufficient conditions, plus differential validation of the oracle.

entry.title: FurE: Efficient Instance-Specific 3D Fur Reconstruction without Animal-Fur Datasets

author.name: Srinjay Sarkar, Prakhar Kaushik, Soumava Paul, Alan Yuille

entry.summary: Presents FurE, a strand-based animal fur reconstruction method that recovers editable per-strand grooms from multi-view images using a root-conditioned latent field with a PCA decoder learned from human-hair data, plus fur-thickness cues from Gaussian Frosting and part-based priors. It sidesteps the lack of animal-fur datasets by transferring from human hair.

entry.title: Product-Aware Deterministic Rounding for Quantized Matrix Multiplication

author.name: Piyush Sao, Narasinga Miniskar, Pedro Valero-Lara, Keita Teranishi, Sudip Seal

entry.summary: Studies deterministic product-aware rounding for quantized matrix multiplication, where scalar rounding decisions interact through the product. Using null-space reduction it preserves the relaxed product while leaving at most rank-r fractional decisions, and a conditional-expectation completion yields a polynomial-time algorithm with bounded squared product error relative to the best admissible rounding.

entry.title: What Should We Freeze? Guarded Freezing: Connectivity Shapes the Fine-Tuning of Pretrained Models

author.name: Leonel Aguilar

entry.summary: The paper studies fine-tuning with frozen subnetworks, showing that freezing weights alone is insufficient because updates elsewhere can change inputs to the frozen core. It proposes removal-value, a capacity-based score for selecting what to freeze, and introduces guarded freezing that cuts or accounts for connectivity into frozen regions, preserving substantially more old-task accuracy than the DEFT baseline in CNNs and deriving drift-based corrections for transformers with shared residual streams.

entry.title: When Does Synergy Help Active Feature Acquisition? A PID-Based Study

author.name: Jie Li, Maruf A. Dhali, Hjalmar R. Bouma

entry.summary: SynAFA is a state-dependent active feature acquisition policy combining pairwise joint and conditional information, analyzed through Partial Information Decomposition to distinguish redundant, unique, and synergistic feature contributions. Experiments across five tabular datasets and MNIST-loop show heterogeneous gains, strongest at low budgets on PhysioNet where synergy is verified by permutation tests. This offers a principled account of when interaction-aware AFA helps.

entry.title: Distance-KV: Exploiting Relative Distance for Efficient Long-Context Inference

author.name: Xianpeng Shang, Canbin Huang, Jiang Li, Tian Lan, Qianyi Cai, Xiaojun Quan, Xiangdong Su

entry.summary: The paper finds that KV cache retrieval capability varies substantially with relative token distance even within a single attention head, and introduces Distance-KV, which learns a static retention pattern over the joint space of layers, heads, and relative distances. The pattern is learned offline with the model frozen and reused to prune and compact the KV cache without online importance scoring.

entry.title: UniCache: Task- and Type-Aware KV Cache Compression for Unified Multimodal Models

author.name: Wanqi Yang, Yuexiao Ma, Mei Xie, Xiawu Zheng, Shiwei Liu

entry.summary: UniCache compresses KV caches in unified multimodal models that combine understanding, generation, and editing, recognizing that cache importance varies across tasks, timesteps, and cache types. A single task- and type-aware policy avoids the information loss caused by applying one compression rule across heterogeneous multimodal caches.

entry.title: Clipped or Unclipped? Finite-Sample Trade-offs for Averaged SGD under Heavy-Tailed Noise

author.name: Alexandra Suvorikova, Egor Gladin, Darina Dvinskikh, Artem Agafonov, Mohammad Alkousa, Yuriy Dorn, Vladislav Matyukhin, Alexander Gasnikov

entry.summary: This paper derives finite-sample comparisons of clipped and unclipped Polyak-Ruppert averaged SGD under heavy-tailed noise with finite p-th moments. It shows that for p greater than 2 the Gaussian term can dominate the unclipped deviation bound, so clipping may not improve the leading order, and it obtains logarithmic rather than polynomial dependence on inverse failure probability at p equals 2. The results give practitioners explicit conditions for when clipping helps.

entry.title: Feasible Flow Matching for Graph Reconstruction via Within-Sampling Primal-Dual Guidance

author.name: Haoming Chen, Nicolas Zilberstein, Santiago Paternain, Santiago Segarra

entry.summary: The paper extends Prior-Informed Flow Matching for graph reconstruction with structural side information (degree bounds, triangle counts, edge density) by adding Lagrange multipliers that evolve along each sampling trajectory to correct constraint violations without retraining. It proves the sampler inherits permutation equivariance and bounds expected terminal constraint slack. This yields constrained generative modeling for graphs with guarantees.

entry.title: ILP-BO: Integer Linear Programming-Based Black-Box Optimization

author.name: Hyakka Nakada, Shu Tanaka

entry.summary: ILP-BO transforms kernel-based surrogate acquisition optimization in discrete-domain black-box optimization into an integer linear program, guaranteeing global optimality in candidate selection where standard Bayesian optimization uses non-guaranteed nonlinear or heuristic search. It is framed as a quasi-Bayesian optimization framework.

entry.title: When Does Backpropagating Through Policy Memory Matter? Physical Credit, Optimizer Updates, and Observability

author.name: Xingjian Li, Yi Han, Jianhua Z. Huang

entry.summary: The paper empirically dissects when cutting backpropagation through stored policy memory (as in Transformer-XL key-value caches and truncated BPTT) matters, holding forward computation fixed and varying only derivative edges. In a vessel-trajectory model and quadrotor tracking policy, detaching the cache shrank gradients dramatically under full observability but barely changed them otherwise.

entry.title: MTLiquid: Enabling Efficient Multi-Task Learning using Liquid Neural Networks for Lightweight Healthcare Monitoring Systems

author.name: Rachmad Vidya Wicaksana Putra, Fahad Abdul Rauf, Muhammad Shafique

entry.summary: MTLiquid applies continuous-time neural networks (liquid neural networks) to healthcare monitoring with irregularly sampled physiological signals, adding multi-task capability so a single network solves multiple detection and prediction tasks simultaneously for efficiency. This targets lightweight, resource-constrained clinical monitoring systems.

entry.title: Optimal Transport Dropout for Structured Predictive Uncertainty

author.name: Giacomo Lorenzon, Francesco Regazzoni

entry.summary: Optimal Transport Dropout (OTD) jointly learns the predictive mapping and the law of latent perturbations in Monte Carlo dropout, replacing the usual a priori, coordinate-factorized masking with a learned optimal transport-based perturbation. This yields structured predictive uncertainty without training ensembles or inferring posteriors.

entry.title: Scalable Attribution and Control of Model Behavior During Training

author.name: Sleem Abdelghafar

entry.summary: This paper tackles attributing individual training examples' behavioral contributions when batch members produce similar changes, using mutual information that accounts for within-batch interference. It shows this quantity is a logarithmic function of Behavioral Gradient Uniqueness (BGU) and operationalizes the scores in a practical algorithm, Batch-Space Ghost (BS-Ghost).

entry.title: ASTRA: ADMM-Accelerated Topology Reconfiguration for Dynamic Satellite Constellations

author.name: Jo\~ao Norberto, Ricardo Ferreira, Cl\'audia Soares

entry.summary: ASTRA is a theoretically grounded online learning framework for dynamically reconfiguring satellite constellation topologies, combining an ADMM-based offline solver with efficient online gradient and conditional-gradient updates. It provides regret-style guarantees while making constrained updates computationally practical under realistic, non-uniform constellation assumptions.

entry.title: Beyond One Epoch: Uncertainty-Weighted Sensitivity Regularization for Recommendation Models

author.name: Richard Lettich, Shagun Gupta

entry.summary: The paper analyzes the one-epoch phenomenon in recommendation models via violation of the prequential principle and introduces self-influence asymmetry: later-epoch labels displace embeddings that the shared consumer then exploits, hurting generalization. Using an exact scalar model and local influence analysis, it derives an uncertainty-weighted sensitivity regularization to mitigate the effect.

entry.title: Agentic High-Dimensional Bayesian Optimization with Hypothesis- and Evidence-Guided Search

author.name: Zhixuan Gao, Ke Xue, Rongxi Tan, Ming Chen, Chao Qian

entry.summary: The paper shows that recent LLM-based and agentic Bayesian optimization methods fail to remain reliable in the high-dimensional regime, where choosing modeling assumptions and search geometry matters as much as where to evaluate. It introduces HERA, a Hypothesis- and Evidence-guided Research Agent that adapts modeling assumptions and search decisions during optimization runs.

entry.title: Livin' on a Prior: Likelihood Score Approximation for Inverse Problems

author.name: Rostislav Makarov, Tal Peer, Danilo de Oliveira, Timo Gerkmann

entry.summary: LSA is a generative framework for inverse problems that keeps a pretrained unconditional prior fixed and learns an observation-conditioned model approximating the likelihood score from paired samples, spanning both known and unknown degradation regimes. It is built within a conditional stochastic-interpolant framework and is trainable in the stylized setting of few paired examples.

entry.title: Shaping Persistent Representations from Independent Interactions

author.name: Ji Dai, Quan Fang, Junyu Gao, Rongfeng Guo, Haoyan Rong, YipingHuang, Yongxi Li

entry.summary: Introduces SPRII, a training principle for world models that uses relations between interactions (e.g., trajectories from the same system) as weak supervision for learning persistent context without property labels. Two composable components encourage the learner to organize persistent information into reusable context while retaining the native predictive objective.

entry.title: FestDPO: Few-step Generator Alignment with Direct Preference Optimization

author.name: Jaewoo Lee, Kyuil Sim, Hyeongyu Kang, Kanghoon Lee, Woocheol Shin, Jinkyoo Park

entry.summary: Extends direct preference optimization to few-step generative models whose likelihoods are intractable, using nonparametric likelihood estimation to enable DPO-style alignment from pairwise preferences without training a reward model. FestDPO aligns few-step generators to desirable properties while retaining their sampling efficiency.

entry.title: Separating personal from population gains when calibrating EEG foundation models for new users

author.name: Xilin Tao, Kani Chen

entry.summary: The paper evaluates whether personalization gains in EEG foundation models reflect true individual adaptation or just a stronger population model, testing three frozen EEG foundation models across 235 held-out subjects. Personal adapters improve balanced accuracy over the population model and over adapters fitted to other users, confirming genuine personalization value. This has direct implications for brain-computer interface calibration protocols.

entry.title: EdgeCraft: Automated Model Crafting for Edge IoT

author.name: Genglin Wang, Kaiwei Liu, Liekang Zeng, Wangsong Yin, Shangcheng Jin, Guoliang Xing, Zhenyu Yan

entry.summary: EdgeCraft is an LLM-driven system that converts high-level user intent into deployable edge ML artifacts, navigating search over data representation, model design, training, and runtime customization while meeting dynamic SLOs for quality, latency, and energy. It also addresses low-cost trustworthy verification on target devices.

entry.title: Collaborative Principle Evolution via Evidence Transfer for Scientific Discovery

author.name: Yingming Pu, Hongyu Chen, Tao Lin

entry.summary: Presents COEVOLVE, an LLM-agent framework for automated scientific discovery that runs parallel principle-evolution branches and coordinates them via evidence transfer. It uses value-of-information-gated routing and context-discounted likelihood injection so branches share measurements while keeping independent principle posteriors. This addresses the sequential exploration bottleneck in LLM-driven discovery loops.

entry.title: Control-Geometry Straightening for Sampling-Based Latent Planning

author.name: Ziang Fu, Ning Ning

entry.summary: The authors introduce Control-Geometry Straightening (CGS), an auxiliary loss for joint-embedding predictive world models that aligns pairwise action similarities with latent-difference similarities to make sampling-based planning easier to optimize. They provide theory under linear dynamics linking the objective to temporal straightening and show improved planning across world-model architectures.

entry.title: The Temporal Tug-of-War: Visualizing and Detecting RAG Conflicts in Diffusion Models via Trajectory Variance

author.name: Sravan Karthick T, Pranav Darshan, Pranav A, Minal Moharir, Ivan P. Yamshchikov

entry.summary: Studies how discrete diffusion language models handle conflicts between retrieved context and parametric knowledge in RAG, observing that competing knowledge sources create visible divergence across denoising trajectories. It introduces the Trajectory Variance Score (TVS), a lightweight interpretable detection measure computable from as few as two parallel inference runs.

entry.title: Calibration-Free Surface Normals Estimation in Vision-Based Tactile Sensing using Universal Photometric Stereo

author.name: Zdravko Dugonjic, Stefanie Speidel, Roberto Calandra

entry.summary: Proposes a calibration-free procedure for estimating contact surface normals in vision-based tactile sensors using Universal Photometric Stereo networks, eliminating the need to physically press known-shape probes against each sensor. Real-world experiments across three sensors with different optical systems demonstrate the approach's generality.

entry.title: DegreeSpar: Structured Degree Sparsity for Efficient Secure Transformer Inference

author.name: Yifei Cai, Zhuoran Li, Xiaozuo Shen, Hongyi Wu, Chunsheng Xin

entry.summary: DegreeSpar formulates secure Transformer inference compression as structured sparsification over nonlinear polynomial degrees, addressing the Softmax and GeLU bottlenecks in cryptographic inference. The paper shows that independently stacking existing approximation, token-pruning, and model-pruning methods degrades ViT-S accuracy from 80.20% to 76.41% at matched compression, while jointly optimizing polynomial degrees avoids this accumulation of perturbations. Relevant to privacy-preserving inference.

entry.title: Convergent Plug-and-Play Image Restoration with Annealed Noise Levels

author.name: Samuel Hurault

entry.summary: The paper establishes convergence guarantees for Plug-and-Play image restoration algorithms that anneal the denoiser noise level across iterations, covering deterministic methods like RED-GD and PnP-PGD and stochastic methods like SNORE and a PnP-Flow variant. For each method it identifies an explicit nonconvex objective tied to the terminal denoising level and proves asymptotic stationarity of the iterates.

entry.title: Revisiting AdaGrad in Stochastic Convex Optimization: Last Iterates, High Probability, and Lower Bounds

author.name: Weiming Ou, Xiao Wang

entry.summary: The paper shows AdaGrad and AdaGrad-Norm admit no universal last-iterate rate even with sub-Gaussian noise and bounded iterates, and that bounded variance alone cannot yield high-probability average-iterate rates. It also constructs tight Omega(log T / sqrt T) lower bounds proving the log T factor in existing upper bounds is unavoidable, resolving open questions about these widely used adaptive methods.

entry.title: Sharp training-conditional coverage for conformal prediction under covariate shift

author.name: Mehrdad Pournaderi

entry.summary: This paper derives explicit training-conditional coverage bounds for weighted split conformal prediction under covariate shift, using a single concentration inequality at a fixed population quantile. The key finding is that the relevant scale is a variance proxy built from chi-squared divergence rather than the supremum of the likelihood ratio, with matching two-point lower bounds. This sharpens guarantees for conformal methods beyond marginal coverage.

entry.title: CLIMB-flow: Coupled Linear Inverse posterior sampling via Multiscale-Based flow

author.name: Zeqiu Yu, Ruizhi Yuan, Mathews Jacob

entry.summary: CLIMB-Flow is a posterior sampling algorithm for Bayesian imaging inverse problems built on pyramidal or cascaded diffusion architectures, avoiding the spatial detail loss and nonlinearity introduced by latent autoencoder compression. It alternates end-point estimation from coarse noisy images, data-consistent updates, and coarse-to-fine hierarchical generation in the pixel domain.

entry.title: AgentWare: Automating the Lifecycle of Agentic Applications across the Edge-to-Cloud Continuum

author.name: Michalis Kasioulis, Moysis Symeonides, George Pallis, Marios D. Dikaiakos

entry.summary: AgentWare is an AgenticOps framework that automates provisioning, deployment, observability, and evaluation of LLM-based agentic applications across heterogeneous edge-to-cloud infrastructure. It addresses the gap where existing tools handle agent development, observability, or benchmarking in isolation. The system provides an end-to-end pipeline that prepares execution environments and transforms user-defined agent implementations for distributed deployment.

entry.title: Do Emotion Concepts Generalize Across Sources, Modalities, and Architectures in Vision-Language Models?

author.name: Bohao Xing, Xin Liu, Kaishen Yuan, Deng Li, Rong Gao, Guoying Zhao, Xiaolan Fu, Heikki K\"alvi\"ainen

entry.summary: The paper investigates whether emotion concepts generalize across sources, modalities, and architectures in vision-language models, constructing CMES, a multi-source collection of emotion-conditioned stories, real facial expressions, synthetic portraits, and synthetic scenes. It extracts Ekman emotion vectors from three VLMs per stimulus source and reports four findings, including that image-derived emotion vectors form a low-dimensional geometry similar to text-derived ones. This provides a systematic account of how emotion representations transfer across inputs and models.

entry.title: Conformal Prediction and Conditional Coverage for Tabular Foundation Models

author.name: Sungwoo Park, Sunghee Park, Won Chang

entry.summary: The paper introduces C-USIM, a lightweight application of highest predictive density split conformal prediction to tabular foundation models that accommodates multimodal predictive distributions without additional training or model inference. It provides finite-sample marginal validity under stated assumptions, bounds conditional-marginal coverage gaps via distribution-estimation error and score discreteness, and examines coverage heterogeneity using percentile rank-score plots. Experiments use TabPFN-style models.

entry.title: DF-CBM: Region-Aware Concept Bottleneck Models for Deepfake Detection

author.name: Georgios Tsoumplekas, Vazgken Vanian, Alexandros Doumanoglou, Panos K. Papadopoulos, Yannis Spyridis, Dimitrios Zarpalas, Vasileios Argyriou

entry.summary: DF-CBM is a concept bottleneck model for deepfake detection that provides region-grounded, semantically meaningful explanations of manipulation cues. It builds a compact vocabulary of manipulation concepts from textual artifact annotations and links each concept to plausible facial and boundary regions, addressing the gap between localization-only and language-only explainability methods.

entry.title: AnswerMap: Faithful Spatial Interpretability of VLMs from Answer Posteriors

author.name: Mohamed Eltahir, Fardows Adam, Duaa M. Tahir, Lama Alamoudi, Sana Ammar, Atheer A. Alboloshi, Jory Albluey, Tanveer Hussain, Naeemullah Khan

entry.summary: AnswerMap is a training-free, black-box spatial interpretability method for vision-language models that slices an image into row and column bands, queries a frozen model with yes/no relevance questions, and forms a query-conditioned spatial map from the outer product of row and column posteriors. Because it derives from the output head, it reflects final model behavior and supports continuous read-outs like localization.

entry.title: Using LMs to Model the Effects of Context and Coreference during Sentence Comprehension

author.name: Kohei Kajikawa, Lin Ai, Tatsuki Kuribayashi, Ethan Gotlieb Wilcox

entry.summary: The study systematically varies GPT-2's context window size across four large naturalistic English reading-time datasets, finding a U-shaped relationship: very restricted contexts capture local working-memory limits while expanded contexts of 500 to 1,000 tokens yield the best overall psychometric fit. This suggests strict memory-decay modeling overlooks humans' reliance on long-range discourse structure. The work refines how LMs should be configured as cognitive models of sentence comprehension.

entry.title: Generalization and Memorization along the Learning Trajectory of Neural Language Models: A Geometric Account of Categorization

author.name: Wang Bojun, Holly Jenkins, Elizabeth Wonnacott

entry.summary: Using controlled synthetic grammars, this paper tracks how generalization and memorization develop over training via the geometry of representation space and model behavior. It finds that unoccupied regions of representation space become systematically structured from the earliest stages of learning, forming category-level organization that supports generalization to unattested combinations, while prolonged training in larger models increasingly separates observed from unobserved grammatical combinations. This provides a geometric account of categorization in language models.

entry.title: OptiArena: Can LLMs Improve Executable Algorithms under Fixed Resource Budgets?

author.name: Wenjun Peng, Xinyu Wang

entry.summary: OptiArena is a budget-controlled testbed evaluating whether LLMs can improve executable game-playing algorithms through five rounds of code edits under fixed scaffolds, bounded evaluator feedback, and fixed resource budgets. It features two optimization regimes, surface obfuscation controls, calibrated references, held-out and stress splits, and diagnostics for degradation and exceptional failures, with LLM API cost reported separately. This moves beyond static QA and code-generation benchmarks toward iterative algorithmic improvement.

entry.title: AdaTutoRank: Learning to Rerank Document Sets via Adaptive Tutoring Optimization for RAG and Deep Research

author.name: Kailin Jiang, Lei Liu, Jian Xi, Yangqi Chen, Hui Xu, Hongwei Zhao, Bin Li, Yu Lu, Haibo Shi

entry.summary: AdaTutoRank targets set-level document reranking for RAG and deep research, addressing the sparse-credit problem in aggregate-rubric scoring where redundant and decisive documents receive identical supervision. It appears to use on-policy distillation with adaptive tutoring optimization to give finer-grained credit for composing complementary, non-redundant document sets. The work matters because retrieval set composition strongly conditions downstream answer quality.

entry.title: MixDetect: Word-Level Localization and Quantification of AI Editing

author.name: Hongrui Bao, Yubing Ren, Zhendong Pan, Fang Fang, Shi Wang, Yanan Cao

entry.summary: MixDetect is a word-level framework that localizes and quantifies AI editing of human-written text, predicting per-word whether it was edited and, conditionally, how substantial the edit is, so editing scope and intensity are estimated separately. Training constructs word-level supervision from source-edited pairs while inference needs only the input text. It moves AI-text detection beyond binary human-vs-AI classification toward realistic partial machine involvement.

entry.title: Are You Sure You're Sure? Two Confounds in a Sycophancy Benchmark

author.name: Atharv Gupta, Akshat Jindal, Lavanya Nigam, Aryan Sood

entry.summary: This paper audits the SycEval sycophancy benchmark, showing that its prompt templates vary two features alongside the timing property they claim to isolate: objection strength escalation (with target-naming differences at weak levels) and a second unmentioned confound, undermining the reported finding that preemptive objections cause more caving than in-context ones. It is a careful methodological critique with direct implications for how sycophancy experiments should be controlled. Benchmark confounds like this propagate into flawed conclusions about model behavior.

entry.title: Beyond Memory Construction: Rethinking Memory Access for LLM-based Conversational Agents

author.name: Donghua Cai, Yongheng Deng, Yifei Wang, Zijun Shen, Ju Ren

entry.summary: Shows that the dominant paradigm of LLM-based memory construction (rewriting interactions into structured memory units retrieved via RAG) becomes lossy, unstable, and costly in long-horizon, high-entropy conversations. Proposes Threader, a memory system that shifts focus from memory construction to efficient, structure-aware access over raw interaction data. Relevant to building conversational agents that remain coherent over long interactions.

entry.title: Grounding Memory Summarization in Utility Intent

author.name: Zhenyu Lei, Mingjia Shi, Xingbo Fu, Haoyu He, Qi R. Wang, Jundong Li

entry.summary: Argues that memory summarizers optimized for human-facing faithfulness misalign with their real objective of preserving evidence for future queries, and shows conditioning summarization on query-answer pairs improves answer quality in transferable ways. Proposes MemSuit, a self-distillation framework where a query-conditioned teacher produces utility-aware memory entries that a student learns to reproduce from raw conversations, while mitigating collateral erasure of evidence. Relevant to memory-augmented conversational systems.

entry.title: MIC: Explaining Image-Claim Inconsistencies in AI-Generated Multimodal Misinformation

author.name: Ruihong Zeng, Jonathan Tonglet, Preslav Nakov, Iryna Gurevych

entry.summary: Introduces MIC, a fact-checking framework that goes beyond AI-image provenance detection to verify whether an AI-generated image's content is consistent with the context implied by its claim, explaining inconsistencies using world knowledge. Combines supervised fine-tuning with GRPO-based RL for task adaptation and explanation quality. Timely for combating the growing wave of AI-generated multimodal misinformation.

entry.title: Evaluating Machine Unlearning in ASR

author.name: Diogo Dinis, Francisco Teixeira, Bhiksha Raj, Alberto Abad, Isabel Trancoso

entry.summary: This paper brings machine unlearning research to automatic speech recognition for right-to-be-forgotten compliance, applying several MU techniques to an ASR model and evaluating privacy-utility trade-offs for single-subject, then sequential and simultaneous unlearning. Gradient ascent-based algorithms achieve strong trade-offs, while complex approaches over-unlearn samples and become identifiable as unlearned, suggesting standard privacy evaluation tools need adaptation for ASR. This fills a gap in a compliance-critical area.

entry.title: ReMCTS: Reflection-Enhanced Monte Carlo Tree Search for Code Generation

author.name: Huifei Wang, Xinying Huang, Yiheng Sun, Yifan Yuan

entry.summary: ReMCTS is an execution-grounded, memory-augmented MCTS-style search framework for code generation that organizes candidates as tree states, retains branch-local debugging context, and retrieves cross-branch failure experience. It improves over direct generation in 8 of 10 model-dataset pairs on HumanEval and MBPP-Sanitized under held-out evaluation.

entry.title: Adapt Semantics, Not Structure: Few-Instance Schema Calibration for Scientific PDF Extraction

author.name: Zixiao Dong, Wei Yang, Zihao Liu, Chenshu Li, Longzhang Liu, Tao Tan, Hong Xie

entry.summary: CPSE frames few-instance schema calibration for scientific PDF extraction: it decomposes a schema into an invariant structural contract and mutable field semantics, jointly calibrating extraction prompts and field-level descriptions from a few gold annotations. This avoids costly manual tuning of hundreds of field definitions.

entry.title: AraDynFact: Dynamic Evaluation of Factual Knowledge in Arabic

author.name: Ignacio Iacobacci, Faroq Altam, Zhaozhi Qian, Muhammad Alqurishi

entry.summary: AraDynFact is a dynamic evaluation framework for measuring LLMs' factual knowledge and cultural sensitivity across the diverse Arabic-speaking world. It addresses gaps in existing benchmarks, which focus on translation or generic reasoning and rely on expensive human-in-the-loop processes, by automating knowledge-coverage evaluation. The framework aims to capture historical, social, and regional nuances of Arabic culture.

entry.title: Acoustic Progress Propagation for Long-Horizon Speculative Decoding in ASR

author.name: Yuanyuan Jia, Qianqian Yang

entry.summary: The paper proposes a progress-aware speculative drafter for autoregressive ASR that recurrently propagates an acoustic progress state across draft steps and feeds it back into audio cross-attention to guide token generation, jointly training the drafter and progress predictor over variable draft horizons. On five ASR test sets it achieves lossless end-to-end speedups of 1.657x and 1.227x with Qwen3-ASR-0.6B and Qwen3-ASR-1.7B respectively, improving macro-averaged speedup over AnchorDraft by 34.3% and more. This addresses saturation of acceptance length for long draft horizons.

entry.title: Language-Augmented Video Action Anticipation: Design Fundamentals, Benchmarks, and Open Challenges

author.name: Mahsa Mohammadi, Zeyu Fu, Sareh Rowlands

entry.summary: A review of language-augmented video action anticipation that organizes the literature via an evidence-aware design map crossing task regime with the point where language-derived information intervenes. Characterizes task regimes along six axes and five task families, and identifies benchmarks and open challenges.

entry.title: Beyond Volume Overlap: Surface Matching for Topology-Aware Coronary Artery Segmentation

author.name: Rafael Velasquez, Esther Puyol-Ant\'on, Pablo Arbel\'aez

entry.summary: The paper argues that Dice-based evaluation is poorly suited to thin tubular anatomy like coronary arteries, where missing distal branches barely affects volume overlap. It introduces a bipartite surface-matching metric under radius-tolerant localization that decouples false-positive and false-negative branches, improving evaluation fidelity for clinical use.

entry.title: PQR3D: Progressive Query Refinement over Reference-Conditioned Temporal Windows for Multi-View 3D Object Detection

author.name: Hui Ye, Yudong Liu, Yiran Chen, Rajshekhar Sunderraman, Shihao Ji

entry.summary: PQR3D improves camera-only multi-view 3D detection by refining queries within reference-conditioned temporal windows instead of propagating persistent query states across frames. This enables random frame sampling and independent inference, with motion-aligned query transfer and masked self-attention separating denoising queries from detection.

entry.title: One Perception, All Maneuvers: Directional Traffic Signal Understanding for Maneuver-Level Signal Intent Prediction

author.name: Ang Zou, Runzhe Zheng, Zhigang li, Zhen Yang, Han Xia, Xuewei Li, Zequn Qin, Xi Li

entry.summary: The paper reformulates traffic signal perception from instance-level detection and color recognition into Directional Traffic Signal Understanding, predicting structured signal states for straight, left-turn, right-turn, and U-turn maneuvers from a front-view image. This closes a semantic gap between what a signal displays and which ego maneuver it permits, directly serving downstream planning.

entry.title: QuacamFM: Quaternion-Constrained Flow Matching for Camera Pose Estimation

author.name: Bao-Long Tran, Cuong Le, Tahereh Dehdarirad, Fredrik Viksten, Per-Erik Forss\'en

entry.summary: Introduces a flow matching formulation for camera pose estimation that respects the unit-norm constraint of quaternions, unlike prior diffusion-based approaches that treat quaternions as unconstrained 4D vectors. This yields smoother, more geometrically valid generation trajectories for multi-view pose hypotheses under sparse-view ambiguity.

entry.title: LoCoVSR: Local Context Diffusion Posterior Sampling for Video Super-Resolution

author.name: Matan Ben Chorin, Michael Elad

entry.summary: LoCoVSR combines diffusion posterior sampling with spatio-temporal context learning in a moving-average form for pixel-space video super-resolution. A localized window of adjacent low-resolution frames recovers each center frame with a shared noise trajectory, enabling arbitrary-length videos, parallel inference, and reduced error accumulation.

entry.title: LoopTrack: A Simple Baseline for Parameter-Efficient Transformer Tracking

author.name: Liang Peng, Chenxiao Li, Libo Zhang, Xingping Dong, Heng Fan

entry.summary: Proposes LoopTrack, a parameter-efficient visual tracker that repeatedly applies a shared set of Transformer blocks in a loop rather than stacking distinct blocks, plus lightweight target-aware looping and gated designs to exploit target cues. The goal is deployment-friendly tracking on resource-limited devices with competitive accuracy. It offers a simple strong baseline for efficient tracking.

entry.title: Groupwise Selective State-Space Filtering for Accurate and Streaming Action Boundary Detection

author.name: Mustafa Bora \c{C}elik

entry.summary: This paper presents a class-agnostic action boundary detection adapter using groupwise selective state-space scans over pre-extracted video features, achieving F1 scores of 0.457/0.622/0.611 on Breakfast, GTEA, and 50Salads. A stateful variant supports streaming inference with zero neural look-ahead, one-sample peak confirmation, and bounded memory.

entry.title: MetaSampling: Making Frame Samplers Efficient for Long-Video Question Answering

author.name: Ashim Dahal, Bikramjit Banerjee

entry.summary: MetaSampling is a training-free, plug-and-play strategy applied on top of existing long-video VQA frame selectors that dynamically reduces the number of frames passed to the MLLM while preserving or improving answer accuracy. It is evaluated across 36 paired configurations of frame selectors, MLLM backbones, and VQA benchmarks. This improves the efficiency of long-video understanding pipelines without retraining.

entry.title: MotionSpaceFlow: Representation-Aware Flow Matching in Direct Motion Space

author.name: Qing Yu, Kent Fujiwara

entry.summary: MSFlow is a flow-matching framework that generates human motion directly in continuous motion space without a learned encoder-decoder, using representation-aware noise scaling to handle the anisotropic structure of direct motion representations. This avoids the bottleneck of reconstruction-oriented latent spaces and allows direct manipulation of individual frames and joints.

entry.title: Trustworthy synthetic visual media: Evidence across the media lifecycle

author.name: Zexi Jia, Zhiqiang Yuan, Jie Zhou, Jinchao Zhang

entry.summary: This review examines how trust in images and videos must shift from appearance-based judgment to provenance evidence when generative systems can produce and revise realistic media without a stable history. It surveys approaches for recovering or recording evidence across the media lifecycle and evaluates when such claims survive ordinary processing or deliberate manipulation.

entry.title: SurgGMF: Fully Causal Gaussian Motion Forecasting for Anticipatory Surgical Scene Rendering

author.name: Jingqian Sun, Yichao Tang

entry.summary: SurgGMF forecasts future Gaussian motion states (position, scale, rotation residuals) from historical Gaussian motion fields for anticipatory rendering of deformable surgical scenes, rather than predicting future RGB frames directly. A full-causal-last rendering protocol prevents target leakage, supporting robotic perception and decision support in surgery.

entry.title: Revisit to Segment: Working Memory Distillation for Reasoning Segmentation

author.name: Cilin Yan, Yilun Qiu, Wanyang Zhang, Rui Zu, Xiaolong Jiang, Yao Hu, Jiayin Cai

entry.summary: The authors observe that multimodal LLMs produce reasoning traces and localization proposals that can act as working memory when revisiting an image, improving reasoning segmentation. They propose distilling this self-generated revisiting guidance into the backbone model (RS-WM) so it benefits with or without working memory at inference time. This connects test-time iterative refinement ideas with training-time distillation for segmentation.

entry.title: LVMT: Video Mask Transformer for Long-term Video Segmentation

author.name: Narges Norouzi, Niccol`o Cavagnero, Idil Esen Zulfikar, Bastian Leibe, Gijs Dubbelman, Daan de Geus

entry.summary: LVMT improves online video segmentation for long, complex videos with long-term occlusions via a lightweight GRU-based temporal propagation module that adaptively selects what object information to carry forward. To enable training on long videos despite memory limits and vanishing gradients, it introduces Truncated Query Propagation, a strategy that processes videos in segments. This addresses a well-known weakness of current video segmentation models.

entry.title: Ego-Forge: Text and Geometric-Attention Free Exo-to-Egocentric Video Generation

author.name: Mohammad Mahdi, Luc Van Gool, Danda Pani Paudel

entry.summary: Ego-Forge synthesizes egocentric video from third-person footage and a target head trajectory without requiring text captions of the unseen view or expensive geometry-guided attention, removing input requirements of prior work like EgoX while targeting cross-activity, in-the-wild generalization. The task requires hallucinating content never observed by the exocentric camera. Simplifying inputs for egocentric video synthesis improves practical usability.

entry.title: BiMoGen: Bidirectional Motion-Text Generation via Unified Masked Discrete Diffusion

author.name: Wanjiang Weng, Yongliang Wu, Xiaofeng Tan, Xingyu Zhu, Wenbo Zhu, Hongsong Wang

entry.summary: BiMoGen unifies text-to-motion generation and motion-to-text captioning within a masked discrete diffusion framework, using iterative bidirectional prediction to avoid the fixed generation order and error persistence of autoregressive approaches. This targets temporal coherence and cross-modal consistency in human motion modeling. Applying masked discrete diffusion to bidirectional motion-text tasks is a natural but well-executed design choice.

entry.title: FlowTool: Controlling Tool Parameter in Image Retouching via Flow Matching

author.name: Thanh-Long V. Le, Steven Walton, Seunghyun Yoon, Branislav Kveton, Trung Bui, Eunho Yang, Viet Lai

entry.summary: FlowTool reframes tool-based image editing as flow matching: a VLM backbone handles multimodal understanding while a Diffusion Transformer generates tool parameters as an editing plan via conditional rectified flow, trained with two-stage supervised flow matching. It directly models the distribution of high-quality tool parameters conditioned on image and instruction.

entry.title: Electric Potential Patterns Forecasting in the Southern Hemisphere with Deep Learning Techniques

author.name: Francesco Pio Ramunno, Simone Mestici, Igino Coco, Maria Walach, Stefano Massetti, Maria Federica Marcucci, Brandon Panos, Andr\'e Csillaghy

entry.summary: This work applies deep learning to forecast the full spatial structure of high-latitude ionospheric electric potential patterns in the Southern Hemisphere, relevant to space weather operations. The authors compare three architectures, including a probabilistic diffusion model conditioned on multivariate solar wind inputs, against empirical climatological models and physics-based MHD simulations. Accurate real-time forecasting here protects satellite navigation, radio communications, and power infrastructure.

entry.title: Concepts Complement Dense Semantics: Learning Compact Sparse Spaces for Text-Image Retrieval

author.name: Yoonseo Kim, Jungwoo Choi, Cheonyoung Park, Youngwook Kim, Yongho Song, SeongKu Kang

entry.summary: GRASP complements dense vision-language embeddings with a compact, grounded sparse space that stores interpretable visual-textual concepts mined from the corpus. A lightweight sparse head predicts which concepts are relevant to each image or text, providing explicit lexical evidence for fine-grained cross-modal matching. This improves retrieval precision where dense embeddings blur fine-grained information.

entry.title: EdgeVLN: Runtime-Aware Deployment Ready Quantized Vision Language Navigation Model

author.name: Rithvik Jonna, Man Namgung, Aakash Gurram, Tinoosh Mohsenin

entry.summary: EdgeVLN is a deployment-ready quantized vision-language navigation model combining a quantized StreamVLN with LATTE, a lightweight causal transformer for real-time stopping decisions, executed via a custom llama.cpp VLN driver that reconstructs streaming context and prunes memory on-board. It targets memory, latency, and energy budgets of edge robotic platforms while preserving navigation behavior.

entry.title: REALM: A Coarse-to-Fine Generative Framework for Embodied Reactive Listening

author.name: Peizhen Li, Longbing Cao, Yang Zhang

entry.summary: A coarse-to-fine framework for audio-driven reactive listening motion generation, combining history-aware temporal alignment of speaker cues with the listener's ongoing motion and stochastic refinement for local facial events like brief expressions and blinks.

entry.title: Learning with Object-centric Representations of Tactile Interactive Perception for Robot Manipulation

author.name: Xinyi Yang, Zilin Si, Zhuowei Xu, Zeynep Temel, Oliver Kroemer

entry.summary: This work builds an object-centric, context-aware manipulation framework that learns task-agnostic object representations via tactile exploration, using a token learner to select representative tactile segments and contrastive alignment with text embeddings. It addresses the transient, sparse nature of tactile signals for properties like material, contents, and softness that vision cannot reveal. It matters because tactile exploration could ground manipulation policies in hidden physical properties.

entry.title: MomWorld: Momentum-Aware Latent World Model for Long-Horizon Autonomous Driving

author.name: Ziying Song, Shengkai Zhang, Lei Yang, Haozhuang Chi, Yuchen Liu, Jiangtao Su, Lin Liu, Ziyang Liu, Chen Lv

entry.summary: MomWorld is a momentum-aware latent world model for long-horizon driving that extracts scene motion trends from historical-to-current observations and propagates latent momentum into future horizons, jointly predicting configuration and momentum states with a learnable momentum persistence mechanism. It addresses the failure of single-latent-state rollouts to retain useful dynamics over long horizons. It matters for safer long-horizon planning in autonomous driving.

entry.title: DexTaG: Tactile-as-Guidance in Reinforcement Learning for Dexterous Manipulation

author.name: Han Yang, Yian Wang, Yunlong Song, Zhenjia Xu, Chuang Gan

entry.summary: DexTaG uses tactile signals as guidance in RL for dexterous manipulation, addressing the kinematic gap between glove-captured human motions and robot hands for contact-rich tool use like in-hand reorientation, while preserving natural human contact patterns. Unlike per-trajectory optimization, it aims to avoid training a separate policy for each reference. This matters for scalable dexterous skill learning from human data.

entry.title: GAE: General Action Expert for Real-Time Humanoid Teleoperation

author.name: Yuefan Wang, Huaicheng Zhou, Xiao He, Zhijie He, Mingchuan Yang, Huayi Zhang, Li Chai, Jinxin Liu, Donglin Wang

entry.summary: GAE is a unified framework for low-latency, general-purpose humanoid whole-body teleoperation built on a large-scale human motion dataset aggregated from videos, animations, and motion capture with standardization and augmentation. A two-stage pipeline addresses noise and embodiment mismatch in human motions to enable responsive synchronization between operators and humanoid avatars. The goal is extending human physical presence into remote social, service, and labor activities.

entry.title: MarsLab: A Martian Rover Simulator for Planetary Rover Autonomous Navigation

author.name: Hoyun Kim, Beomsu Kim, Giseop Kim

entry.summary: MarsLab is an open-source, ROS2-native Mars rover simulator built on NVIDIA Isaac Sim, combining HiRISE-derived and procedural terrain with customizable rock, crater, solar-illumination, and atmospheric-dust settings, and running a Perseverance-class rover model. It fills a gap among existing mission-oriented simulators, fixed analog datasets, and task-specific environments for developing rover autonomy. The platform targets navigation algorithm development under Mars-relevant conditions like changing illumination and dust.

entry.title: QuadHand: A Compact Quadrotor Aerial Manipulator with MRC-SDF-Based Whole-Body Motion Planning

author.name: Rui Jin, Ruiyang Liu, Xinhang Xu, Haotian Jin, Yi Wang, Yizhuo Yang, Lihua Xi

entry.summary: QuadHand is a compact quadrotor aerial manipulator with a 3-DoF arm, gripper, and passive center-of-gravity compensation to reduce arm-induced disturbances, paired with MRC-SDF, a robot-centric signed distance field representation balancing geometric fidelity and computation. A spatiotemporal whole-body trajectory optimization framework enables close-proximity 3D physical interaction. It advances aerial manipulation hardware and planning together.

entry.title: Hierarchical Multi-agent Reinforcement Learning for Warehouse Robot Coordination under Communication Loss

author.name: Weihao Sun, Gehui Xu, Andreas A. Malikopoulos

entry.summary: This paper proposes a hierarchical multi-agent RL framework for warehouse robot teams under communication loss, partitioning robots into groups with centralized intra-group and distributed inter-group coordination. Recurrent predictors estimate unavailable interaction information, a higher-level policy emits compact coordination references, and a predictive safety filter enforces constraints. Simulations show improved task completion and reduced communication overhead under lossy links.

entry.title: Isotonic surrogate modeling for computer experiments with many input variables

author.name: Jaehoan Kim, Simon Mak

entry.summary: This paper proposes a new Bayesian isotonic surrogate model for computer experiments that scales to many input variables, addressing statistical and computational limitations of existing approaches. By efficiently incorporating monotonicity information elicited from physical systems, it improves emulation accuracy and uncertainty quantification at small sample sizes.

entry.title: Dialogue with Eliezer Yudkowsky on FOOM

author.name: aashish

entry.summary: A preserved verbatim Twitter/X exchange in which the author discusses the Hanson-Yudkowsky AI-Foom debate and Eliezer Yudkowsky joins to object, leading to a substantive dialogue on local versus global intelligence explosions, content versus architecture, and what the old arguments predicted about modern AI. The post includes editorial context and notes.

entry.title: No country controls every layer: The hidden AI systems reshaping global power

author.name: greysunsets

entry.summary: A linkpost to an 18-month ABC News visual investigation of the physical and geopolitical substrate of AI: chips, memory, data centers, energy, and the interdependencies between countries, arguing no nation controls every layer of the AI stack.

entry.title: BIRD: Distilling Decision Boundaries into Rationales for MLLM Adaptation

author.name: Anglin Liu, Yanlin Wu, Ruichao Chen, Yuting Zhang, Qingyuan Zeng, Pengxiang Cai, Ziqi Gong, Muchen Li, Jintai Chen
